jobs.title: DIRECTOR, GOVERNMENT FUNDS - Montreal, Ottawa & Toronto
jobs.description:
We are banking at another level. 

 Choosing BDC as your employer means working in a healthy, inclusive, and skilled workplace that puts forward the best conditions to bring together unique teams where employees are empowered to act. It also means being at the centre of ambitious economic and financial projects to see further and to do things differently, to fuel the success of Canadian entrepreneurs.

 Choosing BDC as your employer also means: 
 Flexible and competitive benefits, including an Employee Savings and Investment Plan where BDC matches part of your voluntary contributions, a Defined Benefit Pension Plan, a $750 wellness and health care spending account, to name a few   

 In addition to paid vacation each year, five personal days, sick days as necessary, and our offices are closed from December 25 to January 1 

 A hybrid work model that truly balances work and personal life

 Opportunities for learning, training and development, and much more... 

 Explore the BDC Way in our Culture Book 

 Join a team shaping Canada’s venture capital ecosystem 
 At BDC, the Government Funds team manages capital on behalf of the Government of Canada to strengthen and grow Canada’s venture capital market. This includes deploying $350M under the Venture Capital Action Plan (VCAP), $450M under the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (VCCI), and $450M under the Renewed Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Renewed VCCI). These programs totalling $1.2B AUM are designed to crowd in private capital and support fund managers across the Canadian venture capital asset class.
 Building on this foundation, BDC is now deploying the $1B Growth Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (Growth VCCI), a landmark platform focused on scaling Canada’s most promising funds and innovative companies.
 This is a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of investment, policy, and ecosystem development, with direct exposure to the most prominent Canadian fund managers while contributing to a national priority initiative shaping Canada’s innovation economy.

 POSITION OVERVIEW 
 As Director, you will combine leadership, investment expertise, and complex project management to support the deployment and oversight of government-backed venture capital programs, including VCAP, VCCI, Renewed VCCI, and upcoming Growth VCCI.
 You will play a lead role in investment execution, stakeholder management, and portfolio governance, while engaging closely with fund managers, institutional partners, and internal stakeholders including Government.

 CHALLENGES TO BE MET 
 Investment Expertise 
 Lead complex business and legal negotiations with fund managers and external stakeholders for execution of program delivery including fund investments.
 Provide strategic oversight of investment activities across the portfolio, ensuring alignment between policy objectives, portfolio construction considerations, and market dynamics
 Provide senior investment judgment and guidance on fund performance, risk management, and portfolio development matters

 Fund Oversight & Governance 
 Serve as BDC’s representative on portfolio funds’ LPACs and other governance bodies
 Monitor fund performance, governance, and compliance with fund agreements and program requirements
 Provide strategic insight and constructive challenge to support strong governance practices and enhance fund outcomes
 Guide fund managers on governance and operational best practices to strengthen the long-term sustainability of the venture capital ecosystem

 Leadership and Team Management 
 Demonstrate leadership in team meetings and operations processes, ensuring effective resource allocation, quality control, operational excellence, and alignment with strategic priorities
 Ensure the timely and accurate execution of operational activities, including capital calls, distributions, reporting, and stakeholder deliverables
 Provide coaching, mentorship, and leadership to a team of Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture focused on continuous improvement and professional development
 Identify capability and capacity gaps, oversee recruitment and onboarding activities, and promote knowledge sharing and best practices across the team

 Program Delivery & Stakeholder Management 
 Provide strategic input into the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of current and future government investment programs
 Respond to complex and time-sensitive requests from internal and external stakeholders while maintaining a high standard of service and professionalism
 Oversee the preparation and dissemination of quarterly and annual reporting, performance dashboards, and stakeholder communications
 Ensure high standards of quality, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness across all reporting outputs and program deliverables

 Portfolio & Ecosystem Leadership 
 Build and maintain strong relationships with fund managers, institutional investors, ecosystem stakeholders, and government partners
 Represent BDC Capital and Government Funds at industry conferences, panels, events, and stakeholder forums
 Stay closely connected to venture capital trends, market developments, and emerging opportunities to support strategic decision-making
 Support and lead thought leadership initiatives, market studies, and research projects that generate insights from government investment programs and portfolio activities

 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 Experience and qualifications 
 Minimum of a Bachelor degree in Commerce or a related discipline (finance, accounting, law or business administration preferred), or an equivalent combination of academic training and relevant professional experience
 10 years+ experience in venture capital, private equity, or growth investing, with direct exposure to deal-making at the fund level as well as investment underwriting, structuring, business and legal negotiations and execution
 Demonstrated expertise in venture capital fund structures, LPAs, governance frameworks, and policy-driven investment programs
 Demonstrated ability to lead complex negotiations and manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously
 Significant experience serving on LPACs, Boards of Directors, or equivalent governance bodies
 Ability to manage complex stakeholder relationships involving fund managers, institutional investors, government representatives, and senior executives
 Strong understanding of the Canadian venture capital ecosystem and a well-established network of industry relationships
 Experience leading, coaching, and developing high-performing teams

 Core competencies 
 Strong strategic and investment judgment
 Demonstrated leadership and people management capabilities
 Excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills
 Ability to align operational execution with broader policy, program, and organizational objectives
 High level of rigour, organization, and attention to detail
 Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced, multi-stakeholder environment
 Collaborative mindset with a commitment to team development, knowledge sharing, and excellence

 The position is primarily based in Montreal or Ottawa, with a preference for these locations. Toronto is also acceptable.
 BDC is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace that reflects the communities we serve. We are dedicated to providing an environment where all employees feel valued, respected and able to reach their full potential. We welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and encourage candidates to request accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process.

 Proudly one of Canada’s Top 100 Employers and one of Canada’s Best Diversity Employers, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable, inclusive and accessible environment where all employees can thrive and feel empowered to bring their whole selves to work. If you require an accommodation to complete your application, please do not hesitate to contact us at accessibility@bdc.ca.

 While we appreciate all applications, we advise that only the candidates selected to participate in the recruitment process will be contacted.

jobs.title: Quality Director - Infrastructure - Major Projects
jobs.description:
Quality Director - Infrastructure - Major Projects 

Reporting to the Project Director, the Quality Director plays a pivotal role in ensuring the highest standards of quality are upheld across the project. This individual will lead quality assurance initiatives, implement quality control processes, and collaborate with project teams to maintain compliance with industry standards, project specifications, and client requirements. The Quality Manager will also perform regular site inspections to ensure that activities comply with the project specifications.

You would be joining the East Harbour Transit Hub Alliance that is designing and building a new railway station that will connect 3 different rail lines and improve the daily commute of thousands of riders. This position is based at the site office, 415 Eastern Ave, Toronto.
 What You Will Be Working On 

 Develop, implement, and manage the company’s quality control program across the project.
 Lead by example, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement in quality standards.
 Support project teams in the implementation of tools and technology for QA/QC (e.g.: inspections, deficiency management, etc.)
 Conduct regular site inspections to ensure adherence to project specifications, codes, and industry standards.
 Prepare and facilitate lessons learned, documenting key takeaways and sharing insights across teams to promote continuous improvement.
 Provide strategic leadership and mentorship to site teams, ensuring quality control best practices are embedded at all levels.
 Collaborate with project managers, site supervisors, and trades to address quality concerns and deficiencies and implement corrective actions.
 Review project plans, drawings, and specifications to identify potential quality risks and recommend proactive solutions.
 Lead and coordinate quality audits and inspections by internal teams, clients, and third-party agencies.
 Provide training and guidance to site teams on quality control practices and procedures.
 Prepare and maintain detailed quality control reports and documentation,
 Continuously review and enhance quality control processes to improve project outcomes, demonstrating an innovative mindset and proactive problem-solving.

 What We Are Looking For 
 A degree or diploma in construction management, engineering, or a related field is an asset but not mandatory.
 10+ years of proven experience in the construction industry
 Experience working within the civil and transit sector would be an asset.
 Demonstrated leadership skills with the ability to inspire and motivate teams toward achieving excellence.
 Proficiency in construction management software and tools is an asset.
 Relevant certifications (e.g., CQM, ISO 9001) are advantageous.
 Competent knowledge in CSA Codes and Industry Standards
 Understanding of Jurisdictional Authority of requirements
 Flexible and able to manage multiple priorities simultaneously; meet the time demands of unpredictable activities; capable of handling pressure and challenges in a dynamic business environment
 Effective and efficient problem solving and decision-making skills; thoughtful, proactive, and creative
 Demonstrates a sense of urgency and strong commitment to achieving goals; ability to work in a challenging, fast-paced environment
 Natural leader and team builder who can build strong relationships quickly
 Strong written and oral communication skills

 For Those Who Seek to Redefine 

 The greatest achievements in history are borne from the greatness within people – where human potential meets vision, and passion fuels evolution. Unlocking this potential is the most important thing we do at Bird.

 As a leader in Canadian construction for over 100 years, the impact of our team is etched deeply within the core of our legacy. Beyond Bird, this impact is felt in the fundamental aspects of our everyday lives. From the critical infrastructure we depend on, to the energy and resources that keep us moving - we are powering our communities and shaping Canada’s skylines coast-to-coast-to-coast. Entrenched in the foundation of a culture built more than a century ago is an enduring quest to reimagine what is possible. Our impact is greater than ever, and we are looking for those who seek to redefine their story.

 What We Believe In 

 We Put Safety First 
 A healthy and safe work environment is non-negotiable. We build a culture of operational and psychological safety through engagement, learning and leadership.

 We Lead With Honesty 
 We speak and act with integrity, clarity and care so people can trust our word and our work. Being honest means we can deliver the best outcomes and consistent results.

 We Are Stronger Together 
 Success is a team effort. Our inclusive workplace enables our combined expertise, humility and creativity to unlock our greater potential.

 We Are Driven To Do Great Work 
 We built our name on quality. We have a passion for excellence in our work and relationships that honours our businesses and our industry.

 We Create Opportunity 
 Rooted in a solid foundation, we adapt and grow to face the future. We are committed to elevating each other to chart the best path forward in an evolving world.

 At Bird, we value Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DE&I) and believe it is essential to our success. We will continue to listen, learn, and take action in our commitment to building progress in our organization, and the industry as a whole. Cultivating an environment where all employees feel included, seen, and have a sense of belonging is core to Bird’s culture. We commit to proactively employing a workforce that reflects the communities in which we work, fostering an environment of continuous learning, and never compromising on our values.

jobs.title: Project Director - Industrial East
jobs.description:
Project Director - Industrial East 

Reporting to the Senior Director, the Deputy Project Director will support the delivery of one of Canada’s most complex nuclear construction projects. This role will provide senior leadership across construction execution, safety, quality, project controls, stakeholder management and team integration.

This is a site-based leadership role in Chalk River, Ontario.
 What You Will Be Working On 

 Lead overall project execution, including safety, quality, schedule, cost, risk and stakeholder alignment.

 Provide leadership to project teams, trade partners, consultants and client stakeholders to ensure project objectives are met.

 Help drive construction strategy, sequencing, logistics, resourcing and issue resolution.

 Maintain visibility into project health, including critical path, productivity, KPIs, cost performance, risks and recovery plans.

 Support a collaborative IPD environment with shared accountability, transparency and disciplined decision-making.

 Champion a strong safety culture and ensure work is executed in line with project, client and regulatory expectations.

 Support quality and compliance requirements, including inspection, documentation, verification and closeout.

 Mentor and develop project team members while supporting workforce planning and succession

 What We Are Looking For 
 Degree in engineering, construction management or equivalent experience.
 18 + years of progressive construction/project delivery experience.
 10+ years in a senior leadership role on major construction, EPC, power, nuclear, industrial or infrastructure projects.
 Experience delivering projects valued at approximately $500M+.
 Strong background in construction execution, project controls, scheduling, logistics, safety, quality, risk and stakeholder management.
 Experience in nuclear, power generation, LNG, hydro, heavy industrial, or complex infrastructure projects is preferred.
 Experience with IPD, alliance, joint venture or other collaborative delivery models is an asset.
 Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
 Ability to lead in a site-based, fast-moving, highly complex project environment.
 Nuclear construction, nuclear refurbishment or highly regulated project experience.
 Major EPC or power project experience.

jobs.description:
Senior Director, Data, AI, & Automation Services 

As a member of the Business Systems leadership team reporting to the Vice President, Business Systems, the Director, Data, AI & Automation Services leads Bird's enterprise data, analytics, AI, automation, and information governance services. The role is accountable for translating business strategy into a practical Data, AI & Automation roadmap that improves decision-making, project and operational performance, productivity, and responsible innovation across Bird.

The Director leads the modernization of Bird's data platform and analytics ecosystem, establishes scalable AI and automation capabilities, and advances enterprise data governance, data quality, stewardship, and data fluency. Working with executive sponsors, business leaders, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Enterprise Architecture, and delivery teams, this role ensures data and AI capabilities are trusted, secure, adopted, and measurable in business value.
 What You Will Be Working On 

 Develop and execute Bird's enterprise Data, AI, Analytics, and Automation strategy, aligned with corporate objectives and the priorities of the Business Systems leadership team, translating business strategy into measurable outcomes across decision-making, operational excellence, and innovation.

 Establish and maintain a multi-year roadmap and prioritized portfolio for data modernization, AI adoption, analytics, automation services, and information governance — sequencing initiatives by business value, risk, feasibility, and adoption readiness, and reporting quantified value realization to executive leadership.

 Lead the modernization and operation of Bird's enterprise data platform, including lakehouse, Azure Databricks, semantic models, enterprise data models, metadata, data pipelines, and analytics architecture, in partnership with Business Subject Matter Experts, Data Architects, and Business Analysts.

 Establish and maintain enterprise standards for analytics, reporting, data engineering, AI solution development, and delivery governance — covering architecture reviews, solution design reviews, testing, release management, training, documentation, and operational support.

 Lead enterprise data governance, master data management, data quality, metadata, stewardship, and information lifecycle management, ensuring compliance with privacy, cybersecurity, regulatory, and corporate governance requirements — including ownership of the Semarchy MDM tool and enterprise data standards.

 Establish and operationalize responsible AI governance and lifecycle controls for Generative AI, Microsoft Copilot, machine learning, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation — covering AI inventory, human oversight, third-party AI/data risk, monitoring, incident response, and decommissioning, aligned with recognized frameworks such as NIST AI RMF (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage) and ISO/IEC 42001)

 Deliver trusted analytics, business intelligence, KPI frameworks, dashboards, predictive models, and AI-enabled solutions — including Power BI visualization on the enterprise Lakehouse — that improve executive, operational, project, and functional decision-making, and leverage structured, unstructured, and IoT data to solve complex business challenges and improve project outcomes.

 Lead enterprise automation services and the Automation Center of Excellence, including workflow automation, RPA, AI Agents, reusable patterns and templates, citizen-development guardrails, and consistent benefits realization through KPIs, ROI tracking, and process rationalization.

 Champion enterprise data literacy, AI fluency, self-service analytics, adoption, and change management — including Bird's Data & AI Community of Practice and the Data & AI Fluency Journey — measuring and communicating the business value delivered through data, AI, and automation initiatives.

 Build, coach, and lead a high-performing Data, AI & Automation Services team across Data Engineers, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, AI Specialists, and Automation professionals, and foster a culture of innovation, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer service excellence in partnership with executive leadership, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Architecture, Privacy, and business stakeholders.

 What We Are Looking For 
 Education 

 Post-secondary degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Information Technology, Business, or a related discipline.
 Master's degree considered an asset.

 Experience 

 Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in Data, Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Automation, or Digital Transformation. Prior Director-level (or equivalent senior enterprise leadership) experience is required.
 Demonstrated experience operating at the enterprise leadership level, including partnering directly with executive leadership and cross-functional, influencing strategic decisions, and communicating complex technical concepts in clear business language
 Minimum 8 years of leadership experience managing high-performing technical teams.
 Proven experience developing and executing enterprise data and AI strategies.
 Demonstrated ability to lead organizational change, technology adoption, and enterprise capability-building initiatives, including data literacy, AI fluency, self-service analytics, and responsible AI adoption, across business functions

 Technical Knowledge 

 Strong understanding of Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Generative AI, predictive analytics, and business intelligence.
 Deep knowledge of data warehousing, lakehouse architectures, data governance, and enterprise analytics.
 Experience with data quality management, master data management, metadata management, and information governance.
 Knowledge of AI lifecycle management, responsible AI practices, and modern data engineering methodologies.
 Experience building scalable data platforms and self-service analytics capabilities.

 Data Governance and Data Fluency Competencies 

 Proven ability to embed governance and data fluency practices into analytics delivery, automation initiatives, AI adoption, and business transformation programs.
 Experience translating complex data concepts into clear business language for executives, operational leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders.
 Ability to promote data fluency across business functions by improving data literacy, self-service analytics adoption, and responsible use of AI-enabled insights.
 Strong understanding of data quality, metadata management, master data management, privacy, security, and information lifecycle management.
 Demonstrated ability to establish data governance frameworks, stewardship models, data ownership practices, and enterprise data standards.

 Leadership Skills 

 Strategic thinking and business acumen.
 Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills.
 Proven ability to lead organizational change and technology adoption.
 Excellent verbal, written, and presentation skills.
 Ability to communicate complex technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences.
 Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and organizational skills.

 Preferred Qualifications 

 Experience leading enterprise AI adoption initiatives.
 Experience implementing AI governance and data governance frameworks.
 Experience in construction, engineering, or project-based industries is considered an asset.
 Knowledge of project delivery methodologies including Agile and Scrum.

 Success Measures 

 Adoption and business value realization of AI-enabled solutions.
 Growth in enterprise data literacy and analytics adoption.
 Improvements in data quality and governance maturity.
 Productivity gains through automation and AI.
 Delivery of strategic data platform and analytics initiatives.
 Enhanced decision-making through trusted, accessible, and actionable data.
 Development of a high-performing Data & Automation Services organization.

 Applications 

 Applications are accepted online at www.bird.ca.
 Please describe your experience with Business Intelligence, Machine Learning, Agile methodology, Data Warehouses, Generative AI, Data Governance, Data Fluency, and modern cloud data platforms in your cover letter and/or resume.

250 Yonge Street

 Please note: This is a hybrid role based in Toronto. Candidates outside Ontario would need to relocate to meet the role's in-office requirements.

 About the Role 

 As Director, Technology Delivery Lead, you are accountable for the end-to-end technology delivery of Em, BMO InvestorLine's premier AI agent. You will lead the integrated delivery system across AI engineering, wealth platforms, Microsoft Azure, data, architecture, quality engineering, cybersecurity, operations, and third parties to deliver safe, resilient, scalable, and measurable client outcomes.
 You will operate as the principal technology counterpart to the Product Owner for Em. Together, you are jointly accountable for overall delivery: the Product Owner leads product vision, client value, priorities, and acceptance; the Technology Delivery Lead owns the integrated technology plan, engineering execution, technical quality, production readiness, and predictable delivery. This role is not a program coordination position. It is a hands-on senior technology leadership role with clear decision rights and accountability for outcomes.

 Mandate and Decision Rights 

 Own the integrated technology delivery plan for Em from discovery and architecture through build, evaluation, release, operation, and continuous improvement.
 Jointly commit scope, sequencing, release outcomes, and delivery forecasts with the Product Owner, balancing client value, technical feasibility, risk, cost, and capacity.
 Make or escalate timely technology delivery decisions across architecture, engineering, environments, data, integration, testing, controls, and production readiness.
 Hold delivery teams and partners accountable for agreed outcomes, quality standards, dependencies, and evidence-based release criteria.
 Protect the product from unmanaged technical debt, fragmented ownership, late-stage controls, and delivery practices that are not fit for AI.

 Key Responsibilities 

 1.      End-to-End Technology Delivery 

 Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
 Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
 Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
 Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
 Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.

 2. AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership 

 Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
 Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
 Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
 Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
 Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.

 3.      Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration 

 Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
 Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
 Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
 Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
 Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.

 4.      Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery 

 Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
 Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
 Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
 Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
 Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.

 5.      Quality, Risk and Responsible AI 

 Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
 Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
 Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
 Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
 Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.

 6.      Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership 

 Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
 Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
 Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
 Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
 Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

 Key Success Measures 

 Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
 Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
 AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
 Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
 Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
 Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
 Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

 Required Skills and Competencies 

 Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
 Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
 Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
 Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
 Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
 Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
 Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
 Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

 Qualifications and Experience 

 15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
 Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
 Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
 Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
 Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
 Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
 University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.

 Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
 Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
 Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
 Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.
 Build trust through candour, transparency, inclusion, disciplined follow-through, and continuous learning.

jobs.description:
Application Deadline: 

12/30/2026 

 Address: 
33 Dundas Street West

Data Analytics & Reporting 

 This role is HYBRID, 2 days/week in office (Remote/Virtual is not an option). Out of province candidates will require relocation. 

 About the role: 
 BMO Canada Wealth Digital is accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across its customer-facing digital platforms to enhance client experiences, improve operational efficiency, and enable innovative wealth management solutions. We are seeking an experienced AI Delivery Director to lead the planning, execution, and delivery of strategic AI initiatives that support the evolution of our Wealth Management digital capabilities.

 This is a senior delivery leadership role requiring the coordination of cross-functional teams across Engineering, Architecture, Security, Risk Management, Compliance, and Business organizations. The successful candidate will be responsible for driving the delivery of secure, compliant, and resilient Multi-Agent AI solutions that leverage enterprise AI capabilities, including the AI Gateway, Policy Engine, Identity Fabric, AI Registry, Guardrails Runtime, Model Context Protocol (MCP) services, and AI Observability platforms.

 The AI Delivery Director will provide end-to-end leadership across the delivery lifecycle, from intake, discovery, and prioritization through implementation, deployment, adoption, and business value realization by adopting and utilizing AI tools in SDLC. Working closely with engineering leaders, product owners, architects, and executive stakeholders, the role will ensure AI-enabled solutions are delivered on schedule, aligned with enterprise standards, and integrated effectively within the broader technology ecosystem.

 Key Responsibilities 

 1.      End-to-End Technology Delivery 

 Lead delivery across multiple cross-functional product and platform teams, establishing one integrated plan, clear critical path, transparent dependencies, and accountable owners.
 Convert the product roadmap into executable technology increments, release plans, capacity models, milestones, and outcome-based commitments.
 Drive delivery discipline across scope, schedule, cost, quality, resources, risk, and benefits, using forecasts rather than artificial certainty.
 Identify constraints early, remove impediments, resolve cross-team trade-offs, and escalate decisions with clear options and recommendations.
 Ensure each release has explicit entry, exit, acceptance, operational readiness, and rollback criteria.

 2. AI Engineering and AI SDLC Leadership 

 Apply deep knowledge of generative AI and agentic systems, including LLM orchestration, tool use, retrieval-augmented generation, prompt and context engineering, evaluations, guardrails, memory, and human oversight.
 Embed full-lifecycle AI SDLC practices across requirements, design, build, test, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and model or prompt change management.
 Ensure AI quality is measured using fit-for-purpose evaluations covering safety, groundedness, relevance, accuracy, latency, reliability, and client experience.
 Champion specification-driven development, automation, reusable engineering patterns, and AI-assisted software delivery where approved.
 Ensure deterministic software testing and probabilistic AI evaluation are integrated into CI/CD and release decisions.

 3.      Azure, Architecture and Platform Integration 

 Provide senior technical leadership for solutions deployed on Microsoft Azure and integrated with BMO InvestorLine and Wealth Management platforms.
 Partner with solution, enterprise, security, data, and platform architects to maintain an approved, scalable target architecture and prevent local optimization or avoidable technical debt.
 Ensure APIs, event flows, data services, identity, access, observability, resilience, and non-functional requirements are designed and delivered end to end.
 Drive environment readiness, infrastructure as code, automated deployment, telemetry, performance engineering, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and production support readiness.
 Promote reuse of enterprise AI capabilities, shared services, patterns, and controls while preserving clear service boundaries and ownership.

 4.      Advanced Agile and Value-Stream Delivery 

 Establish and continuously improve an advanced Agile operating model organized around persistent, cross-functional teams and measurable client or business outcomes.
 Lead portfolio and product-level planning, backlog readiness, dependency management, release forecasting, and flow optimization across multiple teams.
 Use evidence-based metrics such as lead time, cycle time, throughput, work in progress, predictability, escaped defects, reliability, evaluation performance, and value realization.
 Reduce handoffs, unnecessary governance, meeting load, and blocked work; create fast decision paths and clear single-point accountability.
 Coach delivery leaders, Scrum Masters, engineering leads, and teams in modern product delivery, DevSecOps, continuous delivery, and learning-driven retrospectives.

 5.      Quality, Risk and Responsible AI 

 Build quality, privacy, security, regulatory compliance, model risk, accessibility, and responsible AI requirements into delivery from inception, not as release-end checkpoints.
 Partner with Legal, Risk, Compliance, Cybersecurity, Privacy, Model Risk, Data Governance, and Technology Risk to establish proportionate controls and auditable evidence.
 Ensure full-spectrum observability across application, infrastructure, data, model, prompt, agent, safety, and client-experience performance.
 Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and learning reviews for technology or AI quality events.
 Maintain transparent risk, issue, dependency, and decision records and ensure material risks are escalated promptly.

 6.      Stakeholder, Financial and Partner Leadership 

 Serve as the senior technology delivery voice for Em with InvestorLine, Wealth, Technology & Operations, Applied AI, governance partners, and executive forums.
 Provide concise, fact-based reporting on outcomes, delivery confidence, risks, financials, quality, and decisions required.
 Own technology delivery financial stewardship, resource planning, vendor performance, commercial dependencies, and delivery commitments.
 Lead co-build and vendor engagements with clear accountability, knowledge transfer, architecture compliance, security obligations, and measurable outcomes.
 Create an inclusive, high-accountability environment that develops leaders, strengthens technical depth, and keeps teams focused on client outcomes.

 Key Success Measures 

 Predictable delivery of roadmap outcomes and releases, with transparent forecast accuracy and controlled scope change.
 Measurable improvement in delivery flow, engineering productivity, automation, quality, and time to value.
 AI evaluation thresholds and non-functional requirements met before release and sustained in production.
 Stable, secure, resilient production performance with effective observability, incident management, and continuous improvement.
 Clear ownership, faster decisions, fewer cross-team handoffs, and effective dependency resolution.
 Measurable client adoption, experience, business value, and risk outcomes delivered in partnership with the Product Owner.
 Effective financial, capacity, vendor, and technical-debt management.

 Required Skills and Competencies 

 Expert-level technology delivery leadership in large, complex, regulated environments, with accountability for multiple teams and production outcomes.
 Deep practical knowledge of AI/ML and generative AI delivery, including agentic architectures, LLM application patterns, evaluations, guardrails, observability, and responsible AI controls.
 Strong knowledge of wealth management and digital investing platforms, including client journeys, advice or guidance experiences, market and portfolio data, trading-related integrations, and regulatory considerations.
 Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Azure cloud architecture and delivery, cloud-native engineering, APIs, integration, identity and access, data services, telemetry, resilience, and DevSecOps.
 Mastery of advanced Agile, product operating models, value-stream management, Lean flow, Scrum or Kanban, portfolio planning, CI/CD, test automation, and evidence-based delivery metrics.
 Ability to challenge constructively, make decisions under ambiguity, translate technical complexity into business implications, and influence senior executives.
 Commercial and financial acumen, including technology investment, capacity, vendor, contract, and delivery-performance management.
 Exceptional leadership, communication, facilitation, negotiation, and talent-development skills.

 Qualifications and Experience 

 15+ years of progressive experience in technology delivery, engineering, architecture, platform, or product technology leadership, including senior leadership accountability.
 Demonstrated success delivering enterprise-scale digital products or platforms from strategy through production and ongoing operation.
 Demonstrated delivery of AI/ML or generative AI solutions in production, ideally involving multi-agent systems or other complex AI-enabled client experiences.
 Significant experience with Microsoft Azure and modern software engineering practices in a regulated enterprise.
 Experience in wealth management, brokerage, digital investing, banking, or similarly regulated financial services is strongly preferred.
 Proven experience leading cross-functional internal and partner teams through complex dependencies and high-stakes releases.
 University degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related discipline; relevant advanced degree or certifications are considered assets.
 Experience in Wealth Management or Capital Markets AI space (highly desirable) or Financial Institutions or Technology firms.
 Domain knowledge of investment, securities, trading from a technology perspective, having worked in such ecosystems.

 Leadership Expectations 

 Act as an owner: accountable for outcomes, not activity or coordination alone.
 Put clients, safety, quality, and sustainable value ahead of pace without evidence.
 Create clarity: make responsibilities, decisions, risks, dependencies, and delivery confidence visible.
 Lead with technical credibility while empowering engineering and product leaders closest to the work.
 Build trust through candor, transparency, inclusion, disciplined follow-through, and continuous learning.

jobs.title: Director, Non-Financial Risk Assessment Programs
jobs.description:
Application Deadline: 

12/19/2026 

 Address: 
100 King Street West 

 Job Family Group:

Capital Mrkts Sales & Service 

 BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

 Role Summary 

 The Director, Non-Financial Risk Assessment Programs leads how Capital Markets carries out BMO's main non-financial risk identification and assessment programs: PRC (Process, Risk & Control) and Risk ID inventories and RCSA (Risk & Control Self-Assessment) and RCRAs (Regulatory Compliance Risk Assessment). The Director is the main point of coordination between the first line (1LOD) Business Control teams and the second line (2LOD) enterprise program owners. They make sure assessments are accurate, defensible, delivered on time, and meet ONFR and ECP requirements.
 The Director brings a deep understanding of how risks, controls, processes, products, business units and legal entities connect across Capital Markets. They advocate with enterprise program owners for structures and methodologies that fit the business. The role improves inventory quality, makes execution consistent across business units (BUs), reduces the workload on Business Controls and Business Units and improves portfolio level assessments

  Key accountabilities 

 1. Inventory governance and PRC management 

 Own year-round governance and data-quality oversight of BU PRC inventories (products and services, internal activities, processes, specific risks and controls).
 Lead the annual PRC Inventory Confirmation.
 Manage organizational and ownership changes, including BU realignments, lift-and-shifts, new inventory builds, MCC/ME updates and inventory rationalization.
 Monitor inventory health through Risk Mart and Power BI. Find missing attributes, linkages and data-quality issues, then drive remediation and escalate unresolved gaps.
 Make sure applicable Master Common Controls (MCCs) and shared controls are adopted correctly in BU control inventories, including SOX designations.

 2.  Capital Markets risk structure and cross-program linkages 

 Act as the authoritative interpreter of PRC, RCSA, RCRA for Capital Markets.
 Act as Capital Markets' expert on how products and services, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities connect, and keep that view current as the business and organization change.
 Advocate with the enterprise program owner for the data structure, taxonomy and linkage design that best fits Capital Markets, including how KRIs, Issues and Events connect to PRC risk and control records.
 Give business requirements and practical input on changes to the GRCE data model, workflow and future-state integration, including aggregation at the Legal Entity level.

 Make sure Capital Markets inventories apply the agreed linkage standards consistently. This includes keeping Issues linked to Key Controls complete and accurate
 Find structural gaps or misalignments, such as missing, orphaned or inconsistent linkages, and bring them to the program owner with recommended fixes.
 Use the linked data to support RCSA residual risk ratings, overrides and Targeted Risk Evaluations (TREs) with evidence, and to show where control weaknesses, KRI breaches and loss events cluster.
 3.  Risk assessment execution (RCSA and RCRA) 

 Lead the PRC/RCSA/RCRA Annual Plan.
 Oversee risk categorization (key vs. non-key) and ensure assessments are right sized taking a risk based approach.
 Oversee reviews of TREs, including inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk, overrides and rationales. Ensure High Residual Risk ratings have corrective actions to improve control effectiveness.
 Lead RCRA execution and work with Business Regulatory Control teams to maintain and accurate inventory of risk evaluation points (REPs). Reconcile RCRA results with the regulatory and privacy TREs in the RCSA so regulatory compliance risk feeds into the BU risk profile.
 Manage slippage and deferral requests, and exception and exemption requests, in line with Directive requirements.
 Coordinate Effective Challenge from Operational Risk Officers (OROs), Risk Specialty Areas (RSAs), Enterprise Control Functions (ECFs) and other programs. Track comments, how they're resolved, and due dates.
 4.  Advocacy with 2LOD program owners 

 Act as Capital Markets' lead advocate with the 2LOD program owners (ONFR, ECP and Regulatory Compliance, and Risk Specialty Areas). Represent the business's interests in methodology, Policy, Standard & Procedure changes.
 Influence program design so requirements suit Capital Markets' products, trading activities and legal entity structure and aid towards reducing risk.
 Negotiate realistic timelines, scope and sequencing for program deliverables. Prepare well- supported rationale for exceptions, exemptions or alternative approaches when they're justified.
 Bring the business's perspective, practical constraints and lessons learned to enterprise working groups and consultations. Share upcoming program changes with Director, Risk Programs for inclusion in broader communications across Capital Markets.
 Build trusted, credible relationships with 2LOD so issues are resolved collaboratively and escalated only when needed.
 6.  Reporting and executive enablement 

 Produce AE summary materials and approval packages, and keep approval evidence in GRCE.
 Provide risk profile insights and committee reporting (for example, VRC).

 7.  Continuous improvement and future-state capability 

 Lead improvements to methodology, process, reporting and systems with ONFR. Standardize tools, templates and procedures.
 Represent Capital Markets in working groups, user acceptance testing (UAT) and platform evaluations to shape GRCE and future assessment capabilities.
 8.  People leadership 

 Lead, develop and set priorities for team members and Business Control teams across concurrent assessment cycles.
 Build a culture of accountability, data quality and practical, business-friendly risk partnership.

 Key relationships 

 1LOD: Business Controls, Risk Domain Leads, Business Unit Leads, Accountable Executives, Operational Resilience & Risk Programs, Portfolio Analytics, Capital Markets Assurance Role, Enterprise Control Functions
 2LOD: ONFR and ECP program & methodology owners, OROs, RSAs, Regulatory Compliance and Privacy

 Qualifications 

 10+ years in operational or non-financial risk, risk and control self-assessment, or governance at a large financial institution, including people leadership. Capital Markets experience strongly preferred.
 Deep understanding of how Capital Markets products, processes, risks, controls, business units and legal entities relate, and the ability to turn that into clear structural requirements for enterprise program owners.
 Deep knowledge of the three lines of defence model, risk and control taxonomies, residual risk methods and Effective Challenge.
 Proven ability to influence and negotiate with 2LOD and enterprise program owners, representing business interests credibly and constructively.
 Hands-on experience with a GRC platform (Archer preferred) and with data and reporting tools (Power BI, Risk Mart).
 Track record of leading enterprise programs on regulatory deadlines and producing audit- ready, AE-ready and committee-ready materials.
 Strong judgment and executive presence, and the ability to escalate issues diplomatically with senior stakeholders.

jobs.description:

 BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service financial services provider. We offer corporate and investment banking, treasury management, as well as research and advisory services to clients around the world. #bmocapitalmarkets

 We are looking to bring on a VP into our Global Finance Risk team, to be based out of the Toronto office. 
 This person will be responsible for managing risk across prime, counterparty credit, and business and developing the risk framework, which includes margin risk methodologies.  The person will also collaborate across teams, including trading, credit, market risk, counterparty, and the front office to work cohesively and collaboratively to ensure all risk coverage.  They will also be responsible for stress testing and scenario analysis for the business. 
 The role provides direct risk oversight of a business supporting sophisticated counterparties and structured financing activity. Responsibilities extend beyond routine monitoring and require both technical risk expertise and sound judgment.

 The resource would be expected to: 
 Support the counterparty and platform risk management of BMO’s cash and synthetic Prime Brokerage and Equity Delta One business lines
 Solutions-oriented client engagement throughout the lifecycle of a client
 First line of defense in risk managing credit risk and monitoring platform exposure
 Generation of key risk analytics and development of new tools to support insights and emerging risk trends
 Understanding market and credit risks within Prime products and effectively communicating to senior management and control functions
 Evolving the risk framework and other risk governance items to ensure a proper control environment and strategic platform development
 Support senior team members in responses to Regulatory inquiries and periodic requests
 Key in-business coverage for emerging counterparty risk events and crisis management
 Contributes to growing / elevating the BMO and BMO Capital Market Prime Brokerage brand with a commitment to and presence in the community
 Balances the Bank's risk appetite with the client needs in making recommendations/proposals
 Manages firm’s risk and takes action to reduce exposure in developing and delivering client strategies
 Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

 Global platform includes Prime Brokerage and Swap offerings across US, Canada and the UK.
 Client portfolios comprise of a broad range of asset classes and investment strategies, including:  Equities (incl. Common Stock, ETFs, ADRs, MLPs, REITs), Corporates (IG & HY), Convertible Bonds, Options & Indexes
 Hedge fund and real money counterparties

 Key Responsibilities: 
 Daily management of client portfolio exposures and counterparty-related risk issues
 Support of operational risk and platform trade processing associated with client counterparty risks
 Participation in prospective client pitches and term negotiations, modeling commercial risk terms and constructing incentives to support strategic, risk-efficient returns growth through ongoing client dialogue
 High level of engagement with Sales, Trading and other members of the business as it relates to client management and ongoing business initiatives
 Thoughtful and complete analysis and communication of risk concerns both internally within the business and among control function partners
 Identifying and escalating emerging risks – credit, market, operational or legal – to senior management and Global Finance management.  Continuously assessing and adapting to new products and market stress events and proactively proposing risk solutions
 Facilitating new client trades and managing existing portfolio exposures to ensure that risks, primarily market-driven counterparty risk, but also documentation, legal and reputational risks are well-controlled
 Work closely with Counterparty Credit, Credit Risk Management and other key stakeholders on onboarding of new clients, implementation of margin methodology, as well as maintaining ongoing dialogue and promptly escalating issues with existing clients
 Develop strategic risk solutions, analytics and platform enhancements to help advance BMO’s competitive advantage
 Maintain a positive culture within the team by cultivating a productive and collaborative work environment
 Ensure full compliance with risk procedures and other Global Finance or Global Markets policies

 Qualifications: 
 B.S. – Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Finance / Statistics or related discipline.
 Between 5 - 7 years of experience in Prime Finance risk or general experience with Delta One and Global Prime Finance trading
 Experience with VaR and stress testing.
 Strong data querying and quantitative analysis skills are required, knowledge of Python, SQL and AI Development tools.
 Comfort with using data querying skill set to design risk dashboards, graphic user interfaces linked to internal databases and enhanced risk reporting.
 Exposure to and strong understanding of equities products, such as Delta One, Swaps, and derivatives across all asset classes.  Experience with Synthetic Prime is a plus.
 Strong understanding of market risk and counterparty risk processes and metrics.
 Knowledge of relevant Prime financing platforms, asset types, market structure and client investment strategies.
 Experience with data infrastructure transformation, financial engineering and/or quantitative expertise in risk modeling / data analytics.
 Experience with risk decision-making authority carrying direct economic impact.

About Coursera + Udemy 

 Coursera and Udemy are now one company, bringing together two mission-driven brands to create the world’s most powerful platform for turning learning into progress. Together, we help more than 300 million learners and 12,000+ enterprise customers build the skills they need for a world being reshaped by AI. Read more about the combined company by visiting our  blog.

 Why join us now? 

 AI is transforming how people learn, work, and grow, and the need for new skills has never been greater. Coursera brings trusted content and credentials from leading university and industry partners, while Udemy brings a dynamic skills marketplace and global network of real-world experts. By combining these strengths, we can connect more people and organizations to the skills they need, when they need them.

 Shape what comes next 

 By joining our team, you’ll have the opportunity to reshape how the world learns and applies skills—and help millions of people participate in the new economy. Bring your ideas, expertise, and perspective to meaningful work that can make a difference at global scale.

 How we work 

 Coursera + Udemy lets you choose the best way to work, whether it’s from home, an office, or a collaboration space. We’re a globally distributed team that comes together intentionally for collaboration, complex problem-solving, and key milestones — creating opportunities for teams to come together. If you’re ready to make a global impact, help scale unique products across Coursera + Udemy, and grow your career, apply below.

 Job Overview: 

 Within Professional Services, you'll lead the Solutions Architecture team through a fundamental change: from a technical intake team that passes integration work to third parties to a team that designs and builds the integrations we choose to own on Workato. You'll decide which integrations are strategic to own and which third parties can deliver faster, and you'll balance capacity across Coursera and Udemy technical work. You'll lay a foundation to build from, so that integrations are productized and reusable rather than one-offs, and you'll upskill the team to design, build, and test the way an engineering team does. You'll also take ownership of integrations built by third parties for both Coursera and Udemy, and decide what, if anything, to migrate in house. This is a highly operational role. You'll redesign how the team works with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Customer Support, define workflows that are not yet defined, and build the delivery discipline, capacity model, and metrics that make the function run like a well-oiled machine. You'll report to the Senior Director of Professional Services and partner closely with the Director of AI Innovation to streamline how the team works.

 Responsibilities: 

 Lead the shift from a technical intake team that routes work to third parties to a team that builds the integrations we choose to own, and set the criteria, service levels, and pricing for what we own versus what third parties deliver.

 Own the integration roadmap and prioritization with Product, Partnerships, Engineering, and Support, and make capacity and load-balancing tradeoffs across Coursera and Udemy technical work.

 Establish the Workato foundation and productize what we can, with shared standards and reusable components, and a custom layer on top that is easy to adapt. Build reuse into design review.

 Take ownership of the inherited integrations, six years of third-party work on the Coursera platform and a handful on Udemy. Document them, decide what, if anything, to migrate, retire, or keep, and steward the code and its environment.

 Hire and upskill the team to design, build, and test like engineers, aligned with Coursera Engineering's standards. Use AI-assisted development deliberately so the team builds fundamentals first, and manage token usage.

 Redesign how the team works, including Jira, intake, and workflows with Product, Partnerships, Presales, and Support, and train Support to deflect development-related tickets.

 Own the run and support model for what we build, including monitoring, maintenance, versioning, and service levels. Meet security, contractual, and data privacy standards, and serve as the senior escalation point for high-risk issues.

 Partner with Presales on early scoping and own the technical handoff from Sales into delivery. Work with the Director of AI Innovation and Solutions on the pilot-to-PS transition review and on streamlining the team's work.

 Run utilization and project tracking, manage the technical service catalog, pricing, SOWs, and margin, and build metrics that show impact on deal size, time to production, retention, and quality.

 Basic Qualifications: 

 8+ years of experience in solutions architecture, technical professional services, or integration consulting, with a strong focus on API integrations (REST, SOAP, GraphQL) and cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.

 Proven experience leading and developing technical teams, ideally globally distributed, and running a technical delivery function, including capacity planning, utilization, and cross-team workflows.

 Experience building reusable, productized integrations on an iPaaS platform and designing for reuse across customers.

 Experience applying engineering standards (SDLC, design and code review, testing) to integration delivery, and coaching a team to adopt them.

 Experience taking over third-party-built or inherited code and making build, buy, partner, and migrate decisions, including managing third-party partners.

 Direct experience in pre-sales activity for technical services, including discovery, scoping, and SOW creation.

 Strong communicator with stakeholders from engineers to executives. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

 Preferred Qualifications: 

 Hands-on experience with Workato, or a comparable iPaaS platform such as MuleSoft, Boomi, Jitterbit, or Tray.io.

 Integration experience with SSO, ERP, HRIS, and LMS/LXP systems.

 Experience integrating teams, codebases, or service portfolios through a merger or acquisition.

 Proficiency in data analytics and SQL.

 Compensation 

 Coursera offers competitive pay and fair compensation practices across all regions. Job titles may span multiple career levels, and the targeted hiring base salary range for this role in Canada is $175,000 - $218,000. Actual compensation will depend on factors such as experience, education, transferable skills, business needs, and location. This range may be adjusted over time and may include eligibility for variable pay, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

 We anticipate the application window will be open until December 7, 2026. Based on business needs, this opportunity may remain posted beyond or closed before the anticipated application window.

jobs.title: Director, Finance
jobs.description:
Director of Finance
 Full-Time | Remote 
 Lead the Numbers. Shape the Future. Grow with GraceMed.
 GraceMed is a growing, multi-location healthcare and aesthetics organization offering a wide range of plastic and cosmetic surgeries, dermatology services, aesthetic treatments and medical-grade skincare.
 As we continue to expand, we are looking for an experienced finance leader to help shape the next stage of our growth. This is an opportunity to take ownership of our financial reporting and accounting operations while playing an important role in strategic planning, business performance, organizational transformation and the integration of new clinics and acquisitions.
 Working closely with executive leadership, physicians and clinic managers, you will help strengthen our financial infrastructure, build scalable processes and translate financial information into meaningful business insights.
 If you are a hands-on finance leader who enjoys balancing technical accounting expertise with strategic thinking, operational partnership and people development, we would love to hear from you.
 Why Join GraceMed?
 Make a meaningful impact: Play an influential role in shaping the financial operations and future growth of an expanding healthcare organization.

 Be part of the bigger picture: Work directly with executive leadership and operational teams, contributing to business strategy and important organizational decisions.

 Build and improve: Take ownership of financial processes, systems and controls, with the opportunity to introduce improvements and build scalable practices.

 Grow with us: Be part of an evolving organization with opportunities for professional development and increased leadership responsibility.

 The Opportunity
 Reporting directly to the Vice President, Finance, the Director of Finance will lead GraceMed's accounting and financial reporting functions, ensuring strong financial governance, accurate reporting and effective financial operations across the organization.
 This role will play a key part in supporting GraceMed's continued growth and evolution by providing financial insight, strengthening internal controls, driving process improvements and supporting the financial integration of new clinics and acquisitions.
 As a trusted financial partner to the executive team, you will prepare and present financial results, strategic priorities and recommendations to support organizational decision-making. You will also work closely with clinic managers, physicians and operational leaders to ensure finance is viewed as a collaborative and value-added business partner.
 This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for an experienced finance professional who combines strong technical accounting expertise with commercial acumen, exceptional communication skills and a people-centred leadership approach.
 What You'll Do
 Financial Reporting and Analysis
 Lead the general ledger and monthly, quarterly and annual financial close processes, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting.

 Oversee journal entries, accruals, reconciliations and financial statements to ensure accuracy and compliance with applicable accounting standards.

 Prepare consolidated financial statements, management reporting packages and monthly financial variance analysis.

 Provide meaningful financial insights and recommendations to senior leadership, including analysis of revenue, expenses, labour, EBITDA and cash flow.

 Prepare and present financial performance, strategic priorities, key business drivers and recommendations to the executive leadership team.

 Support executive, Board, investor and lender reporting requirements.

 Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Planning
 Lead the annual budgeting process across clinics and corporate departments.

 Develop and maintain financial forecasts, models and business cases to support strategic initiatives and operational decisions.

 Monitor financial performance against budgets and forecasts, identifying risks, opportunities and areas for improvement.

 Provide financial analysis and recommendations to support business growth, investment decisions and cash management.

 Clinic Operations and Business Integration
 Partner with clinic managers, physicians and operational leaders to understand financial performance and identify opportunities to improve profitability and efficiency.

 Build strong internal customer relationships, providing responsive, practical financial guidance and support to operational stakeholders.

 Lead and support the financial integration of newly acquired and established clinics, including accounting systems, banking, payroll, accounts payable and internal controls.

 Support acquisition due diligence, financial analysis, purchase price accounting and integration activities.

 Standardize financial reporting, accounting practices and processes across clinic locations.

 Identify opportunities to streamline financial workflows and improve reporting accuracy and efficiency.

 Treasury and Financial Operations
 Oversee cash management, banking activities, accounts payable, accounts receivable and working capital management.

 Review payroll processing and related reconciliations in collaboration with internal teams and external providers.

 Ensure timely and accurate completion of statutory remittances, tax filings and financial payments.

 Maintain appropriate financial controls and approval processes for banking transactions and expenditures.

 Internal Controls, Systems and Process Improvement
 Develop, implement and maintain financial policies, procedures and internal controls across the organization.

 Strengthen month-end and quarter-end close processes, financial documentation and reporting practices.

 Identify opportunities to improve financial systems, reporting tools, automation and data quality.

 Support financial system implementations, upgrades and process improvements.

 Identify opportunities to improve organizational efficiency, financial accountability and business performance through effective financial processes and controls.

 Audit, Compliance and External Relationships
 Lead the coordination of annual external audits and quarterly financial reviews.

 Maintain effective relationships with external auditors, banks, tax advisors, payroll providers and other professional service partners.

 Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax regulations, lending requirements and internal policies.

 Coordinate audit schedules, supporting documentation and external stakeholder reporting.

 Team Leadership
 Lead, mentor and develop members of the accounting and finance team, establishing clear responsibilities and performance expectations.

 Demonstrate a servant leadership approach, empowering team members, removing barriers and providing the guidance and support needed for them to succeed.

 Foster a collaborative, accountable and service-oriented finance culture.

 Identify opportunities to strengthen team capabilities, improve workflows and support succession planning.

 What You Bring
 Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline.

 CPA designation preferred; candidates with significant relevant financial leadership and technical accounting experience will also be considered.

 7–10+ years of progressive accounting and finance experience, including financial reporting, month-end close, budgeting and forecasting.

 At least 3 years of experience leading and developing an accounting or finance team.

 Strong technical accounting knowledge, including general ledger management, financial statements, reconciliations, accruals and internal controls.

 Demonstrated ability to interpret financial results, develop strategic recommendations and prepare and present financial performance, strategic priorities and business results to C-suite and executive leadership.

 Experience reporting directly to, and working collaboratively with, a Vice President of Finance, CFO or other senior executive. Comfortable operating in a high-visibility role and providing direct financial insight, recommendations and constructive challenge to senior leadership.

 Above-average written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, practical and actionable insights for both financial and non-financial audiences.

 Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills, with a demonstrated ability to develop trusted relationships with internal customers, physicians, clinic managers and executive stakeholders.

 A servant leadership mentality, with a genuine commitment to supporting, coaching and developing others while fostering accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

 Demonstrated experience with budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, variance analysis and cash-flow management.

 Experience coordinating external audits and working with auditors and other professional service providers.

 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency with Microsoft 365.

 Assets That Will Set You Apart
 Experience in healthcare, medical clinics, professional services, retail or other multi-location environments.

 Experience with mergers and acquisitions, including financial due diligence, review of due diligence reports, purchase price allocations, working capital calculations and post-acquisition integration.

 Experience in organizational restructuring, business transformation or turnaround environments, including the ability to assess financial performance, identify operational inefficiencies and implement sustainable improvements.

 Experience with Power BI, including dashboard development, financial reporting and KPI visualization.

 Experience implementing or improving accounting and enterprise operating systems.

 What Success Looks Like
 In your first year, you will have:
 Established reliable, timely and consistent financial reporting across GraceMed's clinics and corporate operations.

 Strengthened financial controls, accounting processes and month-end reporting practices.

 Developed meaningful financial insights and reporting to support executive and operational decision-making.

 Built strong working relationships with clinic managers, physicians and key stakeholders, positioning Finance as a trusted internal business partner.

 Identified opportunities to improve financial performance, streamline processes and support organizational growth.

 Developed a capable, accountable and collaborative finance team.

 Contributed meaningfully to GraceMed's strategic priorities and ongoing organizational development.

 Salary: Based on experience
 Location: Fully Remote (Oakville or surrounding is ideal)

 GraceMed is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workforce. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates with disabilities throughout all aspects of the selection process.
