Harlo Entertainment owns and operates some of Toronto's most beloved hospitality and entertainment brands. The portfolio includes Shake Shack Canada, Mimi Chinese, Sunnys Chinese, Linny's, Kasa Moto, Shinji Japanese and Playbook Commons, alongside Valerie and Roses Social — the celebrated outlets at Hotel X Toronto. Each Harlo brand is distinctively crafted, and each is united by a shared commitment to warm, engaging hospitality and curated guest experiences that keep people coming back. From conceptualization to creation, Harlo takes a value-oriented approach — pairing creative vision with operational discipline to drive performance, growth, and lasting brand equity across the hospitality, entertainment, lifestyle, and technology industries.
 
Check out our website to learn more: www.harloentertainment.com
 
We are a people first culture. We strive to create great outcomes and to establish win-win partnerships through integrity, reliability, inclusivity, and great communication. Our greatest asset is our people, as they are the powerhouse behind our outcomes. 
 
We always bring our best. We hold ourselves accountable for over-delivering on a consistent basis. We take responsibility for the outcome of our work. We find a way to make it possible. We are in the business of storytelling and remarkable experiences to create moments that matter. We ooze passion and pride in everything we do. We are relentless, driven and proud. We dig deep, we get our hands dirty. There is no challenge is too big or too small for our team.
 
Harlo Entertainment is looking for a highly motivated individual to join our exciting, fast-paced team as a Chief Operating Officer. 
 
Chief Operating Officer (COO)
Act as a proactive business partner and trusted advisor to the Managing Partner, leading the day-to-day operations of Harlo Entertainment. The COO turns strategy into execution, overseeing supply chain, brand licensing operations, people and culture, and cross-functional projects to build a scalable, high-performing organization.
 
Strategic Business Partnership:
·      Act as a proactive business partner to the Managing Partner, translating strategy into clear operating plans, priorities and accountabilities.
·      Collaborate with the executive team to develop and implement the company's long-term strategic vision and annual operating plan.
·      Identify and prioritize key strategic initiatives and ensure alignment with overall business goals across all companies and brands.
·      Lead the launch and operational setup of new companies, brands and ventures, working with the Managing Partner, CFO and external counsel.
·      Facilitate communication between departments to ensure alignment on strategic priorities.
 
Operations & Operational Excellence:
·      Oversee day-to-day operations across the business, ensuring efficient, consistent and high-quality execution.
·      Assess and improve internal processes, systems and tools to enhance productivity and build a scalable operating model.
·      Establish operating metrics and KPIs for each business unit, and lead regular performance reviews with department heads.
·      Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, policies and governance across the organization.
·      Foster a culture of accountability and continuous improvement.
 
Supply Chain:
·      Lead end-to-end supply chain management, including demand planning, sourcing, manufacturing, logistics, warehousing and fulfillment.
·      Build and manage relationships with suppliers, manufacturers, co-packers and logistics partners, including negotiation of terms and contracts.
·      Partner with the CFO on inventory management, product costing and working capital to improve margins and cash flow.
·      Ensure product quality, regulatory compliance and on-time, in-full delivery to customers and channel partners.
·      Identify and mitigate supply chain risks, including supplier concentration, lead times, tariffs and freight disruptions.
 
Brand Licensing & Commercial Execution:
·      Oversee the operational execution of brand licensing programs, including onboarding licensees and partners, product approvals and brand standards.
·      Ensure licensees and partners meet contractual commitments on quality, timelines and brand guidelines.
·      Work with sales, marketing and product teams to bring new products and brand extensions to market on time and on budget.
 
Project Management:
·      Lead and oversee cross-functional projects, ensuring timely execution and alignment with strategic objectives.
·      Monitor project progress and performance metrics, adjusting plans and resources as needed.
·      Report regularly to the Managing Partner on operational performance, risks and priorities.
 
Team Leadership:
·      Lead, mentor and develop department heads and operations teams, ensuring they have the skills and resources to deliver.
·      Encourage a collaborative, innovative and high-performing team environment.
 
What you'll need:
·      Bachelor's degree in Business, Operations, Supply Chain or a related field; MBA an asset
·      10+ years of progressive operations experience, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role (COO, VP Operations)
·      Proven experience leading end-to-end supply chain operations, including sourcing, manufacturing, logistics and supplier management
·      Experience with brand licensing, consumer products or entertainment businesses an asset
·      Track record of building scalable processes, systems and operating models in a growing, multi-entity business
·      Experience leading HR and people functions, and building and developing high-performing teams
·      Strong commercial and financial acumen, including budgeting, margin management and working with KPIs
·      Experience with ERP, inventory and project management systems; high proficiency in Excel
·      Proactive, curious self-starter with the ability to prioritize and drive results in a fast-paced environment
·      Strong negotiation skills with suppliers, partners and licensees
·      Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with strong attention to detail
 
What We Offer
·      Competitive compensation, including comprehensive benefits, spending account and professional development program.
·      Opportunity to develop skills and gain experience in multiple disciplines in a fast-paced environment.
·      Dynamic and fun office culture with colleagues who share the same core values.
·      Exclusive perks from our portfolio companies.
·      Unlimited vacation policy. 
 
Equal Opportunity Employer

jobs.title: Director, FP&A
jobs.description:
At Range Group we believe in the power of the professional travel advisor. We represent over $4.5 billion in annual travel sales. All our investments stem from a common thesis, that travel advisors add real value to a trip. Travel advisors when equipped with technology and 24/7 support are irreplaceable. Equally important is our philanthropy. Range Foundation channels 10% of group profits to social impact. From exploration grants, improved access to education, new discoveries on sea and land, cultural infrastructure, and helping our global neighbors in times of need — we are investing to build a better future.

 About the Role
 This is a hands-on senior finance leadership role for someone who operates at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and execution. You’re as comfortable building a complex multi-entity model from scratch as you are presenting the story behind the numbers to the executive team.

 As Director, FP&A, you will own the analytical engine that supports decision-making across Range Group’s portfolio of travel brands — leading enterprise planning and forecasting, managing a small team, and working directly with senior leadership to evaluate opportunities, navigate risks, and drive performance.

 What You’ll Do

 Financial Modelling & Planning 

 Build, maintain, and continuously improve financial models covering consolidated Group performance, brand-level P&Ls, cash flow forecasting, and scenario analysis.

 Own the Group-level cash flow tracker and EBITDA bridging model, ensuring accuracy and timeliness week over week.

 Lead the annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes across the organization.

 Support ad hoc financial analysis — acquisition modelling, business case development, and covenant compliance.

 Drive continuous improvement in financial planning frameworks, forecasting methodologies, and analytical tools.

 Performance Management & Executive Insights 

 Own enterprise-wide performance reporting — financial reviews, KPI dashboards, executive scorecards, and variance commentary.

 Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership.

 Translate financial results into clear, decision-ready insights that prompt action.

 Identify and proactively flag emerging risks, opportunities, and performance trends across the portfolio.

 Strategic Business Partnership 

 Partner with executive and business leaders to align financial plans with strategic priorities and growth objectives.

 Evaluate investments, business initiatives, and strategic opportunities through modelling and scenario analysis.

 Provide financial leadership on strategic initiatives, business cases, and investment decisions.

 Support executive and Board reporting requirements.

 Treasury & Foreign Exchange Management 

 Own foreign exchange exposure tracking, reporting, and scenario analysis across the Group's multi-currency operations. 

 Partner with treasury, banking partners, and external advisors to evaluate foreign exchange risks and mitigation strategies.

 Assess the financial impact of currency fluctuations on forecasts, budgets, cash flow, and business performance.

 Develop recommendations and decision-support materials for leadership regarding FX risk management and capital planning.

 Monitor market trends and currency movements, proactively identifying risks and opportunities that may impact business performance.

 Team Leadership & Capability Building 

 Lead a small finance team — including a Finance Manager and intern — as a player-coach: owning models and analysis end-to-end while delegating and developing where appropriate.

 Foster a high-performance, analytically rigorous culture within the team.

 Support ERP and reporting tool improvements from a finance data and output perspective.

 Champion the evolution of finance from a reporting function to a true strategic business partner.

 What You’ll Bring 

 8+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Corporate Finance, Strategic Finance, or Finance Business Partnering — with a track record of owning complex models in a multi-entity environment.

 Advanced Excel skills — non-negotiable. You build models from scratch, structure them for auditability, and are fast and precise in the tool.

 Strong accounting foundation: you understand how the P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement connect inside a model.

 Proven experience leading enterprise budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.

 Experience analyzing foreign exchange exposure, multi-currency financial impacts, and scenario modelling within a corporate FP&A, finance, or strategic finance environment.  

 Strong executive presence, comfortable presenting to senior leadership and capable of influencing and constructively challenging stakeholders.

 Experience in multi-entity and multi-currency operating environments.

 CPA designation strongly preferred; candidates without the designation will be considered where technical skills and experience are strong.

 Background in travel, technology, hospitality, or another fast-paced, multi-brand environment is an asset.

 Who You Are 

 You are a builder. You prefer to own models end-to-end and take pride in work that is structured, auditable, and built to last.

 You are intellectually curious and detail-oriented, but able to zoom out and connect the numbers to a broader business narrative.

 You operate well with ambiguity and can manage competing priorities without losing accuracy or composure.

 You are a collaborative leader who still wants to be close to the work — energized by doing, not just directing.

 You communicate with a low-ego, peer-level style — credible with senior stakeholders, collegial with the broader team, and proactive about surfacing issues.

 Why Join Range Group
 This is a rare opportunity to bridge corporate finance and executive strategy in a multi-brand travel and technology portfolio. You’ll have genuine influence — shaping how capital is allocated, how performance is communicated, and how the finance function evolves as the company grows.

 The role carries real complexity: multi-entity consolidations, multi-currency exposure, and a direct reporting line to the Chief Finance Officer. You’ll lead a small team and have the space to build the frameworks and processes that become the foundation for the company’s next phase.

 Hybrid Work Model
 We’re based in Toronto and targeting three days in office per week, with flexibility built in.

 We provide a competitive compensation package with a strong pay for performance rewards approach. Employees have the opportunity to participate in incentive programs and compensation tied to business and individual performance. The actual compensation may vary depending on local market conditions, geography and relevant job-related factors such as knowledge, skills, qualifications, experience, and education/training. #LI-Hybrid 

 We are committed to providing employment accommodation in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act. If you require accommodation due to a disability at any stage of our hiring process, please advise us when completing your application. 
 The Range Group may use artificial intelligence throughout the recruitment process to screen, assess or select applicants for this position. These tools assist our hiring team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. 

We thank all candidates for their interest however only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer – Digital Assets & Capital Markets
jobs.description:
Salary: CAD $250,000 - $300,000 per year.

Chief Financial Officer – Digital Assets & Capital Markets 
 Company: Secure Digital Markets (SDM)
 Location: Toronto, Ontario
 Compensation: Target $250,000-$300,000 + performance bonus + equity participation
 Employment Type: Full-Time | Executive Leadership
 About Secure Digital Markets 
 Secure Digital Markets (SDM) is an institutional digital asset and financial services firm providing sophisticated clients with access to digital asset liquidity, execution, lending, and capital markets solutions.
 Operating at the intersection of cryptocurrency, institutional trading, and financial markets, SDM serves a global client base that demands speed, expertise, discretion, and institutional-grade execution.
 As we enter our next stage of growth, we are seeking a strategic Chief Financial Officer to strengthen our financial infrastructure, optimize capital deployment, and help drive long-term enterprise value.
 The Opportunity 
 This is not a traditional accounting-focused CFO position.
 We are seeking a commercially minded, capital-markets-oriented finance executive who understands how financial businesses create value and how capital can be strategically deployed to accelerate growth.
 Reporting to and partnering closely with the CEO, the CFO will oversee corporate finance, treasury, liquidity, capital allocation, financial reporting, investor relations, and strategic transactions.
 The successful candidate will bring sophisticated financial expertise, ideally gained within institutional digital assets, cryptocurrency trading, market making, exchanges, hedge funds, or related capital markets environments.
 Given SDM's international operations, the CFO must also understand the complexities of managing financial operations across Canada and the United States.
 This is an opportunity to shape financial strategy, influence major investment decisions, and build the financial foundation for SDM's next stage of growth.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Capital Strategy, Treasury & Investments
 Lead SDM's enterprise-wide treasury, liquidity, and capital allocation strategy.
 Optimize balance-sheet management, capital reserves, collateral utilization, and risk exposure across trading, lending, and investment activities.
 Evaluate capital deployment opportunities based on profitability, risk-adjusted returns, and long-term shareholder value.
 Oversee banking, custody, counterparty relationships, regulatory capital requirements, and financial oversight of fund and investment initiatives.
 Strategic Finance, Reporting & Performance 
 Develop financial models, budgets, forecasts, and scenario analyses to guide strategic decisions.
 Establish clear visibility into revenue, profitability, margins, and return on capital across business lines.
 Build scalable financial reporting systems, management dashboards, internal controls, and financial processes.
 Ensure accurate financial reporting and readiness for audits, regulatory reviews, and investor diligence.
 Partner with leadership to evaluate new products, investments, hiring decisions, and resource allocation.
 Cross-Border Finance & Regulatory Coordination 
 Oversee financial operations, reporting, and consolidated financial oversight across Canadian and U.S. entities.
 Manage cross-border financial considerations, including intercompany transactions, transfer pricing, taxation, and capital movement.
 Coordinate with legal, tax, compliance, and regulatory advisors to support effective corporate structures and regulatory compliance.
 Investor Relations & Capital Raising 
 Lead financial strategy and execution supporting investor relations, fundraising, and capital partnerships.
 Develop financial models, investor presentations, diligence materials, and a compelling financial narrative for institutional investors.
 Represent SDM in investor discussions, communicating financial performance, capital strategy, risk management, and growth opportunities.
 Strategic Transactions & Executive Partnership 
 Lead financial evaluation, due diligence, valuation, and structuring for acquisitions, investments, and strategic partnerships.
 Maintain institutional-quality financial information and transaction readiness.
 Serve as a trusted strategic partner to the CEO and shareholders, providing independent financial judgment and constructively challenging investment and operating decisions.
 Ideal Candidate & Qualifications 
 We are seeking an accomplished finance executive with 12+ years of progressive experience in financial leadership, treasury, or capital markets, including meaningful senior management responsibility.
 The ideal candidate will bring:
 Digital Assets & Capital Markets: Direct experience in institutional cryptocurrency, digital asset trading, market making, exchanges, hedge funds, brokerage, or sophisticated capital markets environments.
 Treasury & Capital Management: Strong expertise in liquidity management, capital allocation, balance-sheet risk, collateral management, and financial risk oversight.
 Cross-Border Financial Expertise: Demonstrated experience managing financial operations across Canada and the United States, including multi-entity reporting, taxation, and regulatory considerations.
 Strategic Financial Leadership: Proven ability to build financial models, forecasting frameworks, reporting infrastructure, and financial decision-making processes.
 Investor Relations & Transactions: Experience supporting institutional capital raises, investor communications, M&A, or strategic transactions.
 Executive Experience: Previous leadership as a CFO, Deputy CFO, Treasurer, Head of Finance, VP Finance, or comparable senior finance executive.
 Experience with institutional lending, investment funds, or structured financial products is highly desirable.
 CPA, CFA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualifications are beneficial but not required.
 Leadership Profile 
 The successful candidate combines financial rigor, commercial judgment, and an entrepreneurial mindset.
 You are analytical, intellectually independent, and comfortable challenging assumptions when financial evidence does not support a proposed strategy.
 You can communicate complex financial information clearly, build credibility with institutional investors, and work effectively alongside entrepreneurial founders and executive leadership.
 Above all, you take ownership. You establish accountability, make sound decisions under pressure, and turn financial analysis into meaningful business outcomes.
 Compensation 
 SDM offers a competitive executive compensation package based on experience and demonstrated results.
 Miami: CAD $250,000–$300,000 base salary*
 Annual Incentive: Performance-based bonus
 Long-Term Incentive: Equity / ESOP participation
 *Exceptional candidates may be considered outside the stated salary ranges. 
 Why Secure Digital Markets? 
 This is an opportunity to play a central role in shaping the future of an established institutional digital asset business.
 Rather than inheriting a mature finance organization, you will help determine how capital is allocated, how financial decisions are made, and how SDM scales its operations.
 Working directly with entrepreneurial leadership, you will influence strategic investments, strengthen institutional financial infrastructure, and help position the company for its next phase of growth.
 For the right executive, this is an opportunity to have a direct and measurable impact on enterprise value.

jobs.title: Data & AI Operations Director
jobs.description:
About us

 Qualio is a unified quality and compliance management platform that helps regulated organizations get products to market faster with reduced risk. Trusted by biopharma, medtech, and diagnostics companies worldwide, Qualio eliminates fragmented systems that create audit delays and compliance blind spots. Our platform enables audit readiness in weeks through multi-standard automated gap analysis and evidence reuse across ISO and FDA requirements. Qualio is ISO 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO 27701 certified, reflecting our commitment to security, quality, and privacy.

 The Qualio team is all-remote, and currently distributed across North America, Europe and Australia.

 What's the opportunity?

 The way software companies operate is being rebuilt right now, and the teams that figure out how to run AI-natively will move at a speed the rest can't match. Not by bolting a chatbot onto an existing process, but by taking workflows apart and reassembling them around what these tools can actually do.

 We've also reached the size where product, delivery, and go-to-market can no longer coordinate by proximity. The seams between them are where our leverage leaks out: a feature ships that the field can't articulate, a positioning shift lands that delivery hasn't been briefed on, a customer commitment gets made that the roadmap doesn't reflect.

 This role owns both, because they're the same problem.

 You can't rewire how a company works without seeing how the work actually flows across it.

 What will I be doing?

 Own our AI-native transformation. Partner across the organization to take our major workflows apart and rebuild them. You'll own enablement, change management, and the measurement that shows whether a new workflow is actually used and actually saves time.

 Assess the existing data infrastructure and actively make changes to improve data hygiene and maintenance in order to execute changes.

 Act as a team of one to implement sweeping operational change.

 Partner with leaders across the business, from product and engineering, to GTM, to operations, and support strategic decision making and initiative prioritization.

 Take Qualio's most ambiguous, highest-stakes business questions from "no one knows" to a decision we can act on and own the outcome.

 Bring a sharp, independent voice into company planning and our biggest capital-allocation calls.

 Partner with our finance, revenue ops, and product organizations to standardize and distribute the key operating metrics.

 Set the direction for how Qualio monetizes the AI era: agents, consumption/usage-based billing, and our APIs; with a real point of view on where the model is going, not just where it is.

 What skills do I need?

 Experience 

 8 to 10+ years of expertise in Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and NLP, with a proven track record of implementing modern Generative AI, LLMs, and Agentic workflows in SaaS environments over the last 3+ year.

 You’ve built agents or LLM-powered tools on top of company data yourself, so you know what good data for agents looks like and can guide teams building their own.

 Excellent analytical problem-solving skills with ability to unearth insights and turn them into recommendations and action plans.

 BA/BS in Economics, Math, Finance, Engineering, CS, or other quantitative field; MBA or other advanced degree a plus.

 Strong written and verbal communication skills, able to synthesize findings and concisely articulate them to an array of audiences.

 Self-starter with a demonstrated ability to adapt to a rapidly-changing environment.

 Extremely organized and structured, with a proven ability to run projects and processes from end-to-end.

 Ability to effectively build and maintain cross-functional relationships, manage multiple competing priorities, and drive projects to completion.

 Added plus if you also have exposure to monetization, pricing & packaging, or business-model design — especially in the AI/consumption era.

 Benefits

 The opportunity in helping life-saving products get to market faster

 Medical coverage (with premiums for our most popular plan fully covered for you and your eligible dependents)

 Dental and Vision coverage

 401(k) with up to 4% company matching

 Dependent Care & Health FSA, HSA, Short/Long Term Disability, Basic & Voluntary Life Insurance

 12+ weeks of Paid Parental Leave

 Flexible Time Off (FTO) policy - take time when you need it

 Generous one-time allowance for your home office setup

 Annual Learning & Development stipend

 Regular team gatherings and all-org meetups 

 A note to candidates

 Studies have shown that women and people of color are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they meet every single one of the qualifications as described in a job description. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive company and we are most interested in finding the BEST candidate for the job. That candidate may be one who comes from a less traditional background, and that’s okay. We would strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don't believe you meet every one of the qualifications described.

jobs.title: Director of Technology Operations
jobs.description:
Coinspaid Dev is the engineering brand behind the technology, infrastructure, and R&D expertise built within Coinspaid. With more than 120 engineersand over 11 years of industry experience, Coinspaid Dev brings together software engineering, infrastructure, security and R&D teams with experience building distributed systems and blockchain infrastructure operating across more than 20 blockchain networks.

Coinspaid Dev emerges as an independent engineering brand with a straightforward mission: to advance blockchain infrastructure engineering and contribute practical expertise back to the industry. The structure is new. The experience behind it is not.
 
Director of Technology Operations
We are building the next operating model for a ~150-person technology organization behind production-critical financial infrastructure.
We are looking for a Director of Technology Operations to lead that transformation.
This is not a traditional infrastructure or IT operations role. The mandate is to evolve Technology Operations from a primarily reactive model toward a scalable organization built around clear ownership, platform engineering, automation, self-service, operational excellence, resilience and measurable outcomes.
You will initially lead several established technology functions through their existing Heads and Leads, with approximately 25 people across Platform/DevOps, Corporate IT and Operational Excellence. The mandate is broader than the initial team size: you will help shape the operating model of a ~150-person technology organization and build capabilities designed to scale significantly beyond today's structure.
Your responsibility will go beyond managing these teams. You will help shape how the broader technology organization operates: how production services are owned, how incidents and changes are managed, how engineers consume infrastructure capabilities, how operational risks are identified, and how recurring manual work is systematically eliminated.
A major part of the role is organizational transformation. We expect you to assess the current model, challenge it where necessary, define the target state, develop the leaders underneath you, and deliver measurable improvements rather than simply introduce new processes.
The goal is straightforward: as the company grows, Technology Operations should become more reliable, resilient and scalable while requiring less manual coordination, less operational toil and less executive intervention.
What you will do
Lead the transformation of Technology Operations across Platform/DevOps, Corporate IT and Operational Excellence, moving the organization from reactive operations toward ownership, automation, self-service and measurable outcomes.
Define the Technology Operations strategy, target operating model, organizational structure, responsibilities, priorities and transformation roadmap.
Lead multiple established technology functions through Heads, Leads and other managers, creating clear accountability and developing leaders who can operate with increasing autonomy.
Lead the evolution of DevOps toward a Platform Engineering model that reduces operational toil, increases self-service and improves developer productivity while maintaining reliability and security.
Partner with Engineering to establish a "you build it, you own it" model, where product teams retain ownership of their services in production while Technology Operations provides the platform, standards, tooling and operational framework that enable them to operate reliably.
Develop Service Management toward Operational Excellence: strengthen service ownership, incident and problem management, introduce risk-based change governance, reduce unnecessary manual controls, and use operational data to eliminate systemic causes of failures.
Transform Corporate IT toward a secure, automated employee technology model, with strong identity and access lifecycle management, device management, governance and employee self-service.
Continuously assess the current organization, technology landscape and operating model, identify structural and operational gaps, and turn them into concrete improvement initiatives.
Improve the maturity, reliability, scalability and efficiency of technology operations supporting production-critical systems.
Define meaningful operational metrics and use them to identify systemic problems, measure transformation outcomes and drive improvements rather than simply report performance.
Own the Technology Operations contribution to digital operational resilience, including ICT business continuity, disaster recovery, backup and restoration, resilience testing, recovery objectives, crisis readiness, and remediation of findings from incidents and resilience exercises.
Partner with Security, Risk and Compliance to maintain an effective ICT risk management and control environment, including technology risk identification, critical service dependencies, ICT third-party risk, resilience testing, audit readiness and regulatory remediation.
Ensure operational and technology risks are identified early, understood, prioritized and addressed appropriately.
Support the company through audits, certifications, regulatory requirements and other controls relevant to financial and technology organizations.
Own and optimize budgets, technology vendors, infrastructure investments and external partnerships within the function.
Partner closely with Engineering, Security, Risk, Compliance, Product, Finance and other business functions.
Represent Technology Operations in cross-functional and executive discussions and communicate complex technology and operational topics clearly to different audiences.
Help prepare the technology organization for the next stage of the company's growth, including increasingly complex enterprise customers, new products and a larger engineering organization.
What we are looking for
Significant leadership experience in Technology Operations, IT Operations, Infrastructure & Operations, Platform/Production Operations, Platform Engineering or a comparable technology function.
Experience as a manager of managers, with responsibility for several teams or functions through Heads, Engineering Managers, Team Leads or equivalent leadership roles.
Previous experience as a Technology Director, VP/Head of Technology Operations, Platform/Infrastructure leader or in a comparable senior role within a product engineering organization is highly relevant.
Proven examples of significant organizational or technology transformation: changing operating models, building or restructuring functions, introducing new capabilities, increasing operational maturity, scaling teams or materially changing how technology organizations operate.
Experience leading or evolving DevOps, SRE or infrastructure capabilities toward Platform Engineering, including developer self-service, automation and reduction of operational toil.
Strong understanding of modern production ownership models and the relationship between Platform Engineering and product engineering teams.
Experience with production-critical systems where availability, reliability, security and operational failures have direct business impact.
Experience with IT and Service Management in modern product/engineering environments, including incident, problem and change management.
Experience transforming Corporate IT or employee technology environments, including identity/access lifecycle, endpoint/device management, automation, governance and employee self-service.
Practical experience with business continuity, disaster recovery and operational resilience in production-critical environments, including BIA, RTO/RPO, backup and restoration, resilience testing and remediation.
Experience working with Security, Risk and Compliance teams and managing technology and operational risks.
Exposure to audits, certifications, regulatory requirements and operational controls relevant to financial institutions or other regulated environments.
Working knowledge of regulatory frameworks relevant to technology operations in financial services, such as DORA, and the ability to translate regulatory requirements into pragmatic engineering and operational controls, is a plus.
Experience managing budgets, vendors, contracts and technology investments.
Ability to operate effectively when requirements, organizational boundaries or the final solution are not yet fully defined.
Track record of developing leaders and building teams that can operate without constant escalation or executive intervention.
Ability to move between strategic topics and operational problems: understand what requires executive attention, delegate what should be owned by your leaders, and personally step in when the situation requires it.
Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with technical teams, senior business stakeholders and executive leadership.
Experience in fintech, payments, banking, financial infrastructure or another regulated and production-critical technology environment would be highly valuable.
How we think about this role
We are not looking for a traditional IT or infrastructure leader whose primary focus is maintaining existing systems and following established processes.
We need someone who is comfortable entering an environment where not everything has already been defined — and who sees that ambiguity as part of the mandate.
You should be able to understand how the organization actually operates today, distinguish symptoms from systemic problems, bring the right people together, make decisions with incomplete information, and turn those decisions into measurable organizational and technology improvements.
You will not be expected to solve every problem personally. A major part of your role will be to build strong Heads and Leads who can own their areas independently, while you focus on the most important organizational, strategic and cross-functional challenges.
At the same time, limited resources, legacy approaches or imperfect processes should be constraints to work with — not reasons why progress cannot happen.
What success looks like
Within the first 6–12 months, we expect to see measurable movement in addition to plans:
reduced recurring operational toil;
increasing developer and employee self-service;
stronger and clearer service ownership;
fewer repeated incidents and systemic operational failures;
more risk-based and automated change management;
improved developer and employee experience;
clearer operational and resilience metrics;
measurable progress toward a Platform Engineering model;
stronger operational resilience and risk management;
and Heads and Leads operating with greater autonomy.
You will have established a clear target operating model and transformation roadmap, but success will not be measured by the existence of the roadmap itself. It will be visible in how the organization operates.
Success means the organization requires less manual coordination and executive intervention while becoming more reliable, resilient, faster and more scalable.

jobs.title: Director, Issuing Solutions Sales & Business Development

About Us

 Join Visa and do work that matters – to you, to your community, and to the world. Progress starts with you.

 Job Description 

 The Director, Issuing Solutions Sales & Business Development, Canada will be responsible for accelerating the growth of Visa's Value-Added Services business across the Canadian market. 

 This is a client-facing commercial role combining sales, business development, market development and consultative solution selling. The Director will identify new opportunities, build qualified pipeline, develop senior client relationships, shape solutions and actively advance opportunities through the sales cycle to deliver commercial outcomes. 

 The successful candidate will operate at the intersection of client strategy, technology and sales execution. They will engage Canadian issuers to understand strategic priorities and business challenges, identify whitespace, lead client discovery, develop compelling business cases and solution strategies, and bring together the appropriate Visa capabilities to address client needs. 

 Working closely with Visa's Account Executives, Specialist Sellers, Product, Visa Consulting & Analytics (VCA), Solutions Engineering and other cross-functional partners, this individual will help clients navigate opportunities across Visa's evolving portfolio while maintaining clear accountability for pipeline creation, sales execution and revenue growth. 

 The role requires a hands-on commercial leader who is equally comfortable creating an opportunity, shaping the solution and selling the value proposition. 
 Essential Functions 

 Sales & Commercial Execution 
 Develop, own and advance a pipeline of Issuing Solutions opportunities across Canada, with accountability for revenue growth and commercial outcomes. 
 Lead client engagements throughout the sales cycle, including prospecting, discovery, opportunity qualification, solution positioning, business-case development, commercial discussions and close. 
 Build and maintain senior-level relationships across existing and prospective Canadian issuer clients. 
 Proactively uncover new client needs and translate those needs into actionable sales opportunities. 
 Develop compelling value propositions and commercial narratives that connect Visa capabilities to measurable client business outcomes. 
 Partner closely with Visa Account Executives and Specialist Sellers to establish account strategies, coordinate client engagement and progress opportunities. 
 Maintain strong sales discipline around pipeline management, forecasting, opportunity progression, risks and next steps. 

 Client Discovery & Solution Development 
 Lead structured client discovery to understand strategic priorities, operational challenges, technology environments and modernization needs. 
 Translate client challenges into integrated solution strategies across Visa's broader portfolio rather than approaching clients solely through individual products. 
 Develop client-specific business cases that clearly articulate strategic value, expected outcomes and commercial rationale. 
 Provide consultative and technical sales leadership throughout complex opportunities, engaging product and technical specialists when deeper solution expertise is required. 
 Help bridge client strategy, business requirements, Visa capabilities and technical feasibility to accelerate opportunities through the decision-making process. 
 Navigate complex client environments involving multiple decision-makers and business and technology stakeholders. 

 Canada Market Development & Go-to-Market 
 Identify whitespace across Visa's Canadian issuer relationships and translate that whitespace into targeted commercial opportunities. 
 Develop account-level and market-level go-to-market strategies reflecting the unique structure and dynamics of the Canadian payments ecosystem. 
 Create qualified opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA, fraud and risk, digital enablement, network solutions, post-purchase experiences and other relevant Visa capabilities. 
 Develop executive relationships that position Visa as a strategic business and technology partner. 
 Identify emerging client needs and market trends and translate those insights into actionable sales strategies. 
 Bring Canadian market and client insights back into Visa to help inform commercialization strategies, product priorities and future go-to-market approaches. 
 Work across Visa's broader organization to create coordinated client strategies and bring the appropriate resources and expertise to priority opportunities.  

 Leadership Profile 

 The ideal candidate will combine the commercial drive of a seller, the structured thinking of a consultant and the solution orientation of a sales engineer. 

 This individual should be comfortable walking into an issuer with an open-ended business challenge, leading discovery, identifying where Visa has a credible right to play, developing the business case, mobilizing product and technical expertise, advancing commercial discussions and ultimately helping close the business. 

 The successful candidate will have a builder mindset and strong sales orientation. They will be energized by identifying opportunities that are not yet fully formed and creating the strategy, relationships and internal alignment necessary to convert those opportunities into revenue. 

 Key Measures of Success 

 Success in this role will be demonstrated through: 
 Building and converting a healthy pipeline of Canadian Issuing Solutions opportunities. 
 Generating new sales and contributing directly to Canada revenue objectives. 
 Identifying previously untapped whitespace within Visa's issuer relationships. 
 Converting discovery and strategic client conversations into qualified commercial opportunities. 
 Developing strong executive relationships across priority Canadian financial institutions. 
 Building compelling business cases and solution strategies for larger, complex or multi-solution opportunities. 
 Accelerating commercial opportunities across Pismo, Verifi, VCA and Visa's broader Value-Added Services portfolio. 
 Strengthening coordination across Account Executives, Specialist Sales, Product, VCA and technical teams. 
 Establishing a scalable foundation for continued growth of Visa's Issuing Solutions business in Canada. 

 Visa requires at least 3 days in office, expectations of these days will be confirmed by your Hiring Manager.

 Qualifications 

 Basic Qualifications 
 Significant experience in sales, business development, market development, management consulting, solution engineering, financial services, payments, fintech or enterprise technology. 
 Demonstrated experience developing and advancing complex B2B sales opportunities. 
 Proven ability to establish and maintain relationships with senior client executives and key decision-makers. 
 Strong commercial orientation with experience identifying potential opportunities, developing value propositions and progressing opportunities through a structured sales process. 
 Experience leading client discovery and translating complex business challenges into actionable solutions and business cases. 
 Ability to understand technically complex products and effectively connect technology capabilities to business outcomes. 
 Strong communication, executive presentation, negotiation and stakeholder-management skills. 
 Demonstrated ability to operate successfully in a highly matrixed organization and influence across teams without direct authority. 

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience within the Canadian banking, payments, fintech or financial-services ecosystem. 
 Experience working directly with financial institutions, issuers, payment processors, fintechs or technology platforms. 
 Demonstrated understanding of the Canadian payments landscape and the dynamics associated with established domestic payment infrastructure. 
 Experience selling or developing opportunities involving payments technology, issuer processing, digital payments, fraud and risk, consulting or other enterprise technology solutions. 
 Experience combining commercial selling with consultative discovery and solution-oriented sales methodologies. 
 Demonstrated ability to build new markets, develop whitespace opportunities or commercialize emerging solutions. 
 Ability to work comfortably across business, product and technology stakeholders. 

 Visa is an EEO Employer 
 Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Visa will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with EEOC guidelines and applicable local law.

jobs.description:
About Us 
Visa is a world leader in payments technology, facilitating transactions between consumers, merchants, financial institutions and government entities across more than 200 countries and territories, dedicated to uplifting everyone, everywhere by being the best way to pay and be paid.

 At Visa, you'll have the opportunity to create impact at scale — tackling meaningful challenges, growing your skills and seeing your contributions impact lives around the world.

 Job Description 

 The Director, Client Success is a pivotal lead individual contributor responsible for owning the holistic post-sale Client Services relationship for applicable clients and providing operational solutions in support of growing clients’ business. The Director is a trusted client advocate and works proactively with their client portfolio to enable new capabilities, manage geographic expansion, and promote product adoption.  The individual is expected to provide thought leadership and strategic guidance during solution development to ensure outstanding client service. The role requires a high level of professionalism, leadership and interpersonal skills to influence and manage relationships with a variety of internal and client stakeholders.

 This role is an exciting opportunity to be at the forefront of Visa’s Client Success transformation by partnering closely with key Visa clients to maximize their benefits realization and value from Visa products through optimizing their performance. Working in conjunction with Account Team members from Sales and Product, you will proactively drive Client Success outcomes in alignment with Visa’s business agenda as detailed in the Sales Account Plan. The individual will also define and deploy client support and service implementation strategies that drive value for our clients and support Visa’s strategy. The Director is the voice of the client on all operational initiatives and issues with key internal functional and region/market partners (e.g., Sales, Product, Legal, Finance, Risk).

 This role serves as a functional specialist, located in Toronto, Canada and reporting to the Sr Director responsible for the Client Services Team in Canada. The position provides subject matter expertise, operational guidance, and strategic support across client service initiatives, acting as a key liaison between stakeholders, business partners, and internal teams. Responsibilities include driving process improvements, supporting service delivery excellence, analyzing business requirements, resolving complex issues, and contributing to the development and implementation of best practices to enhance client satisfaction and operational effectiveness.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Sales Enablement - North America
jobs.description:
Sales Enablement Lead – North America
 Location: Toronto, Canada
 Practice Area: Global Sales | Growth Activation
 Employment Type: Permanent

 Shape strategic deals. Strengthen how we sell. Drive growth. 

 The Opportunity 

 Capco is looking for a Sales Enablement Lead – North America to play a key role in strengthening sales effectiveness, shaping strategic opportunities and driving growth across our US and Canadian businesses. Working closely with regional leadership and reporting to the Global Sales Enablement Lead, you will combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution — supporting high-value pursuits, challenging commercial approaches and delivering practical initiatives that improve how we sell. This is a highly visible, collaborative role for someone who understands how consulting business is won, can engage credibly with senior leaders and has the drive to turn ideas into tangible results.

 What You'll Do 

 Drive Strategic Pursuits and Improve Win Rates 

 Lead and shape priority pursuits, from opportunity strategy and solution development through proposals, commercial discussions and executive presentations.

 Challenge deal strategies, sharpen differentiation and strengthen client value propositions.

 Bring together the right expertise across Capco to develop compelling, commercially sound solutions.

 Champion exceptional quality across strategic pursuits, establishing clear quality standards and review gates to ensure proposals, solutions and client presentations are compelling, differentiated and commercially robust.

 Facilitate pipeline and deal reviews, win strategy sessions and pitch preparation for major opportunities.

 Capture lessons from wins and losses to improve future deal performance.

 Build Sales Capabilities Across Capco 

 Lead and support sales education initiatives that strengthen sales confidence, develop practical selling skills and build growth capabilities across career levels.

 Design and deliver targeted learning, coaching and hands-on development for client-facing teams.

 Strengthen capabilities in opportunity origination, consultative selling, solution shaping, storytelling and strategic account growth.

 Work with regional leaders to identify capability gaps and address them through practical interventions.

 Build commercial confidence and embed effective sales behaviours into everyday client engagement.

 Make Selling More Effective 

 Develop practical playbooks, tools and guidance that improve effectiveness across the sales lifecycle.

 Champion AI-enabled sales productivity, identifying opportunities to simplify work, improve quality and reduce duplication.

 Drive the adoption and effective use of knowledge assets and reusable sales content.

 Translate successful sales approaches into repeatable practices that can scale across the business.

 Work with sellers to identify friction points and deliver improvements that make a tangible difference.

 Connect Expertise and Unlock Growth 

 Work across accounts, domains and capabilities to identify cross-sell opportunities and shape integrated client propositions.

 Connect regional teams with relevant market insights, expertise and growth initiatives from across Capco.

 Support joint pursuits and go-to-market opportunities with strategic partners, including Wipro.

 Turn successful approaches and lessons learned into opportunities for wider adoption across the firm.

 What We're Looking For 

 We are looking for a growth-minded, credible and action-oriented sales professional who understands how consulting business is won and actively collaborates across the leadership team to help Capco succeed. 

 You will bring:

 15+ years of consulting and financial services experience, ideally gained through client-facing consulting, business development, strategic sales or delivery roles.

 Proven experience shaping complex, high-value pursuits, including win strategy, solution development, proposals and senior client presentations.

 Commercial judgement and confidence to challenge senior stakeholders, test assumptions and strengthen deal strategies.

 A strong understanding of financial services, with experience in Banking, Capital Markets, Wealth & Asset Management or Insurance.

 Excellent storytelling and communication skills, translating complex ideas and solutions into compelling client narratives.

 Strong stakeholder management, with the ability to influence senior leaders and mobilize teams across a matrix organization.

 A strategic and analytical mindset, combined with the ability to turn ideas into practical solutions and measurable outcomes.

 A collaborative, entrepreneurial approach, with the confidence to take ownership, challenge constructively and get things done.

 A passion for developing people, sharing knowledge and strengthening the capabilities of the wider organization.

 Above all, you are someone who can see the bigger growth picture while staying close to the detail and execution.

 Bonus Points For 

 Experience designing or delivering sales capability development, coaching or enablement programs.

 Hands-on experience using Generative AI, GPT technologies or AI agents to improve sales productivity.

 Experience in sales operations, commercial management or sales process improvement.

 Experience developing joint propositions or supporting strategic partner pursuits.

 An established network within North American financial services.

 Experience implementing knowledge management, credentials or sales enablement platforms.

 Why Join Capco? 

 Influence growth across North America. Work directly with senior leaders and strategic deal teams to create opportunities, strengthen pursuits and contribute to business growth.

 Shape the future of how Capco sells. Play a leading role in building stronger sales capabilities, embedding effective commercial disciplines and delivering our Capco 30 ambitions.

 Make a tangible difference. This is a role where you will not just recommend improvements - you will shape, build and deliver them.

 Connect the best of Capco. Work across regions, domains, capabilities and strategic partners to bring our collective expertise to clients.

 Be part of an entrepreneurial culture. Join a collaborative, ambitious organization where ideas are valued, initiative is encouraged and individuals can make a visible impact.

 Grow your own career. Gain exposure to senior leadership, complex strategic opportunities and the development of a globally connected sales enablement capability.

 The Impact You'll Make 

 Your success will be measured by the difference you make: stronger deals, more confident sellers, better sales practices and greater commercial effectiveness.  You will help Capco win more business today while building the capabilities and disciplines that support sustainable growth tomorrow.

Benefits 

 We offer a competitive, people-first benefits package designed to support every aspect of your life:

 Comprehensive Benefits Coverage: 100% company-paid health, life and disability insurance, effective from Day 1 of employment.

 Retirement Savings Program: Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) with the option of receiving a matching employer contribution.

 Virtual Health Care: Company-paid virtual health care program available to all employees and their dependents/partners.

 Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP): Company-paid support services for employees and their dependents/partners.

 Parental Leave Top-Up: Enhanced parental leave benefits available from Day 1 of employment.

 New Parent Gift: A company-sponsored gift to celebrate the arrival of a new child.

 Wellness Support: Fitness reimbursement benefit to promote health and well-being.

 Business Coach from Day 1: Personalized one-on-one coaching to support career growth, accelerate development and help achieve your professional goals at Capco.

 Inclusion at Capco 

 We’re committed to making our recruitment process accessible and straightforward for everyone. If you need any adjustments at any stage, just let us know – we’ll be happy to help. We value each person’s unique perspective and contribution. At Capco, we believe that being yourself is your greatest strength. Our #BeYourselfAtWork culture encourages individuality and collaboration – a mindset that shapes how we work with clients and each other every day.

 Use of Artificial Intelligence in Talent Acquisition 

 At Capco, we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support and enhance several parts of talent acquisition. This includes using AI-enabled features within LinkedIn to help source potential candidates, speeding up routine recruitment communications such as emails and creating compelling and brand-aligned job postings that accurately reflect role requirements, and AI-scheduling applications to improve the efficiency of interview coordination.  AI is used as a support tool only. All hiring decisions are made by talent acquisition and hiring teams.

 Why This Role Is Open 

 We are currently hiring for this role due to an existing or newly created vacancy within our organization. This position is open as part of our ongoing business needs, and we are actively reviewing applications to fill this role with a qualified candidate who can make an immediate impact.

CI Financial is seeking a Director, Insurance Operations to lead the modernization and ongoing performance of our Canadian individual life insurance Operations function.

This role combines daily operational leadership with a significant transformation mandate. You will strengthen case progression and carrier advocacy, build actionable Operations Intelligence, improve operational data and technology, develop differentiated advisor service, and lead an established team through sustained change.

This opportunity is suited to an insurance operations leader who has personally delivered meaningful change while remaining accountable for people, service quality, and daily results. 

 What You Will Do: 
 Lead the daily performance and modernization of Insurance Operations.

 Specific modernization priorities, sequencing, performance measures, and resource requirements will reflect the operating baseline, business priorities, available resources, and appropriate approval processes.

 What You Bring: 
 At least 7 years of progressive experience specifically in Canadian individual life insurance Operations, including a minimum of 3 years in a formal operational people-leadership role with direct accountability for people, workload, service quality, capacity, priorities, and escalations.
 Strong knowledge of Canadian individual life insurance products, carrier practices, application processing, underwriting requirements, medical and financial evidence, issue, delivery, placement, and in-force servicing.
 Proven experience modernizing an operation while continuing to deliver effective daily service.
 Experience implementing meaningful process, service, data, or technology improvements that achieved sustained adoption and measurable results.
 Strong analytical and commercial judgment, including the ability to challenge incomplete data, establish credible measures, and translate findings into action.
 Practical experience defining business requirements and working with Technology teams or vendors through assessment, testing, implementation, adoption, and post-launch improvement.

 This role combines leadership of an established operation with the opportunity to define and implement its next stage.

 Risk Modeling & Analysis: Deploy CIGAM’s existing risk models to assess and quantify risks across a range of investment strategies, including equity, fixed income, alternatives, and multi-asset portfolios. Utilize advanced techniques such as factor decomposition, Value at Risk (VaR), stress testing, and scenario analysis.
 Investment Strategy Risk Assessment: Analyze and assess the risk profiles of existing and new investment strategies, ensuring they align with the firm’s risk appetite and objectives. Provide actionable insights to the portfolio managers and the CIO.
 Risk Monitoring: Continuously monitor key risk metrics and factor exposures, ensuring all investment strategies remain within predefined risk limits. Proactively identify and assess emerging risks.

 Collaboration: Work closely with portfolio managers, the strategy team, and other key stakeholders to incorporate risk perspectives into investment decision-making and strategy execution.
 Risk Mitigation: Propose and implement strategies to manage and mitigate risks related to market, credit, liquidity, and operational factors, while optimizing each strategy’s risk-return profile.
 Regulatory Compliance: Ensure that all risk management activities are compliant with relevant regulatory requirements and internal policies.
 Scenario and Stress Testing: Conduct regular scenario and stress testing on investment strategies to assess the impact of adverse market conditions and extreme events.

 Graduate degree in a quantitative discipline such as Finance, Economics, Mathematics, Statistics, or a related field.
 Minimum 10 years of experience in investment risk management (ideally within the asset management or pension fund industry), with a focus on risk modeling, analysis, and monitoring for investment strategies.
 Proven expertise in risk management frameworks such as VaR, stress testing, scenario analysis, and sensitivity analysis.
 Strong understanding of investment strategies including equities, fixed income, alternatives, and multi-asset portfolios.
 Excellent quantitative and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex risk data into actionable insights for both technical and non-technical audiences.

As a Senior Director, Product Owner, you'll set the vision and direction for your Squad, ensuring priorities align with Crew strategy and broader organizational goals. You'll develop and manage a strategic product roadmap, translate complex business and client needs into clear backlog priorities, and lead release planning to deliver impactful outcomes. You'll work closely with partners across Crews, Squads, and business units to manage dependencies, resolve issues, and keep delivery on track in a complex environment. You'll also help strengthen product practices by mentoring other Product Owners, championing continuous improvement, and promoting delivery excellence across teams.

 Product strategy and vision - Set and champion the Squad’s vision, goals, and priorities, ensuring alignment with Crew strategy and broader business objectives. Build and communicate a strategic product roadmap that maximizes client and business value.

 Summary: 

 Revenue Operations is a strategic growth engine at Clio, accountable for optimizing how we acquire, expand, and retain revenue globally. We partner with Sales, Channel, Marketing, Customer Success, Finance, Legal, and Customer Support to design scalable GTM systems, align incentives to company strategy, and enable predictable, durable growth. The Revenue Operations team provides executive level insights, drives cross-functional decision making, and continuously improves GTM effectiveness through data, systems, and process excellence across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

 We are seeking a Director of GTM Planning and Compensation to own and evolve Clio’s global GTM planning, territory design, and incentive compensation functions as a core lever of growth, performance, and behavior change. This role is available to candidates in Vancouver, Calgary, or Toronto, or remotely across Canada (excluding Québec) and the US. 

 This role is responsible for translating company and GTM strategy into capacity plans, territories, quotas, and incentive design that drives the right outcomes across Sales, Channel, and Customer Success. You will operate as a strategic advisor to GTM and Finance leadership, balancing competitiveness, simplicity, scalability, and financial discipline.

 You will lead capacity planning, territory design and maintenance, and incentive compensation planning, governance, and administration globally, oversee compensation systems and analytics, and build a high-performing sales planning function that scales with  Clio’s rapid expansion. Your work will directly influence revenue predictability, seller behavior, retention, and long-term growth.

 What you’ll work on: 
 GTM Planning, Capacity & Quotas 
 Leading GTM capacity planning and quota-setting, translating growth targets into coverage, headcount, and productivity plans across Sales and CS.
 Developing and evolving quota-setting methodologies, ensuring targets are grounded in market opportunity, historical performance, and productivity expectations.
 Partnering with Finance and GTM leadership to model capacity needs, ramp assumptions, productivity, and hiring requirements for annual and long-range planning, including scenario models that show the tradeoffs between headcount, coverage, quotas, productivity, compensation, and revenue before decisions are made.
 Establishing planning frameworks and analytics to monitor capacity, quota attainment, and productivity and inform in-year adjustments.
 Owning quota exceptions, relief policies, and disputes, balancing consistency with practical business judgment.

 Compensation Strategy & Plan Design 
 Owning and evolving Clio's global GTM compensation and rewards strategy spanning SMB and Enterprise segments, partnering with Sales, Channel, and CS leadership to ensure alignment with company objectives, GTM motions, and growth stages.
 Leading the design, modeling, and optimization of Sales and CS compensation plans, pay mix, quotas, accelerators, SPIFFs, and performance levers that drive desired behaviors, improve productivity, and support multi-year growth.
 Partnering with Finance and Sales/CS Ops to model plan effectiveness, risk, and ROI, leading quarterly and annual compensation effectiveness reviews (attainment distribution, cost of sale, capacity utilization), and ensuring plans support revenue predictability, margin targets, and financial planning.
 Developing and delivering clear, compelling compensation education and enablement programs for leaders, managers, and individual contributors, translating complex compensation concepts into simple, actionable narratives that build trust across GTM teams.

 Compensation Administration & Systems 
 Ensuring accurate, timely, and compliant compensation processing in partnership with Payroll, Finance, HR, Legal, and RevOps.
 Establishing and maintaining compensation governance, principles, and decision frameworks to ensure consistency, fairness, and scalability.
 Owning compensation communications, including plan documentation, guidelines, timelines, and appeals processes.
 Leading the refinement, governance, and continuous improvement of Clio's compensation and commission system (Forma.ai), driving automation, self-service, and operational excellence across regions.
 Championing automation, self-service, and AI capabilities across planning and compensation to improve accuracy, scalability, and stakeholder experience.

 Leadership & Team Development 
 Leading, coaching, and developing high-performing GTM planning and compensation teams, fostering accountability, strategic thinking, and continuous improvement.
 Building scalable processes and operating rhythms, including the cross-functional planning calendar with Finance, HR, and GTM leadership, that enable the team to move from transactional execution to strategic impact.
 Supporting change management for new plans, territories, tools, and policies across regions.
 Serving as a role model for cross-functional partnership, ownership, and results-driven leadership.

 Market Leadership 
 Serve as the executive face of Clio's support organization externally, representing Clio at industry events and thought leadership forums. 

 Build Clio's reputation as the reference case for what AI-first support looks like in a high-trust vertical.

 About This Role 
 The primary responsibility of this role is to lead leasing activities for a premier office portfolio located in Downtown Toronto. The portfolio consists of three assets totaling approximately 2.2 million square feet. The Vice President, Leasing will also support the Senior Vice President, National Leasing in managing the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) office leasing team, ensuring the successful execution of leasing mandates across the REMS-managed portfolio.

 Working closely with the Senior Vice Presidents of National Leasing, regional REMS leasing professionals, and brokerage partners, the Vice President will play a key role in developing and implementing leasing strategies across office assets ranging from Class AAA to Class C.  Provide exceptional leadership and client service by fostering strong relationships with clients, colleagues, tenants, and external partners.
 Lead leasing activities for landlord clients, including the planning, negotiation, and execution of transactions that drive occupancy, revenue growth, and asset value.

 Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships and secure new business by collaborating with senior leadership and engaging regularly with key clients and prospective clients.
 Analyze and evaluate potential leasing transactions by assessing market strategy, deal structure, financial implications, asset priorities, and impacts on asset value and income, and provide recommendations accordingly.

 Proven experience leading leasing programs, teams, and client relationships within a landlord-focused environment.

 Strong financial acumen, including the ability to analyze lease economics, asset performance, and investment impacts.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Legal
jobs.description:
Purpose. Performance. People. 

 Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.   

 With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.  

 For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.   

 The Role 

The Managing Director, Legal, is a senior member of the global Legal team and will serve as a trusted strategic advisor to the Head of Private Equity and the Private Equity leadership team, providing commercial, legal and strategic counsel on matters affecting the Private Equity business.

Reporting to the Managing Director, Head of Investment Legal, the role will work closely with senior leadership to anticipate and navigate legal, regulatory, governance and broader business issues, bringing judgment and an enterprise-wide perspective to both current priorities and the future direction of the business.

The Managing Director will also provide senior legal oversight and support on complex investment transactions and asset management matters across CPP Investments’ global Private Equity portfolio, including direct private equity, funds and secondaries, while exercising independent judgment and managing legal and regulatory risk consistent with CPP Investments’ mandate and Guiding Principles. The role will also connect Private Equity leadership with relevant expertise across Legal and the broader organization. 

 The Team 

 CPP Investments’ global Legal department provides legal advice and oversight across investment, regulatory, governance and broader enterprise matters, supporting the organization’s mandate and global priorities.
 Within Legal, the Investment Legal team works closely with CPP Investments’ investment departments, providing legal advice and support on significant investment transactions, asset management matters and strategic business priorities.

 Accountabilities 
 Act as a trusted strategic advisor to the Head of Private Equity and the Private Equity leadership team, providing commercial, legal and strategic counsel on significant matters affecting the business and bringing independent judgment, constructive challenge and an enterprise-wide perspective.
 Develop a deep understanding of Private Equity’s strategy, portfolio, priorities and emerging opportunities and risks, anticipating issues and ensuring Legal is engaged early in significant business, investment and organizational decisions.
 Work closely with Private Equity leaders and investment teams to provide strategic, creative and commercial advice across investment, asset management and enterprise matters.
 Provide senior legal oversight and support on complex and significant transactions across direct private equity, funds and secondaries, including structuring, governance, investment recommendations, negotiations and regulatory matters, within CPP Investments’ legal services model.
 Act as a senior point of escalation for significant or complex Private Equity legal matters, exercising judgment as to when issues require broader Legal or senior management engagement.
 Anticipate and help manage legal, regulatory and governance risks arising from new investment strategies, products, structures and business activities, as well as changes in law or regulation.
 Monitor relevant legal and regulatory developments and translate their implications into practical advice for Private Equity leadership and investment teams.
 Build strong relationships across Legal and other enterprise partners to bring the full capabilities of CPP Investments to bear on Private Equity priorities.
 Develop and maintain strong relationships with external counsel, ensuring CPP Investments receives high-quality, commercial and efficient advice.
 Lead and contribute to CPP Investments-wide and Legal initiatives, including the development and interpretation of enterprise and department-specific policies, frameworks and procedures.
 Drive high performance by fostering an inclusive environment, developing talent and building capability across the Investment Legal team.
 Contribute to the evolution and strategic direction of the CPP Investments Legal department and broader Investment Legal operating model.

 What You Bring 
 LL.B./LL.M or JD required.
 12+ years of relevant legal experience at a major law firm or an in-house corporate legal department.
 Deep private equity experience, spanning one or more of direct private equity, funds or secondaries.  International and cross-border experience is strongly preferred.
 Demonstrated ability to act as a trusted advisor to senior executives, combining strong legal judgment with commercial acumen and an understanding of broader business and strategic considerations.
 Excellent judgment and the confidence to provide independent advice, constructive challenge and clear recommendations in complex or ambiguous situations.
 Ability to anticipate issues, connect developments across transactions, portfolios and the broader organization, and translate legal and regulatory complexity into practical business advice.
 Strong relationship-building and influencing skills, with the ability to operate effectively across investment teams, functions, geographies and levels of seniority.
 Strong leadership capabilities, including developing talent, building effective teams and contributing beyond immediate areas of responsibility.
 Flexible, pragmatic and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, global investment environment with competing priorities.

 You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to  high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.   

 We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

 Inclusion & Accessibility 
 CPP Investments is committed to  equitable access to employment and building a workforce that reflects diverse talent and perspectives. If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.   

 Attention: Protect Yourself from Fraud 
 CPP Investments is committed to a secure and transparent recruitment process. We will never ask candidates for payment or financial information at any stage of hiring. All legitimate opportunities are posted on our careers page, and communications will come from our applicant tracking system, Workday.
