jobs.description:
Location: Remote
 Type: Full-Time Employee for US Candidates; Independent Contractor for Canadian Applicants

 **A note before you read further** 

 The world is changing fast, and so is this role. We can't fully tell you what this job looks like in six months. That's true of every role at Human Agency right now. What we need from you, no matter what: accountability, curiosity, and a builder-first mindset. If that sounds exciting, keep reading. If it sounds intimidating but you're still interested, let's talk. If none of that sounds like you, that's okay. This probably isn't your spot.

 About Human Agency 

 We're scaling rapidly and have a growing pipeline of opportunities that demand exceptional talent across disciplines. Our mission is to bring on individuals, from creative producers to technical experts to entrepreneurial leaders, who can help us realize this next chapter of growth.

 We are a company of doers. Leaders roll up their sleeves, teams work flat, and everyone contributes to what ships. Titles don't insulate us from feedback or basics. We invite critique, learn quickly, and keep raising the bar. The best ideas win here, no matter where they come from, because clients trust us to deliver the strongest outcomes every time.

 Our clients' missions, products, and bottom lines are sacred. We immerse ourselves in their world, becoming stewards of their goals and partners in solving big problems. Every product, strategy, or asset we create must be both beautiful and functional; practical, usable, and designed for real-world impact.

 Humans are our most valuable resource, and we only grow by hiring people who push us forward. Across strategy, engineering, design, data, and operations, we seek out teammates who raise the bar and make us better. Always hire up, never down.

 We partner with organizations of all sizes to explore, design, and implement AI strategies that are secure, scalable, and human-centered. We believe AI should amplify human potential, not replace it, and we build with that conviction in every engagement. From advisory and tooling to implementation and education, we meet clients where they are and help them integrate AI in ways that align with their mission and values. Our goal is to empower teams to work smarter, move faster, and unlock new possibilities through thoughtful, responsible innovation.

 And through it all, we lead with purpose, love, and adventure. We do meaningful work with people we create about, and we make the ride an adventure worth taking. Because at Human Agency, who we are and how we work are one and the same.

 The Opportunity 

 Most AI consultants are good at one of two things: writing the strategy or doing the work. We need someone who refuses to separate the two. This role exists because our clients don't just need a roadmap - they need someone who will build the road, navigate the detours, and still show up to the steering committee with a clear-eyed point of view on where they're headed next.

 You'll lead AI transformation engagements end-to-end, from diagnosing what's broken and what's possible to rolling up your sleeves and building the thing alongside the client's team. That might mean designing an AI-enabled workflow on Monday, pressure-testing a product decision with a C-suite on Wednesday, and shipping a working prototype by Friday. The client doesn't see the seams. You own the outcome.

 This is the right role if you've spent years inside Big Four firms, strategy boutiques, or early-stage companies and found yourself frustrated by the gap between advice and execution. You know what good looks like, you've seen what happens when no one stays accountable for making it real, and you're done handing off decks to someone else's team. You want the whole thing - the strategy, the build, the proof.

 What You'll Own 

 Client Engagement Leadership — Run AI transformation projects from discovery through delivery, serving as the primary client relationship owner and the person ultimately accountable for outcomes.

 Strategy and Execution, Both — Develop transformation roadmaps grounded in a client's actual constraints, then stay in the work long enough to see them implemented, not handed off.

 0-to-1 Product Building — Identify high-value AI use cases, prototype solutions, and shepherd them from concept to something clients can actually use, often building hands-on alongside the client's internal team.

 Executive-Level Communication — Translate complex AI concepts, technical constraints, and strategic tradeoffs into crisp, confident communication for boards, C-suites, and frontline operators alike.

 Go-to-Market and Growth Support — Contribute to business development, help scope new engagements, and actively deepen relationships with existing clients as their needs evolve.

 AI Tool Deployment — Apply AI tools aggressively across your own workflow and your clients', not as a demo, but as a working standard for how fast and how well this work can get done.

 Internal Contribution — As a senior member of a flat, growing team, you'll help shape how Human Agency delivers, what we learn, and who we become.

 Who You Are 

 Experience & Skills 

 5–8+ years of experience in management consulting, venture-backed startups, product strategy, or a combination, with direct ownership over outcomes, not just deliverables.

 Demonstrated track record of taking AI from concept to working reality in an organizational context — not just advising on AI strategy, but building or deploying something that worked.

 Fluency with the AI tooling landscape — foundation models, workflow automation, prompt engineering, and the judgment to know when to build versus buy versus recommend against.

 Proven ability to lead client relationships at the senior level, including navigating organizational politics, managing ambiguity, and keeping complex engagements on track without a safety net.

 Strong written and verbal communication — you can write a crisp executive brief, run a working session with a skeptical VP, and explain a technical architecture decision to a non-technical founder, often in the same day.

 Experience in 0-to-1 product building — you've shipped something, taken something from nothing to real, and you can speak concretely about how you did it.

 Bonus: Background in venture studios, high-growth AI or tech companies, or operator roles at the intersection of strategy and product.

 Mindset & Traits 

 You're a builder first. Decks are useful; working things are better. You default toward making something real.

 You manage yourself completely. No one will check on your progress, remind you of a deadline, or coach you through a hard week. You are the accountability structure.

 You have no patience for the gap between strategy and execution and have spent your career closing it.

 You're curious about AI in a way that shows up in your actual work — you experiment, you break things, you have opinions formed by firsthand experience, not secondhand summaries.

 You can hold the big picture and the small detail simultaneously, and you know when to zoom in and when to zoom out without being told.

 You do what the work requires. Not what's in scope, not what's comfortable, not what's in your lane.

 Logistics 

 Location: Remote-first; US and Canada eligible. 

 Travel: Occasional travel required for client engagements, company offsites, and key strategic meetings.

 Application Note: Attach proof of something you've built with AI — a product, a workflow, a tool, a result. If you don't have something to show, this is not the right role.

 Equal Opportunity Commitment 

 Human Agency is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building inclusive, high-performing teams where everyone can do their best work.

 The opportunity 

 Human Agency is hiring a Head of Business Development to lead commercial strategy, pipeline, and growth for our AI solutions. This senior, hands-on role will own go-to-market planning, direct sales of services and product offerings, commercial deal design, and the development of a repeatable business development function. The role combines heavy early execution with the responsibility to build systems that scale sales and improve efficiency over time.

 What you will own 

 Lead GTM and pipeline strategy for AI solutions: target segments, messaging, channels, and repeatable sales plays.

 Own direct sales of services and productized solutions: source leads, qualify opportunities, close deals, and ensure clean handoffs to delivery.

 Design commercial and billing models: craft pricing, commission structures, contracts, and terms that align incentives across Human Agency and portfolio engagements.

 Build BD systems and operations: CRM hygiene, funnel definitions, forecasting, playbooks, compensation plans, dashboards, and SLAs.

 Recruit and develop BD talent: hire sellers and account leads, define ramp plans and performance metrics, and create training and career paths.

 Partner with product, design, and delivery teams: translate customer insights into product improvements and ensure commercial motions map to product-market fit.

 Run experiments and commercial diligence: test GTM approaches, validate revenue models for studio investments, and iterate quickly based on market feedback.

 Be accountable for revenue outcomes: set targets, manage forecasts, and report performance to senior leadership.

 First-year signature deliverables 

 Documented go-to-market plan for core AI offerings.

 Standardized commercial model and term framework for studio engagements and services contracts.

 Predictable pipeline and a functioning BD operating cadence (forecasting, reporting, conversion metrics).

 Initial BD hires and a documented hiring and compensation plan.

 First commercial wins: service contracts and at least one monetized studio engagement.

 A dashboard tying BD activity to revenue and unit economics.

 Success metrics 

 Pipeline coverage and month-over-month pipeline growth.

 New services revenue and ARR attributable to BD activities.

 Funnel conversion rates (lead → qualified → opportunity → closed).

 Gross margin and unit economics on studio engagements.

 Time-to-first-revenue for studio investments.

 Speed and quality of hiring and ramp for BD staff.

 Qualifications 

 Required 

 8+ years in enterprise B2B sales or business development leadership, with experience selling services and complex solutions.

 Proven record of building pipeline and closing deals across multi-stakeholder buying processes.

 Experience designing commercial models, commission schemes, and billing structures.

 Demonstrated ability to build BD systems: CRM, playbooks, compensation, and dashboards.

 Strong negotiation skills and experience structuring creative commercial arrangements.

 Ability to partner with product and delivery teams to align GTM to product-market fit.

 Preferred 

 Experience selling into complex buyer ecosystems (enterprise, multi-site operators, or similar).

 Experience in a venture studio, incubator, or professional services model that blends services and equity.

 Prior experience hiring and scaling early-stage sales teams.

 Mindset and traits 

 Tactical closer who can design scalable strategy.

 Comfortable with heavy early execution and rapid iteration, while building systems to reduce long-term grind.

 High tolerance for ambiguity and a bias for action.

 Strong judgment, humility, and collaborative leadership.

 Commercially rigorous and data-driven.

 Reporting & team 

 Reports to: Partners; direct partnership with the Founder and Managing Director of AI Solutions.

 Compensation & logistics 

 Senior leader compensation with base salary, performance bonuses, commission, and equity participation.

 Remote-friendly (U.S. / Canada). Occasional travel for client meetings, portfolio company engagements, and offsites.

 Why join 

 Lead the commercial engine for Human Agency’s AI practice. You will build systems and a team, own revenue outcomes, and directly influence product and investment decisions that scale real business impact.

 Equal opportunity 

 Human Agency is an equal opportunity employer committed to building inclusive teams.

We invite critique, learn quickly, and keep raising the bar. The best ideas win here, no matter where they come from, because clients trust us to deliver the strongest outcomes every time.

 Our clients’ missions, products, and bottom lines are sacred. We immerse ourselves in their world, becoming stewards of their goals and partners in solving big problems. Every product, strategy, or asset we create must be both beautiful and functional; practical, usable, and designed for real-world impact.

 Humans are our most valuable resource, and we only grow by hiring people who push us forward. Across strategy, engineering, design, data, and operations, we seek out teammates who raise the bar and make us better. Always hire up, never down.

 We partner with organizations of all sizes to explore, design, and implement AI strategies that are secure, scalable, and human-centered. We believe AI should amplify human potential, not replace it — and we build with that conviction in every engagement. From advisory and tooling to implementation and education, we meet clients where they are and help them integrate AI in ways that align with their mission and values. Our goal is to empower teams to work smarter, move faster, and unlock new possibilities through thoughtful, responsible innovation.

 And through it all, we lead with purpose, love, and adventure. We do meaningful work with people we care about, and we make the ride an adventure worth taking. Because at Human Agency, who we are and how we work are one and the same.

  

 The Opportunity 

 You are an entrepreneur. That's the ground-level truth.  What You'll Own 

 Build and operate your own venture from zero to one within the Human Agency studio

 Set the framework and cadence for how ventures are evaluated, funded, and scaled across the studio

 Sell. Whether it's selling the vision to partners, customers, or investors — you close.

 Deploy AI and agents as core infrastructure in everything you build — not as a feature, as the foundation

  

 Who You Are 

 Proven experience as a founder, CEO, or product leader who shipped real products

 Sales DNA — you can get in a room and move people

 AI-native builder — you've built with AI, not just used it. Show us. 

 Comfort with ambiguity at every level — from "what should we build?" to "this thing is on fire"

 Zero interest in process for process's sake. You build. You ship. You iterate.

 You'll lead a team of three channel experts today, with room to grow the team as the program scales, and partner closely with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team on measurement and infrastructure.
 This is a role for a leader who can balance strategy and execution. Part of this job is hands-on; you're comfortable working directly in the campaigns, data and tools, and building AI-assisted workflows yourself, not just directing from above. Success looks like building trust with our market and driving real business impact.

 What Impact We’re Looking for You to Make 
 Own paid media. Lead our paid media budget and team across channels, including paid search, paid social, direct mail, and more - deciding where we invest, how we measure it, and when we shift.

 Partner with Growth Product. You’ll work directly with designers, developers, and product managers building the future of onboarding and activation at Jane, designing and executing thoughtful tests.

 Deliver on web experience. Manage the marketing side of jane.com - the front door to Jane for practitioners, patients, and the broader healthcare community. Partner closely with design and engineering, and own site strategy, conversion rate, and our organic presence across both traditional search (SEO) and AI-driven discovery (AEO).

 Own lifecycle marketing. Design and run the programs that guide practitioners from first touch through trial, signup, and expansion, working closely with product marketing and sales on what happens at each stage.

 Put AI to work. Make Jane easy to find in an AI-first world, and use AI across the demand program itself - research, creative testing, campaign optimization, reporting - so a small team can operate like a much bigger one.

 Sharpen our measurement. We have a solid measurement foundation today. You'll define what the demand program needs next - KPIs, attribution, reporting - and partner with our Marketing Analytics & Operations team to build it.

 Align with Sales and Support. Work deeply with our sales and support teams to design demand programs that support revenue outcomes, not just top-of-page metrics.

 Build the team. Lead, coach, and grow a team of channel experts, and raise the bar on how we plan, test, and learn together.

 What Experience We Need 
 A strong track record in demand gen or growth marketing. 5-7 years driving tangible business impact, ideally with experience managing and scaling multi-million-dollar budgets.

 Deeply analytical. Exceptional at translating numbers into marketing strategy, and comfortable operating in a constrained, highly data-driven environment. Deep expertise across marketing analytics, web optimization, lifecycle, and paid acquisition.

 AI-forward. You're already using AI tools in your day-to-day marketing work, you have a point of view on how AI is changing search and discovery, and you're excited to keep experimenting.

 High-velocity SMB experience. Proven success in high-velocity business models, ideally SMB or consumer. We're not looking for someone whose experience is only account-based marketing or traditional enterprise SaaS.

 A strong collaborator. You know how to work with design, development, and product teams to drive results.

 A builder of teams. A track record of hiring and developing high-caliber growth marketing talent.

 If you don’t meet every single qualification but are excited about this role, we’d still love to hear from you.

 More About Jane 
 Jane is a founder-led, high-growth SaaS company with a remote-first team working across Canada, the US, and the UK, united by our mission to help the helpers.

We build the products and tools that thousands of clinics rely on every day to run their businesses, care for their patients, and grow their communities. That level of impact means every person at Jane plays an important role in how we show up for our customers. We're all responsible for being deeply connected to their needs, obsessed with improving their experience, and proud of the difference our work makes in their day-to-day lives.

Jane is growing fast, and that growth brings exciting challenges that call for adaptability, resilience, learning agility, and humility. We're proud of what we've built and quick to admit what we don't know yet. We listen, learn, and adjust as we go. More than 70,000 businesses run on Jane which has 250,000+ practitioners interacting with our product on a daily basis and growth is continuing to accelerate.

Our goal isn't just delivery - it's delight. We move quickly, communicate openly, and solve real problems together. If you're energized by ambiguity, motivated by impact, and eager to learn with others, you'll thrive at Jane.

 Compensation & Benefits 
 At Jane, we're committed to paying fairly, clearly, and above all, paying for growth. You'll see that our salary ranges are quite large - this is intentional. It reflects the full growth journey someone might take in the role, from developing skills early on to becoming highly proficient and ultimately achieving excellence. Most new hires join at the accomplished stage. A starting salary below this typically indicates a candidate with strong potential who is still developing key skills. Salaries above this usually apply to existing team members who have made a significant impact and bring deep Jane-specific knowledge.
 🇺🇸 For candidates based in the United States, the annual salary range is $187,200 - $265,000
 You can explore our benefits package here: US Benefits 

 🇨🇦 For candidates based in Canada, the annual salary range is $177,600 - $288,600.

 Jane takes job scams and candidate fraud seriously. Jane will only contact you from an @ jane.app email address. We'll never contact you from a personal email, ask for payment, or request purchases during the hiring process. If something doesn't seem right, please reach out to us at hiring@jane.app before sharing any personal information.

jobs.title: Director, Sales Enablement
jobs.description:
Do you believe enablement should be measured in ramp speed and revenue, not completion rates? 

 Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a Director, Sales Enablement to be part of our Sales Enablement & Operations department.
 Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!
 Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.

 The team: 
 Sales Enablement & Operations exists to make sure Jobber’s go-to-market org never has to choose between moving quickly and being ready. We build the systems, tools, and people development that turn strategy into execution: how we forecast and plan, how we pay and motivate, how our tech stack works for reps instead of against them, and how every seller gets better at their craft. The team is organized into peer pillars: Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, Sales Planning & Operations, and Enablement Programs.

 The role: 
 Reporting to the Sr. Director, Sales Enablement & Operations, the Director, Sales Enablement will lead Enablement Programs and make sure every seller at Jobber has what they need to win: the skills, the confidence, and the readiness to perform from day one and through every new launch. You’ll lead a team of five to six, as a peer to the leads of Sales Operations, Revenue Technology, and Sales Planning & Operations. You’re accountable for outcomes, not activity — whether reps are actually ready, whether launches actually land in the field, and whether the enablement investment shows up in ramp speed, pipeline, and revenue.

 The Director, Sales Enablement will: 
 Set the strategy for onboarding, training, certification, and coaching across the sales org, and build, manage, and upskill a team of enablement managers and practitioners.

 Own ramp programs and certification standards across go-to-market roles, and hold the bar on what “certified and ready” actually means.

 Lead enablement for new product, pricing, and process launches, building workback plans that trace every training, content, and certification milestone back from the launch date.

 Build structured, repeatable playbooks and coaching frameworks, and keep them current as products, segments, and motions change.

 Bring AI into how the team builds and delivers enablement — content creation, coaching feedback loops, practice and roleplay, knowledge access — and into what reps are taught to use in their own workflow.

 Partner with Product, Product Marketing, Sales leadership, and Customer Success so enablement priorities match what the business needs next, and launches land with sales rather than at sales.

 Define success beyond completion rates, and report on ramp time, certification pass rates, and downstream impact on pipeline and revenue.

 To be successful, you should have: 
 Extensive experience in sales enablement, revenue operations, or sales leadership, including building and running onboarding, training, or certification programs at scale.

 Demonstrated people leadership experience, including managing managers, and a track record of developing your own team’s skills alongside the field’s.

 A proven track record of leading enablement for product or pricing launches in a B2B SaaS environment, with workback plans that hold up against a real launch timeline.

 Hands-on fluency with AI tools in enablement work itself: content generation, coaching and roleplay, and knowledge management.

 Experience building structured, scalable learning frameworks rather than one-off training events.

 Strong stakeholder management with director-level and senior partners across Product, Marketing, and Sales leadership, and the ability to influence roadmap and go-to-market timing rather than only execute against it.

 Comfort operating with ambiguity and building infrastructure where none exists yet.

 Sharp written and verbal communication.

 A bias toward outcomes over activity, and the judgment to know the difference.

 Compensation: 
 At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $181,400, a midpoint of $213,500, and a maximum salary of $245,500, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.
 We design our compensation to reflect each new hire’s skills, experience against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual’s current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.
 Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us too! You’ll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.
 We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we’re happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

 Location: 
 We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo. 

 What you can expect from Jobber: 
 A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

 We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process. 

 A bit more about us: 
 Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

jobs.title: Account Director (Performance Marketing Agency)
jobs.description:
Lead strategic client relationships across a focused portfolio of performance marketing accounts, developing a deep understanding of each client's business, objectives, challenges, and growth opportunities.

 Translate client business goals into integrated, multi-channel marketing strategies designed to drive measurable results and sustainable growth.

 Build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders through proactive communication, strategic recommendations, and transparent performance discussions.

 Connect the broader marketing ecosystem, including paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, conversion rate optimization (CRO), and analytics, to improve overall campaign performance.

 Provide strategic guidance on Google Ads, paid social, and media performance, identifying the factors behind changes in lead volume, conversion quality, and campaign efficiency.

 Monitor performance trends, reporting, and dashboards to identify risks, uncover opportunities, and address issues before they escalate.

 Challenge client assumptions and recommend changes when necessary, keeping business outcomes and performance objectives at the center of decision-making.

 Coordinate internal media, SEO, creative, analytics, and strategy teams to clarify priorities, maintain delivery momentum, and ensure alignment with client objectives.

 Transform campaign reporting and performance data into actionable insights and recommendations that support better business decisions.

 Maintain accurate budgets, forecasts, timelines, project documentation, and client communications.

 Mentor account team members and support cross-functional collaboration and continuous improvement.

 Use AI tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude, and Perplexity to improve productivity, strategic thinking, and creative workflows, while sharing effective practices and learnings with the wider team.

 Requirements:

 5+ years of experience working in a performance marketing agency, with a strong foundation in paid media, measurable campaign outcomes, and performance-driven strategies.

 Previous account leadership experience in a performance marketing environment, either as an Account Director or through progression from paid media, marketing, analytics, or campaign management into client leadership.

 Strong working knowledge of Google Ads, including the ability to interpret performance changes, investigate declining lead volume, and assess conversion quality.

 Broad understanding of the modern marketing ecosystem, including paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and analytics.

 Solid paid media strategy expertise, particularly across search and social channels, with the ability to translate performance data into strategic recommendations.

 Proven experience managing client relationships, leading strategic discussions, and presenting recommendations to senior stakeholders.

 Experience managing a focused portfolio of approximately 3 to 8 client accounts, with the ability to provide strategic depth and personalized attention.

 Experience working with significant advertising budgets of at least $50,000 per month per client; exposure to budgets of $100,000 or more per month is strongly preferred.

 Strong business-oriented mindset, with the ability to focus on revenue, pipeline performance, lead quality, sales alignment, conversion journeys, and broader business outcomes rather than platform metrics alone.

 Demonstrated ownership, initiative, and adaptability, with a willingness to step beyond formal responsibilities to solve problems and deliver results.

 Strongly preferred: Experience in B2B marketing, lead generation, complex sales environments, longer buying cycles, pipeline management, or sales alignment.

 Strongly preferred: Familiarity with Meta, LinkedIn, SEO, CRM, CRO, and other complementary marketing channels.

 Strongly preferred: Experience in financial services, healthcare, education, SaaS, or other considered-purchase industries.

 Strongly preferred: Proficiency with dashboards, reporting platforms, Google Analytics, and data visualization tools.

 Strongly preferred: Experience mentoring account team members or coordinating multidisciplinary delivery teams.

 Interest in AI-powered workflows and practical experience using tools such as ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude, or Perplexity.

 Excellent communication, strategic thinking, analytical, and collaboration skills, with a low-ego, results-oriented approach.

 Benefits:

 Competitive annual compensation of CAD $80,000–$130,000 for Canada-based candidates.

 Fully remote working arrangement across Canada.

 Monthly work-from-home stipend.

 Summer Fridays.

 Generous vacation entitlement and paid time off.

 Parental and family leave options.

 Comprehensive health benefits and mental health support.

 Company-paid disability and life insurance coverage.

 Employer retirement contributions through a Canadian RRSP matching program.

 Quarterly performance reviews and career advancement opportunities.

 Collaborative, inclusive, remote-first working environment.

 Opportunities to develop expertise in AI-powered marketing, performance strategy, and cross-functional leadership.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Marketing Science
jobs.description:
You will own the end-to-end marketing measurement process for major client accounts, from assessing data quality and building analytical models to presenting findings and guiding investment decisions. You will combine technical execution, client communication, and cross-functional collaboration to establish measurement practices that continuously improve over time.

 Assess client CRM, tracking, and marketing data to determine what can be measured immediately, what requires further development, and which data issues must be addressed first.

 Define the most meaningful business outcomes for each model, selecting measurable funnel stages with sufficient and consistent volume in collaboration with client operations teams.

 Direct tracking and CRM implementation improvements, including conversion tracking, UTM and click ID capture, lead source fields, lifecycle stage definitions, and system integrations.

 Validate implementation changes and ensure data quality before incorporating information into measurement models.

 Manage inconsistencies in historical data, including changes in definitions, broken tracking, and missing or undated events.

 Build and continuously refine Bayesian marketing mix models using tools such as Google Meridian, including prior selection, calibration, diagnostics, and back-testing.

 Translate model outputs into practical budget allocation scenarios, accounting for diminishing returns and channel constraints.

 Design and manage quarterly incrementality experiments suited to B2B environments, including target-account holdouts, geographic splits, budget increases, and platform lift studies.

 Conduct power analysis, establish break-even thresholds, and agree on decision rules before experiments begin.

 Evaluate experiment results objectively, including inconclusive findings, and use them to improve model accuracy and narrow forecast ranges over time.

 Collaborate with data, machine learning, and platform engineers to integrate measurement methodologies into client-facing products and workflows.

 Use AI tools and agents to improve analytical efficiency while independently validating outputs and protecting client information.

 Develop and present monthly Revenue Narratives with account directors, explaining performance, model findings, and recommended investment decisions in language accessible to marketing leaders and finance executives.

 Present quarterly experiment findings and coordinate future testing roadmaps with channel teams.

 Clearly communicate the limitations of available data and models, avoiding unsupported conclusions or misleading claims.

 Document analytical decisions, assumptions, and trade-offs while maintaining rigorous quality standards for all client-facing deliverables.

 Support new business and account expansion by explaining measurement capabilities and helping account and channel teams apply marketing science effectively.

 Requirements: 

 You bring substantial experience in marketing science, analytics, or data science, with a proven ability to turn sophisticated measurement into business decisions. You are comfortable building models independently, working with complex B2B data, and communicating analytical findings to senior stakeholders. You combine strong technical expertise with sound judgment, curiosity, and the ability to manage several client engagements simultaneously.

 Significant professional experience in marketing science, analytics, or data science within an agency, consultancy, or growth-focused organization.

 Demonstrated ownership of measurement initiatives that have directly influenced marketing budgets or business decisions.

 Hands-on experience building and maintaining marketing mix models using Google Meridian, Robyn, PyMC-Marketing, or comparable frameworks.

 Practical experience designing, analyzing, and interpreting incrementality experiments, including statistical power analysis and predefined decision criteria.

 Experience measuring B2B marketing outcomes using CRM platforms such as Salesforce or HubSpot, particularly in environments with long sales cycles and low weekly conversion volumes.

 Experience directing tracking and CRM implementation projects and ensuring the reliability of marketing data.

 Some experience mentoring colleagues, managing a small team, or directing specialist contributors.

 Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience working with weekly data from advertising platforms, CRM systems, and web analytics tools.

 Familiarity with data and cloud infrastructure such as BigQuery, dbt, Amazon SageMaker, or Google Vertex AI is an advantage.

 Working knowledge of web tracking and CRM technologies, including Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics 4, server-side tracking, Salesforce, and HubSpot.

 An AI-forward mindset, with regular use of AI tools and agents, the ability to independently assess their outputs, and an interest in identifying new applications for these technologies.

 Ability to transform complex datasets into clear deliverables that influence client or executive decisions.

 Strong understanding of full-funnel performance and marketing investment across channels, rather than focusing on isolated campaign metrics.

 Excellent storytelling and communication skills, including the confidence to explain when available evidence cannot support a requested conclusion.

 Strong analytical judgment, curiosity, and the ability to challenge assumptions constructively.

 Excellent organizational skills and the ability to oversee measurement activities across multiple client accounts.

 Benefits: 

 Annual base salary ranging from CAD 110,000 to CAD 140,000, with potential eligibility for a bonus. Actual compensation depends on relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

 Fully remote working arrangement from a home office in Canada.

 Medical, dental, and vision insurance, along with disability and life insurance coverage for employees and their families.

 Employer-paid insurance coverage for employees, with a 50% employer contribution toward dependent coverage.

 Access to certified therapists through Spring Health and a Headspace membership.

 Physical well-being resources, including physical therapy through Omada and virtual workouts through Aaptiv.

 Complimentary One Medical membership for primary and virtual care.

 Unlimited paid time off, with a two-week minimum, in addition to paid company holidays.

 Birthday leave and an end-of-year company recharge period from December 24 to January 1.

 Paid parental leave.

 Traditional and Roth 401(k) retirement plans with a 3% company match.

 Annual bonus opportunities that increase over time based on tenure.

 Annual company-wide retreat.

 A remote-first and inclusive work environment that supports professional development, collaboration, and individual well-being.

 Reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and during employment for qualified individuals with disabilities.

jobs.title: Creative Director (eCommerce)
jobs.description:

 Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary creative team, including designers, editors, media producers, and copywriters, providing clear direction, constructive feedback, and opportunities for professional growth.

 Comprehensive healthcare benefits package.

 Flexible statutory holidays, with the option to bank unused days for future use.

 Monthly team events and activities.

 Weekly team lunches.

 Casual dress code and a welcoming team environment.

 Dog-friendly office in Vancouver's Yaletown neighborhood, conveniently located one block from a SkyTrain station.

 Professional development opportunities, including conferences and workshops to support career growth and expand professional expertise.

 Financial support for approved professional development activities, including registration fees, accommodation, travel, meals, and related materials.

 A collaborative and engaging workplace culture that values teamwork, continuous learning, personal development, and shared success.

jobs.title: Director – Americas, Life Sciences Vertical
jobs.description:
Lead the execution of the Americas Life Sciences growth strategy, translating regional priorities into country-level go-to-market plans, targeted sales initiatives, and measurable pipeline objectives.

 Align a broad portfolio of industrial solutions—including automation, digitalization, software, lifecycle services, and control systems—with the operational, technical, and commercial requirements of Life Sciences customers.

 Annual base salary range of $171,217–$293,515 USD, depending on experience, qualifications, skills, budget, and geographic location.

 Health and wellness benefits.

jobs.title: Director of Digital Operations
jobs.description:
Lead and oversee the end-to-end delivery of digital marketing services, including Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Pay-Per-Click advertising (PPC), Social Media Marketing (SMM), and website content management, ensuring consistent quality and measurable customer outcomes.

 Design and implement scalable operational processes, workflows, and service delivery standards to efficiently manage a large portfolio of customer campaigns.

 Establish, monitor, and optimize key performance indicators (KPIs) covering campaign effectiveness, service quality, turnaround times, team productivity, customer retention, and profitability.

 Develop and execute annual operating plans for digital services, aligning operational priorities with broader business objectives and growth strategies.

 Drive improvements in search visibility, website traffic, lead generation, conversion rates, and overall marketing return on investment (ROI).

 Oversee campaign performance analysis using Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console, Google Ads, and other marketing analytics platforms.

 Establish consistent reporting frameworks, performance benchmarks, and actionable recommendations to continuously improve customer results.

 Monitor digital marketing trends, search engine algorithm changes, competitive developments, and emerging technologies to maintain service relevance and competitiveness.

 Collaborate with Product Management to enhance existing digital marketing solutions and introduce new services that address evolving customer needs.

 Lead the adoption of AI-powered tools, automation, and intelligent workflows to improve marketing effectiveness, content production, team productivity, and operational efficiency.

 Drive the evolution of traditional SEO practices toward AI Search Optimization, including Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), improving customer visibility across traditional and AI-powered search platforms.

Director, Enterprise Security & IT
jobs.description:
At Klue, We’re Building the Future of Competitive Intelligence 

 We’re looking for a Security, Compliance & IT Leader 👋 

 As our Director, Enterprise Security & IT, you'll sit at the intersection of security, compliance, and IT operations. You'll be accountable for how Klue protects customer data and how every Kluebee gets equipped to do their best work. Today, these three areas sit under different teams. You'll turn them into one team with one roadmap, working alongside an Engineering org that already builds and runs our product infrastructure.

 Your Mission? To own the security and compliance posture that our customers, our sales team, and our own people rely on. That covers everything we do: from building the product, to the internal automations, to the tools we use, and how we use AI. You'll set the standard, build the systems and set the rhythm to meet it. And in the process, make the secure way, the easy way.

 What's In It for You? 

 You won't inherit a playbook. You'll write it. You'll define the operating model, the culture, and the technical direction for a brand-new function, and shape a small, sharp team of 2 from day one. You'll report directly to the CTO and work closely with the Senior Leadership Team, as well as the Engineering, Product, Sales, and People teams. You'll tackle big questions like how to govern AI agents connected to company systems, and your answers will set policy at Klue. As Klue grows, so do the team and your scope. You have the power to shape what that looks like.

 What You'll Do 
 Own security posture and incident readiness. Mature how Klue prevents, detects, and responds to security issues. Design the incident response process and governance, and make sure everyone knows their role before something goes wrong.

 Run the compliance engine. Own the annual audit cycle against SOC 2 Type II, NIST CSF, and BSIMM, plus penetration testing, from evidence collection to a successful finish. Build audit methodology and documentation that make reviews faster and less painful for the whole company.

 Be the security answer for go-to-market. Keep customer questionnaires, external assessments, and audits moving on time. Review and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits with customers and vendors so what we sign matches what we do.

 Govern vendors, data, and privacy. Run full-spectrum vendor reviews, including sub-processor qualification. Own DLP, data retention, and the privacy framework for an international customer base, including data subject access requests.

 Set the rules for AI and high-risk access. Own AI security governance: policies, risk acceptance, data handling, and permissioning for AI tools, agents, and integrations connected to company systems. Define and enforce access governance for high-risk systems, including admin access reviews, service accounts vs. individual credentials, and controls on sensitive logs and data.

 Make security engineering's job easier. Set the security and compliance standard for Engineering's security work. Give the team the tooling, policy, and guidelines to build against, and translate their technical work into terms leadership and customers can act on.

 Equip and enable every Kluebee. Own devices, access, and tooling across the full employee lifecycle. Manage the vendors behind our IT stack, set and hit reliability targets (SLOs) for corporate systems, and replace ad hoc fixes with repeatable processes that scale. Partner with People so onboarding and offboarding run smoothly. (Product infrastructure stays with Engineering.)

 What Success Looks Like 
 One team, one roadmap. Within two quarters, Security, Compliance, and IT operate as one team with a shared roadmap and a regular operating rhythm.

 Customers get fast, consistent answers. Questionnaires, audits, and sub-processor reviews are completed on time and in a repeatable way.

 AI and access are governed, not improvised. High-risk systems and AI tools are covered by clear, documented policy, and admin access reviews are routine, not reactive.

 Corporate systems are reliable. You define clear SLOs in your first quarter, and Klue meets or beats them.

 We're ready when it counts. Incident response governance is documented and understood, and Engineering's security engineers have the tooling and guidelines to respond fast.

 Day 1 just works. Every new Kluebee has working equipment and access on their first day, with no scrambling.

 The budget is a set of clear choices. You actively manage the function's budget and make defensible tradeoffs between tooling, vendors, and headcount.

 You're the default owner. The CTO and SLT turn to you for security, compliance, and IT. Engineering and GTM teams see you as the partner who makes their job easier, not another layer to work around.

 What You Bring 
 Must Haves 
 You've run security and compliance at a B2B SaaS company handling sensitive customer data. You're comfortable owning DLP, data retention, and privacy frameworks, and you can work through a security questionnaire or audit without panic.

 You've led IT operations for a whole company, covering equipment, access, and tooling.

 You know security frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST) and global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA) in depth.

 You're comfortable with ambiguity and building without a playbook.

 You communicate clearly with both technical peers and non-technical leaders, and can explain a risk to an engineer and to a CEO.

 You've negotiated data protection agreements and security exhibits in vendor and customer contracts.

 You understand AI security and governance: data retention commitments, access and permissioning for AI agents and integrations, and risk acceptance for AI tooling.

 You've worked closely with product and engineering teams to turn security and compliance goals into reality.

 Nice-to-Haves 
 You've owned a DevOps and/or security engineering function inside a larger engineering org.

 You've brought previously siloed security, compliance, and IT teams together under one roof.

 You know privacy and data residency frameworks for an international customer base.

 You've managed distributed or hybrid teams.

 ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️ ⬇️
 Not ticking every box? That’s okay. We take potential into consideration. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be accepted in lieu of the specifics listed above. If you know you have what it takes, even if that’s different from what we’ve described, be sure to explain why in your application.
 At Klue, we're committed to building a high-performing team where people feel a strong sense of belonging, can be their authentic selves, and are able to reach their full potential. If there’s anything we can do to make our hiring process more accessible or to better support you, please let us know, we’re happy to accommodate.

 Why Klue Might Be the Perfect Fit For You 
 At Klue, you’ll push the boundaries of what’s possible. For yourself, your team, and our customers. The environment here feels more startup than corporate. You’ll roll up your sleeves, build, iterate, and level up. This is a place where your ideas matter, you can shape what comes next, and leave your mark.
 If you’re looking to join a category-defining company… where you own big outcomes, influence real customers, and work with smart, gritty people… you’ll thrive here. 

 Unlock Your Potential. Take Risks. Take Action. Innovate 

 How We Work at Klue 
 We love the balance of connection and flexibility. We work Office-First, with a hybrid touch, and work together in our vibrant offices on Mondays, Wednesdays & Thursdays to collaborate, brainstorm, and build together.
 Our main hiring hubs are in:
 🇨🇦 Vancouver (HQ) 

 🇨🇦 Toronto 

 🇬🇧 London 

 Our Commitment to You 
 High Performance Culture. We reward high performance and growth through career development, coaching, and annual performance reviews.

 Comprehensive benefits: Extended health & dental coverage that starts on Day 1. Fun perks like discounts at Goodlife and Perkopolis are gravy.

 Ownership: All full-time employees have the opportunity to participate in our Employee Stock Option Plan.

 Our Vacation Policy is Take The Time You Need. We just ask that you give notice and don’t leave your team hanging. 

 Top-tier tools. All employees will receive a Mac (or PC, if that’s your jam) and access to A+ tooling. 

 AI First. All employees are encouraged to lean into AI to work smarter and faster. Built something cool lately? Show us at our Friday Show, Don’t Tell Meetings.

 Growth / Leadership. Direct access to our leadership team, including our CEO, and opportunities to connect with incredible people across the company.

 Social connection. There’s no shortage of ways to stay connected and have fun. We get together once a year in Vancouver for a company- wide kickoff. Throughout the year our Hubs hold regular social events.

 Dog-friendly spaces. Bring your four-legged friend along in Vancouver or Toronto, as our offices are pup-approved.

 About Klue 
 We’re on a mission to help organizations stop losing winnable deals. Klue’s AI agents generate market, competitor, and buyer insights in a unified platform. We ensure it’s trustworthy, automated, and activated across every department, so they have the answers they need to own their market.
 ✨ Here’s what makes us tick:
 Klue is AI-first at its core. It’s wired deep into our internal processes and tooling, powering our small but mighty team. It drives Klue’s autonomous agents that handle the heavy lifting for customers: collecting intel, generating insights, and ensuring content is updated and available across departments. Our agents help them scale their impact, stay ahead of the market, and reclaim the time that used to be consumed by manual, repetitive busywork.

 About this position 

 We’re looking for a Director of Creator Operations to own the systems and processes that connect how Later finds, engages, and supports creators. Creators are on one side of every campaign we run, and as we bring the creator experience together across our programs, we need one leader to design how outreach, success, and support work as a single system. Later Creator is the core of this role, and the scope extends to how we support affiliate creators across Later Influence.

 You’ll own both ways we bring creators in: the sales-led motion, where our team reaches creators person to person, and the product-led motion, where outreach runs at scale through the product. Reporting to the VP of Revenue and Business Operations as part of Later’s Operations team, you’ll partner closely with the General Manager of Creator, Creator Growth, Creator Success, Creator Support, Product, and Engineering. You’ll manage one direct report, who owns HubSpot design and administration, and direct engineering and product resources on the integrations between our systems. This is a high-visibility role with regular exposure to senior leadership.

 What you’ll be doing 

 Strategy and targets 

 Own the infrastructure behind creator acquisition and engagement across the sales-led and product-led motions, from first touch through activation and campaign participation.

 Build the creator acquisition targets, and the forecast behind them, with the General Manager of Creator, so Creator Growth leadership has a number they can execute against and see coming.

 Shape funnel strategy jointly with Creator Growth: they own the number and its execution, and you own the structure, the forecast, and the target model it runs on.

 Own the roadmap for a consolidated creator engagement and tracking system, and decide what gets built and in what order.

 Turn creator funnel data into decisions on where to put outreach effort, headcount, and automation.

 Systems and integration design 

 Act as the primary integration designer between the creator product experience and the Success and Support teams that engage creators.

 Partner with Product the way a product manager would: write the requirements for engagement flows, routing, and handoffs, and work with Engineering to ship them.

 Own HubSpot as the system of record for creator marketing, engagement tracking, and the person-to-person outreach our Creator Success team runs.

 Consolidate the creator outreach tech stack: assess each tool, retire the overlap, and make the remaining systems work from one shared record of each creator.

 Own the budget for HubSpot and the other creator engagement tools, and decide where that spend goes as the stack consolidates.

 Use AI and automation to take manual work out of outreach, routing, and follow-up, and measure what it saves.

 Outreach and engagement operations 

 Own the systems behind product-led outreach to creators at scale, including segmentation, triggers, sequencing, and measurement.

 Design the routing and handoff rules that move a creator between automated outreach and a person on our team at the right moment.

 Build the engagement flows that bring affiliate and awareness creators into campaigns and keep them participating.

 Define the standards (data definitions, field governance, and service levels) that keep outreach, success, and support data accurate and trusted.

 Leadership and team 

 Lead and develop your HubSpot design and administration direct report with clear goals, regular coaching, and a growth plan.

 Set the talent bar for Creator Operations and raise it with each hire and each process you ship.

 Address performance gaps quickly and directly, in partnership with People.

 Direct engineering and product work on integrations through clear requirements, priorities, and follow-through.

 Clear blockers for the Creator Success and outreach teams before they escalate.

 What success looks like 

 Within your first 60 days, you have mapped how creators are acquired, engaged, and supported today across every tool and team, set a baseline for the creator funnel, and shipped at least one change that removes manual work for Creator Success.

 By 90 days, the plan to consolidate the creator outreach tech stack is agreed with Product and Engineering, and you have built the creator acquisition, activation, and campaign participation targets, with a forecast that the General Manager of Creator and Creator Growth leadership have signed off on.

 By 6 months, the consolidated engagement and tracking system is live for Later Creator: every creator touch, automated or personal, is tracked on one record, and routing between product-led and person-to-person outreach runs on documented rules.

 By 12 months, the creator engagement stack is consolidated onto one system that supports all of Later’s affiliate creators, and affiliate creator acquisition is growing faster than the baseline you set in your first 60 days, without added headcount.  6-8 years in Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, or Growth Operations, with a track record of building the systems behind a high-volume acquisition funnel.

 Experience running B2C or creator-facing outreach at scale across both product-led and person-to-person motions, including designing how the two hand off.

 Deep HubSpot experience, including designing lifecycle stages, workflows, routing, and engagement tracking for a team that works directly with customers or creators.

 A track record of designing integrations between a product and the go-to-market systems around it, working with Product and Engineering on requirements, prioritization, and release.

 Experience building targets and forecasts for a sales or outreach team that another leader executes against: you can build the model, set the number, and explain the gap.

 A record of using AI and automation to remove manual work from operations, with results you can measure.

 Experience leading through others, including managing a direct report, owning a tooling budget, and directing technical work across teams without formal authority.

 You get up to speed quickly in a new domain, break complex multi-system problems into concrete plans with owners and milestones, and own the result end to end.

 Experience with other marketing automation platforms (for example, Klaviyo, Braze, or Iterable) is a plus.

 An understanding of social platforms and how creators build audiences and earn on them is a plus.

 Experience in the creator economy, affiliate marketing, or a two-sided marketplace is a plus.

 How we work 

 We will do whatever it takes to win: We win when our customers and creators win. We bring full commitment to outcomes that matter, not just effort.

 We have no limit to our aspiration: We think big, push beyond what seems possible, and refuse to let conventional thinking set the ceiling.

 We take our work seriously, but not ourselves: We bring rigor and accountability without ego, and we make space for each other to do our best work.

 Our approach to compensation 

 We take a market-based and data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation biannually, including performance and market-related factors.

 Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable), while for others it is structured as salary only.

 To comply with local legislation and ensure transparency, we share salary ranges on all job postings. Skills, experience, and other factors help determine the final salary we offer, which may vary from the original range posted.

 Accelerate delivery across the 100+ developer organization by implementing robust design tokens and AI-assisted design-to-code pipelines, removing the friction between design intent and shipped reality.

 Partner deeply with the roughly 10 product managers to compress discovery cycles, using AI-driven usability analysis and rapid prototyping to materially shorten the path from customer problem to tested solution.

 Co-author front-end architecture strategies with engineering leadership, ensuring UX standards are scalable, API-aware, and built on shared logic rather than fragmented static screens.

 Represent design in company-wide planning and prioritization conversations, ensuring UX is a first-class input to roadmap decisions.

 Craft and Quality 

 Set and hold the bar for design craft across the portfolio, from interaction design to visual polish.

 Champion accessibility and usability best practices across every product surface.

 Balance speed and quality, knowing when to push for polish and when to ship and iterate.

 Research and Insights 

 Build a lightweight, repeatable approach to user research that keeps design decisions grounded in real customer and creator behavior.

 Translate research and usage data into design priorities that connect to measurable product and business outcomes.

 Make AI-assisted exploration, prototyping, research synthesis, usability analysis, and design-to-development workflows part of the team's operating model, materially shortening the path from customer problem to tested solution before significant engineering investment.

 Model and drive a proactive, learning approach with internal stakeholders and customer and user personas, creating a culture of curiosity where the team becomes deeply familiar with customer and stakeholder workflows, pain points, and needs.

 What success looks like 

 Within the first 30 days, you've met the design team, key PM and engineering partners, and have a clear read on where the product experience is strong and where it's fragmented.

 Within 90 days, you've established a design operating rhythm (critique, planning, quality bar) and identified the first systems-level fix that will meaningfully improve consistency across product lines.

 Within 6 months, a shared design system is in active use across teams, design is embedded early in product discovery, and AI-assisted prototyping and experimentation are materially accelerating the path from idea to validated experience.

 Within 12 months, the UX team operates with clear ownership, predictable delivery, and measurable improvement in usability and consistency across Later's full product portfolio, and you're recognized as a trusted design voice at the leadership table.

 What you bring 

 We are committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. If you identify with any of the following, we encourage you to apply!

 12+ years of experience in product design or UX, including 8+ years leading and growing a design team.

 Proven experience operating as a systems thinker, designing for coherence across multiple products or teams, not just within one workstream.

 Strong technical fluency and a track record partnering deeply with engineering on platform architecture, APIs, data models, frontend frameworks, and implementation tradeoffs; able to make design decisions that are ambitious, scalable, and grounded in how the product is actually built.

 Experience building or scaling a design system, pattern library, or shared UX standards across a growing product surface.

 Strong facilitation and communication skills, comfortable presenting design direction to senior leadership and cross-functional stakeholders.

 Experience mentoring and developing designers at varying levels of seniority, and comfortable balancing hands-on craft with strategic, portfolio-level thinking.

 Demonstrated proficiency with AI-assisted design, prototyping, and development tools, able to rapidly turn ideas into working or near-working experiences rather than relying exclusively on static mocks.

 Experience in B2B SaaS, marketplace, or platform products is a plus; experience in influencer marketing, creator economy, or social/commerce adjacent spaces is a bonus.

 How we work 

 We will do whatever it takes to win: We win when our customers and creators win. We bring full commitment to outcomes that matter, not just effort.

 We have no limit to our aspiration: We think big, push beyond what seems possible, and refuse to let conventional thinking set the ceiling.

 We are relentless: We keep going. Through ambiguity, setbacks, and competing priorities, we find a way forward.

 We deeply understand our business: If we don't have the knowledge, we figure it out. We take ownership of understanding how Later works and what drives results.

 We take our work seriously, but not ourselves: We bring rigor and accountability without ego, and we make space for each other to do our best work.

 Our approach to compensation 

 We take a market-based & data-driven approach to compensation. We leverage data from trusted third-party compensation sources to help us understand the market value of a role based on function, level, geographic location, and scope. We evaluate compensation bi-annually, including performance and market-related factors.

 Our salaries are benchmarked against market Total Cash Compensation for the geographic location of our job posting. Compensation for some roles is structured as On Target Earnings (OTE = base + commission/variable) while for others it is structured as Salary only.

 To comply with local legislation and ensure transparency, we share salary ranges on all job postings. Skills, experience and other factors help determine the final salary we offer which may vary from the original range posted.

 Additionally, all permanent team members are eligible to participate in various benefits plans as part of their overall compensation package.

 OTE Range: $220,000 – $275,000 USD OTE (base + bonus) 
 Where we work: 

 We have offices in Boston, MA; Vancouver, BC; and Vancouver, WA. For select positions, we are open to hiring fully remote candidates. We post our positions in the location(s) where we are open to having the successful candidate be located. 

 Diversity, inclusion, and accessibility: 

 At Later, we are committed to fostering a culture rooted in an inclusion-first mindset at every level of the company, embracing the importance of hiring and building teams for culture add rather than culture fit. We openly build and maintain unbiased hiring, pay, and promotion practices to create a foundation for an equitable workplace, paving the way for systemic change.

 We are committed to creating a diverse environment and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, or age. Please let us know if you require any accommodations or support during the recruitment process.

jobs.description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

 If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us! 

 Lumentum Canada was awarded the 2022 National Capital Region’s Top Employers for the 6th consecutive year and the 2022 Career Directory Canada’s Best Employers for Recent Graduates for the 5th consecutive year. 

 The Senior Director, Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) is responsible for establishing and leading Lumentum’s global EHS strategy, policies, processes, and procedures. This role ensures that all manufacturing sites operate in compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements and consistently achieve Lumentum’s EHS objectives and performance standards.
 The Senior Director partners with site leadership, Operations, Facilities, Engineering, Human Resources, Legal, and other corporate functions to reduce risk, protect employees and the environment, and promote a culture of accountability and continuous improvement across the company.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Develop, maintain, and govern Lumentum’s global EHS policies, standards, processes, and procedures.
 Establish global EHS objectives, goals, metrics, and improvement priorities aligned with business and operational requirements.
 Ensure manufacturing sites implement and comply with corporate EHS requirements and applicable laws and regulations.
 Provide direction, support, and oversight to site EHS leaders and management teams.
 Monitor site performance through dashboards, reviews, audits, and management reporting; identify trends and drive timely corrective actions.
 Lead the investigation of significant incidents, near misses, and environmental events, ensuring root causes are addressed and lessons learned are shared across sites.
 Support sites in reducing workplace injuries, environmental impacts, hazardous exposures, operational risks, and regulatory non-compliance.
 Coordinate responses to regulatory inspections, notices, and enforcement matters in partnership with Legal and site leadership.
 Establish minimum EHS requirements for new facilities, expansions, equipment, processes, and acquisitions.
 Promote consistent employee training, awareness, engagement, and accountability for EHS performance.
 Provide regular EHS performance updates and risk assessments to executive management.
 Lead the development and execution of multi-year EHS improvement plans and strategic initiatives.
 Establish appropriate governance, escalation, and accountability when sites are not meeting EHS objectives or compliance requirements.

 Qualifications 
 Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Health and Safety, Occupational Safety, Environmental Science, Engineering, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
 10 or more years of progressive EHS experience, including significant experience supporting manufacturing or industrial operations.
 Experience leading EHS programs across multiple sites, regions, or countries.
 Strong knowledge of applicable environmental, occupational health, and workplace safety laws and regulations.
 Demonstrated experience developing and implementing global EHS policies, standards, management systems, and governance processes.
 Experience conducting risk assessments, audits, incident investigations, compliance reviews, and corrective-action programs.
 Ability to travel internationally as required.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Professional certification such as Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH), or equivalent.
 Experience in the semiconductor, photonics, electronics, or other high-technology manufacturing industries.
 Experience implementing or managing ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 management systems.
 Experience leading EHS programs during facility expansions, acquisitions, integrations, or significant operational change.
 Fluency in additional languages relevant to Lumentum’s global operations.

jobs.title: Program Director, Risk Transformation & Execution
jobs.description:
This position is accountable for leading global risk transformation and execution initiatives for Global Operations Risk and Controls, with primary responsibility for the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) program across Line 1. The role will translate strategy into practical execution plans, coordinate delivery across businesses and functions, and provide senior leaders with clear visibility into progress, quality, risk, and outcomes.  

 The role combines enterprise program leadership, data analytics, executive reporting, and identification of AI and automation opportunities. The successful candidate will work directly with complex and imperfect data, conduct targeted quality reviews, challenge scope and assumptions, identify trends and themes, and translate findings into practical recommendations. As priorities evolve, the role will apply these capabilities to other Operations Risk and Control Transformation initiatives.  

 This is a highly visible individual-contributor role requiring strong judgment, analytical capability, and the ability to lead across a complex global organization through influence rather than formal authority.  

 Position Responsibilities: 
 Lead global risk transformation and execution  
 Own integrated plans, milestones, governance, and escalation for global risk transformation initiatives, with RCSA as the initial priority. 
 Drive delivery across businesses and functions, challenging scope, capacity, sequencing, and other risks to committed outcomes. 
 Build alignment and accountability across ELT areas, L1B teams, Process Owners, Line 2, Technology, and delivery partners through influence rather than formal authority. 

 Generate actionable insights  
 Analyze risk, control, execution, and remediation data to identify trends, gaps, emerging risks, and management actions. 
 Conduct targeted business analysis and sample quality reviews, including assessments of scope, exceptions, control effectiveness, and supporting evidence. 
 Translate findings into clear requirements, practical recommendations, and targeted feedback for accountable teams. 

 Enable senior leadership decisions  
 Deliver concise ELT and ERC reporting on execution, delivery confidence, control effectiveness, quality, and emerging risks. 
 Create clear executive narratives that explain what is progressing well, what requires attention, why it matters, and what action is needed. 
 Present credible options and recommendations where leadership decisions on scope, timing, capacity, prioritization, or investment are required. 

 Advance AI, automation, and process improvement  
 Effectively use AI tools to improve manual processes, deepen insights, and drive efficiency.
 Identify high-value opportunities for automation, analytics, and process redesign.
 Define and prioritize practical use cases, then engage the broader team and delivery partners to design and implement solutions.
 Support adoption and measure whether new capabilities improve execution speed, quality, consistency, and risk outcomes.

 Qualifications: 
 Significant experience in operational risk, controls, transformation, program management, data analytics, or a related financial-services discipline. 
 Demonstrated experience leading or supporting RCSA execution, control assessment and testing, or a comparable enterprise risk program is required. 
 Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional programs across multiple businesses, functions, or geographies. 
 Strong analytical capability, including experience working with large or imperfect data sets, reconciling inconsistencies, identifying trends, and translating findings into practical recommendations. 
 Experience preparing senior executive materials, management reporting, and recommendations for governance forums. 
 Experience identifying or delivering AI, automation, analytics, or process-improvement opportunities is strongly preferred. 
 Bachelor's degree in business, finance, risk, engineering, data/analytics, or a related discipline; a relevant graduate degree or professional risk/control certification is an asset. 

 Competencies: 
 Enterprise program leadership: translates strategy into practical execution plans and maintains momentum across complex global initiatives. 
 Analytical problem solving: moves comfortably between executive issues and the underlying process, data, and control detail.
