jobs.title: AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance
jobs.location: Toronto, Ontario; Boston, Massachusetts; Montreal, Quebec
jobs.description:
As AVP, Actuarial AI & Data Governance, you will lead the strategy, governance and enablement required to accelerate responsible adoption of AI and strengthen data capabilities across Actuarial.

 Reporting to the VP, Actuarial Innovation, you will partner with Actuarial leaders, enterprise AI and Data teams, Data Governance, Technology, Risk and other partners to establish and embed data governance, along with lead the shift from individual AI use cases to embedding AI and trusted data into core actuarial workflows and ways of working.

 You will lead the evolution of Actuarial data governance, establishing clear ownership and stewardship, strengthening data quality management, and creating greater transparency and accountability for the data that underpins critical actuarial processes. You will work across Actuarial and enterprise partners to ensure data issues are identified, prioritized and addressed, while aligning Actuarial practices with broader enterprise data standards and governance.

 You will also establish the frameworks and capabilities that enable Actuarial to innovate responsibly and at scale, including AI portfolio prioritization, citizen-led development, responsible AI governance, capability building and value realization. You will provide a trusted view of the Actuarial AI portfolio and help leaders determine where to invest, accelerate, scale, redirect or stop initiatives based on business value, feasibility and risk.

 The role will be instrumental in developing an AI- and data-enabled actuarial function, improving productivity, quality and speed of insight while strengthening the governance and accountability required to maintain trust in actuarial data and AI-enabled processes.

 Position Responsibilities 
 AI & Data Strategy and Transformation 
 Develop and execute the Actuarial AI and Data strategy, aligned with broader Actuarial priorities and enterprise AI, Data and Technology strategies.
 Partner with Actuarial leaders to identify and redesign priority workflows where AI, automation and better use of data can materially improve how actuarial work is performed.
 Establish a clear roadmap for AI and Data capability development, balancing near-term opportunities with longer-term transformation priorities.
 AI Portfolio Governance & Value Realization 
 Establish and evolve a transparent governance and prioritization framework for the Actuarial AI portfolio, including intake, assessment, prioritization, decision rights and pathways for delivery.
 Maintain a trusted view of the AI portfolio, including strategic alignment, expected value, delivery progress, dependencies, risks and realized outcomes.
 Lead structured portfolio reviews and provide recommendations on which opportunities should be accelerated, scaled, redirected, paused or stopped.
 Develop and maintain a value-realization framework with measurable baselines and outcomes,
 AI Enablement, Adoption & Capability Building 
 Build Actuarial AI literacy and capability through a structured learning, experimentation and adoption program.
 Partner with learning and talent teams to embed AI capabilities into broader Actuarial skill development. 
 Drive the transition from individual AI use cases toward repeatable capabilities and transformed workflows that can be adopted and scaled across the function.
 Data Governance & Data Capability 
 Define and evolve the data governance framework for Actuarial, aligned with enterprise policies, standards and controls.
 Establish clear data ownership and stewardship models for critical actuarial data, with explicit accountability for data quality and effective use.
 Develop practical mechanisms for identifying, logging, prioritizing and resolving material data-quality issues.
 Partner with enterprise Data, Technology and business teams to improve the accessibility, reliability and usability of data required by Actuarial.
 Provide governance and strategic direction without duplicating enterprise ownership of data platforms and technical infrastructure.
 Leadership & Stakeholder Engagement 
 Serve as a strategic advisor to senior Actuarial leaders on AI, data and emerging technology, translating complex topics into clear choices, implications and actions.
 Engage leaders to establish shared ownership of workflow transformation and measurable business outcomes
 Lead and develop a small, high-impact team and extend its reach through partnerships across Actuarial, enterprise AI, Data, Technology, HR/Learning and other functions.
 Communicate progress, outcomes, risks and strategic choices clearly to senior leadership.

 What we are looking for: 
 FSA/FCIA designation, or equivalent
 Deep understanding of actuarial processes, supported by hands-on experience across core actuarial workflows.
 Strong understanding of how AI, advanced analytics and modern data capabilities can be applied to knowledge-intensive business processes.
 Leadership and management skills, leading both direct and indirect teams
 Strong business acumen with an aptitude for strategic, critical, and analytical thinking
 Strong verbal and written communications skills
 Strong relationship management skills and ability to work within and across departments
 Understanding the needs of various stakeholders across the organization
 Ability to manage multiple projects of varying priorities levels and scope

 The Director will lead and manage a team, providing clear direction, oversight, and ongoing development, while ensuring procurement-related third-party risk activities are executed in line with internal policies, audit expectations, and regulatory requirements.

 The successful candidate will bring deep expertise in audit, regulatory compliance, and Risk & Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) and will serve as a key point of contact for regulators (e.g., OSFI), Internal Audit, and Second Line Risk. This role requires a strong, confident leader with a strategic and critical mindset, capable of influencing stakeholders, challenging constructively, and delivering consistent, high-quality outcomes.

 Position Responsibilities: 
 Quality Assurance & Control Oversight 
 Lead and execute a comprehensive Quality Assurance Program across VISM, VGM, and Sourcing teams

 Ensure all activities are completed in accordance with defined TPRM processes, system requirements, and documentation standards

 Identify, challenge, and escalate non-compliance, including:
 Contracts executed prior to completion of required risk assessments

 RCSA Ownership & Risk Governance

 Ensure risks and controls are clearly defined, consistently applied, and aligned to enterprise and regulatory expectations

 Centralized issues management and remediation tracking

 Risk data accuracy and reporting integrity

 Regulators (including OSFI), Internal Audit, and Line 2 Risk

 Lead responses to:
 Regulatory reviews and examinations

 Internal audit inquiries and testing

 Supplier due diligence and external questionnaires

 Ensure all outputs are accurate, consistent, evidence-based, and defensible

 Policy, Guidelines & Advisory 
 Develop and maintain TPRM guidelines, processes, and playbooks aligned to regulatory expectations

 Provide guidance to business units on:
 Handling supplier confidential documentation requests

 Application of TPRM requirements in complex or non-standard scenarios (e.g., exceptions, travel-related vendors)

 Leadership & Strategic Direction 
 Lead, manage, and develop a high-performing team, providing clear direction, priorities, and performance expectations

 Set and execute a strategic vision for Quality Assurance and TPRM governance

 Foster a culture of accountability, integrity, and continuous improvement

 Apply a critical and independent mindset to challenge processes, identify gaps, and strengthen the control environment

 Build team capability through training, coaching, and ongoing development

 Partner with senior stakeholders across Procurement, Risk, and Business Units to influence outcomes and strengthen risk management practices

 10+ years of experience in Third Party Risk Management (TPRM), Operational Risk, Audit, or Compliance

 Deep expertise in:
 Audit practices and regulatory expectations

 RCSA frameworks, control design, and risk assessment methodologies

 Strong experience engaging with:
 Regulators (e.g., OSFI)

 Internal and external audit functions

 Proven ability to communicate complex risk positions using audit-grade, regulator-ready language

A central part of the mandate is to move traditional infrastructure and operations toward a modern platform engineering model built on automation, self service capabilities, developer enablement, operational resilience and AI powered operations.
 This leader will consolidate platforms and platform engineering across GWAM Technology. The priority is to modernize the infrastructure environment, drive greater automation and AI enablement, improve operational efficiency, and establish stronger accountability for services and costs.

 Set and deliver the strategic roadmap for GWAM Platforms and IT Operations, including governance, prioritization, capacity planning and investment management

jobs.title: Vice President, Group Functions Technology - Finance & Treasury Systems
jobs.description:
The VP Group Functions Technology (GFT) Finance Systems is accountable for formulating and driving global information services, technology strategies, management, and implementations for Manulife Group Finance (GF) as well as day to day operations for our finance and treasury portfolios. This role is the Information Services lead for the Finance and Treasury and has a clear mandate to identify opportunities to utilize technology to maximize productivity as well as efficiencies while supporting the evolving needs of the business and their clients across Canada, the United States, Japan, Hong Kong and the rest of Asia.  This includes developing the IS application strategy and overseeing its execution to meet goals within agreed targets and budget for GFT Finance Systems. 

 This role is accountable for effectively leading and managing large and complex IS application integrations and the coordination of technical infrastructure projects, ensuring that the communication of requirements and expectations are clear and projects are completed on time and deployed in a controlled and user inclusive manner across the enterprise globally. 

 This role will require a deep understanding of both financial processes and cash management best practices, as well as the ability to drive operational excellence and delivery efficiency.  This role has accountability directly to the SVP & CIO of Group Functions Technology and to provide services to the heads of the various Group Finance Functions and their teams including the VP, Chief Accountant as well the SVP & Treasurer.  

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Individual Accountabilities: 

 Partner with the functions and provide thought leadership, develop and provide authoritative advice related to emerging and innovative solutions. 
 Develop a service oriented team and culture across GFT and collaborate with cross-functional teams to define and prioritize technology requirements for finance and treasury initiatives. 
 Operate within budget targets to add value while ensuring business goals are met. 
 Oversee all technology roles, services, budgets and savings within GFT and manage the relative spend ratio between build and run. 
 Implement technology vision and operating model within GFT. 
 Drive operational excellence and continuous improvement in service management to effectively achieve associated SLA’s and SLO’s and enable the success of the technology strategy for business units throughout the enterprise. 
 Maintain and adhere to governance for Sox compliance, regulators, internal and external auditors as well as all key risk and control standards for Information Risk Management. 
 Execute technology talent strategy and headcount planning across the areas of accountability and the selection, retention and development of senior level professional staff for the GFT group, across Canada and global operating area. 

 Key Shared Accountabilities: 

 Leveraging technology to optimize efficiencies and standardized business processes.

jobs.title: Director, Customer Performance, Brand
jobs.description:
Our Purpose 

 Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential. 

 Title and Summary 

Director, Customer Performance, Brand 

Overview

Mastercard operates the world’s fastest payment processing network, connecting consumers, financial institutions, merchants, governments, and businesses in more than 210 countries and territories. Every day, everywhere, we use our technology and expertise to make payments safe, simple and smart. We know safety and security are the top priorities of our customers, cardholders and partners, so we won’t stand still in developing new and better ways to keep payments safe.

• Do you have extensive experience leading operations, enablement, risk, compliance, audit, or merchant monitoring programs?
• Do you have deep knowledge of program governance, operational controls, case management, data analysis, and customer risk monitoring practices?
• Are you an experienced people leader with strong judgment, stakeholder management, and program execution skills?
• Are you innovative, strategic, and able to build scalable capabilities that enable the BRAM Investigations team while preserving clear accountability for investigative case direction and outcomes?
Mastercard’s Franchise Brand Performance Team advances ecosystem health and profitability by engaging our customers to optimize performance and to enhance the strength of our brand, acceptance network, and data.

Role

• Lead a new BRAM Operations and Enablement team focused on strengthening the operational foundation, oversight, tools, analytics, and program management capabilities that support the global BRAM program
• Establish scalable operating models, procedures, controls, documentation, quality assurance practices, and governance routines to support consistent BRAM execution
• Provide operational oversight and enablement support for investigative assessment processes by promoting consistency, strong documentation, timely handoffs, and alignment with Mastercard Standards and governance expectations, while the BRAM Investigations team retains accountability for case direction and investigative conclusions
• Develop playbooks, training, process guidance, and knowledge-sharing routines to support the BRAM Investigation Team and consistent program application
• Oversee operational workflows, escalation processes, repeat-offender governance, case assignment protocols, testing priorities, and referral paths
• Partner with the BRAM Investigation Team and cross-functional stakeholders while maintaining clear accountability boundaries for operations, enablement, and day-to-day investigation management
• Lead evolution of standards, procedures, and program requirements related to BRAM operations, merchant monitoring, customer escalation governance, and Specialty Merchant requirements
• Oversee program-level quality assurance for complex investigations and assessment outcomes, including trends, consistency, documentation quality, and process improvement opportunities
• Provide strategic direction for customer escalations, referrals, repeat-offender reviews, and matters requiring elevation to governance forums
• Own case tracking and case management capabilities, including enhancement prioritization and planning, testing, implementation, data integrity, reporting, and user adoption
• Lead development of AI-enabled monitoring and advanced analytics capabilities to identify emerging risk trends, support prioritization, and improve program oversight at scale
• Oversee complex data analysis, KPIs, reporting, and operational insights to support leadership visibility, program performance, customer risk governance, and continuous improvement
• Manage the Merchant Monitoring Program operating model, governance, reporting, enhancements, stakeholder coordination, and alignment with Brand Performance priorities
• Support BRAM Announcements and lead internal quality assurance reviews across Brand Performance Programs

All About You

• Extensive experience in operations, enablement, risk management, compliance, payments, audit, merchant monitoring, or related disciplines
• 8+ years’ experience leading operational programs, risk assessments, monitoring activities, governance routines, or compliance program management, with demonstrated ability to develop scalable processes and clearly document outcomes
• Proven ability to lead teams, manage complex workstreams, translate program requirements into operational practices, and drive practical solutions in a global operating environment
• Deep experience with program governance, operational controls, customer risk escalation processes, case management systems, data quality, and reporting practices
• Solid understanding of the card payment ecosystem, including key participants, transaction flows, acceptance models, and how risk can present across the network
• General cybersecurity awareness and acumen, including familiarity with common cyber-enabled threats, data protection considerations, and the role of strong security practices in protecting the payments ecosystem
• Strong strategic judgment, attention to detail, organizational discipline, and critical thinking skills, with demonstrated ability to build repeatable processes, manage governance forums, and identify opportunities for continuous improvement
• Must be self-motivated and able to manage time effectively with competing priorities while providing direction, accountability, and support to team members
• Experience, confidence, and high level of tact and integrity due to frequent interaction with senior internal and external stakeholders and regular exposure to confidential data
• Superior written and verbal communication skills, including ability to communicate complex issues clearly and influence outcomes across diverse stakeholder groups
• Advanced analytical, data interpretation, operational reporting, and problem-solving skills 
• Must be able to work in a fast paced and dynamic environment, handle multiple priorities, consistently meet established deadlines, and deliver exceptional results through direct work and team leadership 
• Strong technical skills including Microsoft Office; experience with case management, reporting, analytics, monitoring, automation, or AI-enabled tools preferred 

Mastercard is a merit-based, inclusive, equal opportunity employer that considers applicants without regard to gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, disabled or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We hire the most qualified candidate for the role. In the US or Canada, if you require accommodations or assistance to complete the online application process or during the recruitment process, please contact reasonable_accommodation@mastercard.com and identify the type of accommodation or assistance you are requesting. Do not include any medical or health information in this email. The Reasonable Accommodations team will respond to your email promptly. 

 Corporate Security Responsibility 

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
 Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

 Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

 Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and

 Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

In line with Mastercard’s total compensation philosophy and assuming that the job will be performed in Canada, the successful candidate will be offered a competitive pay based on location, experience and other qualifications for the role and may be eligible to participate in a discretionary annual incentive program. This posting reflects one or more current openings on our team. 
 Pay Ranges 
Toronto, Canada: $148,000 - $237,000 CAD

 The Sr. Director, HR Shared Services Strategy & Transformation is responsible for shaping and enabling the future evolution of HR Shared Services.
Working in close partnership with the SVP of HR Services and VP of Employee Care, this leader will translate the HR Services vision into an actionable transformation strategy and roadmap, bringing together process reimagination, technology, AI and automation, employee experience, operational insights and change execution.
The role leads a small team of specialists supporting transformation, technology enablement, continuous improvement, service readiness, content strategy, reporting and governance. A critical part of the role is looking beyond how work is done today and identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, digitize, consolidate or eliminate work.
Success in this role requires someone who can operate at both the strategic and execution levels, partnering with senior leaders to define where HR Services needs to go while translating that vision into business cases, roadmaps and measurable outcomes.

The Strategy & Transformation Team Enables HR Shared Services To:
• Deliver a great self-service HR experience built on easy-to-use technology and employee-centric HR content.
• Partner with the SVP of HR Services and VP of Employee Care to translate the HR Services vision into a prioritized transformation roadmap.
• Create and implement strategies to evolve HR Shared Services in response to changing business needs, M&A, technology advancements and broader HR priorities.
• Reimagine HR processes and service delivery, challenging existing ways of working and identifying opportunities to simplify, automate, digitize, consolidate or eliminate work.
• Partner closely with Workforce Innovation to identify, prioritize and scale AI, automation and emerging technology opportunities that improve employee experience and unlock HR capacity.
• Equip HR Shared Services teams, including Employee Care representatives, with the information, tools and resources required to provide exceptional service when additional support is needed beyond self-service.
• Partner to deliver a technology roadmap that improves employee experience and increases the effectiveness, efficiency and scalability of HR Shared Services.
• Drive continuous improvement across processes, technology and service delivery.
• Ensure Shared Services is prepared to absorb new and changing services resulting from HR transformation and broader business priorities.
• Provide governance for Shared Services, including budgeting, transformation prioritization, HR leadership alignment, scorecards and reporting.

   Key Responsibilities 
 1. HR Shared Services Strategy & Transformation 
 Partner with the SVP of HR Services and VP of Employee Care to shape the future-state strategy for HR Shared Services and translate that strategy into a clear, sequenced transformation roadmap.
 Own the approach for how HR Shared Services evolves to support HR and business transformation initiatives, including changes arising from M&A, geographic expansion, new HR capabilities and evolving business requirements.
 Anticipate how changes in the business, HR priorities, technology and the external environment should influence the future service model.

 2. Process Reimagination & Workforce Innovation 
 Challenge existing processes and ways of working and identify opportunities to simplify, automate, digitize, consolidate or eliminate work.
 Work in close partnership with Workforce Innovation to translate HR Shared Services opportunities, employee pain points and operational challenges into potential solutions, establishing clear business requirements, expected outcomes and priorities.
 Build business cases, prioritize opportunities and help move transformation initiatives from concept through implementation and measurable impact.
 The expectation is to go beyond incremental process improvement and continually ask how work could be fundamentally redesigned.

 3. AI, Digital & Technology Strategy 
 Partner closely with the Product Manager in Workforce Innovation and HR Technology to shape and execute the HR Shared Services technology roadmap, ensuring it aligns with the broader Workforce Innovation strategy and the evolving needs of HR Services.
 Bring a strong understanding of HR Shared Services operations, employee needs and transformation priorities to jointly identify, prioritize and implement opportunities leveraging AI, automation, agentic capabilities and emerging technologies.
 Partner on the continued evolution of platforms such as ServiceNow and Workday to improve self-service, increase resolution, simplify employee experiences and create greater efficiency and capacity across HR.
 Continuously evaluate how emerging technology can change how HR work is performed, including opportunities to automate, simplify or eliminate work rather than simply digitizing existing processes.

 4. Employee Experience & Self-Service 
 Partner with the VP of Employee Care to continually improve the end-to-end employee HR support experience.
 Drive the strategy for HR knowledge, content and self-service enablement, including the evolution of the HR portal and integration of knowledge and support across HR and McKesson Technology.
 Create a simple, intuitive experience that enables employees and people leaders to resolve needs through self-service wherever possible while making it easy to access human expertise when needed.

 5. Transformation & Service Readiness 
 Ensure Employee Care and broader HR Shared Services teams are prepared to successfully absorb new services, capabilities, technologies and business changes.
 Partner with transformation teams and operational leaders to assess impacts, determine capacity and resource requirements, prepare teams, enable technology and knowledge, and proactively identify and resolve implementation risks.
 Ensure employees supporting HR Shared Services have the information, training, tools and resources required to effectively deliver new or changing services.

 6. Reporting, Insights & Performance 
 Own the HR Shared Services measurement and reporting strategy, including data definitions, scorecards and partnership with People Analytics.
 Use data and insights to understand demand, case volume, resolution, employee experience, operational performance and emerging trends.
 Move beyond reporting activity to translate insights into opportunities for service improvement, simplification, automation and further transformation.

 7. Governance, Investment & Business Cases 
 Lead key HR Shared Services governance processes, including transformation prioritization, business cases, budgeting, technology investment, scorecards and HR Leadership Team alignment.
 Develop strong business cases that articulate required investment and expected outcomes including employee experience improvements, capacity creation, efficiency, service quality and scalability.
 Ensure transformation investments are prioritized against the overall HR Services strategy and deliver measurable value.

 8. Team & Stakeholder Leadership 
 Lead and develop a high-performing team of transformation and HR Shared Services specialists.
 Build strong partnerships across HR Services, Employee Care, Workforce Innovation, HR Technology, People Analytics, HR COEs, McKesson Technology and the business to move transformation priorities from strategy through execution.

 Demonstrated experience taking transformation initiatives from strategy and business case through implementation and measurable outcomes.
 Experience leading significant technology-enabled process or operating model change.

 Additional Qualifications 
 The strongest candidate will bring a combination of:
 Previous experience in HR Shared Services, HR operations or a comparable service delivery environment.
 Demonstrated experience transforming an operating model
 Technology-enabled transformation experience.
 AI, automation and digital transformation experience.
 Understanding of how emerging technology can reshape HR service delivery and how HR work is performed.
 Process redesign, reimagination and continuous improvement.
 Technology strategy and roadmap development.
 Experience with ServiceNow and/or Workday.
 Business case development and investment prioritization.
 Employee experience and self-service design.
 Data, analytics and performance measurement.
 Change management and organizational readiness.
 Program and project management.
 Strong executive communication skills.
 Relationship and stakeholder management across HR, Technology and business leaders.

We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable.  À propos du poste 

 McKesson est à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice), Gouvernance des données stratégique et expérimenté(e) pour diriger les programmes de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise afin d’améliorer la qualité des données, la conformité réglementaire, la confiance des parties prenantes et l’excellence opérationnelle. Cette personne définira et mettra en œuvre des stratégies de gouvernance couvrant la gouvernance des données, la gestion des métadonnées, le catalogage des données, la qualité des données, la gestion des données maîtres (MDM) et les capacités de traçabilité des données (data lineage).

 Le ou la titulaire collaborera étroitement avec les équipes d’affaires, technologiques, de gestion des risques, de conformité et de données afin d’établir des cadres de gouvernance, des normes, des politiques et des contrôles soutenant la prise de décisions fondée sur les données et le respect des exigences réglementaires. Ce rôle requiert une solide combinaison de leadership, d’influence, d’expertise en gestion des données et d’engagement des parties prenantes au sein d’un environnement organisationnel complexe.

 Ce que vous ferez 
 Diriger la stratégie de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise, y compris le modèle opérationnel, les politiques, les normes et les mécanismes de contrôle.

 Favoriser l’adoption et l’optimisation des plateformes de gouvernance et de catalogage des données.

 Établir et superviser les programmes de qualité des données, de gestion des métadonnées, de gestion des données maîtres et de traçabilité des données.

 Collaborer avec les équipes des Risques, de la Conformité, de la Protection de la vie privée, de la Sécurité et de l’Audit afin d’assurer la conformité réglementaire et la maturité des pratiques de gouvernance.

 Développer des indicateurs de gouvernance, des KPI de santé des données et des rapports destinés à la haute direction.

 Travailler avec les parties prenantes de l’entreprise pour définir la propriété des données, l’intendance (data stewardship), la reddition de comptes et les priorités de gouvernance.

 Diriger des équipes multidisciplinaires responsables d’initiatives d’envergure en gouvernance et en gestion des données.

 Recruter, développer et mobiliser des équipes performantes en favorisant une culture de responsabilité, de collaboration et d’amélioration continue.

 Exigences de base 
 Plus de 12 ans d’expérience professionnelle en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, architecture des données, analytique, conformité ou dans un domaine connexe, dont au moins 4 ans d’expérience en gestion d’équipes.

 Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.

 Expérience dans la direction de programmes et de modèles opérationnels de gouvernance des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

 Expérience dans l’implantation ou la gestion de plateformes de catalogage, de gestion des métadonnées ou de gouvernance des données.

 Expérience en gestion de la qualité des données, traçabilité des données, intendance des données et contrôles de gouvernance.

 Expérience de collaboration avec des équipes de conformité, de gestion des risques, de protection de la vie privée, d’audit ou de réglementation.

 Capacité démontrée à diriger des initiatives transversales et à influencer des parties prenantes de haut niveau.

 Expérience dans l’élaboration de politiques, de normes, de KPI et de cadres de reddition de comptes en matière de gouvernance.

 Compétences et expérience privilégiées 
 Maîtrise en gestion de l’information, informatique, administration des affaires, analytique des données ou dans un domaine connexe.

 Expérience dans des secteurs réglementés tels que les soins de santé, les produits pharmaceutiques, les services financiers ou l’assurance.

 Connaissance de plateformes de gouvernance des données telles que Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview ou des outils similaires.

 Expérience avec les principes DAMA-DMBOK et les cadres de gestion des données d’entreprise.

 Connaissance des règlements en matière de protection des données, des mécanismes de gouvernance et des cadres de gestion des risques.

 Expérience à diriger des initiatives de transformation des données à l’échelle de l’entreprise.

 Excellentes compétences en communication auprès des dirigeants et en gestion du changement organisationnel.

 Certifications pertinentes en gouvernance des données, gestion des données, protection de la vie privée ou technologies infonuagiques.

 Modalités de travail hybrides ou à distance pouvant être offertes selon les besoins de l’entreprise et la situation géographique.

 Capacité à participer à des réunions virtuelles et en personne et à travailler efficacement dans un environnement soutenu par la technologie.

 POSITION SUMMARY  
 The Director, HR Technology Governance & Project Management leads the planning, governance, project management, and vendor management disciplines that turn HR priorities into an executable technology portfolio. The role owns HR technology intake, quarterly and annual planning, portfolio prioritization, capacity planning, and delivery visibility across major HR technology initiatives.  
 The Director serves as a connective leader across HR Product, HR Systems, McKesson Technology, and HR functional teams, ensuring work is appropriately evaluated, sequenced, resourced, governed, and delivered. The role directly manages strategic HR technology vendor relationships and leads a team responsible for project management, vendor management, and portfolio execution.  

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES  
 1. HR Technology Planning, Intake & Prioritization | 30%  
 Own the enterprise HR technology intake and planning process, including quarterly PI Planning and annual portfolio planning.  
 Establish the cadence, criteria, and governance used to evaluate incoming demand, assess capacity and dependencies, prioritize investments, and translate HR and Product priorities into an executable roadmap.  
 Maintain a transparent technology backlog and provide leaders with clear recommendations and tradeoffs when demand exceeds available capacity.  

 2. HR Technology Project Management & Delivery | 30%  
 Lead the HR technology project management capability and establish consistent standards for project planning, execution, risk management, status reporting, and delivery.  
 Direct and develop project managers responsible for medium through large, complex HR technology initiatives.  
 Maintain portfolio-level visibility into scope, timelines, dependencies, resource requirements, and delivery risks. Ensure issues are surfaced early, decisions are made at the appropriate level, and projects deliver against committed outcomes.  

 3. Portfolio Governance & Executive Visibility | 10%  
 Maintain a consolidated view of the HR technology portfolio that gives leaders clear visibility into work in flight, planned investments, capacity constraints, dependencies, and decisions requiring leadership attention.  
 Establish practical governance connecting intake, solution design, prioritization, delivery, and operational handoff.  
 Partner with HR Product leaders to translate strategy and priorities into sequencing and execution plans.  

 4. HR Technology Vendor Management | 15%  
 Directly manage key HR technology vendor relationships and lead vendor governance across the portfolio.  
 Own relationship management, performance reviews, QBRs, escalations, renewal planning, contract coordination, and ongoing assessment of vendor value and performance.  
 Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance, HR Product, HR Systems, and McKesson Technology on commercial decisions, contract strategy, technology roadmaps, and vendor performance.  

 5. Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership | 15%  
 Lead, develop, and set direction for a team responsible for HR technology project management, vendor management, and portfolio execution.  
 Serve as a senior HR technology leader with the executive presence to represent portfolio priorities, risks, and tradeoffs with HR and technology leadership.  
 Build strong cross-functional partnerships with HR Product, HR Systems, functional COEs, and McKesson Technology, ensuring clear accountability and effective handoffs from strategy and prioritization through delivery and ongoing operations.  

 MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS  
 Education  
 Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Information Systems, Technology, Project Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.  

 Experience  
 12+ years of professional experience and 4+ years of management experience
 Significant experience leading technology portfolios, programs, project management, or technology governance in a complex enterprise environment.  
 Demonstrated experience managing intake, prioritization, capacity planning, and portfolio governance across competing business demands.  
 Experience directly leading and developing project or program management teams responsible for complex, cross-functional initiatives.  
 Demonstrated experience directly managing strategic technology vendor relationships, including vendor performance, escalations, QBRs, contract and renewal planning, and ongoing relationship management.  
 Experience partnering closely with Product organizations to translate product strategy, priorities, and roadmaps into executable technology plans.  
 Experience working across HR, Product, and Technology organizations in a matrixed enterprise environment.  
 Experience with HR technology and enterprise platforms strongly preferred.  

 KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS  
 Strong portfolio, program, and project management discipline.  
 Ability to translate strategy into executable roadmaps, delivery plans, and resource decisions.  
 Strong judgment around prioritization, capacity, risk, and business tradeoffs.  
 Executive presence and the ability to communicate complex portfolio issues, risks, and recommendations clearly with senior leaders.  
 Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly working with Product leaders to connect product strategy and priorities to technology planning and execution.  
 Strong relationship management and influencing skills across HR, Technology, Product, Procurement, and other enterprise functions.  
 Strong vendor management and commercial judgment, including the ability to manage strategic vendor relationships and performance.  
 Ability to create clear executive-level portfolio visibility from complex underlying work.  
 Experience establishing governance that improves decision-making without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.  
 Working knowledge of HR technology ecosystems and platforms such as Workday, ServiceNow, Moveworks, and related HR applications preferred.  
 Strong written and verbal communication skills.

McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care. 

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you. 

 ENGLISH DESCRIPTION FOLLOWS 

 Modalités de travail: Il s’agit d’un poste hybride qui exige que les candidat(e)s travaillent sur place au moins 2 jours par semaine dans notre bureau de Montréal. Les autres jours peuvent être travaillés à distance, selon les besoins de l’équipe et de l’unité d’affaire.

 À propos du poste (sommaire): 

 Relevant de la vice-présidence, Conformité et éthique (Canada), le ou la directeur(trice), Conformité et éthique exerce un rôle de leadership stratégique et est responsable de la mise en œuvre, de la supervision et de l’amélioration continue du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité de McKesson Canada.

 La personne titulaire du poste dirige les initiatives liées à la protection des renseignements personnels, à la conformité, à l’éthique et à la gouvernance afin de protéger l’organisation, de soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise et de favoriser une culture d’intégrité et de responsabilisation. Elle fournit une orientation stratégique sur les questions de protection des renseignements personnels, de réglementation, d’éthique et de conformité, et collabore avec les différentes unités d’affaires afin de cerner et d’atténuer les risques, de renforcer les contrôles et d’assurer le respect des lois, règlements, obligations contractuelles et politiques de l’entreprise applicables.

 La personne titulaire du poste est responsable de l’exécution et de la supervision des principaux volets du programme, notamment les programmes de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité et d’éthique; la gouvernance des politiques; les évaluations des risques; la surveillance de la conformité; les enquêtes; la gestion des incidents liés à la protection des renseignements personnels; la formation et la sensibilisation; la gestion des mesures correctives; les relations avec les organismes de réglementation; ainsi que la production de rapports destinés à la haute direction. Elle traduit les objectifs stratégiques en solutions d’affaires concrètes qui favorisent une croissance responsable tout en assurant une gestion efficace des risques.

 La personne titulaire du poste dirige et développe une équipe de professionnel(le)s de la protection des renseignements personnels et de la conformité, et agit comme conseillère de confiance auprès des leaders de l’entreprise. Elle supervise les processus de gouvernance, notamment les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP), les initiatives de protection des renseignements personnels dès la conception et les programmes de surveillance de la conformité. Elle collabore également avec les Services juridiques, les Ressources humaines, l’Audit interne, la Conformité d’entreprise, la Sécurité de l’information, la Gouvernance des données et d’autres fonctions afin d’améliorer l’efficacité organisationnelle et la maturité du programme de conformité.

 Pour réussir dans ce rôle, il faut faire preuve de réflexion stratégique, d’un excellent jugement, d’une grande capacité d’influence au sein de l’organisation et d’un solide sens des affaires, ainsi que d’une capacité à diriger le changement dans un environnement complexe et hautement réglementé.

 Vos responsabilités: 

 Leadership stratégique et gouvernance 

 Mettre en œuvre les priorités de la fonction et superviser l’exécution de la stratégie de McKesson Canada en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité au moyen des programmes, initiatives et ressources confiés à la fonction.
 Fournir une expertise spécialisée et une orientation stratégique aux leaders des équipes d’affaires et des différentes fonctions en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité, d’éthique et de gouvernance.
 Piloter des initiatives visant à renforcer la culture de conformité, la prise de décisions éthiques, la responsabilisation et la sensibilisation aux risques.
 Collaborer avec les leaders de l’entreprise afin d’intégrer les principes de protection des renseignements personnels, de conformité et de gouvernance à la planification des activités, aux initiatives de transformation et aux processus opérationnels.
 Assurer le leadership et la supervision des instances de gouvernance et des activités de production de rapports.
 Évaluer, promouvoir et diriger l’adoption responsable de technologies émergentes afin de renforcer l’efficacité des programmes de conformité, de protection des renseignements personnels et de gouvernance, d’améliorer la surveillance et l’efficacité opérationnelle, et de permettre à l’organisation de concentrer davantage ses efforts sur les priorités à fort impact fondées sur les risques, tout en respectant les attentes réglementaires et éthiques.
 Établir les priorités de la fonction et superviser l’affectation des ressources afin d’assurer une mise en œuvre efficace des programmes, l’alignement organisationnel et l’évolution continue du programme de conformité.
 Diriger des initiatives de changement organisationnel visant à renforcer les capacités en matière de conformité, les pratiques de gouvernance ainsi que l’adoption, par les équipes d’affaires, des exigences liées à la conformité et à la protection des renseignements personnels.

 Supervision du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité 

 Diriger la mise en œuvre, le fonctionnement et l’amélioration continue des principales composantes du programme de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité de McKesson Canada.
 Exercer une influence sur les cadres de gouvernance, les normes, les politiques, les procédures et les contrôles liés à la protection des renseignements personnels, à la conformité et à l’éthique, ainsi qu’aux pratiques connexes de gouvernance de l’information, et contribuer à leur évolution.
 Soutenir l’intégration de nouvelles unités d’affaires, d’acquisitions, de produits, de services et d’initiatives stratégiques aux cadres établis de conformité et de protection des renseignements personnels.
 Promouvoir les principes de protection des renseignements personnels dès la conception et superviser les processus de gouvernance en la matière à l’échelle de l’entreprise, notamment les évaluations des facteurs relatifs à la vie privée (EFVP), les examens de l’utilisation des données, les consultations en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et les évaluations des risques connexes.

 Gestion des risques, surveillance et enquêtes 

 Diriger les évaluations des risques liés à la protection des renseignements personnels et à la conformité afin de cerner les risques émergents, d’évaluer l’efficacité des contrôles et d’élaborer des stratégies d’atténuation.
 Superviser les activités de surveillance, d’audit et d’évaluation fondées sur les risques afin de cerner de façon proactive les tendances, les vulnérabilités et les possibilités d’amélioration.
 Superviser les enquêtes et les évaluations portant sur des préoccupations potentielles en matière de protection des renseignements personnels, d’éthique, de conformité ou de réglementation, et veiller à ce que les situations soient examinées, résolues et documentées de façon appropriée.
 Veiller à l’élaboration, à la mise en œuvre, au suivi et à la communication des plans de mesures correctives et préventives par l’intermédiaire des mécanismes de gouvernance appropriés.
 Surveiller l’évolution de l’environnement réglementaire et évaluer ses répercussions sur l’organisation ainsi que les stratégies d’intervention appropriées.

 Relations avec les organismes de réglementation et les parties prenantes externes 

 Soutenir la gestion des demandes de renseignements, des enquêtes, des audits et des inspections réglementaires ainsi que des obligations en matière de production de rapports.
 Collaborer avec les Services juridiques et les parties prenantes des différentes unités d’affaires afin de gérer les risques réglementaires et d’assurer des réponses cohérentes à l’échelle de l’organisation.

 Formation, communications et culture 

 Diriger les programmes de communication, de sensibilisation et de formation en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité afin de promouvoir une conduite éthique et le respect des exigences réglementaires.
 Favoriser une culture dans laquelle chacun(e) se sent à l’aise de signaler ses préoccupations et renforcer la sensibilisation, à l’échelle de l’organisation, aux mécanismes de signalement, aux obligations de conformité et aux responsabilités en matière de protection des renseignements personnels.
 Collaborer avec les Ressources humaines, les Services juridiques, la Sécurité de l’information, l’Audit interne et les leaders de l’entreprise afin d’offrir des formations efficaces et de mettre en œuvre des initiatives visant à renforcer la culture organisationnelle.

 Gouvernance des données et soutien aux objectifs d’affaires 

 Collaborer avec les équipes de Gouvernance des données, de Sécurité de l’information et des Technologies ainsi qu’avec les leaders de l’entreprise afin de renforcer la gouvernance de l’information, la gestion responsable des données, la protection des données et les pratiques d’utilisation responsable des données.
 Favoriser l’innovation au sein de l’entreprise en fournissant des conseils pratiques et fondés sur les risques en matière de protection des renseignements personnels et de conformité, afin de soutenir les initiatives stratégiques et les objectifs opérationnels.
 Promouvoir des normes de gouvernance cohérentes dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires tout en conciliant les exigences réglementaires et les besoins de l’entreprise.

 Rapports et analyses 

 Présenter à la haute direction des rapports stratégiques et des recommandations portant sur la conformité, la protection des renseignements personnels, l’éthique et les risques.
 S’appuyer sur des indicateurs, des tendances et des analyses pour évaluer l’efficacité des programmes, soutenir la prise de décisions et favoriser l’amélioration continue.
 Communiquer à la direction les risques émergents, le rendement des programmes et les recommandations stratégiques.

 Gestion d’équipe 

 Constituer, diriger et développer une équipe hautement performante grâce à l’accompagnement, au développement des talents, à la planification de la relève, à la gestion du rendement et à l’engagement des employé(e)s.
 Établir les priorités, affecter les ressources et favoriser la responsabilisation afin d’atteindre les objectifs d’affaires.
 Promouvoir au sein de l’équipe la collaboration, l’innovation, l’amélioration continue et le développement professionnel.

 Exigences de base: 

 Baccalauréat ou expérience professionnelle équivalente.
 De 8 à 12 ans ou plus d’expérience progressive en protection des renseignements personnels, conformité, éthique, gestion des risques, affaires réglementaires, gouvernance, soins de santé ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Au moins trois ans d’expérience en leadership, incluant des responsabilités en matière de développement des talents et de réalisation d’initiatives complexes à l’échelle de l’entreprise.
 Expérience dans l’identification et l’utilisation de technologies émergentes pour favoriser l’innovation, améliorer l’efficacité organisationnelle, renforcer la gestion des risques et soutenir la croissance de l’entreprise dans un environnement réglementé.
 Expérience dans la gestion d’interactions avec les organismes de réglementation ainsi que dans la conduite d’enquêtes, d’audits, de programmes de surveillance et d’évaluations des risques.
 Capacité démontrée à exercer une influence auprès des membres de la haute direction et à diriger des initiatives interfonctionnelles complexes.
 Solide sens des affaires et excellentes capacités en matière de planification stratégique, de leadership du changement et d’efficacité organisationnelle.
 Excellentes aptitudes en communication, en animation, en présentation, en négociation et en gestion des relations.
 Capacité éprouvée à concilier la gestion des risques et l’atteinte des objectifs d’affaires dans un environnement hautement réglementé.

 Compétences et expérience privilégiées: 

 Maîtrise ou autre diplôme d’études supérieures pertinent.
 Titre professionnel en protection des renseignements personnels (CIPP/C, CIPM ou l’équivalent).
 Solide connaissance des lois canadiennes sur la protection des renseignements personnels, de la réglementation du secteur des soins de santé, des cadres de conformité et des principes de gouvernance.
 Bilinguisme (français et anglais).

 Le/la titulaire de ce poste aura à soutenir de façon quotidienne des clients internes et/ou externes à l’extérieur du Québec et/ou aux États-Unis. Par conséquent, ce poste requiert une maîtrise de l’anglais à l’écrit et à l’oral.  About the Role (Job Summary): 

 The Director, Compliance & Ethics reports to the Vice President, Compliance & Ethics (Canada) and serves as a strategic leader responsible for the implementation, oversight, and continuous improvement of McKesson Canada’s Privacy & Compliance Program.

 The Director leads privacy, compliance, ethics, and governance initiatives that protect the organization, support business growth, and foster a culture of integrity and accountability. The role provides strategic guidance on privacy, regulatory, ethics, and compliance matters, partnering across business units to identify and mitigate risk, strengthen controls, and ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, contractual obligations, and company policies.

 The Director is accountable for the execution and oversight of key program elements, including privacy, compliance, and ethics programs; policy governance; risk assessments; compliance monitoring; investigations; privacy incident management; training and awareness; corrective action management; regulatory engagement; and executive reporting. The role translates strategic objectives into practical business solutions that enable responsible growth while managing risk.

 The Director leads and develops a team of privacy and compliance professionals and serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders. The role provides oversight of governance processes, including Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), privacy-by-design initiatives, and compliance monitoring programs, while collaborating with Legal, Human Resources, Internal Audit, Enterprise Compliance, Information Security, Data Governance, and other functions to enhance organizational effectiveness and compliance maturity.

 Success in this role requires strategic thinking, sound judgment, organizational influence, business acumen, and the ability to lead change in a complex and highly regulated environment.

 What You'll Do (Responsibilities): 

 Strategic Leadership & Governance 

 Implement functional priorities and oversee the execution of McKesson Canada’s Privacy & Compliance strategy through the programs, initiatives, and resources assigned to the function.
 Provide subject matter expertise and strategic guidance to business and functional leaders on privacy, compliance, ethics, and governance matters.
 Drive initiatives that strengthen compliance culture, ethical decision-making, accountability, and risk awareness.
 Partner with business leaders to embed privacy, compliance, and governance principles into business planning, transformation initiatives, and operational processes.
 Provide leadership and oversight for governance forums and reporting.
 Evaluate, promote, and lead the responsible adoption of other emerging technologies to strengthen compliance, privacy, and governance program effectiveness, enhance oversight, improve operational efficiency, and enable greater focus on high-impact, risk-based priorities while aligning with regulatory and ethical expectations.
 Establish functional priorities and oversee resource allocation to ensure effective program delivery, organizational alignment, and continued compliance program maturity.
 Lead organizational change initiatives that strengthen compliance capabilities, governance practices, and business adoption of compliance and privacy requirements.

 Privacy & Compliance Program Oversight 

 Lead the implementation, operation, and continuous improvement of key components of McKesson Canada's Privacy & Compliance Program.
 Influence and support governance frameworks, standards, policies, procedures, and controls related to privacy, compliance, ethics, and associated information governance practices.
 Support the integration of new business units, acquisitions, products, services, and strategic initiatives into established compliance and privacy frameworks.
 Champion Privacy by Design principles and oversee enterprise privacy governance processes, including Privacy Impact Assessments (PIAs), data use reviews, privacy consultations, and privacy risk assessments.

 Risk Management, Monitoring & Investigations 

 Lead privacy and compliance risk assessments to identify emerging risks, evaluate control effectiveness, and develop mitigation strategies.
 Oversee risk-based monitoring, auditing, and assessment activities to proactively identify trends, vulnerabilities, and opportunities for improvement.
 Oversee investigations and assessments relating to potential privacy, ethics, compliance, or regulatory concerns and ensure matters are appropriately reviewed, resolved, and documented.
 Ensure corrective and preventive action plans are developed, implemented, monitored, and reported through appropriate governance channels.
 Monitor changes in the regulatory environment and assess organizational impacts and response strategies.

 Regulatory & External Stakeholder Engagement 

 Support regulatory inquiries, investigations, audits, inspections, and reporting obligations.
 Collaborate with Legal and business stakeholders to manage regulatory risk and ensure consistent organizational responses.

 Training, Communications & Culture 

 Lead privacy and compliance communications, awareness, and education programs that promote ethical conduct and regulatory compliance.
 Foster a speak-up culture and support organizational awareness of reporting mechanisms, compliance obligations, and privacy responsibilities.
 Partner with Human Resources, Legal, Information Security, Internal Audit, and business leaders to deliver effective training and culture-building initiatives.

 Data Governance & Business Enablement 

 Partner with Data Governance, Information Security, Technology, and business leaders to strengthen information governance, data stewardship, data protection, and responsible data use practices.
 Enable business innovation by providing practical, risk-based privacy and compliance guidance supporting strategic initiatives and operational objectives.
 Promote consistent governance standards across business units while balancing regulatory requirements and business needs.

 Reporting & Analytics 

 Deliver strategic compliance, privacy, ethics, and risk reporting and recommendations to senior leadership.
 Leverage metrics, trends, and analytics to evaluate program effectiveness, support decision-making, and drive continuous improvement.
 Communicate emerging risks, program performance, and strategic recommendations to management.

 People Leadership 

 Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team through coaching, talent development, succession planning, performance management, and employee engagement.
 Establish priorities, allocate resources, and drive accountability to achieve business objectives.
 Promote collaboration, innovation, continuous improvement, and professional development across the team.

 Basic Requirements: 

 Bachelor's degree or equivalent business experience. 
 8-12+ years of progressive experience in privacy, compliance, ethics, risk management, regulatory affairs, governance, healthcare, or related disciplines. 
 Minimum 3 years of leadership experience with responsibility for talent development and delivery of complex enterprise initiatives. 
 Experience identifying and leveraging emerging technologies to drive innovation, improve organizational effectiveness, strengthen risk management, and enable business growth in a regulated environment.
 Experience leading regulatory interactions, investigations, audits, monitoring programs, and risk assessments.
 Demonstrated ability to influence executive stakeholders and lead complex cross-functional initiatives.
 Strong business acumen, strategic planning, change leadership, and organizational effectiveness capabilities.
 Excellent communication, facilitation, presentation, negotiation, and relationship management skills.
 Proven ability to balance risk management with business enablement in a highly regulated environment.

 Preferred Skills/Experience: 

 Master's degree, or other relevant advanced degree.
 Privacy designation (CIPP/C, CIPM, or equivalent).
 Strong knowledge of Canadian privacy laws, healthcare regulations, compliance frameworks, and governance principles. 
 Bilingual (French/English).

jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

 What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

 Directeur(trice) principal(e) de l’architecture de solutions/Senior Director, Solution Architecture

 À propos du poste

 McKesson recherche un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e), Architecture d’Entreprise et Expérience Numérique pour diriger la stratégie d’architecture couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation des solutions héritées (legacy) et la gestion de l’expérience numérique. Ce leader définira la vision de solutions technologiques modernes, évolutives, sécurisées et centrées sur le client afin de soutenir les priorités de l’entreprise et d’améliorer les résultats opérationnels.
 Dans ce rôle, vous dirigerez les pratiques d’architecture qui relient la stratégie d’affaires à l’exécution technologique. Vous collaborerez avec les dirigeants, les équipes produits, ingénierie, sécurité, opérations et les parties prenantes métier afin de moderniser les plateformes, simplifier les environnements hérités, orienter la stratégie d’expérience numérique et renforcer la gouvernance architecturale. Vous développerez également les talents, influencerez les décisions à l’échelle de l’entreprise et aiderez les équipes à livrer des solutions technologiques à fort impact dans un environnement complexe et réglementé.

 Ce que vous ferez

 Diriger la pratique d’architecture d’entreprise couvrant l’architecture de solutions, l’architecture applicative, la modernisation et la gestion de l’expérience numérique.
 Définir les normes d’architecture, les feuilles de route, les modèles de gouvernance et les cadres décisionnels permettant une livraison technologique sécurisée et évolutive.
 Collaborer avec les dirigeants et les responsables métier afin d’aligner la stratégie d’architecture sur les objectifs d’affaires, les besoins des clients et les priorités de l’entreprise.
 Diriger les stratégies de modernisation des applications et plateformes héritées, y compris la rationalisation applicative, la migration vers le cloud, l’intégration, l’automatisation et la réduction de la dette technique.
 Orienter l’architecture de l’expérience numérique afin d’améliorer l’utilisabilité, l’accessibilité, la performance, la fiabilité ainsi que les parcours clients et employés de bout en bout.
 Conseiller les équipes sur les modèles d’architecture modernes, notamment les API, les microservices, les plateformes cloud natives, l’intégration de données, la gestion des identités, la sécurité et l’observabilité.
 Superviser la planification du portefeuille d’architecture, la stratégie fournisseurs, les recommandations d’investissement et la création de valeur mesurable.
 Développer les responsables et les équipes d’architecture grâce au mentorat, à la gestion des talents, à l’évaluation de la performance et à un leadership inclusif.

 Exigences de base

 13 ans ou plus d’expérience professionnelle en technologie, dont au moins 6 ans dans des fonctions de leadership en architecture, ingénierie, livraison d’applications, plateformes numériques ou transformation technologique. 
 Diplôme universitaire en informatique, systèmes d’information, ingénierie ou domaine connexe, ou expérience équivalente.
 Expérience dans la direction d’architectures d’entreprise, de solutions ou applicatives dans des environnements technologiques de grande envergure.
 Expérience de la conception et de la modernisation d’architectures de solutions d’entreprise en s’appuyant sur des plateformes intégrant l’intelligence artificielle et des technologies émergentes afin de stimuler l’innovation, l’évolutivité et la création de valeur.
 Expérience dans l’élaboration de stratégies d’architecture, de feuilles de route, de normes, de modèles de gouvernance et de recommandations destinées aux dirigeants.
 Expérience dans la modernisation d’applications, de plateformes ou de capacités numériques héritées.
 Expérience en gestion de responsables, d’équipes d’architecture ou d’équipes technologiques multidisciplinaires.
 Expérience de collaboration avec des parties prenantes métier et technologiques de haut niveau pour influencer la stratégie et l’exécution.
 Expérience en planification budgétaire, gestion des fournisseurs, priorisation de portefeuille ou prise de décisions d’investissement technologique.

 Compétences et expériences privilégiées

 Expérience avec les plateformes cloud, les stratégies API, les microservices, l’architecture événementielle (event-driven), le DevSecOps ou l’ingénierie de plateformes.
 Expérience en gestion de l’expérience numérique, plateformes d’expérience client, portails, applications mobiles/web ou solutions omnicanales.
 Expérience dans les secteurs de la santé, de la distribution pharmaceutique, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, du commerce de détail ou d’autres environnements d’entreprise réglementés.
 Expérience des cadres d’architecture d’entreprise, des comités de revue d’architecture, de la modélisation des capacités ou de la gestion de portefeuille applicatif.
 Expérience de direction de programmes de transformation à grande échelle impliquant plusieurs équipes, fonctions ou unités d’affaires.
 Excellentes compétences en communication avec les dirigeants et capacité à simplifier des décisions technologiques complexes pour des audiences métier.
 Capacité démontrée à améliorer la performance opérationnelle, réduire la dette technique et accélérer la mise sur le marché.
 Style de leadership axé sur la collaboration, la vision stratégique, la conduite du changement, l’orientation client et le développement des talents.

 Déplacements, présence au bureau et exigences physiques

 Le modèle de travail peut être à distance, hybride ou en présentiel selon les besoins de l’entreprise et de l’équipe.
 Des déplacements occasionnels peuvent être requis pour des réunions de leadership, des sessions de planification, des rencontres avec des fournisseurs ou des activités de collaboration d’équipe.
 Le poste requiert une utilisation régulière de l’ordinateur ainsi qu’une participation à des réunions virtuelles et en personne.

 About the Role 

 McKesson is seeking a Senior Director, Solution Architecture to lead architecture strategy across solution architecture, application architecture, legacy solution modernization, and digital experience management. This leader will set the vision for modern, scalable, secure, and customer-centered technology solutions that support enterprise priorities and improve business outcomes.
 In this role, you will lead architecture practices that connect business strategy to technology execution. You will partner with senior leaders, product, engineering, security, operations, and business stakeholders to modernize platforms, simplify legacy environments, guide digital experience strategy, and strengthen architecture governance. You will also develop leaders, influence enterprise decisions, and help teams deliver high-impact technology solutions in a complex, regulated environment.

 What You’ll Do 

 Lead the enterprise architecture practice across solution architecture, application architecture, modernization, and digital experience management.
 Define architecture standards, roadmaps, governance models, and decision frameworks that enable scalable and secure technology delivery.
 Partner with executive and senior business leaders to align architecture strategy with business objectives, customer needs, and enterprise priorities.
 Lead legacy application and platform modernization strategies, including rationalization, cloud migration, integration, automation, and technical debt reduction.
 Guide digital experience architecture to improve usability, accessibility, performance, reliability, and end-to-end customer and employee journeys.
 Advise teams on modern architecture patterns, including APIs, microservices, cloud-native platforms, data integration, identity, security, and observability.
 Oversee architecture portfolio planning, vendor strategy, investment recommendations, and measurable value delivery.
 Build and develop architecture leaders and teams through coaching, talent planning, performance management, and inclusive leadership practices.

 Basic Requirements 

 13+ years of professional technology experience, including 6+ years of leadership experience in architecture, engineering, application delivery, digital platforms, or technology transformation. 
 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field, or equivalent experience.
 Experience leading enterprise, solution, or application architecture across large-scale technology environments.
 Lead the design and modernization of enterprise solution architectures, leveraging AI-enabled platforms and emerging technologies to drive innovation, scalability, and business value.
 Experience developing architecture strategy, roadmaps, standards, governance, and executive-level recommendations.
 Experience leading modernization of legacy applications, platforms, or digital capabilities.
 Experience managing leaders, architecture teams, or cross-functional technology teams.
 Experience partnering with senior business and technology stakeholders to influence strategy and delivery.
 Experience with budget planning, vendor management, portfolio prioritization, or technology investment decisions.

 Preferred Skills/Experience 

 Experience with cloud platforms, API strategy, microservices, event-driven architecture, DevSecOps, or platform engineering.
 Experience with digital experience management, customer experience platforms, portals, mobile/web applications, or omnichannel solutions.
 Experience in healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, supply chain, retail, or other regulated enterprise environments.
 Experience with enterprise architecture frameworks, architecture review boards, capability modeling, or application portfolio management.
 Experience leading large-scale transformation programs across multiple teams, functions, or business units.
 Strong executive communication skills with the ability to simplify complex technology decisions for business audiences.
 Demonstrated ability to improve operational performance, reduce technical debt, and increase speed-to-market.
 Leadership approach aligned to collaboration, strategic insight, change leadership, customer focus, and talent development.

 Description of Travel or In-Office and Physical Requirements 

 Work model may be remote, hybrid, or office-based depending on business and team needs.
 Occasional travel may be required for leadership meetings, planning sessions, vendor engagements, or team collaboration.
 Role requires regular use of a computer and participation in virtual and in-person meetings.

Who We Are 

 At Momentum Financial Services Group, we help people move forward by reimagining how money works for those who need it most. With more than 40 years of experience, we’re the team behind Money Mart—Canada’s largest non-bank branch network—and a leader in financial solutions for underserved communities.

 From short-term loans to money transfers and prepaid cards, we power the products, technology, and operations that connect over a million customers a year to the money they need, when they need it.

 At MFSG, we come together across teams and departments to create something bigger than ourselves: solutions that remove barriers and give people access to money they might not get anywhere else. Whether you're solving problems, building systems, or shaping strategy, your work fuels real support for real people.

 We’ve Got You Covered 

 Compensation Philosophy: Our strategy is simple—we aim to match the market. We regularly review industry standards to ensure our total rewards package is competitive and fair. This commitment helps us attract and retain talented individuals who share our purpose.

 Discretionary Annual Bonus: Enjoy the opportunity for a discretionary bonus based on individual performance and company success.

 Comprehensive Benefits: Our benefits include health and dental plans with 100% of the premiums covered. We also offer an Employee Assistance Program to support your mental well-being and provide resources for personal challenges.

 Retirement Plans: Plan for your future with our robust retirement savings options, ensuring you’re set for the long haul.

 Hybrid Work Environment: Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model, allowing you to balance remote work with in-office. When you're at our corporate head office, enjoy a relaxed and collaborative environment featuring breakout rooms for brainstorming and unwinding, plus a variety of snacks to keep you energized throughout the day.

 Perks and Rewards: Enjoy reimbursement for tuition assistance and professional development, discounts through Perkopolis and participate in our rewards and recognition programs to celebrate your contributions.

 Please note: The salary range for this position is between C$ 170,000 - C$180,000 

 The Job: Director, Cybersecurity Program Management 

 Reporting directly to th CISO, The Director, Cybersecurity Program Management leads the planning, governance, and delivery of the organization’s cybersecurity program. Reporting directly to the CISO, this role translates security strategy into an integrated portfolio of initiatives with clear priorities, accountable owners, budgets, milestones, and measurable outcomes. The Director works across Cyber, IT, Risk, Compliance, and business teams to resolve dependencies, manage delivery risks, and ensure security investments address business and regulatory priorities.

 This is a delivery-focused leadership role requiring direct involvement in execution, issue resolution, and stakeholder management, alongside accountability for program governance and performance.

 You’ll partner closely with IT, Cyber Ops, DevOps, Risk, and Compliance to strengthen our security posture and ensure it remains scalable, resilient, and aligned with business priorities.

 What You’ll Do
