jobs.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
jobs.location: Remote Canada; Remote Germany; Remote UK; Remote US
jobs.description:
Mozilla Foundation is a non-profit building a better technology future — powered by people, open by design, fueled by imagination. 

 We deliver people-first alternatives to today’s extractive systems. We build side by side with developers, innovators and advocates, united in the belief that a better technology future is not only possible — it’s ours to create! 

 Team 

 Our CEO is increasingly focused outward on the Board, funders, partners, and public conversations that will shape the Foundation’s next chapter. This newly created Chief of Staff role exists to extend the CEO’s reach inside the organization and make that outward focus possible. 

 Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll serve as the CEO’s strategic partner, internal proxy and trusted extension of their leadership. You’ll hold the CEO’s strategic agenda, translate the CEO’s priorities into organizational alignment, represent the CEO internally where needed, and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within clearly delegated authority. You’ll determine what reaches the CEO, prepare the CEO for consequential moments, and escalate only what requires the CEO’s judgment. 

 As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, you’ll partner strategically with other members of the ELT and work closely with the CEO’s Executive Program Manager to make sure the CEO’s time, priorities, and commitments stay aligned and moving. 

 You’ll also partner with the Foundation’s Investment Committee and its technical and strategic advisors, keeping their focus on the right questions, their recommendations aligned with the Foundation’s strategic priorities, and decisions moving efficiently from evaluation to funding. 

 Job responsibilities 

 Here’s what you’ll likely be focused on for the first 6 months: 

 Building a strong working partnership with the CEO, aligning on priorities, ways of working and clearly defining the scope of your delegated authority. 

 Establishing a trusted partnership with each member of the Executive Leadership Team, learning their priorities, pressures and ways of working. 

 Developing a deep, cross-functional understanding of the Foundation’s work and how each function connects to the CEO’s priorities. 

 Translating the CEO’s priorities into a concise, clear set of strategic outcomes that leaders understand and can use to guide the decisions they own, with a current view of what’s changing and which decisions are approaching. 

 Defining with the CEO what truly requires their attention, and ensuring issues reach them decision-ready, with context, options and a recommendation. 

 As the Chief of Staff to Mozilla Foundation’s CEO, you will… 

 Serve as the CEO’s thought partner in developing, pressure-testing and refining strategic priorities, synthesizing executive insight and external developments to anticipate what will need to be known or decided in the next 30, 60 and 90 days. 

 Direct the CEO’s time toward strategy, external relationships, development, Board leadership and the Foundation’s highest-consequence decisions. 

 Filter rather than forward, so significant shifts in strategy, material risks, major budget decisions and Board-level matters reach the CEO early, with context, options and a recommendation. 

 Maintain a current view of the CEO’s top priorities, identify where work is drifting from strategic intent, and surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention before they become emergencies. 

 Enable the Executive Leadership Team to operate as one team around the CEO’s priorities, so the right issues reach the ELT at the right level and decisions and commitments are followed through. 

 Partner with ELT members on cross-functional issues that need CEO-level alignment but not the CEO’s direct involvement. 

 Represent the CEO’s position in internal discussions and make decisions on the CEO’s behalf within delegated authority, bringing anything beyond it back to the CEO promptly. 

 Ensure the CEO enters every Board meeting, funder and partner conversation, speech and public engagement fully prepared, with concise briefings, organizational context and answers to likely questions. 

 Identify external opportunities that warrant the CEO’s attention, and ensure commitments the CEO makes externally translate into clear internal follow-through. 

 What this role is not 

 This is a role of influence. It exists to ensure the CEO can lead effectively through the Executive Leadership Team. 

 The Chief of Staff does not manage the Executive Leadership Team or run the Foundation’s operations. Each executive leader owns execution and decisions within their area. 

 This role does not make decisions beyond the authority the CEO has delegated. Anything outside that authority returns to the CEO. 

 This role does not have any direct reports and also doesn’t manage the CEO’s calendar, scheduling or administrative support. 

 Your Professional Profile 

 Significant, verifiable experience as a strategic partner at CEO or executive-team level, with a track record of leading high-stakes work and turning ambiguity into structure and action. 

 Experience working across multiple legal entities is a plus, including navigating differences, building influence, and coordinating work across entities where relevant.  

 A proven record of driving complex, cross-functional priorities from idea to execution by defining outcomes, ownership, milestones and decision points. 

 Exceptional judgment and discretion, including handling confidential information and navigating complex executive dynamics with integrity. 

 Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority, build trust across functions and at the most senior levels, and give direct feedback with care. 

 Outstanding written and verbal communication, with experience distilling complex information into decision-ready briefs, recommendations, presentations and executive communications. 

 Strong analytical and strategic problem-solving skills: you frame the right question, gather the right information, test assumptions and recommend a practical path forward. 

 Disciplined prioritization, with the agility to move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues without losing the thread. 

 Direct experience supporting Board governance, fundraising or other high-stakes external relationships at an executive level. 

 A track record of doing high-impact work out of the spotlight, measuring your success by the CEO’s and the team’s, and acting in the best interests of the CEO and the organization. 

 A demonstrated commitment to Mozilla Foundation’s mission and to building an open, accessible and trustworthy internet. 

 The ability to work across time zones and occasionally outside standard working hours for Board meetings, major events or urgent organizational needs. 

 Comfortable traveling for Board meetings, leadership gatherings and major events. 

 We Are Excited To See Any Additional Experience With: 

 Senior roles in nonprofit, philanthropic, technology or public-interest organizations. 

 Supporting or advising investment, grantmaking or funding committees. 

 How We Work 

 A few things that are true about how we work at Mozilla Foundation. Here's a summary along with our expectation of how these should show up in this role: 

 Move toward the hard thing: you surface conflicts in priorities, resources or attention early, and give the CEO and executives direct, actionable input, including what they may not want to hear. You disagree constructively in the room, not afterward, and you don’t wait for someone else to raise it.

 Stay curious and current: you stay close to what executives are seeing and what’s happening in our fields and communities, and turn it into the context the CEO needs. You pressure-test assumptions, including your own.

 Work in the open: you document decisions and the reasoning behind them, so executives and teams can follow how and why priorities are set. You favor shared channels over side conversations wherever appropriate.

 Focus and finish: you keep the CEO’s agenda focused on what matters most, make deliberate choices about what does and doesn’t need the CEO, and make sure decisions and commitments are seen through.

 Flex with purpose: you move between long-term priorities and time-sensitive issues as context shifts, and adapt how you work with each executive. Flexibility isn’t about being agreeable; it’s staying responsive while holding to the mission and the CEO’s priorities.

 Lead with care: you hold a high bar for the work while treating people as whole humans. You extend good faith to fellow executives, respect that each owns their area, and talk directly to the person who can solve the problem.

 Salary and Benefits Information 

 Mozilla Foundation is dedicated to fair and equitable compensation for our staff. We aim to pay a competitive and market-based salary based on the responsibilities and requirements of the role. We do not ask for, or take into account, salary histories in our offer process.

 The starting salary ranges for this role are listed below. 

 Germany: €206,448.00 – €232,253.22

 UK: £181,764.00 – £204,483.81

 Canada: $356,400.00 – $400,948.65

 US: $264,000.00 – $296,999.00

 We also offer the following benefits:

 Private Medical Insurance

 Extended Sick Leave

 Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 Retirement Plan contributions

 Paid Time Off: 20 days annual leave + sick days and your birthday

 Company Holidays + EOY Shutdown

 Wellness budget

 Professional Development budget

 Top up program for Pregnancy and Parental leaves

 Benefits are subject to change at any time at the discretion of Mozilla Foundation. 

 Mozilla Foundation Hiring Practices 

 Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, and persons of all sexual orientations and gender identities and expressions.

 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

 We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation at accommodation@mozillafoundation.org.

jobs.description:
Do you want your voice heard and your actions to count? 

 Discover your opportunity with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), one of the world’s leading financial groups. Across the globe, we’re 150,000 colleagues, striving to make a difference for every client, organization, and community we serve. We stand for our values, building long-term relationships, serving society, and fostering shared and sustainable growth for a better world.

 With a vision to be the world’s most trusted financial group, it’s part of our culture to put people first, listen to new and diverse ideas and collaborate toward greater innovation, speed and agility. This means investing in talent, technologies, and tools that empower you to own your career.

 Join MUFG, where being inspired is expected and making a meaningful impact is rewarded.

 Overview 
 The role supports the Financial Risk function within MUFG Canada Risk Management, with a focus on the production, analysis, governance and continuous enhancement of liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and interest rate risk in the banking book reporting. Reporting to the Financial Risk Vice President, the incumbent is responsible for preparing and maintaining recurring risk reports, supporting ECL and portfolio credit risk analysis, monitoring risk appetite and limit metrics, maintaining EUC and procedure documentation, and assisting with committee materials for IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk and Market Risk governance forums. The role requires excellent technical capability, including advanced data analysis, Excel/Power Query/VBA automation, source-data reconciliation, AI literacy and the ability to responsibly leverage AI-enabled tools to improve reporting efficiency, data quality, trend analysis, control effectiveness and management insight. The incumbent must demonstrate strong knowledge of the underlying risk metrics, data sources such as OVS extracts, Bloomberg and internal reporting files, and the ability to translate complex technical outputs into clear, audit-ready commentary and management materials.

 Key Accountabilities 
 Risk reporting, analytics and governance support - responsibilities include:
 Prepare, analyze and maintain recurring Financial Risk reports across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including Liquidity Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Limit Dashboard, Liquidity Stress Testing, daily and monthly liquidity monitoring, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, portfolio concentration, IFRS 9 ECL, Watchlist inputs, Risk Appetite metrics and interest rate risk analytics.
 Compile and validate source data from OVS extracts, Bloomberg, internal risk files, Treasury reports, Middle Office data, Finance inputs, facility and commitment data, exposure reports and locally maintained EUC tools to support recurring production and independent review of risk metrics.
 Support the preparation of IRC, ECC, Liquidity Risk, Market Risk and other governance materials by compiling metrics, drafting commentary, preparing exhibits, explaining drivers, documenting assumptions and ensuring materials are accurate, complete and delivered within required timelines.
 Perform review and challenge of report outputs, investigate material movements or exceptions, document rationale, reconcile data back to source systems, and escalate breaches, data issues or control concerns in accordance with applicable procedures.

 Support for stakeholders - responsibilities include: 
 Coordinate with Treasury, Middle Office, Finance, Operations, Compliance, business lines, regional risk teams and Head Office to obtain data, validate assumptions, clarify methodology, and support timely completion of Financial Risk deliverables.
 Provide support, oversight and guidance to first line and independent risk monitoring functions on risk reporting, risk appetite monitoring, limit usage, breach escalation and remediation tracking.
 Support audit, regulatory and internal review requests by maintaining clear evidence, audit trails, version logs, approvals and supporting documentation for recurring reporting processes.
 Monitor relevant regulatory, Head Office and regional risk requirements and assist in translating them into local policies, procedures, controls, testing approaches and reporting processes.
 Support the review and enhancement of local risk policies, procedures, EUC documentation and user manuals, including documentation for EWI, liquidity limits, LST, market risk reporting, RFR-linked submissions and ECL processes.
 Assist with annual recalibration and methodology review processes for liquidity risk metrics, EWI thresholds, LST assumptions, local limits and other Financial Risk measures, including coordination with ALRMO, Head Office and first line stakeholders.
 Identify opportunities to automate, streamline and strengthen recurring reports, tracking logs, confirmations and control processes while maintaining appropriate governance, documentation and change management.

 Technical Skills 
 Excellent technical skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capability with complex formulas, Power Query, pivot tables, data validation, reconciliations, financial modelling, VBA/macros and automation techniques used to streamline recurring risk reporting processes.
 Strong knowledge of liquidity risk metrics and reporting, including Early Warning Indicators, Liquidity Stress Testing, liquidity limits, limit utilization, funds position, cash-flow analysis, contingency funding plan inputs, liquidity risk appetite measures, threshold recalibration and breach/escalation monitoring.
 Strong knowledge of market risk metrics and analytics, including VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity analysis, limit monitoring, market data validation, rate and spread movements, exposure drivers and recurring market risk reporting packages.
 Strong knowledge of credit risk and ECL analytics, including IFRS 9 ECL, exposure and commitment utilization, portfolio concentration, industry and obligor analysis, facility data, credit exposure trends and credit risk appetite reporting.
 Working knowledge of IRRBB concepts and tools, including interest rate sensitivity, earnings and economic value perspectives, repricing profile analysis, scenario-based impacts, assumptions review and coordination with regional or Head Office stakeholders on IRRBB methodology and tool development.
 Ability to source, extract, reconcile and analyze data from multiple internal and external risk systems, Treasury and Middle Office files, Finance inputs, facility and commitment reports, shared-drive repositories, SharePoint sites and locally maintained EUC tools.
 Advanced data analytics capability, including the ability to work with large and complex data sets, identify data quality issues, perform variance and trend analysis, reconcile outputs across systems, design repeatable controls, and convert raw data into meaningful risk insights and executive-level commentary.
 Practical knowledge of AI-enabled productivity and analytics tools, with the ability to responsibly leverage AI to support data validation, report drafting, process documentation, variance investigation, coding assistance, workflow automation, knowledge management and management reporting, while maintaining appropriate human review, confidentiality and control standards.
 Ability to identify and implement opportunities for automation, AI-assisted analysis and process improvement in recurring reports, EUC tools, tracking logs, confirmations, procedure manuals, management materials and control evidence repositories.
 Experience preparing high-quality committee, management and audit materials, including metric dashboards, variance explanations, trend summaries, breach or exception commentary, methodology notes, procedure documentation and evidence packages.
 Sound understanding of financial risk concepts, governance expectations and control requirements, including liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9 ECL, IRRBB, risk appetite metrics, stress testing, concentration risk, EUC governance and risk measurement methodologies.

 Experience & Abilities 
 Minimum of 3 years of banking, risk management, treasury, finance, audit, data analytics or related financial services experience; experience in a second line risk management function is preferred.
 Demonstrated ability to prepare, analyze and explain recurring risk reports and supporting materials across liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk and IRRBB, including EWI, LST, liquidity limits, VaR, stress testing, DV01, sensitivity measures, ECL, commitment utilization, concentration, risk appetite and governance reporting.
 Strong technical aptitude and curiosity, with a proven ability to learn new systems, adopt emerging technologies, use AI-enabled tools responsibly, and translate technical outputs into practical risk management conclusions.
 Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify data issues, explain key drivers, assess materiality, reconcile outputs to source data, validate AI-assisted outputs and recommend practical control or reporting improvements.
 Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft concise commentary, document rationale, present results, and coordinate deliverables with stakeholders at different levels.
 Ability to manage multiple recurring deadlines, maintain strong attention to detail, preserve accurate audit trails, and ensure technology-enabled improvements remain transparent, controlled and well documented.

 Education & Training 
 University degree in finance, economics, mathematics, accounting, business, risk management, data analytics, computer science, information systems or a related discipline.
 Post-graduate education, professional designation or progress toward a designation such as FRM, CFA, CPA, MBA, data analytics certification, AI-related training or equivalent risk/finance certification is considered beneficial.
 Additional training in liquidity risk, market risk, credit risk, IFRS 9, regulatory reporting, data analytics, automation, responsible AI use, prompt engineering, model/EUC governance or technology risk controls is considered an asset.

jobs.title: AVP - Associate General Counsel - Verafin
jobs.location: Toronto-King St; St. John's - 110 Hebron Way
jobs.description:
As a AVP Associate General Counsel supporting Nasdaq Verafin, you will serve as a senior legal advisor and strategic partner to the Verafin business, providing practical legal counsel across commercial, product, regulatory and strategic matters. You will work closely with Verafin leadership and cross-functional teams to support the continued growth and evolution of a technology business serving banks and other regulated financial institutions.
You will thrive in this position if you combine strong commercial judgment with a deep understanding of the banking and financial services industry and an ability to navigate complex legal and regulatory issues. You are comfortable advising senior business leaders, leading sophisticated negotiations with financial institutions, and partnering with product and technology teams in a fast-moving environment. Experience with anti-money laundering, financial crime or related banking regulation is highly valued, as is an understanding of emerging legal issues relating to artificial intelligence. 

 Key Responsibilities:

 Serve as a senior legal advisor and strategic partner to the Verafin leadership team, providing practical, business-oriented counsel across commercial, product, regulatory, operational and strategic matters.
 Lead and provide legal oversight for complex commercial transactions with Verafin clients, including major banks and other regulated financial institutions, balancing commercial objectives with appropriate management of legal and regulatory risk.
 Advise on legal and regulatory considerations affecting Verafin's products and services, including issues arising from the development, deployment and commercialization of technology used by financial institutions.
 Provide legal support for strategic product initiatives, new products and services, partnerships, international expansion and other business growth initiatives.
 Develop a strong understanding of Verafin's business, products, clients and regulatory environment and act as a trusted legal partner to senior leadership, Sales, Product, Technology, and other business functions.
 Advise on legal matters arising from the regulatory environment applicable to banks and other financial institutions, including anti-money laundering, financial crime prevention and related regulatory requirements.
 Lead the drafting, review and negotiation of complex technology and services agreements and other commercial arrangements with sophisticated financial institutions, including addressing regulatory, outsourcing, data, security, artificial intelligence and operational requirements.
 Partner with Legal, Risk and subject-matter experts across Nasdaq, including privacy, cybersecurity, intellectual property, litigation, compliance and regulatory specialists, to provide coordinated and pragmatic legal advice to the Verafin business.
 Identify emerging legal and regulatory developments relevant to Verafin and its clients and translate those developments into practical guidance for business and product leaders.
 Support the development and continuous improvement of contracting standards, templates, playbooks and legal processes to improve consistency, scalability and speed while maintaining an appropriate risk profile.
 Provide guidance on legal issues relating to artificial intelligence, including the development and use of AI-enabled products, data and intellectual property considerations, customer contractual requirements, risk allocation and emerging AI regulation.
 Help drive innovation within the Legal function by effectively using AI and other legal technology tools to improve legal analysis, contract review, knowledge management and delivery of legal services.
 Exercise independent judgment on significant matters, effectively escalate material risks and represent the Legal function in senior business discussions.

 Required Qualifications:

 Juris Doctor (J.D.) or equivalent law degree and admission or eligibility to practice law in an applicable jurisdiction.
 At least 10 years of post-qualification legal experience, preferably including significant experience advising financial institutions, financial technology companies or other businesses serving the banking sector.
 Significant experience drafting and negotiating complex technology, software, cloud or services agreements with large banks or other sophisticated financial institutions.
 Strong understanding of the legal and regulatory environment in which banks operate, including experience addressing regulatory requirements that affect technology vendors and service providers to financial institutions.
 Demonstrated ability to advise senior business leaders and product, sales and technology teams on complex commercial and legal matters and to translate legal requirements into pragmatic business solutions.
 Strong commercial judgment and proven ability to balance legal risk, regulatory expectations and business objectives.
 Excellent communication, influencing and negotiation skills, with the ability to operate effectively across functions and with senior stakeholders.
 Demonstrated ability to work independently, prioritize competing matters and exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced, global business environment.

 Preferred Qualifications:

 Experience advising banks, financial institutions, financial technology companies or technology providers serving regulated financial institutions.
 Knowledge of anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, financial crime prevention, sanctions, fraud prevention or related banking laws and regulatory frameworks.
 Experience advising on technology products used for anti-money laundering, fraud detection, financial crime management, compliance or risk management.
 Knowledge of legal and regulatory issues relating to artificial intelligence, including AI regulation, governance, data use, intellectual property, contracting and allocation of risk associated with AI-enabled products.
 Demonstrated proficiency in using AI tools in legal practice, including for legal research, contract analysis, drafting, knowledge management or other legal workflows, together with sound judgment regarding appropriate governance and validation of AI-assisted work.
 Experience supporting products throughout their lifecycle, including product development, commercialization, contracting and ongoing regulatory or customer requirements.
 Experience with large or Tier 1 banking clients and the heightened regulatory, outsourcing, operational resilience, cybersecurity, audit and risk-management requirements applicable to their technology providers.
 Experience working in a global organization and collaborating across jurisdictions and multidisciplinary teams.

 This position provides an opportunity to play a senior role in supporting Verafin's continued growth and innovation while helping Nasdaq deliver trusted technology solutions to banks and financial institutions globally.

 Come as You Are 

 Nasdaq is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and identities.

 We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diverse perspectives, experiences, and identities are valued and celebrated.

 We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodation throughout the hiring process.

 What We Offer 

 We’re proud to offer a competitive rewards package that is meaningful, recognizes the unique needs of our employees and their families and incentivizes employees for their contribution to Nasdaq’s overall success.

The base pay range for this role is $161,000 - $225,000. In addition to base salary, Nasdaq provides a generous annual bonus/commission (short-term incentive), and equity (long-term incentive), comprehensive benefits, and opportunity for growth. Exact compensation may vary based on several job-related factors that are unique to each candidate, including but not limited to: skill set, experience, education/training, business needs and market demands.

jobs.title: Director – Enterprise Risk Management
jobs.description:
About Us
 Nasdaq (Nasdaq: NDAQ ) is a leading global provider of trading, clearing, exchange technology, listing, information and public company services. Through its diverse portfolio of solutions, Nasdaq enables customers to plan, optimize and execute their business vision with confidence, using proven technologies that provide transparency and insight for navigating today's global capital markets. As the creator of the world's first electronic stock market, its technology powers more than 100 marketplaces in 50 countries, and 1 in 10 of the world's securities transactions. Nasdaq is home to approximately 4,000 total listings with a market value of approximately $15 trillion. To learn more, visit: http://www.nasdaq.com 
 The Team
 Group Risk Management (GRM) collaborates with businesses as a trusted advisor, facilitating well-informed decisions that support Nasdaq’s strategic objectives. GRM manages and continues to enhance the Enterprise Risk Management, Internal Control, Business Continuity, Crisis Management, and Corporate Insurance frameworks and programs. These programs facilitate the identification, assessment, monitoring, and treatment and reporting of all types of risks, Nasdaq faces.
 The Position
 GRM is seeking an ERM Director supporting the Anti-Financial Crime Division’s – Verafin business.  The position will report to the GRM Head of Expert Functions and will be leading the Enterprise Risk Management initiatives for the Verafin business. The position will be responsible for assisting in the development and implementation of ERM tools, practices, and policies to analyze and report enterprise risks and specifically lead the efforts for Verafin to implement and mature Nasdaq’s risk management framework, aggregate risk information across all risk types, and report risk to Verafin’s management.

 As the ERM Director for Verafin your responsibilities will include: 
 Establish effective risk governance including board approved risk policies, risk appetite, and risk committee/forums. 
 Work closely with executive management and facilitate the creation and maintain a clearly-articulated Risk Appetite for the business, as appropriate, and, working with the management and the businesses, identify risk tolerances within which to operate.
 Serve as a risk management subject matter expert for the business. 
 Build key relationships with business unit and expert function management and serve as a trusted partner to the Verafin management team, contributing to the business unit’s strategic growth initiatives in the context of our risk frameworks.
 Transition Verafin’s risk practices to Nasdaq’s ERM programs including Risk and Control Self Assessments, Incident Reporting, Key Risk Indicators, and Issue & Action Tracking.
 Lead Risk Assessments including Risk and Control Self Assessments (RCSA), Top Risk Assessments, Project Risk Assessments, and New Product Assessments ensuring effective challenge of risk assessments and management of key risks.  Ensure consistency of approach.
 Provide objective assurance and advisory to management including identification of significant risks and risk response strategies and actions.  Analyze risks and financial implications and work with management to ensure that the level of risk remains within an acceptable level. 
 Provide and enhance risk reporting to management and relevant risk forums. 
 Ensure compliance with the Nasdaq’s Business Continuity and Crisis Management Policy including the assisting in the development of Business Continuity Plans and facilitating Crisis Management exercises.
 Serve as a risk management subject matter expert for the business and region.   Monitor industry trends and changes in the regulatory environment. 
 Build key relationships with business unit and support function management and serve as an escalation point for risk issues and support for strategy formulation.   
 Work closely with business unit and support functions to implement best practice risk management framework and risk governance that meet the needs of the businesses and expectations of key stakeholders.
 Communicate risk objectives, framework, and policies to internal and external audiences as appropriate.
 Execute risk management training and promote a pro-active risk culture.  Provide expertise and guidance on risk management concepts.
  Effectively communicate with the broader global risk team and partner with peers to ensure consistency of approach and awareness of issues, challenges, and opportunities; achieving shared goals and objectives and providing value-add to the organization. 
 Pro-actively engage Internal Audit, SOX, Compliance, Information Security, Supplier Risk Management, Business Continuity, and other assurance functions to support an integrated approach to risk management.  Share knowledge and expertise to achieve shared goals.

 Skills, Requirements, and Competencies 
 10+ years of experience in risk management, compliance, and/or audit in the financial services industry, preferably in capital markets or financial technology. 
 Preferred expertise in enterprise risk and operational risk management with familiarity of technology risk management.  Experience in implementing and supporting an integrated risk management framework in a complex organization.      
 Excellent interpersonal and oral and written communication skills.
 Strong communication, facilitation and influencing skills; able to articulate and communicate complex ideas and concepts in a clear, concise, and structured manner while anticipating questions/objectives.
 Inquisitive nature, resourcefulness, and ability to seek out information.
 High attention to detail and accuracy.
 Strong organizational skills; able to successfully multi-task and prioritize work.
 Ability to cultivate relationships and collaborate with multiple stakeholders, including business leaders, legal, internal audit, and technology.
 Demonstrated ability to develop trusted working relationships at all levels of the organization.
 Generates energy and commitment. Ability to drive results, effect/inspire change, and have a positive impact on the organization.
 Ability to act proactively and work effectively across business units, functions, and regional locations.
 Innovative, strategic thinker who can challenge the status quo through openness and without judgement.
 Ability to lead others to solve complex problems; facilitate working groups to solve issues, mitigate issues and develop solutions; evaluate operational or technological measures to assess risk and effectiveness of programs, processes and/or initiatives.
 Action and results-oriented; ability to drive results, effect change, and have a positive impact on the organization. 
 Advanced Microsoft Office skills
 Willingness and ability to travel.
 Ability to deliver as an individual contributor and work within a global team environment. 
 Experience in leading multi-disciplinary projects with complexity, driving timely and effective project execution and meeting project objectives. 
 Knowledge and experience portraying analytical information in visual ways; synthesizing and analyzing large amounts of data and information to identify risks, patterns, and trends and consider interdependencies and impact of actions.    
 Resourceful in analysis and identifying solutions to support decision-making. 
 High attention to detail and accuracy.
 Strong organizational skills; able to successfully multi-task and prioritize work.
 Ability to cultivate relationships and collaborate with multiple stakeholders including business leaders, legal, internal audit, and technology.

 Education Required: Degree qualified in relevant discipline or equivalent working experience.
 Experience Required:  At least 10 years of experience in relevant discipline.

jobs.title: Director, Public Affairs and Regional Lead
jobs.description:
About us 

 At NATIONAL, we are driven by purpose, creativity, and connection. For 50 years, our teams across Canada have been delivering strategic communications expertise that helps organizations shape conversations that matter.

 NATIONAL is seeking a senior communications leader for Newfoundland and Labrador. While this opportunity is currently posted at the Director level, we welcome interest from experienced communications professionals and seasoned executives, with level, scope, and title to be considered based on experience, capability, and market presence.

 This is a rare opportunity for someone who knows the province, understands how decisions are made, and can move confidently between public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, and marketing conversations.

 Our Newfoundland and Labrador presence is an important part of our Atlantic and national network. We work with clients across sectors, regions, and issues, helping them navigate complex environments, build trust, and communicate with clarity. With a strong local and regional foundation and access to the full strength of NATIONAL’s offices across Canada, this role offers the opportunity to help shape what comes next in one of the country’s most distinctive and strategically important markets.

 The role 

 This is a hands-on, senior market-building opportunity for someone who wants to be both strategic and practical, visible and grounded, independent and deeply connected to a national team. We are looking for an entrepreneurial leader who can help grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador while contributing to client work across Atlantic Canada and the broader NATIONAL network. Whether you’re currently living in the region, or looking to return home, the ideal candidate is deeply connected to the province. They understand the local business, political, and community landscape, and they bring the judgment, presence, and credibility to advise executives, engage stakeholders, and represent NATIONAL in the market.

 Our office is located within the Board of Trade in St. John’s, offering a strong connection to the local business community and an energizing space for client work, collaboration, and growth.

 What you will do 

 As a key member of the Atlantic and Canadian Advisory and Public Affairs practice team, you will provide senior counsel to clients navigating complex communications, public affairs, and reputational challenges. Our roster of clients are closely connected to the biggest opportunities and challenges NL is facing. You will bring a strong understanding of government, business, community, and media environments in Newfoundland and Labrador, with particular interest in sectors such as energy, defense, economic development, healthcare and other areas shaping the future of the province. Ideally, your experience and skillset can contribute to client needs outside of NL and outside of Atlantic Canada.

 You will help lead and grow client relationships, identify new opportunities, and connect clients with the right expertise from across NATIONAL. You will be expected to work independently, think strategically, and manage mandates with confidence, while also knowing when and how to bring in colleagues from other offices and practice areas.

 You will represent NATIONAL in the Newfoundland and Labrador market, helping to strengthen our visibility, relationships, and reputation. You will be comfortable in a boardroom, at a community event, in a government relations discussion, or in a marketing strategy conversation. You do not need to be a specialist in every discipline, but you should be an integrated thinker who understands how public affairs, communications, marketing, stakeholder engagement, and reputation intersect. In this role, you will be part of the broader.

 What you bring 

 You are someone excited about local and regional connectivity and are a trusted advisor with strong judgment, sound instincts, and the ability to build relationships across sectors. You are self-motivated and credible with executives, comfortable with elected officials and senior public servants, and able to speak naturally with people from a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives.

 You likely bring:

 Senior experience in public affairs, government relations, strategic communications, crisis communications, public relations, or a related professional services environment

 Strong knowledge of Newfoundland and Labrador’s political, business, community, and media landscape

 Experience or strong familiarity with sectors such as energy, defense, infrastructure, natural resources, economic development, or other regulated or high-profile industries

 The ability to lead client relationships, provide wise counsel, and manage complex mandates with limited day-to-day oversight

 A practical understanding of marketing and integrated communications, with the ability to contribute meaningfully to broader brand, reputation, and campaign conversations

 Strong writing, presentation, facilitation, and relationship-building skills

 An entrepreneurial mindset and interest in helping grow NATIONAL’s presence in Newfoundland and Labrador

 The ability to collaborate across offices, especially with Atlantic Canada, Ottawa, and other teams across the NATIONAL network

 A degree or equivalent experience in communications, public relations, political science, business, public policy, journalism, marketing, or a related field

 How you work 

 You are strategic, but not removed from the work. You can see the larger picture, identify what matters, and turn advice into action. You are calm under pressure, clear in your counsel, and comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always obvious. You have good judgement.

 You build trust easily. You are good in a room, thoughtful in your approach, and able to move between senior executives, community leaders, public officials, colleagues, and clients with confidence and respect. You are a good writer and easily adjust to different mediums and audiences. You are collaborative, but highly self-sufficient. You can build something without needing a large local team around you, and you know how to draw on the strength of a national network when clients would benefit from additional expertise.

 You are values-driven, discreet, adaptable, and committed to excellent client service.

 What we offer 

 The opportunity to help shape NATIONAL’s value as a consultancy in Newfoundland and Labrador

 A senior, market-facing role with room to grow based on experience, capability, and ambition

 A connected national platform with strong Atlantic Canadian collaboration

 Exposure to meaningful client work across public affairs, government relations, corporate communications, marketing, and reputation

 A dynamic, entrepreneurial environment with the support of one of Canada’s most respected communications consultancies

 Competitive compensation, commensurate with level and experience

 Hybrid flexibility with an expectation of meaningful presence in the St. John’s market

 A commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion in all that we do

 How to apply 

 Qualified candidates are invited to apply by submitting a resume and a brief cover letter outlining their interest in the role, connection to Newfoundland and Labrador, and relevant experience.

 NATIONAL is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Should you require accommodation during the selection process, please inform us.

 Please note that only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted. As part of our recruitment process, we use artificial intelligence tools to assist with the screening, assessment, and selection of applicants for this role. Thank you for considering a career with NATIONAL.

  

 NATIONAL Public Relations provides creative communications solutions that move people in thought and actions. We bring together a team of 300 seasoned professionals, who are committed to helping organizations of all sizes and in all sectors understand their challenges and opportunities and solve the issues they are facing. For 47 years, NATIONAL has been at the center of issues and industries that matter, leading change for today and tomorrow.

 NATIONAL is Canada’s leading public relations firm, with offices in Vancouver, Calgary, Toronto, Ottawa, Montreal, Quebec City, Saint John, Halifax and St. John’s. Its network includes Time & Space, a leader in media strategy, data analysis, planning and execution.

 NATIONAL Public Relations is an  AVENIR GLOBAL  company, the largest Canadian-owned global communications firm, ranked among the 25 largest in the world with offices in 23 locations across Canada, the U.S., Europe and the Middle East. For more information about NATIONAL, please visit our   website  or follow us on  LinkedIn  and  X.

 Click here to read our Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Regional Sales Director - GTA (Mississauga)
jobs.description:
At Neo, we stand for the 99% of Canadians—more than 30 million people who deserve reliable access to fair credit and real financial progress. Life at a high-velocity, AI-enabled fintech isn’t for everyone. We move with urgency, sweat the small edges, and build as owners rather than passengers. If you bring ambition and a relentless focus on results, you won’t just fill a role here—you’ll build a better, fairer financial future for all Canadians.
 Since our founding in 2019, Neo has gained massive traction as one of the fastest-growing fintech companies in Canada:
 #1 on Deloitte’s Technology Fast 50 for 2023, 2024, and 2025 — the first company ever to achieve a three-peat at the top!

 #1 Fastest Growing Company in Canada for 2024 by the Globe & Mail

 Top-ranked mobile apps and credit cards built to turn credit progress into financial victory

 Team of 500+ builders

 1M+ customers

 10K+ retail partners

 The Role 
 As a Regional Director of Sales at Neo Financial, you will be a pivotal leader responsible for the profitability and success of your designated region. You will directly manage and develop District Managers, ensuring their effectiveness in driving sales, achieving key performance indicators, and adhering to Neo's operational standards. Your focus will be on maximizing efficiency, optimizing Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), and fostering a high-performance sales culture within your region. This role requires a proactive individual with strong leadership, training, and analytical skills, coupled with the ability to operate independently and travel frequently within the region.

 What you'll be doing: 
 Develop and execute regional sales strategies to achieve company sales goals and drive revenue growth within the assigned region.

 Manage and mentor District Managers. Provide ongoing coaching, support, and guidance to ensure they are effectively managing their teams and achieving sales targets.

 Monitor regional sales performance, analyze data, and implement strategies to improve sales effectiveness and optimize Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) across all districts.

 Ensure District Managers are effectively recruiting, onboarding, and developing their teams, including Store Managers and sales representatives, to maximize sales potential and performance.

 Spearhead regional sales training initiatives, including the implementation of company sales programs, and ensure consistent delivery of training to District Managers and their teams.

 Ensure operational excellence and compliance with company policies and procedures across all districts within the region.

 Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between District Managers and senior sales leadership, ensuring alignment on sales goals, strategies, and initiatives.

 Identify and pursue new growth opportunities within the region, including new locations, channels, and partnerships, to expand market presence and drive revenue growth.

 Prepare and deliver regular sales reports, forecasts, and performance updates to the Senior Director of Sales, providing insights and recommendations for improvement.

 Travel within the region to support District Sales Managers, assess sales operations, and ensure the effective implementation of sales strategies and best practices.

 Who we are looking for: 
 8+ years of experience in sales management, with a proven track record of managing and developing sales teams within a growth channel.

 8+ years of experience with proven ability to drive sales growth, improve team performance, and manage profitability (P&L).

 8+ years of experience in data analysis, performance management, and sales metrics. The ideal candidate is extremely well-versed in understanding numbers, interpreting sales data, and using this information to drive strategic decision-making and improve performance.

 7+ years of experience with excellent leadership, communication, interpersonal, and negotiation skills.

 Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and thrive in a fast-paced, results-oriented environment. You must be self-motivated, highly organized, and able to effectively manage time and resources.

 Valid driver's license and willingness to travel within the region.

 Experience managing sales teams across multiple locations or districts, ideally within a similar industry (e.g., financial services, direct-to-consumer sales).

 Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Sales, Marketing, or a related field is preferred.

 Network of Sales Representatives: Possesses a strong, existing network of high-performing sales representatives suitable for representing Neo Financial.

 Proven ability to: 
 Identify, attract, and develop top-performing sales leaders and representatives within the specific province.

 Understand the unique dynamics of the provincial sales landscape, including key players, competitive trends, and customer behaviors.

 Build and leverage a strong network of professional relationships within the local business community.

 Navigate regional market challenges and opportunities to drive sales success.

 🚀 Total Rewards 
 As Neo continues to grow, we’re committed to offering a competitive, market-leading rewards program that reflects the impact our team members make. In addition to salary, our program includes equity — empowering employees to share directly in our momentum today and in the meaningful value we create for years to come.
 Salary: We provide a strong base salary aligned with market ranges, along with the flexibility to tailor your mix of cash and equity to match your longer term goals. Final compensation is based on your skills, experience, and scope. For exceptional talent, we’re prepared to go above and beyond.

 Equity Ownership (Where Eligible): At Neo, you don’t just work here, you own a piece of what we’re building. As a full-time team member, you share directly in the upside of one of Canada’s fastest-growing companies. When we win, you win — with real ownership and meaningful long-term wealth-building potential tied to our success.

 What does life as an Owner at Neo Include? 
 🇨🇦 You will redefine the financial landscape with top talent in Canada to help everyday Canadians win, and grow quickly while doing it
 📈 For eligible roles, ownership structure that enables you to share in our path to victory
 🏅Earn BIG with our short term incentive plans (STIP)
 👥 Collaborating with the brightest minds to build something meaningful, united by a shared commitment to innovation, curiosity, and excellence
 ❤️‍🩹 Flexible health benefits & life insurance
 🌴 21 Days PTO + stat holidays, and personal leave
 💪 Health & personal spending accounts
 🤑 A wide variety of discounts through our partner network
 🏠 Access to early use of products and discounts on fixed-term Neo mortgages
 👶 Parental top-up & equity vesting during long term leave
 🎉 Neo night events
 🧠 Company wide huddles, and education

 Working at Neo: 
 The people who thrive at Neo are resourceful, growth-oriented, and driven to win. We hold ourselves to high standards because we’re on a mission that matters: to build a more rewarding financial future for all Canadians. As individuals and as a team, we constantly challenge ourselves and each other to raise the bar and deliver exceptional experiences for our customers. Our commitment to customer success drives everything we do, from building world-class products to providing exceptional support at every step of their journey. If this resonates with you, keep reading. 

 We trust, respect, and support each other. This means honest conversations, constructive input, and empowering each other to move fast and think big. You’ll be surrounded by people who push you to be your best. We primarily collaborate in person across our Calgary, Winnipeg, and Toronto offices, where ideas move quickly and teams build momentum together. As we continue to scale and evolve, we’re looking for builders, innovators, and problem solvers who thrive on challenge–people who would rather blaze a trail through uncertainty than follow a well-paved path. 

 At Neo, ownership is part of how we think and operate. For select roles, equity participation reinforces that mindset by giving employees a direct stake in the company’s long-term success. Regardless of role, every team member is expected to think like an owner and make decisions that move the business forward.

 Apply with us: 
 We believe in equal opportunity and are committed to creating an inclusive climate where everyone can thrive. Customers trust us with their finances, so successful candidates for this position will be required to undergo a security screening, including a criminal records check and a credit check. 

 By continuing with your application, you agree to the Candidate Privacy Notice, which guides how we process your personal information for the purpose of your application. 

 Neo Financial leverages artificial intelligence (AI) to reinforce our candidate evaluation process, including the initial assessment of applications and screening of candidates. These tools support our recruitment team; however, all final hiring decisions are made by humans and are not based exclusively on automated processing. If you require further information regarding our data processing practices, please contact us.

 We are hiring for an open, vacant position.

jobs.title: Director, Data Domain Enablement & Delivery Lead - AIA
jobs.location: United States - New York - New York City; Europe - Any Pfizer Site; North America - Any Pfizer Site; Latin America - Any Pfizer Site
jobs.description:
All over the world, Pfizer colleagues are working together to positively impact health for everyone, everywhere. Each position at Pfizer touches and contributes to the success of our business and our world. That’s why, as one of the global leaders in the biopharmaceutical industry, Pfizer is committed to seeking out inspired new talent who share our core values and mission of making the world a healthier place.

 The Commercial AI & Data Strategy team, within the Chief Marketing Office, is responsible for developing and managing the data and data solutions that enable the U.S. Commercial business. A key priority is building AI-ready data products and agentic data operations that provide the trusted, scalable foundation for the company’s AI transformation and ultimately help accelerate innovative therapies to patients.

 The Data Domain Enablement & Delivery Lead is a senior member of the Commercial AI & Data Strategy team within Artificial Intelligence Acceleration (AIA). The role applies deep pharmaceutical sales and marketing domain expertise to help business teams, applications, analytics products, and AI-enabled solutions identify, interpret, connect, and appropriately use commercial data to solve priority business needs.

 This leader serves as the bridge between Commercial stakeholders and data, analytics, product, and engineering teams. The role ensures that business needs are translated into clear domain definitions, data requirements, relationships, rules, quality expectations, and fit-for-purpose data solutions. It guides delivery from problem definition and data discovery through implementation, adoption, and value realization, primarily supporting the U.S. Commercial business.

 The role requires extensive knowledge of pharmaceutical commercial processes, therapeutic-area go-to-market strategy, and the HCP and patient dynamics that shape how commercial data must be interpreted and applied. This includes understanding the patient journey from disease recognition and diagnosis through treatment initiation, persistence, access, and outcomes; HCP specialties, referral and treatment networks, prescribing behavior, adoption dynamics, and engagement needs; and the implications of brand strategy, indication, line of therapy, market maturity, competitive context, field deployment, channel mix, and access conditions. The leader will connect this business context to customer and healthcare professional data, affiliations and account structures, product and indication data, prescription and sales data, patient and journey data, payer and access data, field-force alignment and activity, omnichannel engagement, marketing campaigns, next-best-action use cases, performance measurement, and customer intelligence. The objective is not simply to make data available, but to ensure the right data is applied in the right commercial and therapeutic context to support sound decisions and measurable outcomes.

 The position leads colleagues and works across Commercial, analytics, digital, data, AI, and technology organizations to accelerate delivery, strengthen data understanding, improve reuse, reduce interpretation gaps, and ensure that data products and solutions generate measurable business outcomes

 Working closely with Commercial, Legal, and Privacy teams, the role will help ensure that data is used consistently with regulatory requirements and contractual rights, while enabling the business to confidently leverage data, accelerate innovation, and scale AI responsibly.

 This role will be responsible for establishing multi-functional governance disciplines and codify processes into agentic ways of working:

 Lead the Commercial data domain. Combine data expertise with therapeutic-area strategy, HCP and patient dynamics, and customer context to guide how data is defined, connected, interpreted and applied.
 Manage and develop a team of data domain colleagues. Set priorities, build their capability, and make sure the team delivers consistent domain guidance across Commercial.
 Own the process of turning business questions into fit for purpose data requirements. Specify the population, journey stage, grain, hierarchy, business rules and quality thresholds. Flag gaps, dependencies and interpretation risks early so stakeholders know what the data can and cannot support.
 Build reusable domain knowledge. Own the shared business definitions, glossaries, semantic models, taxonomies and data-product documentation that people and AI agents rely on.
 Set and make commercial data AI-ready. Supply the context, relationships, examples, rules and quality expectations that models and agents need to read the data correctly.
 Keep data use compliant. Work with governance, privacy, legal, security and data owners so every use fits the controls, contractual rights and permitted purposes.
 Enable the people who use the data. Coach business users, analysts, data scientists and application and AI teams hands-on, and run discovery and solutioning sessions that link objectives to available data products.
 Drive delivery with Product Owners. Shape roadmaps for sales, marketing, analytics and AI capabilities, turn priorities into epics and acceptance criteria, coordinate Commercial, data and technology teams, and validate that outputs match the real commercial process.

jobs.description:
All over the world, Pfizer colleagues are working together to positively impact health for everyone, everywhere. Each position at Pfizer touches and contributes to the success of our business and our world. That’s why, as one of the global leaders in the biopharmaceutical industry, Pfizer is committed to seeking out inspired new talent who share our core values and mission of making the world a healthier place.

 The Commercial AI & Data Strategy team, within the Chief Marketing Office, is responsible for developing and managing the data and data solutions that enable the U.S. Commercial business. A key priority is building AI-ready data products and agentic data operations that provide the trusted, scalable foundation for the company’s AI transformation and ultimately help accelerate innovative therapies to patients.

 The Commercial Agentic Data Stewardship Lead will lead a team that will redefine stewardship from a predominantly manual, fragmented set of activities into an AI enabled, policy controlled operating capability. The role will establish the strategy, product roadmap, operating model, and adoption approach for intelligent stewardship agents that continuously discover, classify, map, validate, reconcile, monitor, and improve commercial data, while routing material or ambiguous decisions to accountable human stewards.

 The leader will modernize stewardship across reference data management (RDM), metadata and taxonomy, data quality, hierarchy and mapping management, and market-specific commercial data processes. Scope includes product and market definitions, market hierarchies, brand-indication and brand business unit mappings, activity and account mappings, customer and contract relationships, territory alignment, secondary sales, digital HCP interactions, and other commercially critical reference and mapping domains.

 The role is accountable for making stewardship faster, more consistent, explainable, observable, and scalable. Success requires combining AI and machine learning with deterministic business rules, workflow automation, data contracts, lineage, policy guardrails, and human-in-the-loop controls so that automated actions remain traceable, reviewable, and aligned with business, legal, privacy, security, and contractual requirements.
 Working closely with Commercial, Legal, and Privacy teams, the role will help ensure that data is used consistently with regulatory requirements

 This role will be responsible for establishing multi-functional governance disciplines and codify processes into agentic ways of working:
 Set the agentic stewardship strategy. Define the target-state vision, architecture, operating model and phased roadmap for agentifying U.S. Commercial data stewardship. Automate the high-friction, high-value work first and keep clear human accountability.
 Build intelligent stewardship products. Lead the design of AI/ML agents and services that recommend or execute classification, tagging, matching, merge and survivorship decisions, hierarchy maintenance and remediation. Use them to modernize the core commercial mappings (product, brand-indication, account, customer category, contract-GPO, territory and related) with AI-assisted matching, confidence scoring and exception workflows.
 Govern with humans in the loop and policy built in. Set approval thresholds, decision rights, escalation paths, override controls and auditable review queues based on risk and confidence. Embed privacy, security, regulatory, contractual and appropriate-use guardrails so agents apply the right controls at the point of decision.
 Own the knowledge and context layer. Build and govern the glossary, ontologies, taxonomies, knowledge graphs, playbooks, historical decisions, data contracts and domain rules that let agents interpret commercial data consistently and explain their recommendations.
 Run continuous data quality and observability. Monitor for drift, duplication, broken mappings, inconsistent definitions and policy conflicts, and trigger automated remediation or steward intervention as appropriate.
 Integrate across the data and AI platform. Work with data, architecture and engineering teams to connect stewardship capabilities to MDM, RDM, catalog, quality, workflow, lineage, cloud and AI platforms through governed APIs and MCP-enabled interfaces.
 Clarify the operating model and accountability. Define enterprise, domain, regional and local stewardship roles, set reusable standards and service patterns, cut duplicated work across teams and vendors, and keep business owners accountable for definitions and decisions.
 Drive adoption, value and cross-functional leadership. Lead rollout, training and change management. Track automation rate, first-pass acceptance, exception volume, cycle time, quality gains and manual effort avoided, and monitor model and agent performance overtime. Partner with Commercial, Digital, Legal, Privacy, Compliance, Security and process owners to balance speed, responsible AI and risk.

 Professional Experience and Educational Requirements
 8+ years of multidisciplinary experience across data management, data stewardship, data governance, data quality, metadata, master/reference data, data products, analytics, AI/ML, or related disciplines, preferably within biopharmaceuticals, healthcare, or another regulated industry.
 Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred in Data or Information Management, Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, Statistics, Business, or a related discipline.
 Deep functional understanding of U.S. biopharmaceutical Commercial sales, marketing, customer engagement, customer, product, market, activity, account, affiliation, contract, territory, and sales data domains.
 Demonstrated experience simplifying and standardizing fragmented stewardship activities across business teams, markets, technology platforms, and service partners.
 Hands-on understanding of MDM, RDM, metadata management, business glossaries, taxonomies, ontologies, data catalogs, data quality, lineage, workflow, and data observability.
 Experience applying AI/ML, large language models, semantic technologies, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, anomaly detection, or intelligent automation to enterprise data-management use cases.
 Ability to define where deterministic rules, statistical models, generative AI, agentic workflows, and human review should be used, including confidence thresholds and fallback behavior.
 Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls, decision logs, explainability, model/agent monitoring, exception management, and audit-ready evidence for automated data decisions.
 Working knowledge of responsible AI, privacy, data security, contractual data rights, regulatory expectations, and policy-driven controls relevant to commercial data use.
 Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills, with the ability to make complex data and AI concepts practical for business, legal, privacy, and technical audiences.
 Demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders, navigate complex cross-functional environments, and balance business enablement, innovation, compliance, privacy, and risk.

With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
About the Team 
The Billing to Cash team supports the full customer billing-to-cash lifecycle across PointClickCare's business units, including billing, cash application, collections, escalations, account resolution, and credit risk. The team partners closely with Accounting, Treasury, Sales and GTM leadership, Finance Customer Support, and Account Services to improve Order-to-Cash effectiveness and the customer experience.
 
Position Summary:
Reporting to the Senior Director, Finance Operations, the Director of Finance, Billing to Cash leads a team of high-performing managers and individual contributors to ensure the billing-to-cash process is frictionless for customers and maximizes cash collections. This highly impactful role leads a high-volume Billing to Cash department with more than $700M in annual collections. The successful candidate will bring strong customer service and business-partner skills, leadership capability, and business acumen to support Order-to-Cash effectiveness.
 
Key Responsibilities:
Oversee the effectiveness and efficiency of billing, collections, escalation management, and account resolution across the Accounts Receivable portfolio for all business units.
Ensure the effectiveness of the cash application process to support accurate customer statements.
Identify customer payment trends and develop strategic solutions to protect revenue and support cash collection targets.
Drive collections efficiency through payment automation, including ACH adoption, and optimized billing frequency.
Leverage systems, enhance processes, and break down silos to create a best-in-class Billing to Cash team.
Develop and drive Key Performance Indicator reporting for management and internal teams to support working capital targets, including DSO and inputs to Free Cash Flow, and improve operational efficiency.
Develop and implement a customer risk management framework, policies, and procedures to maximize cash flow and minimize bad debt risk, including credit risk, bankruptcies, unclaimed property, and collateral consents.
Serve as the Finance gatekeeper for extending credit to customers with poor payment history or elevated credit risk, while partnering with Sales and Commercial teams to structure terms responsibly and unlock revenue opportunities.
Partner with Treasury to provide reliable cash flow forecasts.
Partner with controllership and revenue accounting to support timely and accurate financial reporting and period-end close.
Oversee billing validations to support invoice accuracy and timely customer delivery.
Partner with internal stakeholders to resolve upstream issues, optimize billing operations, and minimize billing issues.
Develop a high-performing, tech-forward team that can solve issues end to end and serve as subject matter experts in their areas.
Perform other duties as assigned by management to support overall team objectives.
 
Required Skills & Qualifications:
University education in a relevant discipline; Finance or Accounting preferred.
5+ years of experience leading teams of people managers.
Ability to lead a high-volume Accounts Receivable department collecting more than $500M annually.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Extensive expertise in Order-to-Cash processes and best practices.
Credit control and statutory knowledge, including Anti-Money Laundering and Escheatment.
Strong leadership skills, including team building and motivation, transformation, and organization design.
Demonstrated commitment to PointClickCare's core values: People, Passion, and Performance.
 
Preferred Experience:
Experience in the SaaS industry and with acute and/or post-acute customers.
Experience with major billing-to-cash systems and implementations.
Experience working with Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, and Customer Success teams.
M&A and integration experience.
Experience developing reporting to measure performance.
Experience deploying AI, RPA, or workflow automation tools within Finance or Order-to-Cash operations.

Reporting to the VP Total Rewards, the role executes the platform and AI strategy the pillar sets, redesigns HR workflows and AI-human handoffs ahead of the SAP SuccessFactors-to-Workday migration, and operationalizes the data governance and responsible-AI controls that make automation safe in a healthcare context. jobs.title: Strategy & Corporate Development Director (CA)
jobs.description:
At PointClickCare our mission is simple: to help providers deliver exceptional care. And that starts with our people. As a leading health tech company that’s founder-led and privately held, we empower our employees to push boundaries, innovate, and shape the future of healthcare.
 
With the largest long-term and post-acute care dataset and a Marketplace of 400+ integrated partners, our platform serves over 30,000 provider organizations, making a real difference in millions of lives. We also reinvest a significant percentage of our revenue back into research and development, ensuring our employees have the resources to innovate and make a lasting impact. Recognized by Forbes as a top private cloud company and honored as one of Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, we offer flexibility, growth opportunities, and meaningful work. 
 
At PointClickCare, we empower our people to be the architects of a smarter healthcare future; one that is human-first and accelerated by AI to create meaningful and lasting change. Employees harness AI as a catalyst for creativity, productivity, and thoughtful decision-making. By integrating AI tools into our daily workflows, collaboration is enhanced, outcomes are improved, and every team member has the proficiency to maximize their impact. It all starts with our hiring practices where we uncover AI expertise that complements our mission, and we continue to invest in training and development to nurture innovation throughout the employee journey.
 
Join us in redefining healthcare — so it doesn’t just survive, it thrives. To learn more about PointClickCare, check out Life at PointClickCare and connect with us on Glassdoor and LinkedIn.
 
 
**Travel to Office expectations**
For Remote Roles: If this role is remote, there will be in-office events that will require travel to and from the Mississauga and/or Salt Lake City office. These will include, but not limited to, onboarding, team events, semi-annual and annual team meetings.
 
For Hybrid Roles: If this role is Hybrid, there will be an expectation to reside within commutable distance to the office/location specified in the job listing. This will include, but not limited to, weekly/bi-weekly/monthly events in the office with your specific team. This is a requirement for this role.


Team Summary:
Strategy & Corporate Development is a small team that partners directly with PointClickCare’s Executive Team to decide where the company plays and how it wins over the next 3 – 5 years. This team owns the full arc from insight generation to stakeholder alignment—shaping long-range strategy and financial planning; tracking market, competitive, and regulatory shifts across long-term and post-acute care; sizing our highest-impact new growth opportunities; and deciding whether to build, buy, or partner to capture these opportunities. When the answer is buy, the same team sources, evaluates, negotiates, and closes relevant transactions (M&A, joint ventures), setting them up for successful integration and performance against underwriting theses. This is a small, but high-impact team with consistent opportunities for driving impactful decisions and meaningful senior leadership-level exposure.
 
The team operates in a hybrid model, with most roles based in Toronto and a few remote across the US, consisting of one SVP, two Directors, one Senior Manager, one Manager, and one Senior Analyst.
 
Job Summary:
As PointClickCare approaches $1 billion in ARR, ensuring the whole company aligns behind a clear, coherent strategy becomes ever more critical.
 
The Strategy & Corporate Development Director leads enterprise-level strategy initiatives that shape PointClickCare’s long-term growth agenda, portfolio priorities, and investment decisions. The Director independently frames complex and ambiguous strategic questions, integrates perspectives across end-markets and functions, and develops recommendations for the Executive Team and Board. As a strategic thought partner to the SVP, Strategy & Corporate Development, the Director leads major components of long-range and annual planning, drives alignment on enterprise priorities, and provides direction and quality oversight to other team members supporting strategic initiatives.

Job title
 Director of Program Research and Innovation
 Reporting to
 CEO
 Years of experience 
 10+ years

 Toronto, ON
 Travel required
 Up to 30%
