 Full-time

 About Raising The Village 

 Raising The Village’s mission is to build and strengthen pathways out of ultra-poverty through an approach guided by data, designed with communities, and scaled by partnerships. We work with last-mile communities to implement solutions that raise incomes, sustain impact, and chart sustainable pathways to possibility within 24 months. To date, we have supported more than two million people in Uganda, Rwanda, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, with support from our partners and our team in North America. Find out more about our programs and impact at www.raisingthevillage.org.

 Position overview 

 The Director of Program Research and Innovation leads RTV’s portfolio of implementation-embedded pilots, restricted-funded technical projects, applied experiments, RCTs, and other innovation initiatives that require clear learning ownership. This is not a purely academic research role. It is a strategic, cross-functional leadership role accountable for the full chain from project design to delivery oversight to evidence synthesis to the translation of learning into stronger program choices across RTV.

 Key responsibilities 

 Portfolio strategy & learning agenda 

 Own the end-to-end portfolio of pilots, experiments, A/B tests, RCTs, and restricted-funded technical projects with explicit learning goals. 
 Set the overall learning agenda for this portfolio, ensuring each initiative is linked to strategic questions around program enhancement, adaptation, and scale. 
 Guide the overall evaluation and learning approach for the portfolio, balancing methodological rigor with operational feasibility and decision relevance. 

 Intake, design & governance 

 Lead project intake, prioritization, and stage-gate decisions so that proposed initiatives have a clear rationale, owner, scope, and decision-use case. 
 Shape the design of pilots and experiments in partnership with Programs, Applied Learning, Venn, M&E, and technical subject matter experts. 
 Ensure each project has clear governance, workplans, risks, dependencies, decision points, measurement approaches, and reporting requirements. 

 Project oversight, insights & integration 

 Oversee the operational coordination of projects through implementation, maintaining visibility on delivery progress, tradeoffs, and escalation needs. 
 Translate findings into recommendations for program design, module refinement, scale, and future investment choices, and ensure learning is integrated back into RTV systems and guidance. 

 External engagement & team leadership 

 Lead donor and partner engagement on relevant projects, including concept refinement, progress updates, learning briefs, and final reporting.
 Build and lead a small, high-performing team and establish strong ways of working with matrixed contributors across the organization. 

 Must haves 

 Extensive experience leading applied research, innovation portfolios, learning-driven technical projects, or similar cross-functional work in international development or a related field.
 Strong grounding in evaluation methods, including experimental and non-experimental approaches, with the judgment to balance rigor, speed, and feasibility.
 Demonstrated experience managing initiatives that involve implementation teams, technical experts, data teams, and senior stakeholders.
 Strong ability to translate technical findings into practical recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.

 Strong preferences 

 Strong donor-facing communication and reporting experience.
 Strong people management, prioritization, and decision-making skills in fast-paced environments.

 What success looks like 

 RTV has a clear owner for innovation pilots and restricted technical projects.
 Cross-functional projects move with stronger discipline, visibility, and strategic coherence. 
 Restricted-funded innovation work produces credible evidence and decision-ready learning on time. 
 Learning from pilots is systematically translated into program improvements and scale decisions. 

 Working conditions 

 Hybrid work environment with a model of 3 days in office and two days remote.
 Limited international travel may be required.

 Total rewards 

 Group RRSP matching program, up to 5%.
 Medical, dental, vision, and travel insurance.
 4 weeks of vacation.

As the senior AI scientist and technical authority on our Wealth Management Data and AI team, you will decide how we solve ML and AI problems rigorously, and how we prove the results are accurate, safe and valuable to advisors and clients.

 We are looking for a deeply technical AI leader with a research-grade understanding of modern machine learning and generative AI, and a track record of turning that science into production systems at scale. You will lead and grow a team of AI scientists, ML researchers, data scientists and ML engineers, partner closely with product, technology and business leaders across Wealth Management and RBC, and work with RBC’s broader AI research community to bring frontier techniques into the hands of advisors.

 ​ What will you do? 
 Define and own the AI/ML science roadmap for Wealth Management Canada, covering generative AI, agentic systems, predictive modelling, personalization, forecasting and optimization.
 Identify where emerging research (foundation models, reasoning, retrieval, agents, multimodal, small and fine-tuned models) can create a durable advantage in wealth management, and turn it into funded, testable bets.
 Make build, buy and fine-tune decisions on models, architectures and platforms based on evidence, benchmarking and a clear view of cost, latency, risk and performance.
 Represent Wealth Management’s AI science externally and across RBC, including partnerships with research institutes, universities and technology partners.
 Provide hands-on technical leadership across the model lifecycle: problem framing, data and feature design, training, fine-tuning, prompting and orchestration, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
 Establish the standards for experimental design, offline and online evaluation, A/B testing and statistical validity, so that results are reproducible and claims are defensible.
 Build robust evaluation frameworks for LLM and agent-based systems, including accuracy, groundedness, hallucination, bias, robustness and red-teaming, tied to real advisor workflows.
 Review the technical work of scientists and engineers, coach them on research quality, and raise the bar on how models are designed, tested and explained.
 Own the scientific approach to responsible AI in a regulated environment, including explainability, fairness, privacy, safety guardrails, model risk and ongoing performance monitoring.
 Work with Model Risk, Legal, Compliance, Privacy and Technology to translate emerging regulation and internal policy into practical technical controls and validation methods.
 Communicate model capabilities, limitations and uncertainty clearly and honestly to senior leaders, regulators and non-technical stakeholders.
 Develop and retain AI scientists, researchers and ML engineers, and create a culture of curiosity, scientific debate and learning by experimentation.
 Create career paths and mentoring for technical talent, and build a strong research-to-production pipeline with engineering and product partners.
 Champion a test-and-learn approach where hypotheses, experiments and data drive decisions, and where failed experiments are shared and learned from.
 Define the data requirements AI needs to succeed, and partner with data and technology teams on high-quality domains, a consistent data dictionary and a unified client view that serve both AI and operational use cases.
 Work with product and business leaders across Global Wealth Management, WMC and RBC to translate advisor and client problems into well-posed scientific questions, and scientific results into shipped products.

 What do you need to succeed? 
 Must-have: 
 Advanced degree (Master’s required, PhD strongly preferred) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a related quantitative field;
 8+ years of experience building and applying machine learning and AI, including leading scientists or researchers in a top-tier technology company, research lab or leading financial institution;
 Deep, hands-on expertise in modern ML and generative AI, including LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agentic systems, fine-tuning and evaluation, with a strong grounding in statistics and experimental design;
 A track record of research or applied-science impact, such as peer-reviewed publications, patents, open-source contributions or production models that moved a business metric;

 Experience with responsible AI, explainability, model risk management and AI governance, ideally in a regulated industry;
 Strong leadership skills, with experience hiring, coaching and leading high-calibre scientific and engineering talent;
 Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex scientific concepts and trade-offs to executives and non-technical stakeholders;

 Understanding of the banking industry, preferably Wealth Management, is an asset.

jobs.title: VP, People
jobs.description:
Rewind is a service that protects the critical data that powers businesses of all sizes. Our focus is on backing up data that lives in the cloud - in apps like Jira, GitHub, Confluence and Shopify. We are backed by Insight Partners, Inovia, Bessemer and Atlassian Ventures and are proud to be recognized as one of Canada's 50 fastest growing technology companies ( 2023 Deloitte Fast 50 ). We invite you to read our startup story to learn where we came from and where we’re going.
 Read about our mission, story and values here.
To find out more about our perks, click here.
Some of our Blogs might help you get a better understanding of what we do here. You can find them all here.
 Thriving at Rewind: 
 We embrace the fast-paced, ever-changing nature of startup life. If you love working with speed, agility, and creativity, you’ll feel right at home here. Here's what it takes to succeed with us:
 Team-First Mentality: We put teamwork at the core of everything we do, believing that we are better when we are together. Success is shared, and when the team wins, we all win.

 Performance-Driven Mindset: We are proactive, goal-oriented, and focused on delivering tangible, high-quality results. We go beyond meeting expectations - we aim to exceed them.

 Flexible Work-Life Approach: We encourage balance and understand the need to recharge. While we stay agile for urgent needs, we make sure there's time to recover and enjoy life.

 Customer Centricity: Our commitment to customers shapes everything we do. We listen, build relationships, and innovate - from our dedicated customer support team to our engineers, everyone at our company is focused on solving problems that matter most to our users.

 Taking Initiative: We value ownership and proactive problem-solving. We encourage team members to think creatively, take ownership, and lead improvements. Your ideas and actions drive our success.

 We Make Time for Fun: We work hard and make time to enjoy the journey. It’s not just about hitting milestones—it’s about making the experience rewarding along the way.

 Rewind's mission is to help businesses protect their most valuable digital assets. As we
 continue to scale, we are building the systems, leadership capabilities, and operating practices
 that enable us to grow intentionally while maintaining our culture and values.
 The Vice President, People, leads the design and execution of people strategies and systems that scale with the business. This role ensures our people practices, leadership capabilities, and operating model enable high performance, clear accountability, and sustained growth.

 You are accountable for translating Rewind's values into durable systems, meaningful people
 metrics, and a consistent operating cadence that supports how the company attracts, develops, and retains exceptional talent. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys building structure where it matters, challenging assumptions, and building culture.

 What You'll Do 
 People Strategy & Culture Stewardship
 Set and evolve Rewind's people strategy in support of company goals, growth plans, and long-term sustainability.

 Act as a trusted advisor to the CEO and executive team on organizational health, talent risks, leadership effectiveness, and culture decisions.

 Translate Rewind's values into operating principles, decision frameworks, and leader expectations.

 Partner with leaders to maximize the effectiveness of distributed teams and leverage the benefits of hybrid work.

 Develop and implement organizational health assessments and action plans that strengthen leadership effectiveness, employee engagement, and business performance.

 People Operations & Execution
 Own the operating model of the People team, including structure, capacity,prioritization, and delivery standards.

 Design and implement people processes and operating rhythms that support effective planning, decision-making, and execution across the organization.

 Align People team priorities with company objectives and business needs.

 Establish clear forums and cadences, including talent reviews, leadership reviews, and retrospectives that connect people insights to business decisions.

 Ensure leaders across the company have clarity on expectations, accountability, and follow-through as the company scales.

 People Metrics & Organizational Insights
 Define, track, and continuously improve People team KPIs, including engagement, retention, hiring effectiveness, and performance outcomes.

 Develop and maintain dashboards and reporting that connect people metrics to business outcomes and provide actionable insights to leaders and the executive team.

 Use people data and operational insights to inform discussions regarding organizational capacity, productivity, workforce planning, and organizational health.

 Provide strategic recommendations and action plans based on trends and emerging risks.

 Remote-First & Distributed Work
 Own and evolve Rewind's remote and hybrid work strategy to ensure clarity, equity, and consistency across teams.

 Design systems and norms that support strong performance, collaboration, and connection in a distributed environment.

 Regularly assess what is working, what is not, and where adjustments are needed as the company grows.

 Talent, Performance & Leadership
 Oversee talent acquisition, onboarding, performance management, learning and development, and succession planning.

 Coach leaders to be strong people managers who set clear goals, provide meaningful feedback, and hold themselves accountable.

 Support leadership development with a focus on execution, trust, and growth.

 Ensure performance management practices are consistently applied, including timely feedback, development plans, and decisive action when expectations are not met.

 Mergers, Acquisitions & Organizational Change
 Lead HR due diligence activities for mergers, acquisitions, and strategic transactions.

 Develop and execute people integration strategies, including organization design, change management, communications, and talent retention plans.

 Partner with business leaders to ensure seamless organizational transitions and achievement of business objectives.

 Employee Communications & Change Management
 Develop and execute the company's employee communications strategy and annual communications plan.

 Draft and oversee executive and organizational communications that support change initiatives, reinforce company values, and strengthen employee engagement.

 Ensure consistent, transparent, and timely communication during periods of growth and transformation.

 This role is open for candidate located in Ontario. 

 What You'll Bring 
 Proven experience in a senior people leadership role (VP or Senior Director level) in a scaling technology or SaaS organization that is PE or VC backed.

 Demonstrated success building and scaling people functions and operating models.

 Have built the People function, rather than inheriting a mature one

 Experience in a Canadian or cross-border (Canada and US) workforce

 Strong business acumen with the ability to connect people strategies to business outcomes.

 Demonstrated expertise in organizational design, change management, and organizational effectiveness.

 Experience leading M&A due diligence and post-acquisition integration.

 Experience supporting remote and distributed teams.

 Exceptional communication, influencing, and relationship-building skills.

 Sound judgment and the ability to navigate complex people and organizational situations.

 A pragmatic, hands-on approach and the ability to balance strategic thinking with operational execution.

 Compensation Philosophy 
The actual base salary will vary based on various factors, including market and individual qualifications objectively assessed during the interview process. 
 In some cases, we’re open to hiring at a higher level for the right person and are committed to paying competitively and fairly.
 If your experience is closer to an earlier career stage, we may still consider your application. In that case, we would evaluate the role at a different level within our levelling framework.
 Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at Rewind.

 Why join Rewind 
 At Rewind, you’ll help shape the future of data protection for thousands of businesses. We’re performance-driven, innovative, and not afraid to challenge what’s possible. You’ll join a team that values trust, accountability, and respect for people’s time — and encourages every employee to experiment, think critically, and grow.
 We support innovation through experimentation — including smart use of AI tools — and believe the best ideas come from those who aren’t afraid to push boundaries.

 How Rewind Will Support You 
We know that enjoying the journey is just as important as reaching our goals. We work hard to create a positive, inclusive environment where fun and laughter are part of our everyday routine. We also offer a variety of benefits to support your success both at work and in your personal life which includes but is not limited to: 
 Flexible work hours

 Employee stock options

 Health benefits

 3 weeks vacation

 7 life leave days

 2 Level Up days for professional development

 1 volunteer day

 Summer Fridays and office closed during the holiday break in December

 Paid parental leave

 $2000/year wellness/home office allowance

 $5000/year professional development allowance

 Rewind is committed to building an inclusive, supportive place for you to do the best and most rewarding work of your career. We value how each new hire is an opportunity for us to bring in a different perspective, and we are always eager to further diversify our company. We strongly encourage candidates of all different backgrounds and identities to apply.

 AI Usage 
 Our recruitment process may include the use of artificial intelligence–enabled tools to help manage and review applications efficiently. These tools assist our team, but hiring decisions are ultimately made by human reviewers.

jobs.description:
Location: This role can be based anywhere in Canada (excluding Quebec) as a fully remote position. For candidates located in the Vancouver, BC Lower Mainland, there is flexibility to work remote, hybrid, or onsite at our Surrey headquarters. This role is also open to candidates in the USA as a fully remote position.

 Please note that employment is contingent upon the successful completion of reference checks and background checks.

Safe Software is looking for a VP, Revenue Operations to join our Revenue Operations team. As VP, Revenue Operations, you will design and enforce the operating model our entire go-to-market organization runs on, reporting directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and presenting regularly to the board. This is a builder’s mandate: the CRM isn’t fully configured, the forecasting process is mostly informal, the Rules of Engagement are still being written, and the AI tooling stack is unevaluated. You’re not fixing a broken system — you’re building the one Safe’s revenue org will run on for years. We have an immediate opening and are excited to find the right candidate to join our team. 

 About The Team 
 As a part of the Revenue Operations team, you’ll build and lead a function that’s still taking shape — RevOps analysts, a Sales Enablement team, and a broader GTM Enablement capability, five to seven hires in total. Safe builds FME, the only All-Data, Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform, trusted by 25,000+ enterprise customers in 125+ countries to bring their data to life. Profitable, growing, and scaling toward $250M ARR with a clear path to $700M, Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound and outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, and Canada — and it needs a single operating authority to keep those motions from colliding. That’s this role. You’ll report to the CRO and work daily with VP Sales East, VP Sales West, and the EMEA leader, each of whom has strong opinions and moves fast.

 What You’ll Be Doing 
 As VP, Revenue Operations, you will operate at all altitudes — one week presenting forecast accuracy to the board, the next telling a VP Sales their deal doesn’t meet the bar to advance stage, regardless of how the conversation started. Both are the job.

 Rules of Engagement — Ownership & Accountability 
 Write the rules everyone will actually operate inside. Safe is building a multi-motion revenue engine — direct field, inbound BDR, outbound BDR, partner channel, EMEA, Canada — and without clearly defined and enforced Rules of Engagement, those motions conflict, accounts get double-touched, partners get burned, and trust between functions collapses. You write it, socialize it across every stakeholder (including strong-willed VP Sales leaders who will push back), get it approved by the CRO, and enforce it through process design and CRM configuration.

 Define territory and account ownership. Who owns what account, what happens at renewal, how partner and direct conflict is resolved, and what triggers an escalation to the CRO.

 Set lead routing and BDR handoff standards. How inbound and outbound leads are qualified, assigned, accepted, and rejected, with SLA definitions for each stage and accountability for every gate.

 Design the partner co-sell and channel conflict policy. Clear rules for when the partner leads, when direct leads, and how sourcing credit is allocated, reviewed and agreed with the Partner Leader and EMEA Leader at launch.

 Hold the qualification gates. Define MEDDPICC field requirements by stage, what must be true before a deal advances, and what RevOps will kick back regardless of who is asking.

 GTM Enablement 
 Close the ramp gap. At Safe’s current hiring pace across AEs, BDRs, SEs, CSMs, and partners, the difference between a 30-day ramp and a 90-day ramp is a material revenue number — this role owns closing that gap.

 Build the function, not just the content. The Sales Enablement team reports directly into this role. You’ll build it, hire against a capability scorecard, and hold the team accountable to ramp and productivity outcomes, not just content creation.

 Design role-based onboarding. Structured, milestone-gated onboarding tracks for every GTM role — AE, BDR, SE, CSM, and partner — with clear ready-to-carry-quota certification criteria and a defined ramp timeline per role.

 Own the sales methodology and playbook. The single source of truth for how Safe sells — pitch structure, discovery framework, objection handling, competitive positioning, and deal execution standards — updated quarterly with input from the field and calibrated against win/loss data.

 Turn Gong data into a coaching loop. Use Gong and other tooling to create a systematic feedback loop from deal recordings and call reviews to enablement content updates, so the playbook reflects what actually wins, not what the last training deck said.

 Revenue Architecture & AI-Native GTM Stack 
 Give the CRO one version of the truth. Build the weekly, monthly, and quarterly forecasting process — call accuracy, coverage ratios, deal velocity — so the CRO walks into every board meeting with zero surprises.

 Own the numbers that matter. Pipeline model, funnel metrics, win-rate analytics, rep productivity, CAC payback, and NRR by segment and vertical, owned by you, trusted by the board.

 Evaluate and integrate the AI-native GTM stack. CRM (HubSpot), conversation intelligence (Gong), outbound automation, intent data, and agentic AI workflows — owning use-case prioritization, adoption, and value realization across the revenue org. AI architecture, security review, and governance decisions are made in partnership with IT and Engineering.

 Enforce data governance with teeth. Own the data model in CRM, ensuring field hygiene, account hierarchy, and MEDDPICC field consistency across every pod, globally.

 Executive Leadership & Cross-Functional Authority 
 Earn credibility through data, not hierarchy. Working with high-performing, highly opinionated VP Sales leaders is a feature of this role, not a bug — you’ll push back on a VP Sales who wants to move a deal to the wrong stage, enforce an ROE that a regional leader finds inconvenient, and do it in a way that preserves the relationship.

 Present to the board and hold up under questioning. You’ll present pipeline health, forecast accuracy, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to Safe’s board — output that’s clear, accurate, and defensible, from someone who can handle hard questions from investors without flinching.

 Own the cross-functional cadence. Finance, Marketing, CS, Product, and Legal all have legitimate interests in how the GTM org operates — you mediate those interests and own the QBRs, planning cycles, and headcount models that keep the org moving in the same direction.

 Leadership & Impact 
 This is single-threaded ownership of the operating system, not a shared function. You set the Rules of Engagement, own the forecasting methodology, and hold budget and vendor authority over the RevOps and Enablement tooling stack. When a VP Sales and the model disagree, the model doesn’t move without your sign-off — and you carry that authority directly to the CRO and, on a regular cadence, to the board.
 The board stops asking why the number moved. Forecast accuracy becomes predictable enough that variance is the exception the CRO has to explain, not the norm.

 The rules hold under pressure. Rules of Engagement survive contact with a strong-willed VP Sales who wants an exception — and when they don’t, that’s a deliberate call you made, not a gap they found.

 RevOps becomes a real team. What starts as a single-person mandate becomes a functioning function of RevOps, Enablement, and analytics talent that other departments route through by default.

 GTM tooling delivers measurable outcomes. AI and automation investments are evaluated against clear success criteria — rep productivity, pipeline data quality, forecast accuracy, and adoption rates — before scaling. Pilots that don't meet the bar are discontinued; those that do are operationalized.

 Qualifications, Skills, and Competencies 
 Safers come from a variety of backgrounds with a diversity in skills and knowledge. That said, we find that those who are most successful in this role have experience with the following areas.
 Required skills: 
 10–15+ years in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, or GTM Strategy at a scaling B2B SaaS company, at VP or Senior Director level with direct board-level exposure

 Experience building and enforcing a Rules of Engagement framework across multiple GTM motions, including the hard conversations with sales leaders who push back

 A track record presenting pipeline health, forecast, and GTM efficiency metrics directly to a board or equivalent investor group

 Experience holding strong field sales leaders accountable through data and rigor rather than hierarchy

 People leadership experience — hiring, developing, and holding accountable a multi-functional team spanning RevOps analysts and sales enablement

 Ownership of the full RevOps stack — CRM architecture, forecasting model, territory design, quota mechanics, and tooling evaluation

 Strong analytical range: comfortable building a bottoms-up coverage model, explaining CAC payback to a CFO, and translating rep-level data into a board-ready narrative

 Hands-on experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying agentic workflows or AI-assisted tooling in a live GTM environment — including the ability to assess feasibility, data readiness, and security requirements before committing to production

 Deep HubSpot or Salesforce architecture experience, including data model and process enforcement design

 Effective communication skills

 Desired skills / Bonus points: 
 Background in data, infrastructure, or integration software

 Experience with MCP, Salesforce Agentforce, Clay, or similar agentic GTM infrastructure at production scale

 Experience navigating a PE-backed or founder-owned growth inflection from $100M to $250M+

 Familiarity with partner channel economics and co-sell Rules of Engagement design

 Experience building a RevOps function from solo operator to a team of 3–5

 A Bachelor’s degree in a related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience

 About Safe Software 
 Safe Software transforms organizations with FME, the only All-Data Any-AI Enterprise Integration Platform connecting all your data, anywhere, at any velocity. 
 With over 30 years of expertise and 25,000+ enterprise customers across 125+ countries, we simplify your data journey, wherever it leads.
 Founded in 1993, Safe is headquartered in Surrey, BC with over 300 team members and counting. We’re always looking for talented individuals with diverse backgrounds who are determined to learn and grow. Are you ready to join the team?

 Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion 
 Safe Software is an equal opportunity employer and we truly believe that innovation and strength begin with diversity and inclusion. 
 We welcome all candidates regardless of race, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, ability, disability, national or ethnic origin, political belief, religion, or family status. 
 Should you require accommodations during the recruitment process, please contact hr_dept@safe.com.

 Notice Regarding Use of Automated Tools in Hiring 
 At Safe Software, we use automated tools to help us process applications and identify qualified candidates. These tools may assist in screening resumes and summarizing interview content based on the information you provide. This helps our team review applications efficiently while ensuring every candidate is considered based on the requirements of the role.
 Please be assured that the final hiring decision is always made by a member of our team. For more information on how we protect your privacy, please see our policy. If you have questions about this process, please contact us at hr_dept@safe.com.

jobs.description:
Lab Summary: 

 Samsung Research America (SRA) develops next-generation technologies in software, user experience, and services for future products. Headquartered in Silicon Valley with locations across North America, we partner with industry and academia to translate research and innovation into tangible outcomes. We lead in machine intelligence by building AI that is user-centric and physically grounded—AI that understands not just what users want, but their physical context and environment.

 Samsung is uniquely positioned to bring this vision to life through nearly 500 million connected devices we sell annually. Our mission is to holistically integrate AI into connected ecosystems—homes, offices, robotics, and beyond—creating a platform that scales quickly while providing deep contextual understanding and spatial awareness.

   The AI Center in Toronto, Canada plays a pivotal role in developing next-generation software, user experiences, and intelligent services that enrich consumers’ lives. This lab actively contributes to the international research community through publications and presentations at major conferences.

   Areas of Research: 

 Computer Vision

 Contextual/Multi-Modal Modeling

 3D Perception & Scene Understanding

 Inference and Reasoning

 Machine and Deep Learning

 Human Computer Interaction (HCI)

 Natural Language Processing

 Position Summary: 

 Samsung’s AI research team in Toronto is looking for an outstanding and highly self-motivated leader to head the lab. The candidates should have extensive expertise in deep learning, computer vision and physics-based AI.

 The AI research center is a key part of Samsung’s global R&D effort and aims to have direct impact on future Samsung products reaching hundreds of millions of users globally. The candidate will work with a team of research scientists and engineers tackling real-world problems involving Samsung’s Artificial intelligence products. The candidate can also have the opportunity to publish at top-tier conferences in deep learning, computer vision, and language understanding.

 Position Responsibilities: 

 Build, manage, develop, lead, and support the AI research team, with the outcome of high-impact research insights that influence the product roadmap

 Present research findings and insights both within and outside of the company

 Serve as a thought partner with the executive, cross-functional, and line of business leadership teams

 Be an evangelist of research practices throughout the company, influencing partner teams

 Drive innovation programs within the relevant fields of Artificial Intelligence,

 Serve as the external face for the AI Research Lab’s advanced technology capabilities

 Drive key University technology collaboration program to build long term innovation partnerships

 Lead Technology Pathfinding to understand key technology trends and impact for Samsung, to help drive growth and new business opportunities for Samsung

   Required Skills: 

 PhD in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or equivalent combination of education, training, and experience

 10+ years of post-PhD experience leading advanced AI research.

 Deep expertise in vision and multimodal AI and agentic AI (autonomous agents, reasoning, decision-making), plus strong foundations in computer vision, image/video processing, and generative AI applications.

 Significant experience of publishing relevant peer-reviewed articles on artificial intelligence

 Strong algorithmic problem-solving skills, and the ability to program in C/C++, Python, Java, etc.

 Experience in publishing scientific papers in top quality conferences/journals (CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, IJCAI, ACL, SIGGRAPH, CoRL, etc.)

 Experience in DL library such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, etc. with strong hands on experience is required

 Experience working with GPU, parallel programming, and Simulation environments is a plus

 Experience in Android development and graphic rendering is a plus

 Ability to work as a team, motivation for international collaboration, strong communication skills, self-motivated, proactive, flexible and passionate about learning

 Ability to work well in a fast-paced global team environment

 Strong network of relationships with entrepreneurs, VC’s industry executives, and technology thought leaders

 Strong presentation skills and excellent interpersonal skills

 Additional Information 

 Disclosure of Trade Secrets 

 Samsung has a strict policy on trade secrets. In applying to Samsung and progressing through the recruitment process, you must not disclose any trade secrets of a current or previous employer.

 Essential Job Functions 

 This position will be performed in an office setting. The position will require the incumbent to sit and stand at a desk, communicate in person and by telephone, and frequently operate standard office equipment, such as telephones and computers.

 Samsung Research America is committed to complying with all Federal, State and local laws related to the employment of qualified individuals with disabilities. If you are an individual with a disability and would like to request a reasonable accommodation as part of the employment selection process, please contact the recruiter or email sratalent@samsung.com. 

 Equal Employment Opportunity 

 At Samsung, we believe that innovation and growth are driven by an inclusive culture and a diverse workforce. We aim to create a global team where everyone belongs and has equal opportunities, inspiring our talent to be their true selves. Together, we are building a better tomorrow for our customers, partners, and communities.

 Samsung Research America is committed to employing a diverse workforce, and  provide Equal Employment Opportunity for all individuals regardless of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a protected veteran, genetic information, status as a qualified individual with a disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description:
Scribd, Inc. is on a mission to advance human understanding. Our four products — Scribd®, Slideshare®, Everand™, and Fable — help billions of people across the globe move beyond access and into insight, application, and expertise.

 Culture at Scribd, Inc. 
 We support a culture where our employees can be real and be bold; where we debate and commit as we embrace plot twists; and where every employee is empowered to take action as we prioritize the customer.

 We believe the best work happens when individual flexibility is balanced with meaningful community connection. Scribd Flex empowers employees to choose the workstyle and location that support their best performance, while committing to intentional in-person moments that strengthen collaboration and culture. Occasional in-person attendance is required for all Scribd, Inc. employees, regardless of location.

 So what are we looking for in new team members? At Scribd, Inc., we hire for “GRIT.” Traditionally defined as the intersection of passion and perseverance toward long-term goals, GRIT reflects the mindset we expect from every employee. For us, it also serves as a practical framework for how we work: setting and achieving Goals, delivering Results within your role, contributing Innovative ideas and solutions, and strengthening the broader Team through collaboration and attitude.

 This posting reflects an approved, open position within the organization.

 The Team 
 Data & Analytics is building the DNA of an AI native Scribd, Inc. Bringing together Analytics Engineering, Data Science, and Data Analytics, D&A partners across product, technology, content, and the business to scale intelligence, advance understanding, shape strategy, and turn insight into lasting growth across our four brand portfolio.
 Making this ambition real at scale starts with Analytics Engineering. The team transforms fragmented data, inconsistent definitions, and dispersed analytical knowledge into trusted, reusable, production quality data foundations and products that enable intelligence to scale across the company.
 In partnership with Engineering, Analytics Engineers ensure critical data is captured, centralized, documented, secured, and governed. The team builds canonical datasets, shared metrics, and semantic layers, together with the quality, observability, lineage, and evaluation systems that make these assets trustworthy. On top of this foundation, Analytics Engineers develop AI agents and analytical tools that bring reliable intelligence directly into the decisions and workflows of teams across the company.

 The Role 
 We’re hiring for a Director, Analytics Engineering to own scaling data for an AI native Scribd, Inc. You will build, scale, and lead a high performing Analytics Engineering team, turning strong individual contributors into a cohesive and highly effective team. This requires more than hiring and developing exceptional talent. It means establishing an operating model that creates structure without unnecessary bureaucracy, fostering culture and community that balances local priorities with the broader success of the company, and creating the technical foundations and standards of excellence that enable everyone to do their best work. 

Your leadership philosophy is grounded in service. A leader’s role is to provide clarity, create context, remove obstacles, and help others succeed. You will strengthen team dynamics, ensure great work is recognized, create meaningful career pathways, and help individuals navigate obstacles and opportunities throughout their careers. Durable teams are built by distributing ownership, developing leaders, and creating an environment where people feel trusted, supported, and accountable.
 Your pragmatic approach keeps the organization moving forward. Rather than waiting for an ideal end state, you will think in sequences and ask, “What is the right next version?” Communication happens early and often because transparency, thoughtful feedback, and visible decision making build trust and help teams move with confidence.
 Your strong strategic judgment is paired with enough proximity to the work to guide technical decisions credibly. You will connect analytics engineering investments to company priorities, communicate tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders, and contribute thoughtfully to decisions about data modeling, architecture, governance, quality, tooling, and developer experience.
 The transformation happening through AI is an opportunity to expand what talented teams can accomplish. Agentic coding, AI assisted development and analysis, and automated workflows can increase human judgment, creativity, and impact rather than replace them. You approach these technologies with curiosity and pragmatism, applying them where they create clear and measurable value.
 Above all, leadership is about building people and strengthening the discipline they share. Success is reflected in a team that grows more capable, confident, connected, and effective because of your leadership.

 The Essentials 
 10+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, business intelligence engineering or a related discipline, including 5+ years leading and developing technical teams

 Proven track record of building, scaling, and leading high performing teams, turning strong individual contributors into cohesive and highly effective teams that are valued as strategic partners

 Depth in building governed, canonical data models and semantic layers, giving core business concepts one authoritative, discoverable definition instead of letting teams reconcile competing sources

 Experience designing the data quality, observability, documentation, governance, access control, privacy, lineage, and evaluation systems that ensure data and AI products are reliable, explainable, trustworthy, and safe to operate at scale

 Advanced SQL skills and production experience with modern data stack, including AWS, Databricks, Airbyte, Fivetran, Looker, or comparable platforms

 Demonstrated ability to lead cross functional data initiatives from strategy through production adoption and measurable business impact

 Strong judgment in balancing immediate stakeholder needs with long term investments in reusable data products, platform health, and technical debt reduction

 Excellent written and verbal communication with technical teams, business stakeholders, and senior executives

 The Nice to Haves 
 Advanced Python

 Experience leading data cleanup efforts and implementing role based access controls and data retention policies to improve data quality, security, and governance

 Experience designing and building canonical data models and semantic layers that support financial analysis at scale

 Experience leading on call rotations, coordinating incident response, resolving production issues, and driving follow up improvements that strengthen system reliability

 -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

 At Scribd, Inc., your base pay is one part of your total compensation package and is determined within a range. Our pay ranges are based on the local cost of labor benchmarks for each specific role, level, and geographic location. San Francisco is our highest geographic market in the United States.

 In the state of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $202,500 [minimum salary in our lowest geographic market within California] to $268,000 [maximum salary in our highest geographic market within California].

 In the United States, outside of California, the reasonably expected salary range is between $191,500 [minimum salary in our lowest US geographic market outside of California] to $254,000 [maximum salary in our highest US geographic market outside of California].

 In Canada, the reasonably expected salary range is between $177,000 CAD[minimum salary in our lowest geographic market] to $235,000 CAD[maximum salary in our highest geographic market].

 We carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including but not limited to experience; job-related skill sets; relevant education or training; and other business and organizational needs. The salary range listed is for the level at which this job has been scoped. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for a competitive equity ownership, and a comprehensive and generous benefits package.

 Working at Scribd, Inc. 
 Are you currently based in a location where Scribd, Inc. can employ you? 
Employees must have their primary residence in or near one of the following cities. This includes surrounding metro areas or locations within a typical commuting distance:

 United States: 
 Atlanta | Austin | Boston | Dallas | Denver | Chicago | Houston | Jacksonville | Los Angeles | Miami | New York City | Phoenix | Portland | Sacramento | Salt Lake City | San Diego | San Francisco | Seattle | Washington D.C.

 Canada: 
 Ottawa | Toronto | Vancouver

 Mexico: 
 Mexico City

 Benefits at Scribd, Inc. 
 Scribd Flex (flexible work model)

 Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage

 Sierra is the leading platform for customer-facing AI agents, working with many of the world's biggest brands — including The GAP, Rocket Mortgage, SoFi, Sutter Health, and SoftBank — to transform how they serve customers and grow their businesses. We are primarily an in-person company based in San Francisco, with growing offices across North America, Europe, and Asia.
 We are guided by a set of values that are at the core of our actions and define our culture: Trust, Customer Obsession, Craftsmanship, Intensity, and a commitment to balancing Family along the way. These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.
 Sierra was co-founded by Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor who first met while working together at Google over 20 years ago. Bret currently serves as Chairman of the Board of Open AI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce and CTO of Facebook. Clay spent 18 years at Google, where he most recently led Google Labs.
 What you'll do 
 Architect Sierra's most complex deals: Lead our largest multi-BU, multi-geo opportunities, designing sophisticated deal structures and managing risk with precision and conviction.

 Operate as part of the customer's team: Hold trusted relationships across the customer C-suite and working teams.

 Engage at the founder level: Be trusted to regularly engage and manage Sierra's co-founders in front of customers, pitching with co-founder-like conviction and expertise.

 Bring precision to everything: Operate with exacting craft in messaging, positioning, and timing across every interaction.

 Shape strategy: Influence how Sierra approaches its most important accounts and set the standard for the broader sales org.

 Operate as an AI-native seller: Leverage AI tools across the full sales cycle- account research, personalized outreach, call summarization, pipeline forecasting, and deal execution- to automate low-value tasks and reinvest that time into high-value customer relationships, while continuously adopting and experimenting with new tools to work faster and smarter than traditional methods allow.

 What you'll bring 
 10-12+ years of enterprise/strategic sales experience, owning the largest and most complex accounts.

 Demonstrated success closing multi-million-dollar, multi-stakeholder deals spanning business units and geographies.

 Experience managing a $1M+ quota and running end-to-end complex 6- and 7-figure ACV deals.

 Deep, sustained C-suite relationships and the gravitas to be treated as a peer by executive buyers.

 Mastery of complex deal structuring, risk navigation, and pricing.

 Exceptional executive communication and a reputation for precision and trust.

 Even better... 
 Deep familiarity with the AI landscape and the ability to speak credibly to technical and business stakeholders alike.

 Experience operating alongside founders/executives in front of strategic customers.

 Experience building GTM strategies: Building sales teams and sales motions from scratch, or from early stage growth.

 Our values 
 Trust: We do the right thing, even when no one is looking, and even when it’s hard. When we screw up, we take accountability, fully and completely. We act in such a way that if all of our actions were completely visible to our customers, we would be proud.

 Customer Obsession: Our entire business is designed to ensure every agent built on Sierra succeeds, and that we are accountable to our customers and their success. We do whatever it takes to make our customers successful, and we go the extra mile in how we show up as a partner with unreasonable hospitality.

 Craftsmanship: A great company is the aggregation of thousands of things done well. As they say, “how you do anything is how you do everything”. Most important is craftsmanship in building agents that are so great that people thank them at the end of a call. That’s the standard.

 Intensity: We operate with urgency, and we want to win. We are never complacent. We fight to win every deal, big or small, using the full force of the company. And when we fail, we talk about it openly and without blame so we succeed the next time.

 Family: We know that balance and intensity are compatible, and we model it in our actions and processes. We work hard, and turn on the afterburners when needed. But we pick up our parents at the airport when they’re visiting from out of town. We go to our kids’ events. And we show up for one another, in moments of celebration and hardship.

 What we offer 
 We want our benefits to reflect our values and offer the following to full-time employees:
 Flexible (unlimited) paid time off

 Medical, dental, and vision benefits for you and your family

 Life insurance and disability benefits

 Retirement plan dependent on country of employment

 Parental leave

 Fertility and family building benefits

 Lunch, as well as delicious snacks and coffee to keep you energized when working onsite

 Discretionary benefit stipend giving people the ability to spend where it matters most

 Free alphorn lessons

 These benefits are further detailed in Sierra's policies, may vary by region and employment type, and are subject to change at any time, consistent with the terms of any applicable compensation or benefits plans. Eligible full-time employees can participate in Sierra's equity plans subject to the terms of the applicable plans and policies.
 Be you, with us 
 We're working to bring the transformative power of AI to every organization in the world. To do so, it is important to us that the diversity of our employees represents the diversity of our customers. We believe that our work and culture are better when we encourage, support, and respect different skills and experiences represented within our team. We encourage you to apply through the link on this page even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description.
 Sierra is a proud equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws, including veteran status and disability status. Hiring decisions are made by people, based on merit. If you need a reasonable accommodation for a disability, a religious practice, pregnancy or any related condition at any point in the application or interview process, contact us at accommodations@sierra.ai. Requests are handled confidentially and do not affect your candidacy.
 We will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with applicable fair chance laws.

 The incumbent will drive HR programs and insights that are aligned to business and HR outcomes with impact across Actuarial, Risk, and Asset Liability Management (ARALM or “Risk”) and Sunlife Asset Management (SLAM).  You will bring pragmatic, data-driven perspectives and solutions-orientation to initiatives and outcomes and participate as a member of Risk Leadership Team and Enterprise Functions (EF) HR leadership teams.  This role leads, inspires, and develops BOLDER HR professionals operating in a team environment that embodies our values.

 Please note his is a hybrid role requiring regular presence at our Toronto One York office.

 What will you do: 

 Strategic Partnership: Collaborates with leadership, and Business Group HR teams, to develop business strategies and align people strategies to drive organizational success. Articulates annual SMART goals and outcomes the team can deliver to drive achievement of business objectives. Challenges the status quo, including with focus on speed of decision making and digital, innovative thinking.  Seeks to understand business/function opportunities and obstacles and strives to be in front of the business partnering on people & talent changes.  Supports prioritization and makes decisions to focus on highest impact work, including identifying work that (whilst potentially a good idea) is not a current priority.  Drives achievement of ambitious goals through test & learn, measurement, refinement, and holding others accountable, as needed.

 Trusted Advisor: Partners directly with senior executives to provide coaching, consulting, solutions and constructive challenge, where appropriate.  Builds strong, open relationships.  Provides proactive advice using data, insights and analytics, creating a compelling business case to inform business and talent decision making now and for the future.  Coaches team members to build trusted advisor capability with leaders, and global partners.

 HR Outcomes: Helps shape and lead execution of strategic people initiatives, which include transformation, workforce planning, culture management, change management, and organizational effectiveness.  Engages and co-creates solutions with HR colleagues (Centres of Expertise, People Services and HRBPs) to solve business issues and optimize the employee experience.  Builds knowledge of HR, technology and industry trends to advance employee capability, develop and attract talent for the future.  Ensures effective organization and work design, strategic workforce plans including supporting strategies to build a robust leadership pipeline, and actions for an inclusive, inspired workforce with confidence in their careers at Sun Life.  Encourages performance excellence, providing honest, actionable, and timely feedback as well as recognition.  Leads delivery of key HR initiatives in Talent Acquisition, Talent Development, Succession, Engagement, Performance, and Compensation and ensures effective governance.

 Transformation and Digital Innovation: Leads in the people requirements within transformational initiatives, ensuring the people strategy is integrated in the business transformation plans. Embraces and promotes the use of technology, including AI and digital tools, to enhance HR processes, employee experience, productivity, and careers.  Fosters a digital mindset and supports the development of digital skills across the organization. Operates with curiosity and openness in how AI-enabled tools can evolve the work of the HR function, capturing efficiencies and driving more focus on outcomes and impact.

 Mindset: Possesses a learning and growth mindset with willingness to challenge the status quo, try new things, test & learn and empower others to do the same, innovate and find new solutions that solve business problems or create business value.
 Data and Measurement Focus: Grounds decisions in facts, leverages data to generate new insights and opportunities, clearly defines and measures business outcomes to identify course corrections and measure success.  Informs strategies and decisions through knowledge of current external research and trends.  Encourages action based on best data available versus defaulting to comprehensive analyses.

 Job Description: 
 About the role: 
The AVP, Security Architecture is a senior leader accountable for the enterprise security architecture strategy, governance, and evolution of security capabilities across global business and technology environments. 
The role translates business priorities, cyber risk appetite, and emerging threats into architecture direction that protects clients, employees, information, and critical services.

Working closely with the CISO, CTO, enterprise architects, and business technology leaders, the AVP leads the Security Architecture function and embeds secure-by-design, Zero Trust, and defense-in-depth principles into enterprise transformation and solution delivery.

The AVP serves as a senior security design authority within enterprise architecture governance, shapes security investment priorities, and develops a team that provides consistent architectural guidance across business units and geographies.

 What You Will Do?
Key Responsibilities:

 1. Enterprise Security Architecture Strategy and Road mapping 
 Own the enterprise security architecture strategy and target state across identity, cloud, infrastructure, networks, endpoints, applications, data, and security platforms.
 Establish multi-year security capability roadmaps aligned with business priorities, enterprise architecture, the cybersecurity strategy, and organizational risk appetite.
 Translate capability assessments, threat trends, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework into prioritized architecture improvements, with Zero Trust and defense in depth guiding modernization.

 2. Security Architecture Function and People Leadership 
 Lead and develop the Security Architecture team, with accountability for performance, coaching, succession planning, and the skills required to support enterprise priorities.
 Define the function's operating model, engagement processes, and service expectations, providing architecture coverage across security programs and business-led technology initiatives.
 Prioritize demand and allocate capacity across strategic planning, project assurance, governance, and emerging technology work; establish coverage and knowledge-sharing practices that reduce dependence on individual specialists.
 Manage the function's operating plan, assigned budget, and resources, and build business cases for additional capacity or specialist support.

 3. Architecture Governance and Design Authority 
 Establish security reference architectures, standards, reusable patterns, and guardrails in partnership with global domain architects and enterprise security policy owners.
 Serve as senior security design authority for significant initiatives within the enterprise architecture governance process, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
 Represent Security Architecture on enterprise technology review boards, resolve cross-domain design issues, and oversee design assurance against approved security requirements.
 Oversee recommendations for architectural exceptions, compensating controls, and remediation plans; escalate material residual risks to accountable business and risk owners through established governance.

 4. Secure Solution Design and Transformation Oversight 
 Provide security architecture oversight for major business and technology initiatives from early planning through implementation, with review effort proportionate to risk and complexity.
 Embed threat modelling, secure design reviews, and reusable security patterns into delivery practices, partnering with application, data, infrastructure, cloud, and engineering teams.
 Lead architectural direction for security transformation programs, including identity modernization, cloud security, network segmentation, application security, data protection, and cyber recovery.

 5. Security Capability Portfolio and Investment Leadership 
 Direct the strategic evolution, integration, consolidation, and retirement of security tools, services, and capabilities to address enterprise needs and reduce fragmentation.
 Shape investment priorities and present business cases that assess risk reduction, control coverage, technical feasibility, interoperability, operational capacity, and total cost of ownership.
 Maintain an enterprise view of capability gaps, overlapping technologies, lifecycle risks, and technical debt; partner with engineering, operations, procurement, and vendor management to turn roadmaps into achievable investment and delivery plans.

 6. Technology Evaluation and AI Security 
 Evaluate emerging security technologies, vendor capabilities, and service models, providing recommendations on suitability, integration, scalability, and long-term viability.
 Sponsor proofs of concept with clear success criteria for security effectiveness, technical compatibility, operational readiness, and business value.
 Define security architecture requirements and patterns for AI platforms, generative AI, and autonomous agents, addressing identity, data access, tool permissions, monitoring, and human oversight.
 Identify opportunities to use automation and AI within security capabilities, working with responsible teams to validate benefits, control effectiveness, and operational accountability.

 7. Architectural Risk and Resilience 
 Identify systemic security architecture weaknesses and drive mitigation roadmaps with accountable engineering, platform, and business technology owners.
 Translate security, privacy, regulatory, and data residency requirements into architecture requirements in partnership with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, and Legal.
 Integrate requirements for resilience, ransomware containment, recovery, logging, and monitoring into security designs, working with operational owners to establish implementation and validation expectations.
 Use findings from incidents, security testing, audits, and control assessments to improve reference architectures, patterns, and capability roadmaps.

 8. Executive Engagement and Enterprise Partnership 
 Act as a trusted advisor to the Global Chief Enterprise Architect, CISO, CTO, CIO, and business technology leaders on security architecture strategy and significant technology decisions.
 Translate complex architecture choices into clear business implications, investment options, delivery dependencies, and risk treatment recommendations for executive forums.
 Build alignment across global business units and technology functions, resolve competing priorities, and report on architecture coverage, adoption, roadmap progress, and outcomes.

 What Do You Need to Succeed? 
 Qualifications Required: 
 University degree or college diploma in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
 15+ years of progressive experience in cybersecurity architecture, engineering, or related technology leadership roles, including accountability for enterprise security architecture strategy.
 Demonstrated experience leading and developing architecture or security teams, managing priorities and resources, and delivering outcomes in a complex, matrixed organization.
 Experience influencing VP and SVP stakeholders and presenting architecture strategies, investment recommendations, and risk decisions at executive forums.
 Strong knowledge across identity and access management, cloud, infrastructure, network, endpoint, application, API, and data security, including cryptography and secrets management.
 Demonstrated ability to establish enterprise architecture standards, reference patterns, governance processes, and multi-year security capability roadmaps.
 Practical understanding of Zero Trust, defense in depth, threat modelling, secure development, and frameworks such as the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.
 Experience modernizing security platforms and evaluating vendors or third-party services for technical feasibility, integration, control effectiveness, and total cost of ownership.
 Excellent communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with the judgment to balance security, business value, delivery constraints, and operational sustainability.

 Preferred skills: 
 Experience in financial services or another regulated industry with global operations and complex privacy or data residency requirements.
 Experience with hybrid and multi-cloud environments, including AWS, Azure, or Alibaba Cloud.
 Experience defining security architectures for AI, autonomous agents, automation, or other emerging technologies.
 Experience with major security transformations, technology rationalization, or mergers and acquisitions integration.
 Relevant professional certifications, such as CISSP, CISM, SABSA, TOGAF, or cloud security and architecture certifications.

 Key Outcomes and Measures of Success: 
 Enterprise direction: Approved security target states and prioritized roadmaps aligned with business needs and the cybersecurity strategy.
 Architecture coverage: Timely engagement on significant initiatives across business units, with consistent service coverage and review turnaround.
 Secure delivery: Greater use of approved patterns and earlier resolution of design weaknesses, reducing avoidable rework and exceptions.
 Risk treatment: Progress against remediation plans for material architectural weaknesses and timely escalation of unresolved risks.
 Portfolio effectiveness: Reduced capability duplication and technical debt, supported by documented control improvements and lifecycle cost benefits.
 Team capability: Improved skills, succession readiness, knowledge sharing, and capacity to support strategic and delivery priorities.
 Executive confidence: Clear investment recommendations, transparent reporting, and alignment among security, enterprise architecture, and business leaders.

 Unique Requirements: 
 As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide.

 What’s in it for you? 
 Being a member of the Sun Life family, a group of people united by our Purpose: to help Clients and Employees achieve lifetime financial security and live healthier lives. 
 An environment of continuous learning, development, and improvement. 
 As a hybrid organization, you and your leader use business and Client need to choose where you work, at home or in the office.

 What will you do?

 Shape, communicate, and align the digital technology strategy across   business units, ensuring it supports near-term delivery commitments and longer-term modernization objectives.   

 Partner with Business Leads, Product, Client Experience, Architecture, Cybersecurity, Operations, and Enterprise Technology to define platform roadmaps, OKRs, sequencing, and investment priorities.   

 Provide thought leadership on the evolution of shared digital platforms, including identity, web, mobile, integration, data enablement, and reusable digital capabilities.

 2. Platform Delivery & Execution

 Serve as the primary escalation point for platform, delivery, vendor, and dependency-related issues, enabling rapid resolution in a complex environment.   

 Ensure delivery is integrated across product, architecture,   engineering,   operations, cybersecurity, and business priorities.   

 Embed test-and-learn, automation, and continuous improvement practices to improve speed, quality, and sustainability.   

 3. People Leadership & Capability Development   

 Lead, mentor, and develop technology leaders and teams, fostering a collaborative, inclusive, accountable, and execution-focused culture.   

 Design and optimize team structures to support   clear   ownership, delivery outcomes, modernization priorities, and clear accountabilities.   

 Partner with Chapter, Engineering, Product, and Business leaders on workforce planning, role clarity, succession planning, and capability development.   

 Build internal capability in   digital   engineering,   enablement, agile delivery, vendor management, and operational excellence.   

 Coach leaders to manage performance effectively, clarify ownership, and build resilient teams through change and transformation.   

 4. Financial & Vendor Management   

 Lead budget management, including annual planning, cost tracking, capitalization, forecasting, and investment prioritization.   

 Manage strategic vendor and system integrator relationships, holding partners accountable for delivery quality, outcomes, knowledge transfer, and value realization.   

 Drive cost transparency and technology spend optimization across applications, infrastructure, security, vendor, and platform investments.   

 Identify opportunities to reduce long-term dependency on external partners while strengthening internal platform ownership and capability.   

 5. Operational Excellence, Risk & Security   

 Ensure   s tability, security, technology currency, resiliency, and end-of-life decommissioning for applications within scope.   

 Establish governance processes that balance speed of delivery with risk management, audit, regulatory, cybersecurity, and control requirements.   

 Partner with   Application   Operations to ensure effective incident management, change management, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.   

 Proactively manage operational risk,   application   health, technical debt, and service reliability across shared digital capabilities.   

 6. Cross-Functional Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement   

 Act as a strategic technology partner to leaders across Product, Client Experience, Business, Operations, Architecture, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise Technology.   

 Communicate   digital   strategy, delivery status, risks, trade-offs, and dependencies with clarity and transparency.   

 Represent the Digital technology function in executive forums, bringing enterprise perspective, external insight, and pragmatic recommendations.   

 Strengthen alignment between technology investments, business priorities, Client experience outcomes, and enterprise digital strategy.   

 Accountabilities   

 Align digital strategy with business objectives, Client outcomes, enterprise standards, and shared technology priorities.   

 Define and monitor roadmaps, OKRs, modernization priorities, and delivery sequencing.   

 Oversee execution across delivery teams, vendors, system integrators, and enterprise partners.   

 Establish governance, track delivery metrics, and drive productivity, quality, and reliability improvements.   

 Manage budgets, vendor relationships, and cost optimization opportunities.   

 Build and sustain a high-performing, engaged, inclusive, and platform-oriented technology organization.   

 Ensure digital platforms are secure, scalable, resilient, reusable, and positioned to support future growth.   

 What you need to succeed? 

 Qualifications & Experience   

 Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degree or MBA is an asset.   

 10+ years of experience in senior technology leadership roles with demonstrated success delivering complex, mission-critical digital platforms.   

 Experience leading modernization and enablement of digital platforms such as identity, web, mobile, integration, or client/advisor experience platforms.   

 Proven ability to lead technology teams through transformation, platform ownership, and operating model evolution.   

 Strong financial acumen with experience managing sizable technology budgets, vendor portfolios, and total cost of ownership.   

 Strong stakeholder management, executive communication, and organizational leadership skills.   

 Experience in regulated financial services is valuable; depth in digital enablement, engineering excellence, and vendor-heavy delivery environments is prioritized.   

 As this position is posted in several locations, we specify that bilingualism (French, English, both oral and written) is required for Quebec only for the frequent interactions with English and French-speaking colleagues or internal partners across Canada or worldwide 

 Mindset & Behaviours   

 Decisive leader comfortable operating in ambiguity, complexity, and transformation.   

 Strong technical credibility with the ability to challenge architecture, delivery practices, platform decisions, and CI/CD approaches.   

 Builder mindset with equal focus on fixing, scaling, enabling, and simplifying.   

 Pragmatic, outcomes-driven decision-maker who balances speed, stability, risk, and long-term   application   health.
