jobs.description:
Job Description:  
 CLUB CADDIE
 Every course, one move ahead
 Head of Enterprise Sales (MCO)
 Sales & Marketing  |  Reports to: President/Chief Revenue Officer  |  Travel: ~50%  |  Full-Time

 ABOUT CLUB CADDIE
 Club Caddie is a fast-growing golf course management software (GMS) company and a member of the Jonas Software family, a division of Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU). Our platform is the operating system for golf — unifying point of sale, tee sheet, member management, food and beverage, and payments into a single connected system for public, semi-private, and multi-course operators.
 We are built by operators, for operators, and our brand is anchored in four commitments: Unified Operations, Intelligent Action, Revenue Momentum, and Hospitality Memory. As Club Caddie scales its footprint with the country's largest multi-course operators (MCOs), we're investing in the enterprise sales leadership to match that ambition.

 THE ROLE
 The Head of Enterprise Sales owns Club Caddie's go-to-market motion for Multi-Course Operators (MCO) — management companies and ownership groups operating multiple golf facilities across the country. This is a hunting, value-building, and relationship-building role for a seasoned enterprise sales leader who knows how to navigate long, complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and close large agreements.
 You will report directly to the Chief Revenue Officer and work in close partnership with Marketing, Product, Implementation, and Customer Experience to build a durable pipeline of MCO logos, from first conversation through signed agreement and a clean handoff to post-sales. The base salary range for this role is between $110,000 - $120,000. 

 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 Own the MCO Sales Motion
 Build and execute a strategic account plan targeting the top multi-course operators in the U.S. and Canada, prioritizing accounts by fit, size, and strategic value.
 Manage a complex, multi-stakeholder sales pipeline in the CRM with rigor — accurate staging, next steps, forecasted close dates, and clear next steps on every opportunity.
 Lead the full sales cycle: prospecting, discovery, solution design, ROI/business case development, procurement, contracting, and close through an enterprise level sales methodology.
 Build Executive Relationships
 Develop value-based relationships with C-suite and operations leaders (CEO, COO, VP of Golf Operations, CIO) at management companies and ownership groups.
 Represent Club Caddie at industry events — NGCOA, the MCO Retreat (MCOR), and other regional and national golf industry gatherings — to build pipeline and deepen existing relationships.
 Act as a trusted advisor, bringing a point of view on how technology can solve real operational and financial challenges across a multi-course portfolio.
 Negotiate and Close Complex Deals
 Lead commercial negotiations on multi-year, multi-property agreements, balancing win rate, margin, and long-term account health.
 Partner with Finance, Legal, and Implementation to structure deals that are commercially sound and operationally deliverable.
 Manage competitive displacement deals against incumbent point-of-sale and tee sheet providers with a clear, defensible value narrative.
 Drive Cross-Functional Alignment
 Partner with Marketing and the Director of Digital on MCO-specific campaigns, collateral, and messaging that support the pipeline.
 Work closely with the Executive, Product, Customer Experience, and Sales teams to translate enterprise buyer feedback into product improvements, market awareness, and competitor insights.
 Ensure a clean, well-documented handoff from sales to implementation for every closed account, protecting the customer experience from contract to go-live.
 Forecasting & Performance 
 Own MCO segment forecasting and pipeline reporting, contributing accurate inputs to company-wide revenue scorecards and QBRs.
 Track and report on key metrics: pipeline coverage, deal velocity, win rate, average contract value, and sales cycle length.
 Manage deals through a formal sales methodology e.g. MEDDIC, MEDDPIC, etc… to ensure internal and external alignment.
 Continuously refine MCO sales playbooks, pricing strategy, and competitive positioning based on what's working in the field.
 Achieve or exceed the annual targets for MCO sales including new logo and back-to-base revenue targets.

 WHAT YOU BRING
 7+ years of enterprise or complex B2B sales experience, with a track record of closing large, multi-stakeholder agreements; SaaS, hospitality, or golf/club industry experience strongly preferred.
 Demonstrated success selling into complex organizations with long sales cycles and layered decision-making (procurement, ops, IT, finance, executive) leveraging enterprise sales methodologies. 
 Previous success creating value and desire across an entire organization including decision makers and deal champions.
 Strong commercial negotiation skills, with experience structuring multi-year, enterprise-wide contracts.
 Exceptional value-building instincts — comfortable and credible in a room with C-suite executives and front-line operators alike.
 Highly organized and data-driven; disciplined about CRM hygiene, pipeline accuracy, and forecasting.
 Willingness and ability to travel approximately 50% of the time for industry events, on-site customer meetings, and prospect visits.
 Self-directed and resilient — comfortable building a territory and a pipeline largely from the ground up.
 Genuine interest in or connection to the golf industry is a strong plus, but not required.

 WHY JOIN CLUB CADDIE
 Own a high-impact, high-visibility segment of the business, with a direct line to the CRO and executive team.
 Sell a genuinely differentiated, unified platform into an industry that is actively consolidating around modern technology.
 Competitive base plus uncapped commission, benefits, and the backing of Jonas Software and Constellation Software's scale and stability.
 Be part of shaping the next chapter of Club Caddie's MCO strategy, not just executing an existing playbook.

 Club Caddie is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

 Business Unit:

jobs.title: VP, Marketing
jobs.description:
Job Description:  
 About Computrition 

 Computrition, Inc. is a leading provider of enterprise foodservice, nutrition management, and retail technology, trusted by hundreds of organizations across North America, including healthcare systems, military installations, correctional facilities, and higher education institutions. For more than 44 years, we’ve built technology in partnership with our customers, helping them improve operational efficiency, strengthen financial performance, and deliver better nutritional care.

 We’re investing in the future of our platform by adopting modern technologies and working closely with customers to solve complex operational challenges. Our solutions have real-world impact by driving performance enhancement and show up directly in how hospitals, military installations, and other institutions operate every day.

 Computrition offers the stability of an established industry leader and the momentum of a company accelerating growth through innovation. We invest in our people and foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous learning, and professional growth where employees can make a meaningful impact. You’ll join experienced professionals who are passionate about solving meaningful problems and delivering measurable outcomes for customers.

 With team members across the U.S. and Canada, and as part of a growing portfolio of technology companies owned by Constellation Software Inc. (TSX: CSU.TO), we are well-positioned to continue advancing the future of foodservice and nutrition technology.

 If you’re looking to build technology that makes a meaningful impact while growing your career with a stable, innovative company, we’d like to hear from you.

 The role 
 VP, Marketing owns how Computrition is understood in the market and how that understanding turns into pipeline, revenue and retention. This is a player-coach role: you set direction and personally build a meaningful share of the work.

 Reports to: President and CEO 
 Location: Fully remote, United States 
 Travel: Up to 25 percent: industry conferences, customer visits, company events 

 You will work hand in hand with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Operations, and you are expected to know our products well enough to demo them and explain their business impact to a buyer.

 What you will deliver in your first 90 days 
 Baseline metrics: a marketing scorecard with current funnel performance and a first report of marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline 
 Team alignment: match each team member's strengths to our growth initiatives, so their skills are applied where they create the most impact 
 Spend review: a review of marketing vendors and tools, with savings identified 
 Agreed priorities: Marketing's priorities validated with each department leader 

 What you will deliver in your first 12 months 
 A marketing plan and scorecard: an annual plan and budget with an investment case per program, and a monthly scorecard tying marketing activity to pipeline, bookings and retention. 
 Attributed pipeline: agreed marketing-sourced and marketing-influenced pipeline targets with Sales, reported monthly from our marketing automation platform and Salesforce. 
 A refreshed brand and website: a brand refresh and a rebuilt website, delivered on time and on budget. 
 Sales-ready materials: a current, consistent library of product, ROI and competitive materials that Sales and Customer Success actually use. 
 Events with measured return: every major conference run against meeting, pipeline and cost targets, with a post-event ROI report. 
 Customer proof: at least 10 quantified customer stories and an active reference program. 
 Higher output with AI: measurably more content and campaign throughput from the same team. 

 What you will own 
 Growth engine and measurement 
 Own Marketing's operating system: annual plan, budget, vendor management, and a weekly and monthly operating rhythm 
 Build and run the marketing scorecard, with leading and lagging KPIs and targets 
 Own attribution across our marketing automation platform and Salesforce, lead scoring, lead handoff to Sales, and data quality 
 Report Marketing's performance in executive and quarterly business reviews 
 Rationalize the marketing technology stack and vendor spend, and keep every marketing account and asset under company ownership 
 Agree Marketing's priorities and service levels with each department every quarter 
 Revenue support: new business and existing customers 
 Run campaigns and account-based programs that create qualified pipeline for new-business sales 
 Run expansion, adoption and retention programs with Customer Success for the installed base 
 Turn Product's value model into seller-ready business-case tools, and maintain a database of customer outcomes that proves value delivered 
 Maintain a proposal and RFP content library, including support for public-sector and government responses 
 Run win/loss analysis and feed the findings to Sales, Product and messaging 
 Product and sales marketing 
 Partner with Product on positioning, naming, packaging input and launch readiness for new products and releases 
 Produce and maintain product sheets, presentations, demo stories, case studies and competitive battlecards 
 Govern messaging so every customer-facing asset is consistent and current 
 Run co-marketing with technology and channel partners 
 Events: in person and virtual 
 Build the annual event calendar with an investment case and ROI target for each event 
 Run national and regional conferences end to end: pre-booked meetings, booth, customer receptions, follow-up and ROI reporting 
 Run webinars, virtual events and our customer user conference 
 Support internal company events, including our annual employee conference 
 Brand and communications 
 Lead the brand refresh and protect brand standards across every channel 
 Own social media strategy, PR, thought leadership, industry awards and customer recognition programs 
 Keep our external profiles (directories, analyst and data sites) accurate 
 Support employer branding and the careers page for recruiting 
 Website and digital 
 Lead the website refresh and own the site's performance: traffic, conversion and lead quality 
 Own SEO and visibility in AI search tools 
 Run the customer newsletter and email programs 
 Internal communications 
 Own the company intranet and its content 
 Produce the company-wide leadership newsletter and internal announcements 
 Run customer surveys through one tool and one intake process, so results are coordinated and acted on 
 Market sensing 
 Turn Product-led competitive and market insights into battlecards, messaging and sales enablement 
 Produce intelligence reports from every major conference 
 With Product and Sales, define ideal customer profiles and segments across healthcare, military, corrections and higher education 
 Bring the voice of the customer into product and pricing decisions 
 AI-enabled marketing 
 Lead AI adoption across the team: AI-first workflows for research, content, campaigns, personalization and reporting 
 Build and deploy practical AI tools and agents, including automation inside our marketing automation platform and CRM 
 Set quality, brand-safety and data-privacy standards for AI-generated content 
 Measure and report the productivity and performance gains AI delivers 
 Grow our visibility in AI search and answer engines 
 What you bring 
 7+ years of B2B marketing in software or technology 
 Proof of delivered results: pipeline, revenue, conversion or retention gains you can quantify and attribute to your own work, and strategic initiatives you took from plan to completion 
 Demand generation and attribution: you have personally built demand programs and pipeline attribution in a marketing automation platform and Salesforce, or comparable platforms 
 Hands-on execution: you personally write, build campaigns, run the marketing automation platform and analyze the data, rather than only directing agencies or delegating 
 Decisiveness: you bring recommendations backed by numbers and own decisions within your authority 
 Deep product fluency: you have learned complex enterprise software well enough to demo it and model the ROI it creates for customers 
 AI literacy in practice: you use generative AI tools daily in production work, have built or deployed AI workflows or agents, and can show measurable gains in speed, quality or results 
 Transformation experience: you have led a brand refresh, a repositioning, a major launch or a rebuild of a marketing function 
 Event ROI: you have run conferences as measured investments, not just logistics 
 Tools: a marketing automation platform, Salesforce (or comparable CRM), a website CMS, web and campaign analytics 
 Remote collaboration: you drive cross-functional work effectively across locations and time zones 
 Preferred 
 Prior experience managing a marketing team 
 Experience marketing both on-premise and cloud software 
 Healthcare technology, healthcare foodservice or clinical nutrition background; a registered dietitian credential or close work with dietitians is a strong plus 
 Marketing to health systems, government or military buyers through long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles 
 Experience in a private equity-backed or holding-company software environment 
 Internal communications experience alongside external marketing 

 How to apply and compensation 
 With your resume, please include: 
 A one-page summary of two or three results you personally drove, with the numbers 
 One sample of work you created yourself (a campaign, page, deck or content piece) 
 A short description of an AI workflow you use in your marketing work today 
 After applying online, also send your resume, with attachments to careers@computrition.com 

 Finalists will prepare a marketing plan from a case study we provide, present it live, and meet with Product and Sales leaders. 

 Compensation: base salary of $115,000 to $140,000, depending on experience, plus an annual performance bonus and benefits. Final title depends on experience. 

 Computrition is an equal opportunity employer.

Job Description:  
 Job Title: President, BEC Legal Systems
 Location:  Remote Canada or USA
 Reports To:  Group Leader

 Company Overview 
 Jonas Software, a subsidiary of  Constellation Software Inc.  (TSX: CSU), is a global acquirer and operator of  vertical market software companies. We acquire, strengthen, and grow exceptional businesses, empowering them to lead within their specialized industries. Being one of the largest groups within Jonas, we are looking for a strategic leader to help us scale.

 About the Role 
 We are seeking a high-impact  President to lead our  BEC Legal Systems software business, a key player in delivering innovative, mission-critical technology to legal professionals and organizations. As President, you will take full ownership of the  P&L, define and execute the strategic direction, and lead a high-performing team to ensure continued growth, customer satisfaction, and long-term market leadership.
 This is a pivotal role for an experienced and entrepreneurial leader who combines operational excellence, business acumen, and a passion for building great teams and products. The ideal candidate will bring a strong understanding of B2B SaaS or Legal Tech and have the leadership skills to drive performance across product, sales, customer success, and operations.

 Key Responsibilities 
 P&L Ownership & Business Performance: 
Take full accountability for the business unit’s financial health, growth, profitability, and operational execution.

 Team Leadership & Culture Building: 
Lead, inspire, and develop a cross-functional team across product, sales, marketing, support, and operations. Champion a strong performance culture and succession planning.
 Customer-Centric Growth: 
Deepen customer relationships, ensure high retention and satisfaction, and shape the product roadmap to meet evolving legal industry needs.
 Operational Excellence: 
Streamline and scale operational processes to support growth while maintaining a high-quality customer and employee experience.

 Proven experience in a senior leadership role with full P&L responsibility, ideally in B2B SaaS or Legal Tech.

 Strong leadership skills with the ability to recruit, retain, and develop top talent.

 Why Jonas Software?

 Shape the long-term strategy and make a visible difference to customers and the legal profession.

Work Location: 
Toronto, Ontario, Canada 
 Hours: 
37.5 
 Line of Business: 
Business Management, Strategy & Support 
 Pay Details: 
$160,000 - $200,000 CAD 

This role is eligible for a discretionary variable compensation award that considers business and individual performance. 
 TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role. The base pay actually offered may vary based upon the candidate's skills and experience, job-related knowledge, geographic location, and other specific business and organizational needs.

 As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

 Job Description: 
 Department Overview

 Global Technology & Solutions (GTS) enables the Bank’s strategy by delivering enterprise technology that supports clients and colleagues, protecting TD through strong fraud, cyber, technology, and physical security controls, enabling agility in response to evolving client needs and market dynamics, and supporting the delivery and execution of work across the organization. GTS is central to how TD modernizes, innovates, manages risk, and delivers secure, reliable, and differentiated experiences.

 Team Overview

 The GTS Strategy and Insights team helps shape where GTS goes next—and how we tell that story. We support GTS’ most senior technology leader and leadership team by developing fact-based analysis, executive-ready narratives, presentations, memos, and insights that help drive alignment and support decision-making for audiences including the Chief Executive Officer, the Senior Executive Leadership team, and the Board of Directors.

 The AVP - GTS Strategy and Insights will lead a team responsible for executive deliverables, strategic planning, enterprise and industry research, executive communications, and performance reporting against GTS priorities. The team sits same organization as Change Management, Communications, and Colleague Engagement, creating strong alignment between strategy, messaging, adoption, and colleague experience to ensure priorities are translated into clear narratives, practical change plans, and measurable business outcomes.

 Job Description

 Reporting to the Head, Strategy and Insights, Product Owner & Analyst Practices the successful candidate will lead the GTS Strategy function and will be accountable for influencing and shaping Senior Executive and Board-level content while overseeing the team’s day-to-day operations and delivery of high-quality analysis, insights, and strategic materials.
 This role is ideal for someone who can operate at the intersection of strategy, technology, and communication—understanding complex technology and business issues, identifying what matters, and translating that thinking into clear recommendations and executive-ready narratives.

 Key accountabilities include: 

 Lead all strategy-related deliverables required through enterprise processes or as directed by ESVP Global Technology and Solutions, ensuring each is grounded in evidence, aligned to GTS priorities, and positioned to support executive decisions.
 Lead the development, planning and communication of strategic narratives, insights, and recommendations that influence Executive and Board discussions, build alignment, and advance GTS' strategic priorities (e.g., Executive level presentations, memos, briefings and other materials for GTS Senior Leadership, Board, and/or Governance forums).
 Set the standard for clear, fact-based, outcome-oriented materials that simplify complex technology, workforce, financial, cyber, data, artificial intelligence, delivery, and regulatory topics for senior executive audiences.
 Responsible for leading the development and refresh of GTS’ short, medium, and long-term strategy, and priorities, translating strategic direction into actionable focus areas, investment ideas, and measurable outcomes.
 Develop insights on strategic issues facing GTS, including technology modernization, software delivery, artificial intelligence adoption, workforce transformation, productivity, cyber resilience, data and cloud, cost management, and regulatory priorities.
 Serve as GTS’ technology research lead by continuously drawing on external sources, including articles, books, podcasts, research, industry forums, and expert perspectives—to proactively identify leading-edge insights from across the technology and financial services landscape, raise critical awareness, and translate relevant insights into strategic deliverables, team priorities, and investment choices.
 Own performance reporting and executive insights for GTS priorities, ensuring timely, accurate, and data-driven assessment of strategic, transformation, financial, workforce, and operational outcomes to support informed decision-making and accountability.
 Drive alignment on GTS strategic priorities by influencing senior stakeholders, resolving cross-functional dependencies, surfacing risks and opportunities, and providing actionable recommendations that support executive decisions and drive measurable business outcomes.
 Lead the Strategy & Insights function, establishing priorities, allocating resources, managing strategic risks and dependencies, and ensuring successful delivery of key commitments.
 Lead, coach, and develop a high performing of team of strategy and insight specialists while fostering an inclusive and collaborative culture.

 Job Requirements

 Required: 

 Demonstrated ability to influence Senior Executives and support complex strategic decisions.
 Experience translating industry trends and external research into strategic recommendations and business outcomes for SVP+ level audiences.
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and strategic thinking capabilities.
 Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including development of executive and Board-level materials.
 Strong business acumen and understanding of technology's role in driving enterprise outcomes.
 Proven ability to synthesize complex technical, financial, and strategic information into clear, compelling messages for senior executive and Board level audiences.
 Strong understanding of technology transformation, software delivery, artificial intelligence-enabled ways of working, data, cyber, cloud, infrastructure, digital tools, and the role of technology in enabling business strategy.
 Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, workback plans, and senior stakeholder expectations in a fast-paced and ambiguous environment.
 Exceptional relationship-building, collaboration, and influencing skills, with a proven ability to align diverse stakeholders, build trusted partnerships, and drive outcomes across functions and leadership levels. Strong business acumen, with the ability to connect technology priorities to enterprise strategy, customer outcomes, colleague outcomes, risk, and financial performance.
 Experience leading teams and building high-performing, inclusive cultures.

 Preferred: 

 Experience in software engineering, technology delivery, technology strategy, architecture, product, data, cyber, or a related discipline.
 Consulting experience, particularly in strategic messaging, executive communications, technology strategy, or enterprise transformation.
 Experience supporting the Chief Executive Officer, senior executive leadership team, Board of Directors, or equivalent senior governance forums.
 Demonstrated strategic curiosity and insight, leveraging external trends, competitive intelligence, and emerging technologies to challenge thinking, shape priorities and inform GTS strategy and decision-making.
 Proven experience translating market, competitive, and technology insights into strategic recommendations that inform investment decisions, transformation priorities, and operating model evolution.

 Additional Information

 This role offers the opportunity to work directly on the strategic agenda for a large, complex technology organization; influence executive and Board-level materials; lead a small, high-performing team; and help GTS make clearer choices about where to focus time, talent, and resources.

 Who We Are: 
 TD is one of the world's leading global financial institutions and is the fifth largest bank in North America by branches/stores. Every day, we strive to make every interaction, product, and experience remarkably human and refreshingly simple for over 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States and around the world. More than 95,000 TD colleagues bring their skills, talent, and creativity to foster deeper relationships, ensure disciplined execution, and build a simpler, faster banking experience. TD is deeply committed to being a leader in client experience, that is why we believe that all colleagues, no matter where they work, are client facing. Together, we are reimagining what banking can be for our clients, colleagues and communities. 

 Our Total Rewards Package 
Our Total Rewards package reflects the investments we make in our colleagues to help them and their families achieve their financial, physical, and mental well-being goals. Total Rewards at TD includes a base salary, variable compensation, and several other key plans such as health and well-being benefits, savings and retirement programs, paid time off, banking benefits and discounts, career development, and reward and recognition programs. Learn more 

 Additional Information: 
We’re delighted that you’re considering building a career with TD. Through regular development conversations, training programs, and a competitive benefits plan, we’re committed to providing the support our colleagues need to thrive both at work and at home.

 Please be advised that this job opportunity is subject to provincial regulation for employment purposes. It is imperative to acknowledge that each province or territory within the jurisdiction of Canada may have its own set of regulations, requirements.

 Colleague Development 
 If you’re interested in a specific career path or are looking to build certain skills, we want to help you succeed. You’ll have regular career, development, and performance conversations with your manager, as well as access to an online learning platform and a variety of mentoring programs to help you unlock future opportunities.

 If you’re passionate about helping clients and building deep, lasting relationships, TD offers diverse career paths where you can grow your expertise and make a meaningful impact.  

 We're committed to your success and foster a respectful workplace where diverse perspectives are valued, everyone has fair opportunities to grow, and you can unlock your full potential to achieve your career goals. Here at TD, we hire and develop the best.

 Training & Onboarding 
We will provide training and onboarding sessions to ensure that you’ve got everything you need to succeed in your new role.

 TD is committed to providing fair and equitable compensation opportunities to all colleagues. Growth opportunities and skill development are defining features of the colleague experience at TD. Our compensation policies and practices have been designed to allow colleagues to progress through the salary range over time as they progress in their role.  As a candidate, you are encouraged to ask compensation related questions and have an open dialogue with your recruiter who can provide you more specific details for this role.

 Job Description: 
 Department Overview 

 Wealth Compliance provides independent oversight, guidance, and effective challenge to support the identification and management of regulatory compliance and conduct risk across TD Wealth.
 Working collaboratively with business, Legal, Risk, Governance and Control, Technology, Operations, and other partners, Wealth Compliance supports regulatory compliance, sound risk-based decision-making, and a strong culture of compliance.

 Job Description 

 Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer of TD Waterhouse Canada Inc. (CCO), who also serves as Associate Vice President, Compliance, the Head of Wealth Compliance Strategy, Emerging Risks & Transformation leads priority initiatives within the CCO’s mandate. The role translates emerging risks and regulatory developments into decision-ready advice and leads cross-functional change to strengthen the Compliance program.
 The role operates within the CCO’s mandate for TD Waterhouse Canada Inc., engaging across businesses, legal entities, and enterprise functions on assigned matters. Its priorities include strategy and emerging risk, transformation and remediation, and improvements to Compliance governance, processes, controls, reporting, data, technology, and operating practices.
 Operating with a high degree of autonomy within delegated authority, the Head advises the CCO and other senior leaders, provides objective analysis and effective challenge, and builds alignment across organizational boundaries. The role leads assigned initiatives from assessment through implementation and transition to ongoing operating ownership, with a focus on proportionate, risk-based outcomes.

 Key Accountabilities 

 Strategy, Emerging Risk, and Regulatory Insight 
 Monitor regulatory, industry, business, technology, data, cyber, and operational developments; assess their regulatory compliance and conduct implications for the CCO’s portfolio; and identify matters requiring action or escalation.
 Assess interdependencies across business lines, legal entities, regulatory obligations, and Compliance activities, working with regulatory change and subject-matter teams.
 Develop evidence-based recommendations setting out the issue, options, trade-offs, and proposed course of action for the CCO and other senior leaders.
 Support Compliance strategy, annual planning, and management objectives by developing analysis and recommendations and leading assigned priorities.
 Lead assigned regulatory impact assessments and implementation planning, or provide advice and coordination where other teams retain ownership.

 Transformation and Priority Initiative Delivery 
 Lead assigned Compliance transformation, modernization, remediation, and strategic initiatives from initial assessment through implementation.
 Establish objectives, governance, roles, deliverables, milestones, dependencies, and measures of success; monitor progress and escalate material risks, delivery concerns, and unresolved matters.
 Assess the impact of business and enterprise change on Compliance accountabilities, capacity, controls, infrastructure, and operating models.
 Identify process and operating-model improvements and opportunities to use data, technology, analytics, automation, or artificial intelligence where they strengthen oversight, decision-making, or operational effectiveness.
 Challenge proposals that may create regulatory risk, control weaknesses, unclear accountabilities, unnecessary complexity, or unsustainable Compliance obligations.
 Coordinate resolution of cross-functional dependencies and clarify proposed ownership and outcomes with the relevant stakeholders.
 Establish implementation readiness, stakeholder adoption, documented operating ownership, and appropriate post-implementation monitoring for transition to business-as-usual operations.

 Compliance Program Effectiveness and Governance 
 Support assessments of Compliance program effectiveness, maturity, and alignment with regulatory expectations and enterprise requirements.
 Assess governance, processes, controls, procedures, reporting, and infrastructure to identify gaps and recommend proportionate improvements.
 Lead assigned regulatory, audit, issue-management, control-enhancement, and program-improvement initiatives, or provide advice and coordination where another team retains delivery ownership.
 Support practical and defensible responses to regulatory examinations, inquiries, findings, and other regulatory matters.
 Support the development of risk indicators, management information, trend analysis, and forward-looking reporting that inform oversight and decisions.
 Recommend consistent, risk-based Compliance practices, clear ownership, and appropriate documentation, avoiding duplication across assigned initiatives.

 Executive Advice and Stakeholder Engagement 
 Advise the CCO and other senior leaders on complex, sensitive, or evolving matters, providing independent Compliance guidance and constructive challenge.
 Prepare decision-ready briefings, presentations, governance reports, and other materials that explain the issue, implications, options, and recommended action for the intended audience.
 Build relationships across Wealth, Compliance, Legal, Risk, Governance and Control, Technology, Operations, and other corporate functions, aligning stakeholders with different mandates and priorities.
 Explain regulatory, risk, technology, and transformation matters to senior, technical, and non-technical audiences, supporting timely decisions and transparent escalation.
 Represent the CCO or Wealth Compliance at designated committees, regulatory and industry forums, working groups, and stakeholder discussions, as assigned.

 Leadership and Capability Development 
 Lead cross-functional teams, working groups, project resources, consultants, or direct reports, as applicable, with clear expectations for assigned outcomes and delivery.
 Coach colleagues and share knowledge to build capabilities across Wealth Compliance.
 Foster collaboration, inclusion, innovation, constructive challenge, continuous improvement, and prudent risk management.
 Support workforce planning, role clarity, operating-model development, organizational change, and broader Compliance priorities, as assigned.

 Assignment Portfolio 
 Assignments within the CCO’s mandate may include strategy and annual planning; emerging regulatory compliance and conduct risks; regulatory change, examinations, inquiries, engagement, and remediation; Internal Audit, Compliance Testing, issue management, and control-framework enhancement; Compliance modernization, policy and procedure improvement, and operating-model, business, or enterprise change; governance and executive reporting; and data, analytics, automation, artificial intelligence, or technology enablement. These examples are illustrative and do not establish permanent ownership of each area. Other strategic priorities and special projects may be assigned by the CCO.

 Measures of Success 
 Assigned emerging-risk and strategic assessments provide timely, evidence-based recommendations and identify matters requiring action, monitoring, or escalation.
 ·         Advice and decision materials support timely, informed decisions by clearly presenting material risks, implications, options, trade-offs, and recommended action.
 Assigned initiatives deliver against agreed outcomes, milestones, and governance expectations, with material risks, dependencies, and changes to delivery plans addressed or escalated.
 Completed initiatives have documented operating ownership, appropriate transition and monitoring arrangements, and evidence of improvement against agreed objectives.
 Where used, data and technology enablement is proportionate and responsible and contributes to agreed improvements in oversight, risk coverage, decision-making, or operational effectiveness.
 Assigned cross-functional matters progress with clear accountability, with material dependencies resolved or appropriately escalated.
 Coaching and knowledge-sharing contribute to colleague development and a culture of collaboration, constructive challenge, and compliance.

 Job Requirements 

 Essential Qualifications and Capabilities

jobs.title: Senior Director, Growth and Partnerships
jobs.description:
Teladoc Health is the global virtual care leader, offering comprehensive virtual care solutions spanning virtual care including primary, mental health, expert medical, devices and licensed platform services. Teladoc Health serves the world's leading insurers, employers, and health systems and helps millions of people around the world resolve their healthcare needs with confidence. Serving over 9 million Canadians, Teladoc Health has been in Canada for more than 20 years and operates in 175 countries world-wide.

 Summary of Position 

 The Senior Director, Growth and Partnerships is responsible for driving business development and commercial growth for Teladoc Health Canada, and positioning Teladoc as a leader in transforming the future of healthcare in Canada. The role has a primary focus on private‑sector (B2B) markets, including employers, insurers, and intermediaries, with responsibility to support and pursue public‑sector (HHS) opportunities as aligned with business priorities. 

 This role is accountable for growing Teladoc’s position as a leader within Canada’s health benefits and insurance ecosystem by originating, developing, and closing new business; expanding strategic client relationships; and advancing partnerships that enable innovative, clinically‑integrated healthcare solutions. Working cross‑functionally with leaders across Teladoc (in Canada and globally) in clinical, marketing, operations, and product, the Senior Director develops and executes a business development and go‑to‑market strategy that drives revenue delivery and growth targets aligned with Teladoc’s broader role in shaping the future of healthcare access, experience, and outcomes. 

 The Senior Director owns the end‑to‑end growth and client lifecycle across assigned markets—from market strategy and go‑to‑market execution through sales engagement, client adoption, value realization, renewal, and expansion—ensuring that commercial success reinforces Teladoc’s leadership position in Canada’s evolving healthcare landscape. 

 Essential Duties and Responsibilities 

 Strategic Growth:
 Achieve the established revenue objectives, including business development growth targets (organic, net new, cross-sell)
 Define and execute a multi-year growth roadmap aligned with Teladoc’s capabilities and innovation cycle across priority markets (insurers, intermediaries, and employers) including public payors (as directed)
 Translate insights from external market trends and internal win/loss analyses to identify new growth opportunities and inform development of new products / services
 Lead cross-functional go-to-market planning for new products and collaborate on pricing and value-proposition strategies that resonate with target clients

 Sales Operations and Revenue Performance:
 Lead end-to-end pipeline, including discovery with strategic accounts, proposals and RFXs, pricing, and contract execution balancing in-year performance with long-term growth  
 Drive operational rigor through data-driven insights, including CRM, performance dashboards, adoption, and client value
 Lead, mentor and motivate a team of sales and client management professionals and be responsible for target setting, compensation, forecasting, pipeline management, and performance management

 Client Retention and Expansion
 Build and sustain strong client relationships to support retention, expansion, and long‑term partnership growth
 Proactively understand client priorities and evolving needs through regular engagement, market awareness, and ongoing dialogue
 Lead a consultative, solution‑oriented approach with strategic accounts, positioning Teladoc as a trusted innovation and thought partner
 Engage directly with clients through executive‑level meetings, workshops, and working sessions to deliver value aligned to client objectives
 Own the customer success and experience strategy, ensuring clients achieve measurable outcomes that support renewal and upsell opportunities
 Evaluate, strengthen and expand strategic alliances and channel partnerships that enhance Teladoc’s reach, capabilities and market presence
 Act as a trusted executive partner to client senior leaders, reinforcing Teladoc’s role as a strategic partner rather than a transactional vendor
 Represent Teladoc with clients and in the broader market through conferences, trade exhibitions, and industry forums (virtual and in‑person, as required)
 Monitor and follow client and industry trends to anticipate needs and inform engagement strategies
 Other relevant duties as assigned

 Supervisory Responsibilities 
 Yes, interim responsibility of overseeing a team of sales and client management professionals

 Qualifications Expected for Position 
 Minimum of 10 years’ experience in a strategy, sales and client executive leadership position
 Minimum of 5 years’ experience in Healthcare including specifically in group insurance and benefits industry
 Proven ability to operate at the executive and board level, shaping strategy and influencing investment decisions.
 A Bachelor’s degree required (Advanced Business Degree or MBA preferred)
 Proven track record in relationship‑led growth and business development, including securing and expanding strategic client and partner relationships
 Strong executive communication and presentation capabilities, with the ability to engage and influence senior internal and external stakeholders; French proficiency considered an asset
 Demonstrated people leadership experience, with a history of building, leading, and developing high‑performing teams
 Advanced proficiency in leveraging technology to support sales execution, client engagement, performance insight, and executive‑level communication

 Salary Range 
 $150,000 to $200,000/year

 Position Type 
 Net New

 Work Environment                                        
 Hybrid (Office & Remote) 

 Travel: up to 40% 

 Why Join Teladoc Health? 

 Impactful, Connected Healthcare: Support millions of Canadians across the country with accessible care within rural regions & provincial health systems, at no cost to patients. 

 Focus on Quality & Safety: Upholding the highest excellence of clinical quality standards is paramount to Teladoc Health. 

 Collaborative, Supportive Network: Our diverse community is dedicated to transforming healthcare in Canada. Be a part of a growing team across Canada, that thrives on engagement, learning and growth. 

 Our Work Truly Matters: Recognized as the world leader in whole-person virtual care, Teladoc Health uses innovative platforms to provide accessible care across the full continuum of care, at every stage in a person’s health journey. 

 Growth and Innovation: We are growing rapidly - Come grow with us and support our expanding mission to make healthcare more accessible. 

 Diversity and Inclusion: At Teladoc Health we believe that personal and professional diversity is the key to innovation. We hire based solely on your strengths and qualifications, and the way in which those strengths can directly contribute to your success in your new position.

jobs.title: Director, Platform Engineering
jobs.description:
Join the team leading the next evolution of virtual care.  

 At Teladoc Health, you are empowered to bring your true self to work while helping millions of people live their healthiest lives.

 Here you will be part of a high-performance culture where colleagues embrace challenges, drive transformative solutions, and create opportunities for growth. Together, we’re transforming how better health happens.

 Position Summary 
 We are seeking a Director, Platform Engineering & DevOps to lead the development and maturation of our enterprise Platform Engineering organization.

 This leader will be responsible for building a modern, automation-first platform primarily focused on Microsoft Azure, while supporting remaining legacy workloads in AWS and on-premises data centers during the company's migration to Azure.

 The Director will lead the Platform Engineering team and partner closely with Network Engineering, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), Security, and application Engineering to deliver secure, reliable, scalable, and highly automated infrastructure platforms.

 A key objective of this role is to move the organization toward a self-service Platform Engineering model, enabling application teams to deploy and manage infrastructure using standardized patterns, Infrastructure as Code, automation, and cloud governance.

 Role and Responsibilities 
 Build, lead, and develop the Platform Engineering organization, including engineering strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
 Lead the design and evolution of the company's enterprise Microsoft Azure platform, including landing zones, governance, identity, networking, security, observability, and resiliency.

 Support the migration of applications and infrastructure from AWS and on-premises environments to Azure.

 Establish Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation as the standard approach for provisioning and managing infrastructure.

 Develop reusable Terraform modules, CI/CD pipelines, reference architectures, and standardized deployment patterns.

 Build self-service platform capabilities and "golden paths" that improve developer productivity and reduce manual infrastructure provisioning.

 Partner with Network Engineering on hybrid cloud connectivity, cloud networking, Private Link, DNS, routing, firewalls, and application delivery.

 Partner with SRE to establish platform availability objectives, observability standards, resiliency practices, incident improvements, and operational readiness, leveraging Datadog Application

 Partner with SRE and Application Engineering to establish consistent standards for application and platform telemetry, including metrics, logs, distributed traces, dashboards, alerting, and service-level monitoring.

 Ensure cloud and platform services are appropriately instrumented and integrated with the enterprise observability platform.

 Partner with Security to implement secure-by-default platform patterns, cloud governance, policy enforcement, and compliance controls.

 Establish cloud cost-management and FinOps practices across Azure and remaining AWS environments.

 Recruit, mentor, and develop engineering leaders and senior technical talent.

 Provide executive-level communication regarding platform strategy, technology risks, investments, reliability, and cloud transformation progress.

 Required Qualifications 
 10+ years of progressive experience in cloud infrastructure, DevOps, Platform Engineering, systems engineering, or related disciplines, including significant engineering leadership experience.

 Deep technical knowledge of Microsoft Azure, including enterprise cloud architecture, networking, security, governance, resiliency, and platform services.

 Strong experience with Infrastructure as Code and automation, particularly Terraform, CI/CD pipelines, and Git-based engineering workflows.

 Demonstrated experience leading complex cloud transformation initiatives, including hybrid environments, enterprise cloud migrations, or modernization of mission-critical infrastructure.

 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience building or leading an enterprise Platform Engineering organization or Internal Developer Platform.

 Working knowledge of AWS and experience supporting or migrating AWS workloads.

 Experience with Azure Landing Zones, Microsoft Cloud Adoption Framework, Azure Well-Architected Framework, and Azure Verified Modules.

 Experience with Kubernetes and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).

 Experience with GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, GitHub Actions or comparable DevOps platforms.

 Experience with enterprise observability and APM platforms, preferably Datadog, and technologies such as OpenTelemetry.

 Experience implementing SRE practices including SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, resiliency engineering, and incident management.

 Experience implementing cloud FinOps and cost optimization practices.

 Experience operating technology platforms in healthcare, SaaS, financial services, or another regulated environment.

 Success Metrics for the Role 
 Success will be measured by the Director's ability to build a scalable Platform Engineering organization and improve the speed, reliability, security, and efficiency of infrastructure delivery.
 Increased percentage of infrastructure deployed and managed through Infrastructure as Code.

 Increased adoption of standardized Azure landing zones, reusable platform services, and self-service capabilities.

 Reduced infrastructure provisioning and application deployment lead times.

 Progress migrating targeted AWS and on-premises workloads to Azure.

 Improved platform availability and achievement of defined SLOs.

 Increased adoption and effectiveness of standardized observability and APM practices across platform and application services, including improved service visibility and reduced mean time to detect and restore.

 Reduction in infrastructure-related incidents, configuration drift, and manual production changes.

 Improved developer satisfaction and adoption of Platform Engineering services.

 Improved cloud governance, security compliance, and cost efficiency.

 Successful recruitment, development, and retention of a high-performing Platform Engineering team.

 As part of our hiring process, we verify identity and credentials, conduct interviews (live or video), and screen for fraud or misrepresentation. Applicants who falsify information will be disqualified.

 Why join Teladoc Health? 

 Teladoc Health is transforming how better health happens. Learn how when you join us in pursuit of our impactful mission. 

 Chart your career path with meaningful opportunities that empower you to grow, lead, and make a difference.

 Join a multi-faceted community that celebrates each colleague’s unique perspective and is focused on continually improving, each and every day.  

 Contribute to an innovative culture where fresh ideas are valued as we increase access to care in new ways.   

 Enjoy an inclusive benefits program centered around you and your family, with tailored programs that address your unique needs.

 Explore candidate resources with tips and tricks from Teladoc Health recruiters and learn more about our company culture by exploring #TeamTeladocHealth on LinkedIn.

 As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we never have and never will discriminate against any job candidate or employee due to age, race, religion, color, ethnicity, national origin, gender, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, membership in an employee organization, medical condition, family history, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, parental status, or pregnancy). In our innovative and inclusive workplace, we prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. 

 Teladoc Health respects your privacy and is committed to maintaining the confidentiality and security of your personal information. In furtherance of your employment relationship with Teladoc Health, we collect personal information responsibly and in accordance with applicable data privacy laws, including but not limited to, the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA).  Personal information is defined as: Any information or set of information relating to you, including (a) all information that identifies you or could reasonably be used to identify you, and (b) all information that any applicable law treats as personal information. jobs.title: Director, System Engineering Delivery
jobs.description:
Telesat (Nasdaq and TSX: TSAT) is a leading global satellite operator, providing reliable and secure satellite-delivered communications solutions worldwide to broadcast, telecommunications, corporate and government customers for over 55 years.  Backed by a legacy of engineering excellence, reliability and industry-leading customer service, Telesat has grown to be one of the largest and most successful global satellite operators.
Telesat Lightspeed, our revolutionary Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite network, scheduled to begin service in 2027, will revolutionize global broadband connectivity for enterprise and Government users by delivering a combination of high capacity, security, resiliency and affordability with ultra-low latency and fiber-like speeds. Telesat is headquartered in Ottawa, Canada, and has offices and facilities around the world.
 
The company’s state-of-the-art Satellite fleet consists of 12 GEO satellites, the Canadian payload on ViaSat-1 and one LEO 3 demonstration satellite.  For more information, follow Telesat on X and LinkedIn or visit www.telesat.com


The opportunity
Build and scale a highly capable System Engineering Delivery team within the Lightspeed Systems Engineering division, alongside Telesat’s established LEO System Engineering (LEO SE) team. This opportunity is for a high-energy leader who enjoys developing strong managers and engineers, expanding capacity for complex work, and turning demanding technical objectives into disciplined delivery.
As Director, System Engineering Delivery, you will establish and lead a department that will support the consolidation of the Lightspeed technical baseline by delivering complete engineering packages for assigned system portfolios. Your department will also build and maintain shared engineering software tools, including AI tools, to improve engineering throughput, quality and efficiency across the division.
Working in partnership with LEO SE and segment teams, your department will complement LEO SE’s continuing engineering work by adding scalable delivery capacity and reusable engineering capabilities across the division.
Why this role
Build a lasting engineering capability while delivering meaningful technical outcomes on Lightspeed. You will have scope to develop leaders, connect Systems Engineering and software disciplines, and introduce tools that teams use in their everyday engineering work. This role suits a high-energy leader who builds momentum, drives results and thrives in a demanding, fast-moving program environment.

 Welcome to TELUS Digital — where innovation drives impact at a global scale.  With a global team across North America, South America, Central America, Europe, Africa, and APAC, we offer end-to-end expertise across eight core service areas: Digital Product Consulting, Digital Marketing Services, Data & AI, Strategy Consulting, Business Operations Modernization, Enterprise Applications, Cloud Engineering, and QA & Test Engineering.

 Location & Flexibility 
 This role will operate remotely in the United States or Canada OR be based out of one of our major North American office locations - Charlottesville, VA, Durham, NC, Columbus, OH, Boston, MA, Toronto, ON, or Vancouver, BC.
 This role may involve travel of up to 25% to contact center and client locations.

 The Opportunity 
 We are seeking a Director, CX AI Delivery: a consultant and delivery expert who can turn complex contact center and AI programs into predictable, measurable outcomes. You will lead delivery across our CX AI portfolio, spanning Contact Center as a Service (CCaaS) platforms, conversational and agentic AI, agent assist, and CX intelligence, and serve as a trusted advisor to client executives. You will manage a portfolio of client engagements (generally ~$15–20M in revenue), directly lead delivery, product, and engineering leaders, and step in to stabilize and recover programs when needed.

 This is a delivery-first leadership role with an AI lens. You will bring the rigor of a seasoned delivery executive together with a working command of how AI is changing CX: from AI-driven routing and virtual agents to copilots, knowledge, and agentic automation. You will help clients adopt these capabilities responsibly, at scale, and in iterative releases that get value into production quickly. You will also help evaluate vendor and partner solutions and decide how and when new tools enter the ecosystem.

 This position reports to the Managing Director, CX AI Delivery and typically manages 8–12 direct reports, including senior managers, managers, and principal-level delivery and technical leaders. It is primarily evaluated on delivery success, client and team feedback, forecast accuracy, portfolio profitability, and growth of key accounts. This is an opportunistically billable position.
 Responsibilities 
 Strategic Account Governance & Growth 
 Be the executive partner. Act as the primary escalation point and strategic advisor for client executives, ensuring TELUS Digital is viewed as a “Doctor” (consultative partner), not a “Waiter” (order taker).

 Run portfolio health. Drive the commercial success of a ~$15–20M portfolio, leading Quarterly Business Reviews that connect delivery progress to the client’s long-term CX and business goals.

 Grow organically. Identify expansion opportunities in existing accounts by understanding client pain points and bringing a relevant point of view on CX and AI. Support renewals, upsell, and expansion in partnership with strategic sales and customer success teams.

 Extend into managed services and advisory as the practice matures: shape Day 2 support models, operational readiness, and advisory engagements that keep clients engaged after go-live.

 Delivery Excellence & Risk Mitigation

 Manage risk proactively. Identify “red” and “yellow” programs early; step into recovery situations to provide clarity, reset expectations, and stabilize teams and client relationships.

 Push for iterative delivery. Favor smaller releases and faster cycles over big-bang launches, especially for AI capabilities where learning in production is essential.

 Optimize delivery models, balancing onshore/offshore teams, automation, and repeatable assets to improve margins and scalability.

 Manage vendor and partner ecosystems. Work with CCaaS and AI platform partners (e.g., Genesys, Google, AWS, Zendesk, Five9, ElevenLabs, Cresta, Parloa) to deliver joint solutions as well as surrounding services in the client ecosystem.

 Partner on pre-sales. Support the commercial team to shape innovative solutions and lead scoping, estimation, and handoffs into delivery so engagements start with clear requirements and goals.

 Leadership & Talent Development 
 Coach and mentor delivery, product, and engineering leaders on leading their own teams and navigating complex client dynamics.

 Build a high-performance culture with regular 1:1s and performance reviews grounded in radical candor and growth, delivering feedback upward, across, and down with grace and clarity.

 Raise the bar on talent. Participate in senior-level hiring, contribute to the Delivery Playbook, and build career paths and skill development (including AI and platform certification pipelines).

 Operational & Financial Stewardship 
 Own portfolio financials: gross margin, utilization, and effective billable rates.

 Forecast accurately. Maintain precise revenue and resource forecasts so the business can plan hiring and growth with confidence.

 Influence with data. Use reporting language, data visualization, and storytelling to influence internal and external decisions and inspire confidence in stakeholders.

 Collaborate across the business with peers and practice leaders to improve internal processes and operational efficiency, and bring energy to moments that matter: new relationships, key presentations, and recovery situations.

 Experience delivering large-scale CX or contact center transformations that influenced VP- and C-level decision making.

 Working knowledge of how AI is applied in CX: conversational and voice AI, agent assist and copilots, AI-driven routing, knowledge and content for AI, and CX intelligence; ability to discuss architecture, risk, and ROI credibly with both technical and executive audiences.

 Hands-on delivery experience with one or more leading CCaaS or CX AI platforms (e.g., Genesys, Amazon Connect, Zendesk, Google); platform certifications and experience across multiple verticals are a plus.

 Deep understanding of the SDLC and Agile delivery, with a track record of leading complex, custom-built software solutions from discovery to launch, and comfort with iterative, experiment-driven delivery.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Digital Finance
jobs.description:
Venture outside the ordinary - TMX Careers 

 The TMX group of companies includes leading global exchanges such as the Toronto Stock Exchange, Montreal Exchange, and numerous innovative organizations enhancing capital markets.  United as a global team, we’re connecting cross-functionally, traversing industries and geographies, moving opportunity into action, advancing global economic growth, and propelling progress. Through a rich exchange of ideas, meaningful collaboration, and a nimble operating model, we're powering some of the nation's most critical systems, fueling capital formation and innovation, bringing increased opportunity to business visionaries, product ingenuity to consumers, and career exploration to our team.

 Ready to be part of the action? 

 The Managing Director, Digital Finance serves as the senior finance leader accountable for leading the strategic transformation of Finance operations across systems, data, reporting, business processes, and artificial intelligence. In this business leadership capacity, you will establish priorities, set governance standards, and ensure sustained adoption and measurable value creation. Operating as the primary business counterpart to Technology and working in close partnership with the Chief Financial Officer and senior leadership, you will oversee the strategic roadmap to replace manual, fragmented workflows with a trusted, single source of financial data and insight that accelerates enterprise decision-making and supports global growth.

 Reports to: Chief Strategy and Innovation Officer
 Job Location: Hybrid (2–3 days/week in office) – based in Toronto, ON.

 Key Accountabilities 
 Finance Transformation & Portfolio Delivery
 Own and champion the multi-year Digital Finance roadmap and unified backlog across the CFO organization, prioritizing initiatives by business value, control requirements, readiness, effort, and operational cost in close collaboration with Technology.
 Sponsor and drive end-to-end process redesign across record-to-report, plan-to-perform, procure-to-pay, and order-to-cash workflows to modernize core operations.
 Establish robust business cases for all digital initiatives, tracking adoption metrics, cycle-time reductions, redeployed capacity, and internal control enhancements.
 Authorize the decommissioning of legacy reports, spreadsheets, and manual steps following the rigorous validation of modern digital replacements.
 Finance Systems & Core Architecture
 Act as the accountable Finance business owner for Workday Financials and Workday Adaptive Planning in collaboration with Controllership and FP&A process owners, establishing high standards for clean data capture, straight-through processing, chart-of-accounts governance, and audit-ready planning workflows.
 Ensure Workday configurations align with enterprise best practices, spearheading the design and ongoing governance of the Foundation Data Model (FDM) to support scalable accounting, reporting, and analytics requirements.
 Partner with Technology, external implementation specialists, and Workday to conduct recurring architecture reviews and remediate configuration gaps.
 Oversee and approve the business roadmap for the broader finance application ecosystem (close management, consolidations, billing, accounts payable, expense management, treasury, and tax), actively identifying rationalization opportunities.
 Align application release schedules with the financial close calendar, collaborating with Technology, Risk, and Internal Audit to enforce rigorous segregation of duties, access controls, and Internal Control over Financial Reporting (ICFR).
 Finance Data, BI & Analytics
 Direct the team responsible for designing, building, and operating finance data models, data pipelines, and certified financial data products on Snowflake, establishing a single source of truth across all global entities.
 Establish robust semantic layer governance, ensuring every certified data product possesses an assigned Finance owner, approved definitions, and ongoing reconciliation to general ledger accounting outputs.
 Oversee Finance’s enterprise Business Intelligence (BI) capabilities and visualization standards, transitioning teams from static reporting to dynamic, interactive dashboards and executive decision environments utilizing tools such as Amazon QuickSight and native cloud analytics capabilities.
 Accelerate data-driven insights across Finance by collaborating with Finance Business Partners and operational data teams to integrate financial and operational drivers, including trading, clearing, listings, and market data subscriptions.
 Applied AI & Intelligent Automation
 Identify, prioritize, and oversee the rollout of high-impact finance AI use cases—such as variance analysis, exception triage, predictive forecasting, narrative document synthesis, and anomaly detection—ensuring each deployment maintains clear quality thresholds, human-in-the-loop oversight, and independent model validation.
 Drive end-to-end automation of data collation, reconciliation, and distribution throughout the reporting cycle while safeguarding professional financial judgment and formal authorization checkpoints.
 Market Innovation & Continuous Improvement
 Monitor evolving capabilities across Workday, Snowflake, business intelligence ecosystems, and emerging financial technologies, assessing business viability and integrating high-value opportunities into the strategic roadmap.
 Provide strategic advisory to the Finance Senior Leadership Team on emerging technology trends, fostering shared ownership of digital adoption.
 People Leadership & Change Enablement
 Lead, mentor, and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning finance systems, data engineering, business intelligence, and advanced analytics, establishing clear strategic direction while scaling functional capacity.
 Drive enterprise change management, communication, and training programs to embed digital literacy and analytical curiosity across the broader finance organization.
 Manage the Digital Finance operational budget, serving as the business partner to Technology and Procurement for vendor selection and delivery partner management.

 Must Have(s) 
 12+ years of progressive finance experience with comprehensive knowledge of core accounting and financial processes, coupled with advanced financial analysis capabilities.
 Professional accounting or financial credential (CPA preferred; MBA or CFA will also be considered).
 Demonstrated success serving as the business lead for major finance transformations (e.g., enterprise ERP implementations, EPM/planning platforms, or enterprise data and reporting overhauls) from conception through operational adoption and value realization.
 Proven leadership experience guiding data, BI, or analytics personnel, underpinned by sufficient technical literacy in data modeling, SQL, cloud data platforms (e.g., Snowflake), and modern BI suites to establish standards and guide technical execution.
 Deep knowledge of financial governance frameworks, internal controls, and ICFR requirements within large-scale system and process transformation environments.
 Demonstrated track record managing multi-year business cases, departmental budgets, third-party software vendors, and systems integration partners.
 Proven leadership acumen in ambiguous, matrixed environments with strong cross-functional stakeholder management and executive presentation skills.

 Nice to Have(s) 
 Experience with Workday Financials and Workday Adaptive Planning, including Foundation Data Model (FDM) architecture and data integration with Snowflake.
 Direct technical experience with data querying and scripting languages (e.g., SQL, Python).
 Practical experience deploying artificial intelligence or machine learning solutions within corporate finance environments, including model validation and risk management frameworks.
 Industry experience within capital markets, financial services, financial technology, or software organizations.
 Leadership background within multi-entity, multi-currency, and multinational operating structures.

jobs.title: Associate Creative Director, Art Director
jobs.description:
Build something people love 
 Wealthsimple is Canada’s leading financial innovator. The company offers a full suite of simple, sophisticated financial products across managed investing, do-it-yourself trading, cryptocurrency, tax filing, spending and saving. Wealthsimple currently serves more than 4 million Canadians and holds over $169 billion in assets under administration. The company was founded in 2014 by a team of financial experts and technology entrepreneurs, and is headquartered in Toronto, Canada.

 We're proud of what we've built — and we're just getting started. Read our Culture Manual and learn more about how we work.

 At Wealthsimple, we're interested in humans and money — and the complicated ways humans feel about money. Our goal in the creative department is to be a part of that conversation in meaningful ways that are completely innovative and new. We have a deep aversion to making things that already exist and to ads that feel like ads.

 We are looking for an experienced Associate Creative Director, Art Director to help us create innovative, human and ridiculously entertaining work. In this role you will often work as a team with a copywriter partner, but you’ll also collaborate with designers, writers, marketers and engineers across the org. You will be responsible for all aspects of creative development and production on integrated brand campaigns and projects large and small, and you will be leading creative voice in some of our biggest brand moments.

 Be a highly conceptual thinker with strong storytelling and design skills.

 Develop big ideas and bring them to life through every stage of production.

 Own large and small brand projects and campaigns from kickoff to completion, often balancing multiple projects at once.

 Be a maker-owner, but also a director-delegator, and find the right balance between those two roles for each project.

 Provide art direction on visual design for integrated brand campaigns and projects of various scales and types – from film, social, digital, to interactive experiences.

 Be a creative and strategic thinker who can see how creativity can solve business problems.

 Use AI in a variety of ways. Whether it’s moving ideas into functional prototypes, drafts, mockups or animatics that can be evaluated more quickly, or developing and refining AI workflows for internally created assets.

 Present work in a clear, passionate and dynamic way, championing the creative and vision to internal stakeholders.

 Manage relationships with outside production partners when necessary.

 6-10+ years of experience as an Art Director (agency experience preferred, but not necessary).

 Ability to concept and art direct, developing storyboards, comps or animatics without assistance from the Design team

 Extensive experience with integrated campaigns, from strategic development through creative development and delivery

 Production experience across all platforms - film, digital, social, and print

 Well-versed in Adobe Creative Suite and able to be a hands-on creative delivering comps, layouts, and assets across all media types as well as give direction to studio designers where applicable

 Familiarity with AI image and video generation tools.

 A truly collaborative creative approach.

 Give and receive constructive feedback in a respectful manner

 Travel for production when necessary.
