jobs.description:
Zafin is an AI platform company helping regulated institutions modernize how critical work is designed, governed, and delivered. Our technology enables organizations to move faster while maintaining the governance, accountability, and control required in highly regulated environments.

 Our portfolio includes Zafin AIOS, an agent orchestration platform for governed AI work; the Zafin Banking Platform, which helps banks modernize product, pricing, offers, billing, loyalty, and relationship management; and Zafin IO, an integration platform that connects data, systems, and workflows across complex enterprise environments.

 Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Zafin partners with leading financial institutions across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific. As AI transforms the future of financial services, we're building the platforms that help regulated organizations adopt AI responsibly and at scale.

 What is the Opportunity?

 Lead the FinOps function. As Director, FinOps (Cloud Financial Management), you will shape and advance Zafin’s cloud financial management strategy. You will build and lead a scalable FinOps function that delivers measurable, sustainable cost savings while safeguarding platform reliability, security, and engineering productivity.

 Shape cloud investment decisions. You will define how Zafin manages and optimizes cloud investments across its banking technology platforms. Working with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance, you will strengthen financial accountability, increase cost visibility, and embed cost-conscious decision-making across technology and business operations.

 Apply AI and automation. You will use AI-driven analytics, automation, and intelligent cost monitoring to improve forecasting, identify optimization opportunities, detect spending anomalies, and strengthen cloud financial governance.

 Deliver sustainable business value. Your leadership will improve cloud cost efficiency and financial predictability, ensuring Zafin’s cloud investments generate lasting value.

 What Will You Do?

 Define and lead Zafin’s FinOps strategy, governance framework, and cloud cost optimization program across Microsoft Azure and platform services.

 Deliver measurable cloud savings through resource optimization, improved utilization, cost avoidance, and stronger financial accountability.

 Lead cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, and financial reporting to increase cost visibility and improve predictability.

 Partner with Engineering, Cloud Operations, Product, and Finance to embed cost-efficient practices in architecture, infrastructure, and operational decisions.

 Optimize Azure infrastructure spending across compute, storage, networking, AKS/Kubernetes, Reserved Instances, and observability services.

 Establish cost allocation models, tagging standards, financial controls, and unit economics to strengthen cloud cost management.

 Implement FinOps tools, dashboards, AI-assisted analytics, automation, and anomaly detection to uncover savings opportunities and reinforce financial governance.

 Provide executives with clear reporting on cloud spending, savings performance, financial risks, and strategic recommendations.

 Build and mentor a high-performing FinOps team, foster cross-functional collaboration, and create a culture of cloud cost accountability.

 What Do You Need to Succeed?

 Must Haves 

 Relevant experience: 10+ years in cloud infrastructure, platform operations, technology finance, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), or FinOps, including at least three years in a leadership role.

 Cloud financial management: Proven success designing or leading initiatives that deliver measurable, sustained cost savings and improve cost-to-serve.

 Azure expertise: Strong knowledge of Microsoft Azure and the cost drivers for compute, storage, networking, Kubernetes/AKS, and observability services.

 Financial planning and analysis: Expertise in cloud budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, financial modelling, ROI assessment, and savings measurement.

 Financial insight: Ability to translate complex cloud architecture and infrastructure decisions into clear financial implications and actionable optimization strategies.

 Governance and accountability: Experience establishing financial governance practices, cost allocation models, accountability frameworks, and performance reporting.

 Analytical problem-solving: Ability to identify key cost drivers, generate meaningful insights, and translate them into measurable business outcomes.

 Cross-functional influence: Demonstrated success aligning Engineering, Finance, Product, and Technology stakeholders and advancing initiatives without direct authority.

 Executive communication: Excellent stakeholder management skills, with experience presenting financial performance, strategic recommendations, and operational metrics to senior leaders.

 Leadership and change management: Proven ability to build scalable processes, establish operational discipline, lead high-performing teams, and drive organizational change in complex technology environments.

 Nice to Have 

 FinOps Foundation certifications, such as FinOps Certified Practitioner or Professional, and/or relevant Microsoft Azure certifications.

 Experience implementing showback/chargeback models and cloud unit economics at an enterprise scale.

 Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and GitOps practices, including Terraform, Argo CD, or equivalent technologies.

 Experience integrating cloud cost controls and financial governance into engineering delivery pipelines.

 Exposure to AI-driven cloud cost analytics, intelligent forecasting, anomaly detection, and automated optimization solutions.

 Experience establishing a FinOps function or cloud financial management capability within a growing technology organization.

 Familiarity with cloud infrastructure supporting financial services, banking platforms, or other regulated industries.

 Additional Job Details

 In addition to base salary, this position offers eligibility for an annual incentive bonus and a comprehensive benefits package to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance.

We invest in our people through a comprehensive rewards program that supports your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance, including:

 ClearGov has built a strong product marketing foundation, with an established team supporting product launches, messaging, and sales enablement across a growing portfolio. As the company enters its next phase of growth, ClearGov is hiring a Director of Product & Solution Marketing to elevate the function from strong product-level execution to platform-and- solution-level strategy.

 Reporting to the VP of Marketing, this leader will define how ClearGov positions, packages, and brings to market a suite of 13 products across cities, counties, school districts, and special districts, each with distinct needs and buying dynamics. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will help the company make sharper decisions about where to invest, how the products fit together, and how ClearGov expands within its customer base.

 This is a highly visible leadership role with meaningful autonomy and direct access to the executive team and board. The Director of Product & Solution Marketing will serve as a strategic partner to the VP of Marketing, CPO and CRO, translating customer and market insight into portfolio choices and measurable commercial impact.

 This leader will manage an established team of four, creating a five-person product & solution marketing organization, with the opportunity to grow the team as the function expands.

 Key Responsibilities: 

 Lead pricing and packaging strategy: Set the strategic direction for bundling, discounting, and launch pricing in partnership with Product, Finance, Revenue, and external research partners.

 Set portfolio and commercialization strategy: Define how ClearGov’s products fit together, where bundling and cross-sell opportunities exist, and how positioning and go-to-market motions should vary across customer segments.

 Shape executive decision-making: Represent product marketing with the executive team and board, connecting market, customer, and competitive insight to growth priorities and business performance.

 Lead and develop the product marketing organization: Build on the team’s subject matter expertise and strengths in messaging, launches, and enablement while expanding its capabilities in portfolio strategy, market intelligence, pricing, and commercial planning.

 Build a scalable launch and integration model: Partner with Product, Marketing, and Sales on new product / bundle launches and create repeatable approaches for positioning, packaging, and commercializing acquired products.

 Strengthen expansion motions: Partner with Revenue and Marketing leaders to improve cross-sell, upsell, and account-based growth programs across ClearGov’s customer base.

 Establish a market and customer intelligence discipline: Build competitive intelligence, win-loss analysis, and industry engagement that inform product, sales, and portfolio decisions.

 Own the market narrative and field adoption: Craft bold, outcome-based messaging that clearly differentiates ClearGov from spreadsheets and competing vendors, including sharp depositioning that sales can use in live deals. Ensure sales actually uses what the team builds by measuring content adoption, retiring assets that go unused, and tying messaging to win rates.

 Create clear measures of impact: Define how product marketing performance is evaluated and connect the team’s work to adoption, expansion, win rates, and revenue outcomes.

 Critical Skills/Experience: 

 Significant product marketing leadership experience in B2B SaaS, including recent experience at the Director or Senior Director level, or operating at a comparable scope.

 Experience owning go-to-market or commercialization strategy across a multi-product / platform portfolio, multiple customer segments, or distinct buyer personas.

 Pricing and packaging experience, including bundling, discounting, or launch pricing.

 A track record of translating customer, market, and competitive insight into positioning, portfolio, investment, or growth decisions.

 People leadership experience, including building, developing, and elevating a product marketing team.

 Strong partnership with Product, Sales, and Marketing leaders in a mid-market or enterprise sales environment.

 Executive presence and sound judgment, with the ability to operate autonomously, align senior stakeholders, and communicate strategy clearly to executives and board members.

 Comfort operating in a growing, evolving business where portfolio priorities and organizational needs continue to change.

 Experience with mid-market or lower-enterprise B2B SaaS products in the $30K–$60K ARR range and sales cycles of approximately three to four months.

 Preferred Skills/Experience: 

 Experience with programmatic growth motions such as account-based marketing, cross-sell, or upsell at scale.

 Experience with enterprise SaaS products of $75k-$250M+

 Background in GovTech, FinTech, finance, accounting, compliance, or another technical or regulated vertical.

 Experience supporting growth through M&A, portfolio expansion, or product-line integration.

 Experience building win-loss, competitive intelligence, or industry analyst programs.

 Compensation: 

 In the spirit of transparency, we are excited to share the base salary for this position is $165,000 - $200,000 USD or $155,000 - 190,000 CAD, and exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at ClearGov, your final base salary compensation will be determined by factors such as skills, interview performance, education and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that the range mentioned above is the full base salary for the role. Hiring beyond the base range would not be typical in order to allow for future & continued salary growth. We also offer a generous compensation and benefits package (more information on benefits listed below).

 Why Join ClearGov

 How to Apply 
Ready to join us? Apply online today!

jobs.title: Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation
jobs.description:
JOB PURPOSE 
 Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the Director, Enterprise AI Strategy & Transformation leads the development and execution of the organization’s enterprise AI strategy and transformation agenda to drive measurable business value, productivity, operational efficiency, innovation, and informed decision-making. The role serves as the organization’s AI subject matter expert and enterprise coordinating point, providing strategic guidance on AI opportunities, investments, governance, risk, technology, adoption, and value realization. 

 The Director partners with business and functional leaders to identify, prioritize, and implement AI and intelligent automation opportunities aligned with organizational objectives and financial goals. The role initially focuses on leveraging AI to enhance financial and operational performance, including forecasting, reporting, analysis, productivity, workflow efficiency, cost management, and decision-making, with successful capabilities and practices progressively expanded across other functions. The Director oversees the enterprise AI portfolio and lifecycle from opportunity assessment and business case development through solution selection, implementation, adoption, benefits realization, ongoing monitoring, and retirement. 

 KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 AI Strategy, Portfolio & Value Management Develop and maintain the enterprise AI strategy, operating model, portfolio, and roadmap aligned with corporate objectives and financial goals. 
 Identify, evaluate, and prioritize AI opportunities based on strategic alignment, business value, cost, complexity, data readiness, risk, and organizational readiness. 
 Develop business cases, investment recommendations, and implementation roadmaps, including build, buy, configure, or partner options. 
 Establish performance measures, baseline metrics, and value-realization frameworks to track AI adoption, ROI, productivity, cost savings, revenue impact, and other business outcomes. 
 Provide executive leadership with visibility into AI investments, performance, realized benefits, opportunities, and risks. 
 AI Solution Development & Implementation Lead the evaluation, design, development, and deployment of AI solutions across enterprise productivity, function-specific applications, intelligent automation, advanced AI, and emerging agentic capabilities. 
 Partner with business units and end users to identify opportunities, develop practical AI-enabled solutions, and improve processes and ways of working. 
 Oversee AI pilots, proofs of concept, and enterprise implementations through the full lifecycle—from opportunity identification and feasibility through deployment, adoption, benefits realization, monitoring, and retirement. 
 Coordinate with Cybersecurity, Human Resources and other stakeholders to ensure solutions are appropriately designed, implemented, adopted, and measured. 
 Assess solution performance and recommend whether initiatives should be scaled, enhanced, consolidated, paused, or retired based on business value, adoption, cost, and risk. 
 AI Governance, Risk & Responsible Adoption Establish and maintain enterprise AI governance frameworks, policies, standards, controls, and risk-based processes to support responsible AI adoption. 
 Ensure AI initiatives are appropriately assessed for cybersecurity, privacy, data, intellectual property, legal, ethical, third-party, model, and business continuity risks. 
 Maintain an enterprise inventory of approved AI technologies, platforms, models, agents, and material use cases, with appropriate review, approval, testing, human oversight, monitoring, and escalation requirements. 
 Ensure data quality, classification, access, security, information governance, and regulatory requirements are addressed before AI solutions are deployed. 
 Monitor the evolving AI landscape, regulatory expectations, and associated risks, and update governance practices as required. 
 Enterprise AI Adoption & Change Management Lead enterprise AI literacy, adoption, and change-management initiatives across executives, leaders, employees, technical teams, and advanced AI users. 
 Develop and deliver role- and function-specific training, guidance, and resources to promote effective and responsible use of AI. 
 Serve as the enterprise resource for AI strategy, best practices, use-case guidance, and adoption support. 
 Measure AI utilization, adoption, training effectiveness, employee feedback, and business outcomes to continuously improve AI enablement. 
 Coordinate internal subject matter experts, technology teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to support successful AI adoption 
 Vendor, Technology & Partner Management Evaluate AI technologies, vendors, consultants, platforms, and implementation partners against business requirements, value, security, architecture, scalability, risk, and total cost of ownership. 
 Manage AI technology and vendor relationships to ensure service quality, effective implementation, and value realization. 
 Maintain oversight of the enterprise AI technology portfolio to identify duplicate capabilities, unnecessary licensing, overlapping solutions, and opportunities for consolidation. 
 Monitor emerging AI technologies—including generative AI, large language models, predictive AI, intelligent automation, computer vision, and agentic AI—and assess their practical business applicability and potential value. 
 QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS, AND EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS 
  Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Information Technology, Engineering, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred. 
 Minimum seven (7) years of progressive experience in AI, data analytics, digital transformation, automation, technology, or related fields, including significant experience leading enterprise AI or generative AI adoption. 
 Proven experience leading complex, enterprise-wide AI or business transformation initiatives from strategy and business case development through implementation, adoption, scaling, and measurable value realization. 
 Strong business and financial acumen, including experience with budgeting, forecasting, reporting, business case development, technology investment evaluation, performance measurement, and ROI. 
 Strong knowledge of AI technologies, including generative AI, machine learning, predictive analytics, intelligent automation, large language models, AI agents, and emerging AI capabilities, with an understanding of data, cybersecurity, privacy, and AI governance. 
 Strong strategic thinking, analytical, communication, stakeholder management, project management, and change management skills, with the ability to translate complex technology into practical business solutions and influence cross-functional decisions.  
 Strong technical and business judgment to evaluate AI solutions, vendors, risks, data and technology dependencies, and investment decisions. Professional certifications in AI, analytics, project management, responsible AI, or AI governance are considered an asset. 

 PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS Standard office setting - hybrid arrangement (4 days in-office) 
 Fast paced office environment 
 Travel expectations between facilities in Mississauga and North York

jobs.title: Director, Sales Operations (Corporate)
jobs.location: 3737 Thimens Blvd, Montreal (Saint-Laurent), Quebec, Canada; 111 Progress, Scarborough, Ontario, Canada
jobs.description:
“Join us in building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”   

 About Us 

 At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

 The Opportunity 

 The Director, Sales Operations is responsible for owning, standardizing, and continuously improving the commercial operating system across the organization. This is a corporate role working in collaboration with all sales regions in the Atlantic Packaging network (Ontario, Quebec, USA).

 This role does not own sales targets nor manage sales teams directly. Instead, it enables Sales Leadership and P&L owners to execute consistently by providing clear processes, disciplined governance, and effective tools.

 The role addresses recurring structural issues in sales execution (contracts, risk exposure, forecast visibility, onboarding effectiveness, and CRM adoption) and brings process excellence to an area historically driven by individual experience rather than system discipline. Sales Operations builds the system so Sales / Marketing / Legal / Finance / CX work together efficiently.

 The corporate Customer Experience function will report into the Director, Sales Operations, which expect will increase the probability that customer feedback results in retention, growth, and operational improvement.

 Success Factors in the Role 

 Success in this role will be judged on system outcomes, not activity.

 Sales execution becomes repeatable

 Fewer deal-specific workarounds; consistent deal flow through the same stages and approvals.

 Sales leaders use the tools willingly

 Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.

 Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)

 P&L owners can see contract duration mix, terms exposure, and liability accumulation before approving deals.

 Fewer “surprises”

 Fewer last-minute escalations due to undocumented terms, unclear approvals, or cross‑region inconsistencies.

 Improved funnel credibility

 Forecast discussions are grounded in a shared, disciplined view of the pipeline.

 CX feedback loop is integrated into the sales process which will result in better CX scores across the businesses

 What You’ll Do 

 This role sets standards and runs governance. Sales Leadership owns execution. Finance/Credit/Legal co-own approval rules and risk thresholds.

 1. Sales Operating Model & Governance

 Own and maintain the front-end sales operating model, including:

 Contract approval workflows and limits of authority (with Legal).

 Clear rules when customers operate across regions.

 Partner with Legal, Finance, and Credit to make risk explicit and decision-ready.

 Ensure P&L leaders have visibility before commitments are made, not after.

 2. Salesforce Ownership

 Act as business owner of Salesforce (process design, usage standards, reporting logic).

 Drive adoption by defining how and why Salesforce is used:

 Funnel structure aligned with business needs (product mix, seasonality, capacity).

 Standard dashboards for P&L owners and Sales Leadership.

 Reduce “system noise” so the tool supports decisions, not administration.

 3. Funnel Management & Sales Planning

 Define and enforce consistent funnel management practices.

 Provide forward-looking visibility on revenue concentration by:

 Factory

 Asset type

 Industry

 Salesperson

 Other cuts as needed

 Enable proactive capacity and production discussions (vs. reactive firefighting).

 Drive development of sales plans that can be handed off for execution.

 Enable consolidation of this data for the Group.

 4. Contract, Terms & Risk Tracking

 Implement standardized reporting on:

 Contract tenure mix (no contract, quarterly, annual, etc.).

 Payment terms exposure.

 Aggregate liability commitments.

 Make commercial risk measured, visible, and discussable (not implicit or anecdotal).

 5. Sales Training / Motivation / Sales incentive management

 Design and institutionalize a formal sales onboarding and training framework.

 Develop role-specific training (e.g., Salesforce usage, contract basics).

 Build a repeatable cadence for sales meetings to drive consistent themes and execution.

 Administer the sales incentive program, including consistent publishing of performance vs. targets.

 6. Manage corporate CX program

 What You Bring 

 Strong background in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Revenue Enablement.

 Must be fluent in both French/English 

 Comfortable influencing senior sales leaders without hierarchical authority.

 Process-oriented, systems thinker with a strong business bias.

 Credible with Finance, Sales, and Operations alike.

 Required: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.

 7+ years of experience in progressive experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Business Analytics

 Expert in Salesforce, specifically in design, governance and adoption.

  What We Offer 

 Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)

 Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events

 A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition

 Opportunities for advancement and internal movement

 Education assistance for continuous skill development

 Academic scholarships for employees’ children

 Safety equipment and PPE support program

 Retirement savings and wellness initiatives

 Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

 Inclusion and Accessibility 

 Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

 We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

 Please Note:
Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

 Sommaire du rôle 

 Le/La Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives est responsable de définir, standardiser et améliorer en continu le système d’exploitation commercial de l’organisation. Il s’agit d’un rôle corporatif qui travaille en collaboration avec toutes les régions de ventes du réseau Atlantic Packaging, incluant l’Ontario, le Québec et les États-Unis.

 Ce rôle n’est pas propriétaire des objectifs de ventes et ne gère pas directement les équipes de ventes. Son rôle est plutôt de permettre aux leaders des ventes et aux responsables P&L d’exécuter de façon constante, en mettant en place des processus clairs, une gouvernance disciplinée et des outils efficaces.

 Le rôle adresse des enjeux structurels récurrents dans l’exécution commerciale, notamment les contrats, l’exposition aux risques, la visibilité sur le funnel, l’efficacité de l’intégration des nouveaux employés et l’adoption de Salesforce. Il amène de la rigueur de processus dans une fonction qui a historiquement reposé davantage sur l’expérience individuelle que sur une discipline institutionnelle. Les opérations commerciales corporatives bâtissent le système pour permettre aux Ventes / Marketing / Légal / Finances / CX de travailler ensemble efficacement.

 La fonction corporative d’expérience client relèvera du/de la Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives, ce qui est un arrimage naturel puisque la Voix du client, l’adoption de Salesforce, la discipline du funnel, la boucle fermée et les cadences commerciales doivent être connectées au même système de gestion pour transformer les commentaires clients en actions concrètes, soutenir la rétention, favoriser la croissance et améliorer l’exécution opérationnelle.

 Facteurs de succès dans le rôle 

 Le succès dans ce rôle sera évalué sur les résultats du système, et non sur le niveau d’activité.

 L’exécution des ventes devient reproductible

 Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

 Les leaders des ventes utilisent les outils parce qu’ils les aident à gérer le business

 Salesforce est utilisé parce qu’il facilite la gestion commerciale, et non seulement parce qu’il est obligatoire.

 Les risques commerciaux sont visibles avant les décisions

 Les responsables P&L peuvent voir la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité avant d’approuver les ententes.

 Moins de surprises

 Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

 Crédibilité accrue du funnel

 Les discussions de prévisions sont basées sur une vision partagée et disciplinée du pipeline.

 La boucle de rétroaction CX est intégrée au processus de ventes afin d’améliorer les scores CX dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires.

 Portée et responsabilités clés 

 Ce rôle établit les standards et anime la gouvernance. Les leaders des ventes demeurent propriétaires de l’exécution. Les finances, le crédit et le légal codéfinissent les règles d’approbation et les seuils de risque.

 1. Modèle opérationnel des ventes et gouvernance

 Définir et maintenir le modèle opérationnel commercial de première ligne, incluant les flux d’approbation des contrats, les limites d’autorité et les règles applicables aux clients opérant dans plusieurs régions.

 Travailler avec le juridique, les finances et le crédit afin de rendre le risque explicite et prêt à être décidé.

 S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.

 2. Ownership Salesforce

 Agir comme propriétaire d’affaires de Salesforce pour le design des processus, les standards d’utilisation et la logique de reporting.

 Favoriser l’adoption en définissant clairement comment et pourquoi Salesforce est utilisé.

 Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.

 Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.

 Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.

 3. Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes

 Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.

 Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.

 Permettre des discussions proactives sur la capacité et la production, plutôt que de fonctionner en mode réaction ou escalade.

 Contribuer au développement de plans de ventes clairs, prêts à être transférés en exécution.

 Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.

 4. Contrats, termes et suivi des risques

 Mettre en place un reporting standardisé sur la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité.

 Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.

 5. Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes

 Concevoir et institutionnaliser un cadre formel d’intégration et de formation pour les équipes de ventes.

 Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.

 Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.

 Administrer le programme d’incitatifs de ventes, incluant la publication constante de la performance par rapport aux objectifs.

 6. Gestion du programme corporatif d’expérience client

 Assurer l’arrimage entre la Voix du client, les données d’expérience client, Salesforce, les initiatives de ventes et les priorités opérationnelles.

 Mettre en place une boucle fermée permettant de transformer les commentaires, irritants et opportunités d’amélioration provenant des clients en actions concrètes, priorisées et mesurables.

 Renforcer la culture client en rendant les enjeux CX visibles, actionnables et intégrés aux cadences commerciales et opérationnelles.

 Profil recherché 

 Solide expérience en opérations commerciales, excellence commerciale, enablement ou analytique commerciale.

 Capacité d’influencer des leaders de ventes expérimentés sans autorité hiérarchique directe.

 Profil structuré, orienté processus et système, avec une forte proximité d’affaires.

 Crédible auprès des ventes, des finances et des opérations.

 Formation et expérience 

 Baccalauréat requis en administration des affaires, commerce, finance, opérations ou domaine connexe.

 Doit maîtriser couramment le français et l’anglais.

 Minimum de 7 ans d’expérience progressive en opérations commerciales, revenue operations, excellence commerciale ou analytique d’affaires.

 Expertise avancée avec Salesforce, particulièrement en design, gouvernance et adoption.

Reporting to the Vice President of Supply Chain & Strategy, this role is critical for building organizational planning capability to support sustainable, profitable growth.  It ensures alignment between business strategy and operational execution across production, procurement, and distribution. 

 The Director of Planning & Inventory leads a team of managers, planners and analysts with a focus on driving structure, establishing best practices for planning tools and processes, and driving continuous improvement initiatives to enhance forecast accuracy, machine utilization, inventory efficiency, and overall supply chain responsiveness. 

 What You’ll Do 

   Oversee the development and execution of the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP/IBP) process, ensuring alignment between demand, capacity, and financial plans across the organization 

   Direct inventory strategy to balance customer service levels with working capital objectives, minimizing excess/obsolete stock while preventing stockouts

 Exploiter les outils d’analyse et de modélisation pour interpréter les résultats et pour formuler des recommandations claires et réalisables.

 Appuyer les principales décisions et initiatives stratégiques de l’entreprise à l’aide d’analyses fondées sur des données et d’incidences financières.

 Analyse des investissements et scénarios 

 Réaliser des analyses de scénarios et de sensibilité pour orienter les décisions stratégiques, les investissements et l’affectation des ressources.

 Évaluer les options et le risque par rapport au rendement; formuler des recommandations pour contribuer à la prise de décision.

 Collaborer avec l’équipe de comptabilité pour assurer l’alignement sur les politiques en matière de comptabilité, les calendriers de clôture et le rapprochement des chiffres réels par rapport aux plans/prévisions.

 Appliquer des méthodologies rigoureuses en matière d’établissement de budgets, de prévisions, de définition des indicateurs de rendement clés et d’analyse des écarts.

 Rapports à l’intention du conseil d’administration et de la direction 

 Préparer des documents destinés à la direction et au conseil d’administration; y présenter des analyses claires, les risques, les occasions et des recommandations.

 Élaborer des textes et des supports visuels concis permettant de traduire des données financières complexes en incidences stratégiques visant à orienter la prise de décision.

 Coordonner les calendriers et les contributions afin de garantir la remise exacte et opportune de tous les rapports destinés au conseil d’administration et à la direction.

 Encadrer, former, et soutenir les membres de l’équipe par l’entremise de rétroaction régulière, d’évaluations du rendement, et de planification du perfectionnement professionnel.

 Favoriser une culture d’équipe inclusive axée sur le rendement qui correspond aux valeurs et aux objectifs de l’entreprise.

 L’expérience que vous apportez 

 Formation 

 Avoir un baccalauréat en comptabilité, en finance ou dans un domaine connexe.

 Être titulaire du titre professionnel en comptabilité (CPA) est requis.

 Expérience 

 Au moins 10 ans d’expérience dans la gestion financière et d’équipe.

 Aptitudes 

 Avoir un excellent sens des affaires et une excellente compréhension des tendances du secteur; faire preuve d’un esprit stratégique.

 Avoir des connaissances approfondies sur la modélisation financière, les prévisions et l’établissement de budgets.

 Faire preuve d’un esprit d’analyse affûté et d’excellentes compétences en communication; être en mesure de présenter des concepts financiers complexes à des parties prenantes non spécialisées en finance.

 Avoir un souci minutieux du détail.

 Posséder une vaste expérience dans la gestion de budgets et des prévisions pour des organisations de moyenne à grande envergure.

 Avoir une solide expérience dans la production de rapports de gestion, dans l’établissement de budgets et dans l’analyse.

 Nous encourageons et acceptons toutes les candidatures; toutefois, nous communiquerons seulement avec les personnes dont la candidature a été retenue pour une entrevue. jobs.description:
VP, Digital Experience & Growth 

 Job Type: Full time
 Location: Toronto
 Reporting to: CEO
 Role Type: New

 Goway Travel was founded in Toronto in 1970 by Bruce Hodge, a young Australian economist who moved to Canada to follow his dreams.

 From there, we have established ourselves as a global influence with offices in Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila. While the travel industry endured major challenges, our strong foundations allowed Goway to forge ahead. We continually innovated, invested in new technology, and challenged the status quo.

 Still owned and operated by Bruce, with the support of his leadership board, our mission has always been to help our clients realize their travel dreams. Today, we are an industry-leading, global travel company with over 800 employees. Our team of experts utilizes cutting-edge technology to tailor-make 4 and 5-star travel experiences in over 100 countries around the world.

 At Goway Travel, we're not just a company; we're a family of dreamers and doers, inspired by our founder’s incredible journey. He didn't just follow a career path; he followed his heart, and in doing so, he built a company that helps others follow theirs.

 If you’re passionate about travel and innovation, we invite you to be a part of our exciting journey!

 Job Purpose:  

 As our first Vice President, Digital Experience & Growth, reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll own the digital growth engine end to end: the website, search, performance marketing, lifecycle, and the data that ties it all together. This is a rare seat where strategy and hands-on craft meet, and where your work shows up directly in revenue. 

 If you thrive in an environment where innovation meets real-world impact, this role offers the opportunity to shape the technology behind unforgettable journeys. 

 What will be your key responsibilities? 

 Own the vision, governance and performance of Goway’s web properties and portals, leading CRO, UX, merchandising and customer-journey improvements.

 Shape strategy across paid, organic search, referral and emerging channels, tying investment to revenue, profitability, lead quality and long-term customer value.

 Build lifecycle strategy for Direct travellers and Trade partners, including journeys, nurture programs, re-engagement flows, advisor communications, personalization, loyalty, retention and referral.

 Build reporting that links marketing activity and website performance to business results, and partner with Technology on segmentation, audience strategy, lead-quality analysis and customer data strategy.

 Required Skills and Qualifications:  

 15+ years of progressive leadership in digital marketing, digital product, e-commerce, lifecycle, growth, CRM, analytics or customer experience.

 A track record of leading digital transformation or growth initiatives that moved the numbers.

 Hands-on strength in website optimization, SEO, acquisition, conversion, personalization and retention.

 Deep fluency in CRM, journey orchestration, marketing automation, analytics and martech, with the ability to lead across Marketing, Technology, Sales and Operations.

 What can you expect from Goway? 
Imagine working for a company where your career feels like an adventure. At Goway, you’ll join a global community that supports one another:

 We offer a competitive salary accompanied by performance incentives, and we place real importance on time away from work, such as paid personal days for when life calls for them and your birthday off each year.

 Your future matters to us, so we match your RRSP contributions and provide comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage.

 Our commitment to professional growth means you’ll have access to continuous learning and industry-leading training that keeps you at the forefront of travel innovation.

 Travel is in our DNA, so you’ll enjoy exclusive perks and discounts on worldwide getaways.

 Since we operate across Toronto, Vancouver, Los Angeles, Manila, Sydney, and beyond, you’ll collaborate across cultures and shape a career path that reflects your ambitions.

 Goway is an equal-opportunity employer. We celebrate differences and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace for everyone. We appreciate every applicant’s interest. Please be advised that only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

If this role feels like your next step, click "Apply Now" to create your profile, upload your CV, and share a few details about yourself. Our talent team reviews every application, and if your experience aligns with our needs, we will reach out to set up the next step.

To help us fairly and efficiently review applications, we use an automated screening process to assess responses to pre-determined questions. This initial step ensures all candidates are evaluated consistently. Qualified applicants will be reviewed by our recruitment team for further consideration.

Goway Travel Ltd will retain applications, notifications, and records related to this posting for three years, reflecting our commitment to fair and equitable hiring practices.

Please be aware of any suspicious emails or WhatsApp activity from individuals pretending to be recruiters or senior personnel at Goway Travel. We will never ask you to install an app during the recruitment process. If you receive a message of this nature, please ignore it and report it to Goway.

 About Goway 
Founded in Toronto in 1970 by Australian economist Bruce Hodge, Goway has evolved from a one-person dream into a family-owned global leader in tailor-made travel. With our headquarters in Toronto and hubs in Vancouver, Los Angeles, Sydney, and Manila, our team of over 700 talented employees designs travel experiences in more than 115 countries across all seven continents. We’re united by a passion for travel and are committed to doing the right thing: supporting diversity, equity, inclusion, and sustainable tourism that enriches local communities. Whether working remotely or side by side in one of our offices, we operate as one forward-thinking team, transforming wanderlust into life-changing adventures for our fellow Globetrotters. jobs.title: Director; IT Enterprise Applications
jobs.location: Dorval Head Office, Dorval, Quebec, Canada
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

 We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 160,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

 Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

 Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

 Join our team!

 The Opportunity 

 Top Aces is seeking a Director, IT Enterprise Applications, to lead the strategy, modernization and performance of our core business applications supporting Fleet management, flight planning, MRO, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources and Operations.

 This is more than an application support role. You will work directly with business leaders to improve processes, strengthen critical platforms, simplify our application landscape and help shape the future of enterprise technology at Top Aces.

 Our environment includes Ramco Aviation, flight planning HCL Notes, Oracle, UKG, SAP Concur, HCL Notes and Microsoft technologies supporting operations across Canada and internationally.

 What You Will Do 

 Develop and execute the Enterprise Applications strategy and roadmap.

 Lead the modernization and optimization of Pilot planning tools, Ramco, Oracle, UKG and other critical business platforms.

 Lead ERP and business-process assessments and help define the future target state.

 Partner with Fleet management, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Finance, HR and Operations to improve processes and eliminate manual workarounds.

 Establish application governance, ownership, lifecycle management and support standards.

 Rationalize the application portfolio and reduce technical debt and legacy-system risk.

 Strengthen integrations and enable trusted data for BI, AI and automation.

 Manage strategic application vendors and implementation partners.

 Build internal application capability while reducing key-person and vendor dependency.

 Ensure critical applications are reliable, secure, supportable and scalable.

 What You Will Bring 

 10+ years of progressive enterprise applications or technology experience.

 5+ years leading application, ERP or digital-transformation teams.

 Proven experience with ERP modernization and business-process transformation.

 Experience managing complex enterprise application portfolios and vendors.

 Strong understanding of ERP, integrations, APIs, application lifecycle management and IT service management.

 Experience in aviation, aerospace, defense, MRO, manufacturing or another asset-intensive environment is highly desirable.

 Experience with Ramco Aviation/MRO is a strong asset.

 Strong business and executive communication skills.

 Bachelor's degree in Technology, Engineering, Business or a related discipline.

 What Success Looks Like 

 Top Aces moves from fragmented applications and manual workarounds toward a simplified, integrated and resilient enterprise application ecosystem that improves mission readiness, operational efficiency and global scalability.

 Why Top Aces 

 This is an opportunity to shape the enterprise application landscape of a growing global aerospace and defense organization. You will influence major technology and business-process decisions and build an Enterprise Applications capability designed for the company's next stage of growth.

 Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR: 

   Position requires Level II Clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program.

 By joining Top Aces, you will find: 

 A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;

 Opportunities for development and growth;

 Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;

 A flexible schedule;

 Attractive benefit plan.

 Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

 Equal Employment Opportunity 

 At Top Aces, all employees are welcome regardless of race, nationality, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability or age. The masculine form may be used in this job description solely for ease of reading but refers to men, women and gender diversity.

 Proven experience leading and developing teams and managing cross-functional initiatives.

 Experience managing external agencies, consultants, contracts, budgets, and performance expectations.

 Experience overseeing Government Relations agencies, public affairs advisors, or stakeholder engagement programs is a strong asset.

 Strategic marketing and communications leadership.

 Brand stewardship and reputation management.

 Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and executive communication skills.

 Strong agency governance, contract management, and budget oversight capabilities.

 Sound judgement and the ability to navigate sensitive, complex, or high-profile matters.

Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
 
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
 
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
 
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.


The Role
The Director of Computer Systems Validation Program provides support to the Quality, Regulatory and Compliance function in support of qualification of Veeva Vault technology.
 
Primarily responsible for oversight of the assigned Validation teams to ensure on-time, on-budget delivery of computer system validation activities supporting general releases and patches/hot fixes. Plan and drive complex validation tasks (periodic review, new product introduction) across the Validation teams while advancing modern validation practices, including test automation strategies and the governance and validation of AI-driven capabilities. Mentor and develop leaders of the assigned Validation teams providing technical validation expertise, interpretation, and direction to assure compliance with GxP (GMP, GCP, Device) regulatory requirements, company policies and standards regarding validation, document control and change management.
 
Additional responsibility is to support the audit management function by presenting CSV operations during customer audits.

Veeva Ostro operates as a startup within Veeva, and sits at the intersection of life sciences, marketing, and artificial intelligence. As the Head of Data Analytics , you will lead the design, development, and continuous improvement of the data systems and associated measurement analyses that sit at the intersection of our products, customers, and commercial strategy. jobs.title: Senior Vice President, Enterprise Technology & Compliance
jobs.description:
About Kindsight: 
 Kindsight builds technology that helps fundraisers make a difference. For decades, Kindsight has supported the education, healthcare, and nonprofit sectors with fundraising tools and the largest charitable giving database on the market. And as the giving sector evolves, so does Kindsight. As the leader in fundraising intelligence, Kindsight leverages real-time data and AI to help thousands of organizations around the world identify, manage, and engage with donors - at any scale. With purpose-built CRMs that corral all of that donor information and campaign tracking into one place, donor prospect research tools that offer proactive insights and real-time donor intel, and generative AI that creates personalized, meaningful content drafts at scale, Kindsight’s product suite is truly changing the game for donor fundraising. 
 Position Summary: 
 We are seeking a strategic technology executive with extensive experience leading enterprise technology, cybersecurity, and compliance within a growing SaaS business. This leader will enable the business through modern, secure, and scalable technology while accelerating Kindsight's transformation into an AI-native company. Working closely with the CTO, you will lead the enterprise technology strategy that enables the business while complementing the company's product and engineering strategy. You will hire, lead, and develop a high-performing Enterprise Technology organization spanning IT, cybersecurity, and compliance. You will be responsible for ensuring budget discipline while optimizing technology investments and operating costs. In addition to enterprise technology responsibilities, this role will ensure the business operates within legal, regulatory, and ethical boundaries—especially around data, privacy, and global software regulations.
 What You’ll Do: 
 AI Strategy 
 Lead the development and execution of Kindsight’s internal enterprise AI adoption strategy, partnering with executive leadership to improve productivity, automate business processes, and deliver measurable operational and financial outcomes..

 Translate strategy into a clear technology roadmap across infrastructure, systems, and enterprise applications, supporting an AI-native operating model and a scalable, cost-effective SaaS environment.

 Lead enterprise technology transformation initiatives, including Lead-to-Cash, business systems modernization, business intelligence, and AI enablement, with accountability for execution, organizational adoption, and measurable business outcomes..

 Lead technology due diligence and integration for acquisitions, strategic partnerships, and other corporate initiatives.

 IT Operations and Business Systems 
 Own Kindsight’s enterprise technology ecosystem: business systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS), infrastructure, networks, collaboration platforms, and enterprise data architecture.

 Oversee day-to-day IT operations and end-user services, ensuring reliability, performance, and scalability, with strong service management practices including SLAs and incident management.

 Security and Risk 
 Own Kindsight’s enterprise information security program, establishing and maintaining appropriate security policies, controls, monitoring, and risk mitigation practices across corporate technology environments.

 Identify and manage technology risks, including vulnerabilities, third-party exposure, and operational risk.

 Oversee incident response, disaster recovery, and business continuity planning.

 Compliance and Privacy 
 Lead Kindsight’s information security and technology compliance programs, establishing governance, policies, controls, and audit readiness aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and recognized frameworks, including SOC 2 and ISO 27001.

 Establish governance for AI usage, third-party technology risk, and enterprise data management.

 Drive audit readiness, coordinate internal and external audits, and serve as the key contact for auditors, regulators, and enterprise customers.

 Oversee data privacy practices and monitor regulatory developments affecting SaaS and CRM platforms.

 Partnership and Culture 
 Partner with Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, Sales, and Customer Success to establish consistent security and compliance standards, support customer security assessments, and ensure appropriate governance across enterprise and customer-facing technology. Provide clear, concise updates to executive leadership on risk, security posture, and compliance status.

 People and Budget 
 Hire, lead, and develop IT and compliance teams, including directors and managers, with clear accountability, performance expectations, and succession planning.

 Manage the IT and compliance budget and oversee vendor selection, contracts, and performance, ensuring technology investments deliver business value.

 Build a culture of security, compliance, and responsible data use, including employee training programs.

 What We’re Looking For: 
 12+ years of progressive leadership experience in enterprise technology, cybersecurity, or IT operations, including significant executive-level responsibility within a complex SaaS or technology organization.

 In-depth knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (e.g., NIST), compliance standards (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.), and data protection.

 Proven executive leadership of enterprise-wide business transformation initiatives, serving as the accountable executive responsible for strategy, governance, planning, execution, and organizational adoption.

 Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise transformation roadmaps, including program governance, milestones, dependencies, and executive reporting.

 Proven experience creating and leading enterprise-wide communication and change management strategies that keep employees, leaders, and stakeholders informed and aligned throughout transformational initiatives.

 Track record of leading complex cross-functional initiatives across Technology, Product, Finance, Operations, Sales, and Customer Success while driving organizational alignment and measurable business outcomes.

 Demonstrated experience managing enterprise technology budgets, optimizing vendor expenditures, and allocating resources to deliver measurable business value.

 Deep understanding of enterprise architecture, cloud solutions (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud), and scalable infrastructure management.

 Strategic Vision: Ability to align technology roadmap with business objectives to enhance competitive advantage.

 Demonstrated experience deploying AI technologies to improve productivity, automate business processes, and drive measurable business outcomes across enterprise functions.

 Leadership: Exceptional team leadership, mentoring, and talent development skills, with experience managing remote or distributed teams.

 Communication: Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to convey complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders and the Board of Directors.

 Vendor Management: Strong negotiation skills for managing relationships with strategic technology partners and vendors.

 Experience leading enterprise technology within a high-growth SaaS organization, preferably in a private equity-backed environment.

 Bachelor’s or Master’s in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or IT, Cybersecurity or Information Systems and MBA or equivalent is an asset.

 What Success Looks Like 
 Accelerate responsible AI adoption across Kindsight's business functions, delivering measurable improvements in productivity and operational efficiency.

 Maintain a secure, highly available enterprise technology environment.

 Strengthen the company's security and compliance posture.

 Optimize technology investments while improving employee productivity.

 Build and develop a high-performing enterprise technology organization.

 What’s in it for you? 
 Compensation Range: $300,000-$350,000 CAD/USD OTE annually, based on experience, market benchmarks and role complexity. We aim to offer fair, competitive pay that reflects your skills and the market. 

 Time to unplug: Vacation, flex days, volunteer time and a team-wide year-end wellness shutdown.

 Whole-person health: Comprehensive health and dental, 24/7 virtual doctor visits and flexible wellness stipends.

 Flexibility first: Digital-first remote setup with built-in “work from anywhere” travel flexibility.

 Investment in you: Departmental professional development budgets and company-matched retirement savings.

 A team that celebrates: Paid parental leave, peer recognition rewards and company-wide celebrations.

 This advertised position is for an existing vacancy at Kindsight. At Kindsight, we’re proud to be a place where everyone belongs and has an equal opportunity to contribute, thrive and grow. We hire based on skills, potential, and impact, and we believe our differences fuel innovation. We welcome all individuals and do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity and expression, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, colour, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, marital status, pregnancy, sex, citizenship, education, languages spoken or veteran status. We’re building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to do meaningful work and make a difference. 
 We leverage artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools may help with resume screening, drafting job descriptions, creating interview questions and occasionally identifying potential candidates. All hiring decisions are made by our people, not AI. Our intent is to use AI thoughtfully to streamline administrative tasks, improve the candidate experience and support fair, unbiased hiring practices consistent with industry standards.

jobs.title: Director of Governance, Risk, and Compliance
jobs.location: New York City; San Francisco; Toronto
jobs.description:
About EliseAI 
 At EliseAI, we're improving the industries that matter most: housing and healthcare. Everyone needs a place to live and access to quality healthcare, yet both are often harder to secure than they should be. 

By integrating AI agents deeply into existing workflows, we make them more efficient, reduce costs, and improve the experience for everyone.

 Housing: We simplify how renters tour apartments, sign leases, submit maintenance requests, and stay connected with their property team—bringing everything they need for their home into one place.

 Healthcare: We make it easy to schedule appointments, complete intake forms, and we help patients communicate with providers, so everyone can focus on health instead of paperwork.

 With EliseAI, organizations reduce manual work, improve accessibility, and deliver a seamless experience across essential services. We recently raised a $350 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and Bessemer Venture Partners to accelerate this mission.

 About The Role 
 We are seeking a Director of Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) to scale our risk and compliance programs. This role will be instrumental in leading and scaling the GRC team to meet regulatory and IT audit readiness, manage third-party risk, and ensure our policies and processes align with industry standards.
 You will work cross-functionally with Security Engineering, Legal, and business stakeholders to operationalize compliance efforts, support audits, and manage the GRC team to respond to customer and vendor due diligence requests. This is a high-impact role with direct influence on our ability to meet critical compliance timelines and support the operations of the business.

 Key Responsibilities 
 Own and lead the company's GRC program, setting strategic direction across frameworks including SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI, HITRUST, and HIPAA

 Serve as the primary owner of audit relationships, overseeing planning, evidence collection, documentation, and auditor communications

 Define and enforce compliance roadmaps, ensuring cross-functional alignment and accountability on regulatory requirements

 Attract top-tier talent to scale the GRC team, providing mentorship, setting priorities, and managing team performance

 Oversee the vendor risk management program, including third-party due diligence, risk tiering, and escalation of critical findings

 Lead reviews of vendor and client security questionnaires (DDQs) in partnership with Security Engineering, with final sign-off authority

 Own the security and compliance policy framework — driving creation, review cycles, and organization-wide adoption

 Partner with Legal and Security leadership on security-related contractual obligations, including review and negotiation of security addenda

 Requirements 
 8+ years of experience in Governance, Risk, and Compliance, Information Security, or a related field, with at least 3 years in a leadership or program ownership role

 Deep expertise across compliance frameworks including SOC1, SOC 2, PCI, HIPAA, and ISO certifications

 Proven track record managing audit programs end-to-end, including direct relationships with external auditors

 Experience building or scaling a GRC function, including team hiring and development

 Strong understanding of vendor risk management, third-party due diligence, and risk-based decision-making

 Ability to translate complex compliance and risk topics for executive and board-level audiences

 Excellent cross-functional influencing skills — comfortable working with Legal, Engineering, and business leadership

 Willingness to work in person at our office 4-5 days a week

 Why Join 
 Growth and impact. It’s not often that you can get in on the ground floor of a funded startup that’s scaling so fast. That means that instead of following a playbook, you’ll be writing it. Every single day you will be challenged to identify how we can scale and execute on it. You’ll learn what works when you succeed and what doesn’t when you fail. Either way, the rest of the team will be here to support you.

 Benefits 
 In addition to the growth and impact you’ll have at EliseAI, we offer competitive salaries along with the following benefits:
 Equity in the company

 Medical, Dental and Vision premiums covered at 100%

 Fully paid parental leave

 Commuter benefits

 401k benefits

 Fitness & home services stipend to cover part of your expenses so you can focus on what matters

 A collaborative in-office environment with an open floor plan, fully stocked kitchen, and all meals covered in the office

 Unlimited vacation and paid holidays

 We'll cover relocation packages and make the move exciting, not painful!

 Job Compensation Range 
 The salary range for this role is $200,000 - $275,000 USD/CAD. EliseAI offers a competitive total rewards package which includes base salary, equity, and a comprehensive benefits & perks package. Exact compensation is determined based on a number of factors including experience, skill level, location and qualifications which are assessed during the interview process. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided by our Recruiting Team during the hiring process.

jobs.title: Interim Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
jobs.description:
Engagement: Interim · 9 months

Interim Chief Financial Officer (CFO)  
 Company: xNorth
Location: Toronto, Ontario
Engagement Type: Interim Executive Mandates
Typical Duration: 6–12 months 
 About xNorth 
 xNorth is a leading Canadian executive interim management firm providing proven executive leadership to organizations navigating transformation, growth, operational challenges, and critical leadership transitions.
 xNorth is the exclusive Canadian partner of the Valtus Alliance, a global leader in executive interim management with a presence in over 30 countries and more than 1,200 mandates managed collectively in 2025. Through this alliance, we deliver a consistent methodology, rigorous quality standards, and the same level of executive excellence across international markets.
 Our approach is grounded in operational experience. xNorth Partners are former senior executives and operators who bring firsthand leadership experience and remain actively involved throughout each mandate, working alongside clients and interim executives to ensure effective execution and measurable results.
 As xNorth continues to experience rapid growth and increasing demand for executive interim management solutions across Canada, we are expanding our network of experienced Interim Chief Financial Officers.
 Learn more at www.xnorthgroup.com.
 Opportunity 
 Join xNorth's executive talent network and bring your expertise as an experienced Chief Financial Officer to high-impact interim leadership assignments with organizations across Canada.
 Our clients include privately held and family-owned businesses, multinational corporations, private equity-backed companies, and other complex organizations across diverse industries.
 Assignments span a broad range of business situations, from leadership transitions and accelerated growth to financial transformation, performance improvement, mergers and acquisitions, and restructuring.
 As an Interim CFO, you will operate as a key member of the executive leadership team, working closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and the xNorth Partner overseeing the mandate to establish financial priorities, drive execution, and deliver measurable results.
 We are particularly interested in proven CFOs who combine strategic perspective with a hands-on, results-oriented approach, demonstrate sound judgment in complex environments, and can establish credibility and deliver impact from the outset of an assignment.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Responsibilities will vary depending on the nature, scope, and objectives of each mandate and may include:
 Executive Leadership & Strategic Finance 
 Serve as a trusted financial advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and shareholders.
 Define and execute financial strategies aligned with organizational priorities and business objectives.
 Provide financial leadership during periods of transition, growth, transformation, or uncertainty.
 Support executive decision-making through rigorous financial analysis, business insights, and clear recommendations.
 Financial Performance & Operational Excellence 
 Lead financial planning and analysis (FP&A), budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and performance management.
 Identify and execute opportunities to improve profitability, margins, cost structures, and operational efficiency.
 Strengthen financial visibility, accountability, and performance management across the organization.
 Cash Flow, Treasury & Financial Governance 
 Oversee cash flow management, liquidity, working capital, capital allocation, and treasury activities.
 Ensure the integrity and reliability of financial reporting, accounting processes, internal controls, and regulatory compliance.
 Manage relationships with financial institutions, auditors, lenders, and external advisors.
 Transformation, Transactions & Special Situations 
 Lead financial transformation initiatives, including process optimization, systems modernization, and organizational redesign.
 Provide financial leadership during mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, integrations, and other strategic transactions.
 Support refinancing, recapitalization, restructuring, turnaround, and other complex financial initiatives as required.
 Leadership & Organizational Development 
 Lead, mentor, and develop finance teams, ensuring operational continuity and effective execution.
 Assess organizational capabilities and strengthen the finance function as needed.
 Collaborate with business leaders across functions to align financial and operational priorities.
 Ensure effective knowledge transfer and a structured leadership transition at the conclusion of the assignment.
 Ideal Executive Profile 
 We are looking to connect with experienced financial executives who bring:
 Proven CFO leadership experience, with 15+ years of progressive finance experience, including significant accountability as a CFO or equivalent senior finance executive.
 A demonstrated track record of delivering measurable business results in complex, evolving, or demanding environments.
 Broad expertise in financial strategy, accounting, FP&A, treasury, financial governance, and business performance.
 The ability to operate effectively at both strategic and operational levels, from Board-level discussions to hands-on execution.

jobs.location: Remote UK, Remote Canada, Remote US
jobs.description:
CircleCI is the platform that powers continuous integration and delivery for the world's best engineering teams — helping them build, test, and ship software quickly, safely, and confidently, including the new generation of AI-assisted development. Do you want to lead the teams that set that example for customers?

 The Director, Engineering is a strategic leader who directs operational units across the engineering organization. You will own the technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for your engineering organization (typically 4-5 teams including engineering managers), collaborating on organizational engineering strategy and partnering across functions to deliver measurable business impact.

 This is a broad, high-impact seat — you'll partner closely with the VP of Engineering and peer leaders across the org to shape structure, roadmap, and operating standards for a group that's growing and evolving fast.

 This role balances technical depth with strategic thinking, people development with execution, and short-term delivery with long-term sustainability. You will work with Product, Go-to-Market teams, customers, and executive leadership to drive CircleCI's mission forward.

 Strategic Planning

 Your Strategic Responsibilities:

 Lead and grow a multi-team engineering organization, with ownership of its structure, headcount, and provide input for product strategy

 Partner with the VP of Engineering and cross-functional stakeholders on technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for your organization, ensuring alignment with company objectives.

 Raise the bar on engineering practices, operating standards, and delivery quality across the group

 Build and develop a strong management layer — hiring, coaching, and growing engineering managers and leads

 Define operating metrics and team goals; craft strategies to scale infrastructure and meet business objectives

 Cultivate a culture of excellence that closes the gap between business/roadmap commitments and what gets delivered

 Lead distributed engineering teams to deliver highly available, highly secure experiences at scale

 Bring real AI competency to the role — not just personal use of AI tools, but building the systems and practices that let your teams get genuine leverage from AI

 Represent your organization's roadmap, tradeoffs, and constraints clearly to Product and other cross-functional partners

 Your Decision-Making Authority:

 You have full authority to:

 Hire, promote, and performance-manage all engineers and managers within your organization

 Make final decisions on administrative and operational matters within your domain

 Approve technical architecture decisions that impact your organization alongside highly experienced senior engineers

 Prioritize and sequence engineering work; allocate budget for team tools, training, and resources

 Represent engineering in cross-functional forums and make commitments on behalf of your organization

 What We're Looking For

 This is a key role with significant impact on CircleCI's engineering organization and business outcomes.

 5+ years in engineering leadership, including direct management of managers

 Ability to translate business objectives into technical strategy and enable teams to deliver reliable, resilient, and secure features at scale

 A proven track record of building strong, aligned teams across varied technical surfaces

 Thorough understanding of developer tools market, practices, competition, and trends

 Genuine fluency with AI-assisted engineering workflows and what it takes to operationalize them at a team level

 Expert manager with ability to mentor and develop individual contributors and managers; build high-performing teams through recruiting, coaching, and creating growth opportunities

 Drive frameworks for people development, performance, inclusion, and belonging across your organization

 Data-driven problem solver who handles risk and uncertainty; coordinates work spanning departments with alignment to organizational goals

 Strong verbal and written communication skills; ability to influence teams, peers, leaders, executives, and customers

 Comfortable working with globally distributed teams across multiple time zones using synchronous and asynchronous communication, and making hard structural and personnel calls, not just process improvements

 $215,000 — $295,000 CAD 

 United Kingdom Base Pay Range
 £136,000 — £187,000 GBP 

 Expected salary range for San Francisco and the surrounding area.
