Senior Director, Analytics and Data Science, Core Product & Growth
jobs.description:
About Life360

 Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.  

 Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

 Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

 Life360 is a Remote First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US and Canada) regardless of any specified location above. 

 We are AI Native

 We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

 Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

 About The Team

 The Data & Analytics Team (DnA) is a 60+ person organization spanning data engineering, analytics engineering, analytics/decision science, and data science/ML. The science teams are organized into two sub teams, focusing on MAU and Revenue. This role leads decision science and data science within MAU.

 You and your team will be responsible for understanding the drivers behind MAU: why members come, why they stay, and why they return. The team partners with product, marketing, and engineering to put those learnings into everyday work, and that work shapes our roadmaps.

 Our data is unusual for a consumer company. Life360 measures families and circles rather than individuals, so one member's behavior affects another's, which makes measurement a different problem than a standard funnel. With billions of location events, driving behavior, crash detection, and Tile and Pet GPS trackers, we get a rich picture of physical behavior that few consumer companies can build.

 About the Job

 This Senior Director leads MAU Analytics and Data Science.

 You and your team will work across acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention on the analysis, models, and experiments behind each. A lot of what this role owns needs to be built rather than maintained: the measurement, the standards, and how the team uses AI. The team is also raising its craft, and coaching people through that is an important part of the job. Within a year, your team members will be operating at an elevated skill level, proactively bringing key questions to light, and serving as trusted advisors whom stakeholders consult for strategic guidance rather than simple task execution.

 You will report to the Head of Data and work closely with counterparts leading Revenue Analytics and Data Science, and with the leaders of Data Engineering.

 For candidates based in the US, the salary range for this position is $247,000 to $366,000 USD. For candidates based out of Canada, the salary range for this position is $286,000 to $339,000 CAD. We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers. 

 Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits. 

 What You'll Do

 Lead and develop the decision scientists and data scientists on the team, and set the quality bar for both disciplines.

 Own the MAU driver model and the forecast.

 Own the exploratory work that drives the strategy to grow MAU.

 Establish how an analysis gets scoped, run, reviewed, and written up, so its quality does not depend on who picked up the request.

 Partner with your Revenue counterpart and Data Engineering leadership to define common metrics, align on experimentation standards, and introduce unified operating practices across teams.

 Build the operating model that gets the team into the roadmap conversation early, with a view on what to build and what to test.

 Use agents and automated analysis daily, and expect the same of the team.

 Shape how the team works AI-native: what gets delegated to agents, what gets automated, and what stays human judgment.

 What We're Looking For

 Required Experience & Qualifications 

 10+ years in analytics, data science, or decision science, including 5+ years in people management in a senior leadership role.

 Deep expertise in inferential and causal analytics. Able to lead ML practitioners.

 Expert knowledge of engagement, retention, churn, and cohort metrics.

 Experience forecasting a company-level metric and being held to it.

 SQL, plus Python or R. 

 Experience with Databricks, third party experimentation tools (e.g. Statsig), Tableau or similar BI tools, and AI native BI tools (e.g. Hex, AI/BI).

 Hands-on with coding agents (Claude Code or equivalent) in your own analytical work.

 Bachelor's degree or equivalent.

 Nice to Have 

 Familiarity with experiment design to identify and control for network effects.

 Master’s degree or PhD with an emphasis in social science, psychology or other behavioral science.

 Experience leading a team that reports to you but sits embedded with product and engineering teams.

 Experience in a B2C subscription business.

 Core Expectations 

 You have moved an analytics team from reactive to embedded.

 You coach and develop people, and you have grown analysts into leaders.

 On your teams, analysis starts from a hypothesis rather than a data request.

 You have built the standards a team works from, and got people to use them.

 You are curious about why people behave the way they do, not just what they did.

 You decide what the team does not work on, and you can defend it.

 Our Benefits

 Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for US employees). We offer life and disability as well as supplemental plans for medical and dental for Canadian employees.

 401(k) plan with company matching program in the US and RRSP with DPSP plan for Canadian employees.

 Paid parental leave

 Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being

 Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns

 Learning & Development programs

 Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment.

 Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers.

 AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

 Life360 Values

 Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference 

 Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust. 

 Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

 Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families. 

 High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done. 

 Our Commitment to Belonging

 Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.

  

 #LI-Remote

ABOUT US 

 Localcoin, founded in 2017 with headquarters in Toronto, is on a mission to simplify the process and experience of buying or selling digital currencies globally. We envision bringing digital currency to the mainstream financial market through partnerships with leading corporate and franchised retail spaces. With terminals across Canada, Poland, and the APAC region—including Australia, Hong Kong, and New Zealand—Localcoin is now the fastest-growing Bitcoin ATM operator in the world.

 At its core, Localcoin believes that everyone should be able to own cryptocurrency and have a deep understanding of blockchain technology. As a member of our rapidly growing team, you'll join a talented, dynamic group of team members who will encourage you to learn, grow, and thrive in your career every step of the way.

 If you're a self-starter looking to hone your skills in a startup environment that fosters innovation, transparency, and team connectivity, we look forward to hearing from you!

 THE ROLE 

 Reporting to the Vice President of Technology, who leads both Product and Engineering, the  Director of Engineering, Innovations, will lead the teams responsible for Localcoin’s core platform, web applications, and new product initiatives. You’ll partner with Product to evaluate opportunities, shape priorities, and guide delivery.

 Your focus will be on leading people and guiding technical decisions. You’ll draw on your engineering experience and commercial judgment to evaluate architecture, challenge assumptions, and give teams the direction they need to execute.

 This is a leadership-focused role rather than a hands-on development position. The ideal candidate brings strong technical expertise, commercial awareness, and the ability to confidently evaluate architectural decisions, challenge assumptions, and navigate technical trade-offs while empowering their teams to execute.

 WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING 

 Engineering Leadership & Team Development  

 Set clear expectations, coach engineering leads and team members, and hold teams accountable for delivery and quality.

 Oversee team capacity, resource planning, and team delivery on projects. 

 Lead hiring efforts to build a strong engineering team that aligns with business growth plans.

 Foster a culture of collaboration, ownership, and continuous improvement.

 Product Engineering & Strategic Delivery 

 Partner with Product to assess opportunities, shape the roadmap, and agree on scope and delivery commitments.

 Oversee engineering delivery for new product initiatives, platform enhancements, and other strategic technology projects.

 Evaluate technical approaches through both a business and engineering lens, balancing speed to market, scalability, cost, and long-term sustainability.

 Technical Strategy & Decision-Making 

 Guide architectural decisions across product engineering. Work with engineering leads to evaluate options and make trade-offs across delivery speed, reliability, and cost.

 Evaluate technical solutions, challenge assumptions, and contribute alternative perspectives to ensure informed decision-making.

 Maintain a strong understanding of the company's technology ecosystem to guide teams and contribute to strategic technical discussions.

 Engineering Operations & Continuous Improvement  

 Own and improve the software development lifecycle across product engineering teams. Use team-level metrics and feedback to identify bottlenecks, improve delivery velocity and predictability, and maintain a sustainable pace.

 Drive continuous improvements in software quality, deployment practices, and engineering standards.

 WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR  

 Experience leading product engineering teams, developing talent, and improving delivery across multiple teams.

 Strong business acumen with the ability to align engineering decisions with business and product goals.

 Experience leading the development of software platforms, web applications, and new products.

 Technical depth in backend services, APIs, and third-party integrations, with the ability to evaluate architecture and explain the trade-offs to business stakeholders.

 Experience managing competing priorities and leading cross-functional initiatives.

 Strong communication skills and the ability to keep teams and stakeholders aligned as plans change.

 Proven ability to develop talent, build strong teams, and drive accountability.

 Salary Range:  $180,000-$200,00

 WHAT YOU’LL LOVE ABOUT US 

 Competitive Salary & Benefits – We value and reward our team members.

 RRSP Group Matching Program – We invest in your financial well-being.

 Hybrid Work Environment – Enjoy flexibility while being part of a dynamic team.

 Professional Development – Opportunities for learning and growth covered by Localcoin.

 Team Culture & Events – Regular socials, team meetings, and collaborative workspaces.

 Impactful Work – Play a key role in a growing company and make a real difference.

 JOIN OUR INCLUSIVE TEAM 

 Localcoin is committed to building an inclusive, accessible, and equitable workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, ancestry, place of origin, color, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital status, family status, or disability.

 If you require accommodation at any stage of the recruitment process, please notify the Talent team or email careers@localcoinatm.com.

 Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Canada. At this time, we are not able to provide visa sponsorship.

 AI DISCLOSURE STATEMENT 

 We want to share that we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to help screen and assess applications. While technology helps us stay organized and efficient, every hiring decision at Localcoin is made by real people who care about finding the best addition to our team. These tools are used to support our process—not to replace the human judgment and connection that are core to our culture.

jobs.title: Director of Ecommerce Growth
jobs.description:
At Hadley Designs, we believe early learning should be joyful, screen-free, and filled with connection.
 Founded by Becca Hadley, a former teacher and mom who began creating hand-drawn learning tools at her kitchen table, we’ve grown into a leading early childhood education brand trusted by millions of parents, grandparents, and teachers. Our products are developmentally sound, emotionally engaging, and intentionally designed to help children ages 3–8 grow curious, confident, and resilient.
 We serve busy, intentional families who are tired of screens and want more meaningful ways to teach and connect with their kids. From educational posters to busy books, handwriting guides to emotional learning kits, every product is crafted with care and rooted in research.
 Our vision is bold: to become the most trusted children’s brand in the world, present in millions of homes, and passed down for generations, while reaching $100 million in annual revenue by 2030.
 Today, Hadley Designs is an approximately $25 million ecommerce brand selling across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, and other channels. We've built a strong foundation, an established customer base, and a talented team of specialists. Now, our next chapter is about building a repeatable, profitable growth engine that can take us from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 We're looking for an entrepreneurial Director of Ecommerce Growth who has helped scale ecommerce brands before and knows how to turn growth opportunities into measurable business results. Someone who can see the bigger picture, connect the dots across channels, align talented teams, and determine where to invest, what to scale, and what to stop.
 This is an opportunity to take meaningful ownership of our growth strategy, build systems that consistently generate profitable demand, and help shape the next stage of Hadley Designs.

 Role Overview 
 The Director of Ecommerce Growth is responsible for building and leading Hadley Designs' next phase of profitable growth, developing a repeatable demand generation engine that can scale our business from $25 million to $100 million and beyond.
 This is a hands-on growth leadership role that combines strategic thinking, financial accountability, and cross-functional execution. We're looking for someone who thinks like an entrepreneur, understands the economics of scaling an ecommerce brand, and knows how to turn promising opportunities into profitable, repeatable growth systems.
 We've built a talented team of specialists across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, creative, and affiliate marketing. The Director of Ecommerce Growth connects the dots between these functions, aligning priorities, coordinating execution, removing bottlenecks, and ensuring our investments translate into measurable business results.
 This person doesn't need to be the best specialist in every channel, but they must know how to lead specialists, challenge assumptions, diagnose performance, and make the entire growth engine more effective. They take ownership of growth initiatives from strategy through execution, without relying on the CEO to drive every decision.
 The role is channel agnostic. We don't care whether our next major growth opportunity comes from Meta advertising, Amazon external traffic, Shopify, TikTok Shop, creator partnerships, AI-powered content, or an entirely new channel. What matters is identifying where the greatest opportunities exist, validating them through disciplined experimentation, and allocating resources toward what produces profitable, incremental growth.
 Equally important is knowing what not to pursue. The Director of Ecommerce Growth must be willing to challenge existing strategies, stop underperforming initiatives, and redirect resources toward higher potential opportunities.
 The vision: Build a diversified, scalable, and profitable growth engine that consistently generates new customer demand, turns successful experiments into repeatable systems, and operates without requiring the CEO's daily involvement, ultimately helping Hadley Designs become a $100 million brand by 2030.

Metrics that You'll Own 
 Incremental Contribution Profit: Generate at least $1,000,000 in annual incremental contribution profit from growth initiatives, after all attributable variable marketing and program costs.
 Incremental Demand Generation Revenue: Generate at least $7,000,000 in annual incremental revenue through paid media, affiliate marketing, creator partnerships, and new acquisition channels, regardless of whether customers purchase through Amazon, Shopify, or TikTok Shop.
 Marketing Efficiency Ratio (MER): Achieve a minimum 3.0x blended MER across the defined growth portfolio, while meeting contribution profit targets. Final target subject to validated channel economics.
 Growth Experiments: Execute at least 1 meaningful growth experiments per month (12 annually), each with a documented hypothesis, an approved budget, contribution profit target, performance review, and predefined stop criteria.
 Scalable Growth Engines: From the list of 12 growth experiments, at least 3 new experiments are repeatable, profitable growth engines annually, each generating at least $25,000 in incremental monthly revenue with positive contribution profit for three consecutive months.

 Primary Objectives 20% BIG ROCKS – These must be done first and at all costs.
 Build a Repeatable, Profitable Demand Generation Engine: Develop and scale sustainable sources of customer acquisition and revenue across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, affiliates, and emerging channels, prioritizing incremental contribution profit over revenue alone.
 Integrate and Lead Cross-Functional Growth Execution: Align existing specialists across creative, paid media, ecommerce, affiliates, and analytics around shared priorities. Own execution plans, remove bottlenecks, and ensure growth initiatives deliver measurable results without requiring the CEO's daily involvement.
 Own Growth Strategy and Marketing Investment Efficiency: Evaluate marketing performance using contribution margin, MER, acquisition costs, and incremental revenue. Determine where to allocate resources, what to double down on, and what to reduce or stop to maximize profitable growth.
 Build a Disciplined Growth Experimentation System: Identify new growth opportunities, launch at least 1 measurable experiment monthly, and systematically evaluate results. Turn winning experiments into repeatable, scalable growth systems while quickly discontinuing underperforming initiatives.
 Optimize Affiliate, Influencer, and Cross-Channel Demand Generation: Develop a profitable creator and affiliate strategy that connects TikTok Shop, Amazon, Shopify, and paid media. Ensure winning creator content, partnerships, and emerging AI opportunities are integrated into the broader growth strategy rather than operating as isolated programs.

 Regular Work Activities 80% – These must be done ongoing daily/weekly after the BIG ROCKS are complete. 
 GROWTH STRATEGY & PERFORMANCE 
 Monitor growth performance across Amazon, Shopify, TikTok Shop, paid media, affiliates, and emerging acquisition channels.

 AFFILIATE, INFLUENCER & CREATOR GROWTH

 AGENCY, PARTNER & TEAM MANAGEMENT

 SYSTEMS, ANALYTICS & AI

 REPORTING & ACCOUNTABILITY

jobs.description:

 To learn more, visit formswim.com

 The Opportunity 
Reporting to the CEO, you’ll own FORM’s finance function end to end. You’ll start by learning how our accounting function runs today, then partner with the team to strengthen controls and streamline processes as we grow. From there, you’ll lean into financial modelling and become a strategic partner to the executive team.
 You’ll work directly alongside the CEO, with access to our fractional CFO for mentorship. You’ll have real ownership over how FORM plans, reports, and grows, and the support to step up as the role expands. This role requires a hands-on leader who likes being close to the numbers.

 What You’ll Own 
 Lead a two-person accounting team, managing our Senior Accountant and supporting the development of the Accountant on their team
 Work with the team to put scalable internal controls in place for accurate, reliable financial statements

 What Great Looks Like

jobs.title: Director, Computational DMPK (Drug Metabolism & Pharmacokinetics)
jobs.description:
Deep Origin is a biotechnology company building an operating system for science that transforms how life science research is conducted. Our AI-powered platforms simulate biology, streamline R&D workflows, and enable scientists to model complex biological systems at scale. 
 Deep Origin leads the PREDICTS consortium, funded by ARPA-H under the CATALYST program, to build in silico models that predict human drug safety and toxicity. As part of this work we are scaling our capabilities in whole-human modeling and predictive toxicology. 

About the role
 Deep Origin is building VHAT, the Virtual Human Avatars of Toxicology. VHAT takes a molecule, a dose and a patient population and predicts organ-level human toxicity before a compound is synthesized or dosed. Metabolism sits at the heart of that chain. What a drug becomes, which enzymes act on it and how fast they act determine what each organ is exposed to, and every predicted metabolite is screened for its own off-target and organ liabilities. The Metabolism group builds four connected models: drug-metabolizing enzyme, site of metabolism, metabolite structure, and enzyme kinetics. As the group’s leader, you will own those models, mentor the team that builds them, and drive integration of their predicted parameters into the physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model that governs exposure across the VHAT.

 Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

jobs.title: Senior Director, People Operations
jobs.description:
A LITTLE BIT ABOUT Boldr
 Boldr is the first global B-Corp dedicated to delivering world-class Client experiences while creating
 access to dignified, meaningful work in communities around the world.
 We are a global team, united by our desire to connect diverse people with common values for boldr
 impact.

 LET’S START WITH OUR VALUES
 Excellent. Being excellent at what we do sets us apart. It happens when we care about our work and how it lands, set clear standards, and hold each other accountable. We don't stop at meeting the standard; we keep raising the bar.
 Authentic. Real connection happens when we show up as our best, truest selves, help others dothe same, and stand by each other through the harder times.
 Curious. Curiosity keeps us innovative. Better understanding comes from asking helpful questions, seeking to understand before we act, and building on each other's thinking.
 Dynamic. Growth is central to our purpose, and it only happens in dynamic environments where we stay flexible, adaptable and open.
 Empathetic. Great partnerships happen when we take the time to understand the people we work with, our teams, our clients and our communities, for better outcomes for each.

 WHAT IS YOUR ROLE
 As Senior Director, People Operations, you are the operational and governance backbone of Boldr's People function. You own the systems, rewards, and standards that let a five-country division run with consistency and care.
 Three connected disciplines roll up to you across the Philippines, South Africa, Mexico, Canada, and the United States:
 People Operations and Systems: the employee lifecycle, our HRIS (Rippling), people data, service delivery, and self-service.
 Total Rewards: compensation and benefits, Living Wage governance, pay equity, and job banding.
 Business Partnering: ER cases and investigations, multi-country labor law compliance, risk and audit, and the policies and handbooks that keep us fair and consistent.

 This is a role for a builder and an operator. The longer-range strategic agenda, organizational design, performance strategy, and strategic business partnering, sits with the VP and grows alongside our People Success team. Your mandate is to make the backbone genuinely excellent: scalable processes that do not rely on heroics, clean and trustworthy data, sound compliance across every jurisdiction, and a team member experience that reflects our values wherever people work.
 You report to the VP, People, and you are one of the leaders the rest of the division depends on to keep the engine running as we scale.

 WHY DO WE WANT YOU
 We are looking for an impact-driven operator who can give a fast-growing, five-country division the backbone it needs to scale without breaking. Someone who builds systems that last, holds a high bar on compliance and fairness, and still keeps the human center in every process they design.
 You will protect organizational health, bring calm and consistency to sensitive moments, and make the everyday experience of working at Boldr feel reliable and fair in every country we operate in. We do all of this so our team members can thrive as we grow.

 WHAT WILL YOU DO
 People Operations and Systems
 Own the employee lifecycle end-to-end: onboarding, changes, and offboarding, delivered consistently across all five countries.
 Lead Rippling as our HRIS and system of record; design and maintain clean workflows, self-service, and service delivery (ticketing and knowledge base).
 Establish data integrity and reporting discipline: headcount, attrition, and the people data leaders rely on to decide well.
 Partner closely with Payroll to protect accuracy and timeliness in every jurisdiction.
 Modernize People infrastructure through automation and sound system design, so support scales without manual workarounds.

 Total Rewards
 Own compensation and benefits governance across all geographies, anchored to our Living Wage philosophy as the pay floor.
 Direct compensation cycles with rigor and clarity: timelines, manager enablement, auditability, and clear communication.
 Oversee job banding and pay structures using our market data source (Payfactors), keeping pay equitable and defensible.
 Steward pay equity and transparency norms that build trust while managing risk appropriately.

 Employee Relations
 Oversee sensitive ER cases, investigations, grievances, and disciplinary matters through the Business Partnering team, and personally lead the most complex cases, with consistency, fairness, and empathy.
 Build the ER frameworks and manager guidance that keep outcomes fair and well-documented across countries.
 Serve as a trusted, high-integrity escalation point on difficult people matters.

 Compliance, Risk, and Governance
 Ensure compliance across all five countries and both operating models: Managed Outsourcing and Global Employment (EoR).
 Own records, audit, and data protection for People data.
 Translate local labor realities into sound, consistent decisions, flag clearly where in-country counsel is needed, and engage and consult with counsel on these matters.
 Build the governance and risk frameworks that let us scale responsibly.

 Policy Development and Maintenance
 Own the development, maintenance, and governance of People policies and employee handbooks.
 Keep policy current with changing labor law in each jurisdiction, and consistent with our values and B Corp commitments.
 Make policy clear, accessible, and genuinely useful to managers and team members, not just technically compliant.

 Team Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership
 Lead and develop the People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering teams; set clear goals, coach for growth, and build a culture of service excellence.
 Own the budget for People Operations, Total Rewards, and Business Partnering, including people, systems, and vendor costs, and ensure it meets company requirements.
 Establish clarity on decision rights, service levels, and escalation paths, so it is clear how People decisions get made here.
 Partner with the VP, the Talent Acquisition and People Success pillars, Business Operations, Finance, and client-facing teams to keep the backbone aligned to the business and company strategy.

jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering (Canada)

We combine deep expertise in cloud-native development with a relentless focus on quality, speed, and innovation.  We are a company where technologists lead, ideas win on merit, and shipping great software fast is a core value—not a slogan. If you believe world-class engineering teams are the ones that move quickly and build things right, you'll feel at home here.

jobs.title: Director of Development Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
ABOUT NEW ENERGY NEXUS
 New Energy Nexus (NEX) is an international NGO that supports climate solutions and builds a more equitable clean energy economy. Our laser focus is on clean energy entrepreneurs: providing them with funds, accelerators, and networks to thrive. They are our main audience and our agent of change.

We started in California in 2004 and now operate across China, India, Southeast Asia, East and West Africa, and Australia. We have leveraged US$5.4 billion in investment and supported more than 11,000 entrepreneurs.

 ABOUT THE ROLE & OPPORTUNITY
 The Director of Development Strategy & Operations will lead the internal engine behind New Energy Nexus' global fundraising and business development efforts. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, this role sits at the center of NEX's development team — turning what our development and partnerships staff and country teams learn on the ground with funders into a coherent, prioritized fundraising strategy, and making sure the team is coordinated, resourced, and focused on the highest-value opportunities. 
 This is not primarily a donor-facing relationship management role. It is a strategy, team leadership, and fundraising operations role for someone who understands the business and fund development cycle deeply enough to translate frontline intelligence — what funders are signaling, what's landing and what isn't, where proposals are stalling, which markets and programs are attracting interest — into clear direction for where the team should spend its time.
 The Director will lead and develop NEX's global platform-level development team, ensuring that individual team members' skills and expertise are deployed effectively against organizational priorities, while bringing together the knowledge and fundraising capabilities of country leaders, chapter teams, and program leads. The ideal candidate has the analytical rigor and systems mindset of a strong operations leader, paired with real fluency in philanthropic and development finance fundraising, so they can be a credible internal leader and partner to a globally distributed team of fundraisers, country directors, and program leads.

 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 Fundraising Strategy & Prioritization (50%) 
 Help develop a living, prioritized development strategy based on proposal outcomes, funder conversations, and market signals gleaned from team conversations and learnings from fundraisers, country directors, and program leads
 Synthesize funder conversations, proposal outcomes, market signals and intelligence generated across the organization into clear fundraising priorities
 Identify where NEX should be focusing time and effort across programs and geographies, based on funder appetite, pipeline strength, and organizational priorities.
 Maintain a clear view of the funding pipeline across the network — by funder, program, chapter, and stage — and flag risks, gaps, or unrestricted-vs-restricted balance issues early.
 Translate strategy into concrete guidance: which opportunities to prioritize, which proposals need repositioning, where the team is over- or under-invested.
 Serve as a thought partner to the CEO and program leads on funding strategy, drawing on patterns across markets rather than any single relationship.

 Team Coordination & Enablement (35%) 
 Lead and develop the global platform-level development team including recruiting, hiring, onboarding, coaching, and managing performance, and ensure team members' skills are effectively leveraged against NEX's development priorities.
 Translate the development strategy into a clear rolling work plan for the team, aligning ownership, resources, and timelines.
 Build strong collaboration across the global development function, bringing together the expertise and fundraising capabilities of platform-level staff, country leaders, fundraisers, and program leads to maximize collective impact.
 Run the operating rhythm of the fundraising team: pipeline reviews, proposal coordination across programs/chapters/finance/communications, and prioritization check-ins.
 Coordinate multi-country and multi-program proposals, including combining country and program inputs into a cohesive narrative and budget that aligns with broader NEX operational and growth priorities.
 Build and own a central library of fundraising collateral - pitch decks, one-pagers, case studies, program summaries, impact data - so materials for funder meetings and conference talks can be assembled quickly rather than built from scratch each time.
 Draft and maintain core funder and conference decks, adapting a standard set of modular slides/content to each audience so our fundraisers can focus their time on external relationship-building and speaking rather than deck production.
 Partner with the Chief Communications Officer to keep collateral aligned with current messaging, program updates, and brand standards.
 Provide country leads and fundraisers with the tools, templates, frameworks, and support to raise funds effectively and report consistently.
 Build feedback loops so that what is learned through funder and country-level engagement consistently makes its way back into strategy, priorities, and team planning.

 Systems, Data & Reporting (15%) 
 Accountable for the fundraising CRM and pipeline-tracking systems, ensuring data quality, consistent use across chapters, and useful reporting.
 Produce regular and ad hoc reporting and dashboards for NEX leadership on pipeline health, funder trends, and progress against platform fundraising goals.
 Standardize proposal, reporting, and stewardship templates and processes across the global platform-level team.
 Track outcomes against the fundraising strategy and refine it as new data comes in.
 Ensure fundraising protocols and internal as well as external reporting are completed on time and to consistent quality standards

 SUCCESS IN THE FIRST 6–12 MONTHS
 Success in this role will mean building a more coordinated, strategic, and effective global development function. By the end of the first 6–12 months, the Director will have:
 Established clear visibility into NEX's global fundraising pipeline, priorities, risks, and opportunities, with leadership able to make decisions based on reliable, current information.
 Built a strong operating rhythm across the global platform-level development team, with clear ownership, effective collaboration, and team members' skills deployed against the highest-priority fundraising opportunities.
 Improved coordination across platform, country, and program teams so that high-value proposals are prioritized appropriately, developed collaboratively, and submitted on time and at a consistently high quality.
 Established consistent CRM and pipeline management practices across the development function, with data being used to inform strategy, prioritization, and reporting.
 Created a well-organized, accessible library of standardized fundraising collateral and tools that enables fundraisers and country teams to move more quickly and consistently.
 Established effective feedback loops between funder and country-level intelligence, fundraising performance, and the organization's overall development strategy.

jobs.title: Director of Sales

 Help define product-market fit. Test what resonates with mid-market and enterprise buyers, read the signals in our pipeline, and tell us plainly what’s working and what isn’t. Bring market signals and customer feedback to Product and leadership to shape where Botpress goes next.

 Lead an AI-native sales team. Embed AI into how the team researches accounts, develops outreach, prepares for calls, plans deals and forecasts. Model it yourself, share what works, and help sellers spend more time on judgment, strategy and customer relationships.

jobs.title: Director, Operations
jobs.description:
veritree and Job Overview
 veritree is an award-winning climate tech start-up based in Vancouver. Launched in 2021, our technology measures and verifies the impact of global restoration efforts from the ground up. We are on a mission to plant 1 billion verified trees by 2030, collaborating with businesses, planting organizations, and consumers who believe in the transformative power of verified restoration projects to create real and meaningful impact for the planet, nature, and people.

veritree is seeking a Director, Operations to lead our Operations team: the glue that connects our teams and initiatives. Reporting to the COO, you will own veritree’s Revenue Ops, Supply Ops, Business Ops, and Business Intelligence functions. These functions empower our Revenue, Forests, Product & Engineering, and Finance teams to operate as one business.

 We sell verified trees sourced from planting partners worldwide, alongside new business lines in carbon, monitoring technology licensing, and nonprofit programs. That makes our business closer to a two-sided marketplace than pure SaaS: every customer commitment depends on supply, delivery, and data lining up behind it. As we move to a new AI-native platform, our Operations team is evolving into a team of operations engineers who build the tools, automations, and data flows the business runs on.

This is a hands-on role: you’ll run operations first and then evolve the systems behind it. You inherit a capable team and working systems (several of which we’ve outgrown) and leave behind infrastructure the rest of the company can build upon. The role starts at Director-level, with room for advancement as determined by job performance and business needs.

 12 Month Key Outcomes (12m KOs)
 Take the wheel: within your first 90 days, run the weekly operations cadence, own escalations across all four functions, and become the decision-maker on operational calls.
 Operating rhythm: set up how Operations runs for the next stage of the company: a clear meeting rhythm, defined team roles/decision rights, one agreed definition and owner for core metrics (pipeline, ACV, NRR, gross margin, tree inventory), and a 12-month operations roadmap signed off by executive leadership.
 Trusted data and reporting: keep commercial and delivery data clean across HubSpot, NetSuite, and the platform through go-live and beyond, and produce the monthly reporting pack and the operational metrics in board reporting from the BI stack.
 AI and automation: ship AI-powered tools and automations that measurably reduce manual work and save costs across the business.

What You’ll Do
 Cross-Functional Operations
 Run the operating cadence (meeting cadences, monthly business reviews, semi-annual planning) and the forums where Revenue, Forests, and Product & Engineering align on priorities.
 Own the deal desk with Sales, Customer Success, and Forests, so what we sell matches what we can deliver.
 Own the intake, prioritization, and SLA framework for operations requests from every team.
 Own operational readiness on the platform after go-live: close workflow gaps with Product & Engineering and lead change management.
 Make operational and commercial decisions within agreed guardrails (pricing, margin floors, custom deliverables), and escalate exceptions to executive leadership with a clear recommendation.
 Team Leadership & Development
 Lead, coach, and develop the Operations team, including managers and individual contributors.
 Own hiring, onboarding, and ongoing performance management, in partnership with People Operations.
 Evolve the team into operations engineers by defining roles and scopes and building a culture that is both high-accountability and high-support.
 Revenue Operations
 Own HubSpot as our commercial system of record, including deal stages, order and contract workflows, and clean handoffs between Sales, Customer Success, Legal, and Finance.
 Own the customer revenue forecast and its methodology, in partnership with Finance and Revenue leadership.
 Own pricing discipline: the price sheet, margin floors, and a quarterly margin and pricing review.
 Own lead and sales funnel, retention, and unit-economics reporting.
 Supply Operations
 Own demand and supply planning, translating the customer forecast into tree demand by ecosystem and region and partnering with Forests on sourcing and capacity.
 Own order management, inventory allocation, purchase orders, and fulfillment tracking, including future obligations to customers and planting partners, so every order is delivered on time against the right supply.
 Business Operations
 Own the processes, policies, tooling, and Operations budget that keep the business running, and decide what gets automated and what stays manual.
 Run the OKR process and tracker, and support annual operating planning.
 Own the operating model for customer and partner site visits.
 Business Intelligence & Reporting
 Own our data warehouse and BI layer, pulling from HubSpot, NetSuite, the platform, and planting data, as the single source of truth for operational metrics.
 Direct the team’s AI agenda, shipping internal tools, agents, and workflow automations that measurably increase output across the business.

jobs.title: Account Director (Performance Marketing Agency)
jobs.description:
This job posting is available in English and Canadian French. Please scroll down for the French version. 
 Cette offre d’emploi est disponible en anglais et en français (Canada). Veuillez faire défiler pour la version française. 
 ________________________________
 Remote - U.S. & Canada Only | Full-Time 
 Compensation: 
 $80K - $130K USD (U.S.-based candidates)
 $80K - $130K CAD (Canada-based candidates)
 We’re Not Looking for Generic Account Leadership. We’re Looking for a Performance Marketing Leader. 
 Level Agency is hiring an Account Director with deep performance marketing agency experience — someone who knows how to lead client relationships, connect strategy to execution, and drive measurable business outcomes.
 You may be a current Account Director at a performance marketing agency. Or, you may have started hands-on in paid media, analytics, or campaign management before moving into account leadership. Either way, you understand what great performance marketing looks like because you’ve worked close enough to the work to know what actually moves results.
 You can speak credibly about Google Ads. You understand how media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and reporting all connect. You know how to spot issues before they become client escalations. And you’re confident enough to lead a room without making it about your title.
 You’re especially strong when the path to conversion is complex — where lead quality, pipeline, sales alignment, landing pages, and conversion journeys matter as much as media efficiency.
 This is not a “status call and recap email” role. This is for someone who can connect client business goals to marketing strategy, push back with purpose, and lead a focused book of accounts with depth — rather than spreading their attention across a high-volume roster with limited depth.
 This Isn’t for Everyone. 
 We’re building something rare: a place where growth, truth, and high performance go hand-in-hand.
 You’ll thrive here if: 
 ✅ You’ve led client relationships in a performance marketing agency environment.
✅ You understand how modern marketing channels work together — media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, website, CRO, and analytics.
✅ You can speak credibly about Google Ads and paid media strategy.
✅ You care about client business results, not just campaign metrics.
✅ You can lead a focused book of clients deeply, not manage a huge roster shallowly.
✅ Your default is “I’ll handle it,” even when the work sits slightly outside your lane.
 And you’ll struggle here if: 
 ❌ Your experience is primarily brand, creative, ecommerce, or DTC without deeper performance agency experience.
❌ You’ve only managed accounts at the surface level across a very large client load.
❌ You need a narrow job description to know what you should own.
❌ You protect scope before you protect the outcome.
❌ You can’t speak credibly about channel strategy beyond talking points.
 About Level
 We’re an AI-powered performance marketing agency — built for precision, designed to scale, and powered by a scientific mindset. At Level, we blend strategy, media, creative, and machine intelligence to deliver outcomes that matter. Every time. At scale.
 We’ve been named one of Pittsburgh’s Best Places to Work and an Inc. 500 Fastest-Growing Company. Our clients span B2B, education, healthcare, financial services, ecommerce, and more.
 Your Role (and Impact)
 As an Account Director, you’ll lead performance-driven client relationships across a focused book of accounts. You’ll sit at the intersection of client strategy, marketing execution, internal team leadership, and business impact.
 You’ll be the person clients trust to tell them the truth, the person internal teams count on to create clarity, and the person who keeps strategy tied to measurable outcomes.
 You’ll:
 Lead Performance Strategy: Translate client business goals into multi-channel marketing strategies that drive measurable growth.
 Own Client Relationships: Build trust with senior stakeholders through clear communication, proactive thinking, and sharp strategic recommendations.
 Connect the Marketing Ecosystem: Help clients understand how paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and reporting work together to improve performance.
 Bring Paid Media Fluency: Speak credibly about Google Ads, paid social, and media performance — even when you’re not the person making every in-platform change.
 Spot Issues Early: Dig into performance trends, ask better questions, and catch problems before they become client escalations.
 Push Back with Purpose: Challenge client assumptions when needed — always in service of the performance goal, never ego, scope protection, or control.
 Manage a Deep Book: Lead a focused portfolio of accounts with enough depth to truly understand each client’s business, performance drivers, and risks.
 Guide Internal Teams: Partner with media, SEO, creative, analytics, and strategy teams to keep work moving, priorities clear, and outcomes aligned.
 Tell the Story in the Data: Turn reporting, dashboards, and performance analysis into insights clients can act on.
 Own the Details: Keep budgets, forecasts, timelines, documentation, and communication sharp and accurate.
 Requirements
 Must-Haves
 5+ years in a performance marketing agency. You have agency experience rooted in performance, paid media, and measurable outcomes — not primarily brand, creative, or ecommerce-only work.
 Account leadership experience in a performance environment. You are either currently an Account Director at a performance marketing agency or you started in marketing, paid media, analytics, or campaign management before transitioning into account leadership.
 Google Ads fluency is required. You can speak credibly about Google Ads and understand what to investigate when performance shifts, lead volume drops, or conversion quality changes.
 Modern marketing ecosystem understanding. You understand how paid media, SEO, creative, data, CRM, websites, CRO, and analytics connect to drive outcomes.
 Paid media strategy depth. You understand how media channels work together, especially search and social, and can translate performance signals into strategy.
 Client leadership experience. You’ve managed client relationships, led strategic conversations, and presented recommendations to senior stakeholders.
 Focused account management experience. You’re used to leading a meaningful book of clients deeply — roughly 3 to 8 accounts — rather than spreading your attention across a high-volume roster with limited depth.
 Experience with meaningful media spend. You’ve worked with clients spending at least $50K/month in media per client; $100K+/month is strongly preferred.
 Business-first mindset. You talk about revenue, pipeline, lead quality, conversion paths, customer journeys, and business outcomes — not just CTRs, CPCs, and platform metrics.
 Low ego, high ownership. You’re willing to build the dashboard, chase the answer, clean up the ambiguity, or step into the gap when the team needs it.
 Strong Preferences
 B2B, lead generation, or complex-sale experience. Experience with longer buying cycles, pipeline quality, sales alignment, or non-DTC conversion paths is a major plus.
 Meta, LinkedIn, SEO, CRM, CRO, or other channel fluency. You don’t need to be an expert in every channel, but you should understand how they work together.
 Experience in financial services, healthcare, education, SaaS, or other considered-purchase verticals.
 Comfort with dashboards, reporting tools, Google Analytics, and data visualization.
 Experience mentoring account team members or coordinating cross-functional delivery teams.
 AI Expectations
 At Level, AI is a skillset — not a shortcut. In this role, you’ll be expected to:
 Use tools like ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude, and Perplexity to improve how you work
 Share your prompts, process improvements, and ideas with the team
 Experiment regularly and refine your workflows over time
 Embrace discomfort as part of the learning process
 Apply AI tools to increase your speed, clarity, and creativity — not to replace thoughtful work
 AI should make you sharper, faster, and more strategic. It should never replace judgment, taste, accountability, or a strong point of view.
 Our Core Values
 No Ego, All In 
We don’t do “that’s not my job.” We win together, step in where needed, and care more about the outcome than the org chart.
 Better Every Day 
We want the feedback — even when it stings. We test, learn, adapt, and keep raising the bar.
 Relentless for Results 
Activity is nothing without outcomes. We care about the work that moves the business forward.
 Driven by Truth 
We challenge assumptions, follow the data, and tell clients what they need to hear — not just what is easy to say.
 Perks & Benefits
 At Level, we support our people across the U.S. and Canada with benefits designed to promote flexibility, wellbeing, and long-term growth.
 Fully remote across the U.S. & Canada, plus monthly WFH stipend and Summer Fridays
 Generous time off, including unlimited PTO (U.S.), competitive vacation (Canada), and parental/family leave options
 Comprehensive health benefits, mental health support, and company-paid disability & life coverage
 Employer retirement contributions (401(k) in the U.S., RRSP match in Canada)
 Quarterly performance reviews and career advancement opportunities
 Remote First
 This role is open to U.S. and Canada residents and is fully remote. We are unable to sponsor visas at this time.
 Level Is Built on Inclusion
 We are committed to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. Level is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer — we celebrate what makes you, you.
 Ready to Apply?
 Click below to submit your resume. You’ll also answer a few thoughtful questions, so take your time.
 We care more about how you think, how you lead, and how you create impact than whether your path has been perfectly linear.
 Let’s build something together.

 Télétravail – États-Unis et Canada seulement | Temps plein 
 Rémunération: 
 80 000 $ à 130 000 $ US pour les personnes candidates basées aux États-Unis
 80 000 $ à 130 000 $ CA pour les personnes candidates basées au Canada
 Nous ne cherchons pas un leadership de comptes générique. Nous cherchons un leader en marketing de performance.
 Level Agency recrute un ou une Account Director possédant une solide expérience en agence de marketing de performance — une personne capable de diriger les relations clients, de relier la stratégie à l’exécution et de générer des résultats d’affaires mesurables.
 Vous êtes peut-être actuellement Account Director dans une agence de marketing de performance. Ou encore, vous avez commencé les mains dans le cambouis en médias payants, en analytique ou en gestion de campagnes avant de passer au leadership de comptes. Dans tous les cas, vous comprenez à quoi ressemble un excellent marketing de performance, parce que vous avez été assez près du travail pour savoir ce qui fait réellement avancer les résultats.
 Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads avec crédibilité. Vous comprenez comment les médias, le SEO, la création, les données, le CRM, les sites Web, le CRO et le reporting s’imbriquent. Vous savez repérer les problèmes avant qu’ils ne deviennent des escalades client. Et vous avez assez d’assurance pour mener une discussion sans que tout tourne autour de votre titre.
 Vous êtes particulièrement solide lorsque le parcours vers la conversion est complexe — là où la qualité des leads, le pipeline, l’alignement avec les ventes, les pages de destination et les parcours de conversion comptent autant que l’efficacité média.
 Ce n’est pas un rôle de « status call et courriel de récapitulation ». Ce rôle s’adresse à une personne capable de relier les objectifs d’affaires des clients à la stratégie marketing, de challenger avec intention et de diriger un portefeuille de comptes ciblé en profondeur — plutôt que de disperser son attention sur une longue liste de clients gérés en surface.
 Ce poste n’est pas pour tout le monde. 
 Nous bâtissons quelque chose de rare: un endroit où la croissance, la vérité et la haute performance avancent ensemble.
 Vous allez vous épanouir ici si: 
 ✅ Vous avez dirigé des relations clients dans un environnement d’agence de marketing de performance.
✅ Vous comprenez comment les canaux marketing modernes fonctionnent ensemble — médias, SEO, création, données, CRM, site Web, CRO et analytique.
✅ Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads et de stratégie médias payants avec crédibilité.
✅ Les résultats d’affaires des clients vous importent plus que les simples indicateurs de campagne.
✅ Vous pouvez diriger un portefeuille ciblé de clients en profondeur, plutôt que gérer une énorme liste en surface.
✅ Votre réflexe naturel est « je m’en occupe », même lorsque le travail dépasse légèrement votre champ habituel.
 Et vous aurez de la difficulté ici si: 
 ❌ Votre expérience est principalement axée sur la marque, la création, le commerce électronique ou le DTC, sans expérience approfondie en agence de performance.
❌ Vous avez seulement géré des comptes en surface, dans un contexte de très grand volume de clients.
❌ Vous avez besoin d’une description de poste très étroite pour savoir ce qui vous appartient.
❌ Vous protégez le périmètre du mandat avant de protéger le résultat.
❌ Vous ne pouvez pas parler de stratégie de canaux avec crédibilité au-delà des grands principes.
 À propos de Level
 Nous sommes une agence de marketing de performance propulsée par l’IA — bâtie pour la précision, conçue pour croître, et alimentée par une mentalité scientifique. Chez Level, nous combinons stratégie, médias, création et intelligence machine pour générer des résultats qui comptent. Chaque fois. À grande échelle.
 Nous avons été nommés parmi les meilleurs lieux de travail de Pittsburgh et reconnus comme l’une des entreprises à la croissance la plus rapide du classement Inc. 500. Nos clients œuvrent notamment en B2B, en éducation, en santé, en services financiers, en commerce électronique et dans plusieurs autres secteurs.
 Votre rôle et votre impact
 À titre d’Account Director, vous dirigerez des relations clients axées sur la performance au sein d’un portefeuille de comptes ciblé. Vous serez au croisement de la stratégie client, de l’exécution marketing, du leadership auprès des équipes internes et de l’impact d’affaires.
 Vous serez la personne à qui les clients font confiance pour leur dire la vérité, celle sur qui les équipes internes comptent pour créer de la clarté, et celle qui garde la stratégie arrimée à des résultats mesurables.
 Vous devrez:
 Diriger la stratégie de performance: Traduire les objectifs d’affaires des clients en stratégies marketing multicanaux qui génèrent une croissance mesurable.
 Prendre en charge les relations clients: Bâtir la confiance avec les parties prenantes seniors grâce à une communication claire, une pensée proactive et des recommandations stratégiques solides.
 Relier l’écosystème marketing: Aider les clients à comprendre comment les médias payants, le SEO, la création, les données, le CRM, les sites Web, le CRO et le reporting travaillent ensemble pour améliorer la performance.
 Apporter une aisance en médias payants: Parler avec crédibilité de Google Ads, des médias sociaux payants et de la performance média — même si vous n’êtes pas la personne qui effectue chaque changement dans les plateformes.
 Repérer les problèmes tôt: Creuser les tendances de performance, poser de meilleures questions et détecter les enjeux avant qu’ils ne deviennent des escalades client.
 Challenger avec intention: Remettre en question les hypothèses des clients lorsque nécessaire — toujours au service de l’objectif de performance, jamais par ego, protection de périmètre ou besoin de contrôle.
 Gérer un portefeuille en profondeur: Diriger un portefeuille ciblé de comptes avec suffisamment de profondeur pour vraiment comprendre les activités, les leviers de performance et les risques de chaque client.
 Guider les équipes internes: Collaborer avec les équipes médias, SEO, création, analytique et stratégie afin de faire avancer le travail, clarifier les priorités et aligner les résultats.
 Raconter l’histoire dans les données: Transformer les rapports, les tableaux de bord et les analyses de performance en insights que les clients peuvent mettre en action.
 Maîtriser les détails: Garder les budgets, prévisions, échéanciers, documents et communications clairs, exacts et à jour.
 Exigences
 Essentiels
 5 ans et plus dans une agence de marketing de performance. Vous avez une expérience en agence ancrée dans la performance, les médias payants et les résultats mesurables — et non principalement dans la marque, la création ou le commerce électronique seulement.
 Expérience en leadership de comptes dans un environnement de performance. Vous êtes actuellement Account Director dans une agence de marketing de performance, ou vous avez commencé en marketing, médias payants, analytique ou gestion de campagnes avant de faire la transition vers le leadership de comptes.
 Aisance obligatoire avec Google Ads. Vous pouvez parler de Google Ads avec crédibilité et savez quoi examiner lorsque la performance fluctue, que le volume de leads baisse ou que la qualité des conversions change.
 Compréhension de l’écosystème marketing moderne. Vous comprenez comment les médias payants, le SEO, la création, les données, le CRM, les sites Web, le CRO et l’analytique se connectent pour générer des résultats.
 Solide profondeur en stratégie médias payants. Vous comprenez comment les canaux médias fonctionnent ensemble, particulièrement le search et le social, et pouvez traduire les signaux de performance en stratégie.
 Expérience en leadership client. Vous avez géré des relations clients, animé des conversations stratégiques et présenté des recommandations à des parties prenantes seniors.
 Expérience en gestion de comptes ciblée. Vous avez l’habitude de diriger un portefeuille significatif de clients en profondeur — environ 3 à 8 comptes — plutôt que de répartir votre attention sur une longue liste à haut volume avec peu de profondeur.
 Expérience avec des budgets médias significatifs. Vous avez travaillé avec des clients qui investissent au moins 50 000 $ par mois en médias par client; 100 000 $ et plus par mois est fortement souhaité.
 Mentalité orientée affaires. Vous parlez de revenus, de pipeline, de qualité des leads, de parcours de conversion, de parcours client et de résultats d’affaires — pas seulement de CTR, de CPC et de métriques de plateforme.
 Peu d’ego, beaucoup d’ownership. Vous êtes prêt ou prête à construire le tableau de bord, chercher la réponse, clarifier l’ambiguïté ou combler l’écart lorsque l’équipe en a besoin.
 Fortement souhaités
 Expérience en B2B, génération de leads ou ventes complexes. Une expérience avec des cycles d’achat plus longs, la qualité du pipeline, l’alignement avec les ventes ou des parcours de conversion non DTC est un grand atout.
 Aisance avec Meta, LinkedIn, le SEO, le CRM, le CRO ou d’autres canaux. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être expert ou experte dans chaque canal, mais vous devez comprendre comment ils fonctionnent ensemble.
 Expérience dans les services financiers, la santé, l’éducation, le SaaS ou d’autres secteurs à achat réfléchi.
 Aisance avec les tableaux de bord, les outils de reporting, Google Analytics et la visualisation de données.
 Expérience en mentorat auprès de membres d’équipes de comptes ou en coordination d’équipes de livraison interfonctionnelles.
 Attentes liées à l’IA
 Chez Level, l’IA est une compétence — pas un raccourci. Dans ce rôle, on s’attendra à ce que vous puissiez:
 Utiliser des outils comme ChatGPT, Midjourney, Claude et Perplexity pour améliorer votre façon de travailler
 Partager vos prompts, vos améliorations de processus et vos idées avec l’équipe
 Expérimenter régulièrement et raffiner vos façons de travailler au fil du temps
 Accueillir l’inconfort comme une partie normale du processus d’apprentissage
 Appliquer les outils d’IA pour augmenter votre vitesse, votre clarté et votre créativité — sans remplacer un travail réfléchi
 L’IA devrait vous rendre plus aiguisé ou aiguisée, plus rapide et plus stratégique. Elle ne devrait jamais remplacer le jugement, le goût, l’imputabilité ou un point de vue solide.
 Nos valeurs fondamentales
 Pas d’ego, engagement total
 Chez nous, « ce n’est pas mon travail » n’a pas sa place. Nous gagnons ensemble, nous prêtons main-forte là où il le faut, et nous nous soucions davantage du résultat que de l’organigramme.
 Meilleur chaque jour
 Nous voulons recevoir du feedback — même lorsqu’il pique un peu. Nous testons, apprenons, nous adaptons et continuons à élever la barre.
 Obsédés par les résultats
 L’activité ne vaut rien sans résultats. Ce qui compte pour nous, c’est le travail qui fait avancer l’entreprise.
 Guidés par la vérité
 Nous remettons les hypothèses en question, suivons les données et disons aux clients ce qu’ils doivent entendre — pas seulement ce qui est facile à dire.
 Avantages et bénéfices
 Chez Level, nous soutenons nos équipes aux États-Unis et au Canada grâce à des avantages conçus pour favoriser la flexibilité, le bien-être et la croissance à long terme.
 Télétravail complet partout aux États-Unis et au Canada, allocation mensuelle pour le travail à domicile et vendredis d’été
 Congés généreux, incluant des congés payés illimités aux États-Unis, des vacances concurrentielles au Canada et des options de congé parental/familial
 Assurances collectives complètes, soutien en santé mentale, et assurance invalidité et assurance vie payées par l’entreprise
 Cotisations de retraite de l’employeur: 401(k) aux États-Unis et contribution REER au Canada
 Évaluations de performance trimestrielles et occasions d’avancement professionnel
 Télétravail d’abord
 Ce poste est ouvert aux personnes résidant aux États-Unis et au Canada et est entièrement en télétravail. Nous ne sommes pas en mesure de commanditer des visas pour le moment.
 Level est fondée sur l’inclusion
 Nous sommes engagés envers la diversité, l’équité, l’inclusion et l’appartenance. Level est fière d’être un employeur souscrivant au principe de l’égalité d’accès à l’emploi — nous célébrons ce qui fait de vous une personne unique.
 Prêt ou prête à postuler?
 Cliquez ci-dessous pour soumettre votre CV. Vous répondrez aussi à quelques questions réfléchies, alors prenez le temps qu’il faut.
 Ce qui nous importe le plus, c’est votre façon de penser, votre façon de diriger et votre capacité à créer de l’impact — pas que votre parcours ait été parfaitement linéaire.
 Bâtissons quelque chose ensemble.
